About the First Peoples Program


The First Peoples: Tell Us a Story initiative is a specialized professional development program designed to build bridges between First Peoples and Radio-Canada. It aims to amplify Indigenous voices in the media while nurturing lasting, reciprocal relationships with Indigenous communities.


Building on the success of its 2025 pilot, the initiative returns this year with a redesigned format. This paid training opportunity has been expanded to eight (8) weeks and will focus on the craft of storytelling. Throughout the program, you will hone your skills through hands-on workshops led by both Indigenous and non-Indigenous media professionals. You will also have a dedicated platform to share your stories, showcase your culture, language and lived experiences, and highlight your community's achievements.


We are looking for four (4) individuals from First Nations, Inuit or Métis communities ready to take the next step in their media careers.


The program runs full time for eight (8) weeks, from February 1st to March 26, 2027. Full-time availability, Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. (ET) for the entire eight-week program is mandatory.


This program is in hybrid mode (remote work with required travel to Montreal and a regional station).


Candidates must meet the following eligibility requirements:

  • Be 18 years of age or older.
  • Self-identify as First Nations, Inuit or Métis.
  • Be available full time for the duration of the program (February 1st to March 26, 2027).
  • Be willing and able to travel for three (3) separate five-day sessions during the eight (8) weeks (travel and accommodation expenses are fully covered by Radio-Canada).
  • Be able to work and communicate in French (reading, writing and speaking). 

Who You Are:

  • You have a working proficiency in French across speaking, reading and writing. 
  • You have a genuine curiosity about news and current affairs, paired with a passion for storytelling.
  • You have an open, collaborative attitude.
  • You are eager to learn new things.
  • Familiarity with Google Workspace tools is an asset.

Program Overview:

As part of this second cohort, you will complete an eight-week learning curriculum running from February 1st to March 26, 2027.


The program includes the following:

  • Orientation and Onboarding: Settle into the cohort and preview your training plan through a combination of virtual sessions and in-person activities in Montreal. 
  • Theory Instruction (Three (3) weeks, Virtual): Build foundational journalism skills across digital writing, audio/radio storytelling and video production, culminating in one (1) to three (3) portfolio-ready pieces. 
  • Regional Station Placement: Shadow and work alongside Radio-Canada journalists at a regional station to experience the day-to-day rhythm of an active newsroom.
  • Professional Development (Virtual): Take part in sessions designed to support your learning and development. 
  • Closing Week (Montreal): Wrap up the program alongside your peers with a final week of hands-on activities. 

Workplace and Technical Requirements :

The theory instruction will take place primarily online; however, you must be available to travel to Montreal and to a regional station during designated periods. All required travel and accommodation expenses are fully covered by Radio-Canada.


Please note:

  • You must have access to a reliable, high-speed internet connection.
  • You must have access to a desktop computer, laptop or iPad Pro. 
  • Any specialized production gear required for your training modules will be provided by Radio-Canada for the duration of the program. 

Full-time availability for the entire eight-week program is mandatory.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance. 
 
Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Unposting Date:

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

 

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

 

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

 

This role requires full-time on-site presence.

 

Please note that this posting is for two positions.


Your role

 

This technician will be mainly assigned to the MPC Operation in the Toronto Broadcast Centre. The primary function will be to oversee the playback of Digital, Radio and TV signals through an automated system to the Canadian public.

 

Based on established requirements, perform tasks needed for the efficient and accurate presentation of digital, radio or television material for programs or events. Creative problem-solving may be required during presentation. Work is generally performed according to accepted CBC or industry standards, but independent action, judgment and initiative are also needed to solve operational issues. When directions or requirements are not clear, contact staff concerned for clarification, or use independent judgment under severe time constraints. Signal problems or imperfections clearly and promptly to the relevant authority.

 

Key Duties:

  • Perform presentation operations for Digital, Radio and TV programs.
  • Perform necessary checks, adjustments and alignments in accordance with standard procedures to ensure technical equipment remains in good working order.
  • Monitor and control signals, ensuring adherence to approved technical standards, and take appropriate action if quality is below standard. Report errors, imperfections and gaps.
  • Operate, program, and keep in good working order all complex presentation systems.
  • Keep equipment, applications and technical devices in a suitable state and available for use by ensuring they remain in good working condition.
  • Oversee the distribution of complex, fast-paced live news and current affairs programs, using studio or location signals, coping with programming changes, multiple or unknown sources and other elements on an ongoing basis.
  • In the absence of supervisors or management, assist broadcasting staff in solving problems.
  • Direct and coordinate the work of other staff assigned to prepare, set up, install and operate equipment. Help train co-workers.
  • Advise partners on technical operations needs and requirements related to equipment and facilities.
  • Perform, in whole or in part, the functions or duties of an equivalent or lower classification.

 

We are looking for a candidate with the following:

  • Willing to work a variety of shifts in an on-site 24/7 operation, including weekends and holidays.
  • Overall general knowledge of Digital streaming, Radio and TV program production, delivery and presentation methods, including a basic understanding of production crafts. Knowledge generally gained through college studies or equivalent relevant experience in TV/radio broadcasting.
  • Directly related experience, including one year as a broadcast technician.
  • Functional bilingualism (English and French) is an asset.
  • Knowledge of the Digital, Radio and TV server environment is a major asset.
  • Knowledge of Avid, Dalet+, iNews applications, and Windows OS.
  • Able to program complex automated presentation systems.
  • Good knowledge of TV and Radio control rooms is an asset.
  • Knowledge of communication networks and audio hookups.
  • Able to work independently.
  • Must have high availability and be accountable for the smooth presentation of programs.
  • Must demonstrate creativity in finding solutions rapidly.
  • Able to perform assigned duties effectively under tight deadlines, producing quality work and maintaining a positive, professional attitude.
  • Able to rise quickly and effectively to challenges in the work environment.
  • Able to get organized quickly.
  • Excellent communicator.
  • Able to analyze a situation and make decisions efficiently and rapidly, also communicating them effectively.
  • Good sense of initiative.
  • Proactive.
  • Good concentration skills, especially during program presentations.
  • Good attitude toward co-workers; team player.

2026-11-25 11:59 PM

Producer: Radio, Comedy


CBC Radio’s live comedy show Because News is looking for a creative, curious and resourceful Producer to help bring the week’s news to life through comedy. Combining strong journalistic instincts, a sharp sense of humour, excellent production skills, particularly in scriptwriting, editorial storytelling and audio editing, you’ll help create one of Canada’s most beloved comedy programs.

If you love comedy and the news, this is an opportunity to put your newsroom skills to work every day, finding the funny in current events and helping produce smart, surprising audio, podcast and digital content.


The role


The Producer, Radio Comedy works in a highly-collaborative team with the executive producer, host, producers and writers to research, develop, write, produce and edit program segments. The role combines strong editorial judgment, creative initiative and hands-on production skills to deliver distinctive, accurate and engaging content in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

This is a hands-on editing role requiring extensive tape-cutting experience, along with exceptional editorial judgment and sophisticated audio storytelling instincts. The successful candidate will be an accomplished audio editor who can shape raw improvised material into polished, compelling programming under intense deadline pressure.


Main responsibilities

  • Edits each weekly episode to an exceptional standard, bringing a well-trained ear for tape, sharp editorial instincts and masterful editing skills. Works quickly and efficiently to craft tight, compelling listening experiences and versions across radio and podcast.
  • Quickly identifies the strongest moments, cuts what doesn’t work and makes decisive editorial choices that preserve the spontaneity, comedic timing and energy of the live recording  under demanding production deadlines. 
  • Mixes audio bumpers and stings to brand the programme with pod-safe music and taglines. 
  • Demonstrates excellent asset management skills and a thorough understanding of audio specifications across CBC publishing platforms, including file compression, formatting and audio optimization to ensure the highest possible sound quality. 
  • Researches news stories, current events and cultural developments to identify material with strong comedic and editorial potential.
  • Develops, pitches, researches, and writes compelling scripts (quiz rounds), and other program elements, demonstrating extensive writing experience and exceptional writing, editing, and proofreading abilities, with an advanced command of grammar, vocabulary, and language. 
  • Contributes to daily editorial meetings, helping shape the program’s coverage of the news and identify opportunities for satire, parody and commentary.
  • Exercises sound journalistic judgment in evaluating stories, sources, facts and comedic material.
  • Fact-checks scripts and research, verifies information.  
  • Edits and re-writes scripts for the host and contributors, responding to editorial changes and troubleshooting under deadline.
  • Participates in control room operations and live broadcasts, helping coordinate timing, technical elements and communication among the host, guests and production team.
  • Contributes ideas and material for the program’s social media, digital platforms and established TikTok channel, adapting content for different audiences and formats.
  • Identifies emerging comedic voices and perspectives, contributing to a program that reflects the diversity of the communities CBC serves.
  • Supports the executive producer in preparing production plans, coordinating resources and tracking production requirements.
  • Liaises with the in-person audience, welcoming them into the Toronto Broadcast Centre each week. 
  • Keeps abreast of Canadian comedy and talent, competing programming, cultural developments, broadcasting trends and current affairs.
  • Contributes to a positive, respectful and collaborative workplace culture in a team that writes together for much of the week. 
  • Performs other related production duties as required.



Your profile

  • University degree or equivalent combination of education, training and relevant experience, including internships, job shadowing, workshops or other learning opportunities.
  • Experience in journalism, radio broadcasting, podcasting, digital media or a related production environment.
  • Exceptional audio editing skills, with a proven track record of excellence in cutting and shaping broadcast and podcast programming. 
  • Strong journalistic instincts and demonstrated news judgment, including the ability to assess stories quickly and accurately under deadline.
  • Demonstrated ability to write with clarity, precision, creativity and personality, adapting tone and style for comedic contexts.
  • Outstanding research and editorial skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information, identify compelling angles and translate current events into engaging, intelligent content.
  • A strong interest in comedy, satire and current affairs, with an instinct for identifying the comedic potential in news and cultural stories.
  • Extensive experience in live broadcast or live event production, with the ability to manage competing priorities, adapt quickly to changing circumstances, and remain calm and decisive under pressure.
  • Strong organizational skills  and the ability to manage competing priorities while meeting tight deadlines.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work constructively with hosts, performers, writers and colleagues.
  • An interest in discovering and developing new talent and bringing a range of voices and perspectives to the program.
  • A distinctive perspective, lived experience or area of expertise that can enrich the program’s content.
  • Flexibility to adapt to changing production needs, work patterns and hours, including one evening a week (Thursday.) 

Relevant knowledge and skills

  • Advanced knowledge of audio editing software and digital production tools.
  • Significant experience writing and editing material for live performance and broadcast.
  • Excellent command of Canadian English, spelling, grammar and editorial conventions.
  • Experience developing content for social media and digital platforms, with an understanding of audience engagement and platform-specific storytelling is an asset. 
  • Exceptional digital video editing skills are an asset.
  • Familiarity with CBC journalistic standards, policies and practices, particularly as they apply to satire, parody, opinion and commentary.
  • Awareness of the editorial considerations involved in producing comedy based on real people, events and current affairs.
  • Knowledge of radio and podcast production workflows, studio operations and live broadcast techniques.
  • Familiarity with social media publishing, content moderation and digital audience development.
  • Knowledge of Canadian comedy, performers, writers and the broader cultural landscape.
  • Familiarity with relevant union agreements, including those involving the Writers Guild of Canada (WGC) and the Canadian Media Guild (CMG), is an asset.

The ideal candidate combines a journalist’s curiosity with a comedy producer’s imagination. They understand that great comedy begins with great research, thrive on collaboration and can move confidently between developing an idea, writing a script, editing others’ scripts, checking the facts, editing audio and helping bring a live program to air. They will bring sound judgment, creative energy and a collaborative approach to finding the balance between being funny, being fair and being accurate.

CBC New Brunswick is looking for an experienced and dynamic producer to help lead the creation of original and engaging visual content on our TV, digital and social platforms.


The successful candidate will be an editorial leader and an experienced mentor, someone who demonstrates sound editorial judgment and who thrives as part of a team in the fast-paced, high-pressure world of a multi-platform newsroom.


In this role, you will collaborate with journalists across the newsroom to ensure we are marshalling and deploying our video resources across all of our stations effectively in order to set the news agenda and connect our audiences to the news they need to know, the stories that affect their lives and the issues that resonate in their communities.


You will be a strategic thinker who has a deep knowledge of digital, broadcast and social media strategies and trends, and you will put audience needs and audience growth at the centre of all your decision-making. You will have a strong desire to experiment with new forms of storytelling to help us engage more meaningfully with audiences. You will strive to broaden the range of perspectives and experiences reflected in our news content, especially those from people who have been traditionally underrepresented in the media.  


You possess excellent communication and interpersonal skills, are a strong planner and organizer, and are at ease with juggling multiple tasks and priorities at once. You care about the people you work with and have a recognized ability to coach and motivate others.  


You will ensure that all our work adheres to CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices and that it upholds our core principles of accuracy, fairness, balance, impartiality and integrity. 


This role requires full time on site presence in Fredericton. 


Your responsibilities:


  • Under the direction of the senior producer, work with reporters, associate producers, VJs, video producers, videographers and editors to conceive of and produce digital-first visual news and current affairs content that will align with strategic objectives and will resonate with audiences across platforms.
  • Determine story treatments, vet scripts and video, and plan video content rollouts for all platforms. 
  • Work with journalists in the newsroom and in the field to produce live programming across video platforms including our daily television news.
  • Provide editorial oversight to ensure our content is original, relevant and impactful, and meets our journalistic standards.
  • Collaborate with various teams across platforms and locations to ensure our visual content reaches the widest possible audience.
  • Inform best practices and streamline workflows for digital video platforms.
  • Provide feedback and coaching to journalists to help them develop their skills and produce content of the highest quality.
  • Assist with planning coverage for special projects and events.
  • Fill in for the senior producer of visuals as warranted.

Your profile: 


  • Demonstrated experience working in a fast-paced daily multi-platform news environment. 
  • Strong journalistic and critical thinking skills, including knowledge of and familiarity with CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices as well as the legal and ethical issues related to journalism.
  • Ability to manage and organize large volumes of fast-moving information and quickly redirect resources to meet priorities and objectives.
  • Knowledge of and experience in assigning and creating visual content for a variety of platforms (digital, social, television) as well as vetting, editing, fact-checking and packaging.
  • Experience in producing live visual content from the field and/or the control room.
  • Experience executing digital and social strategies including setting objectives, tracking results and reporting on outcomes.
  • A high-energy leader with a positive, team-first attitude and the demonstrated ability to motivate and coach teams, and encourage creativity.
  • A strong proven connection to the communities we serve in New Brunswick, and a deep and nuanced understanding and appreciation of diverse perspectives and lived experiences.
  • A keen desire to live and promote the values of diversity and an inclusive and respectful work culture. 
  • Ability and willingness to work flexible hours as required.
  • Possession of a valid driver’s licence as well as a driving record that meets the minimum requirements of CBC/Radio-Canada's insurance company.
  • University degree in journalism or equivalent with a minimum of five years of journalism experience.

Your role


CBC Newfoundland and Labrador is looking for a Producer, Visual News to lead our visual content focus across digital, streaming, social and broadcast platforms.


Reporting to the Executive Producer and collaborating closely with newsroom leadership; you and other producers responsible for visual news will produce and guide journalists daily. This role is central in shaping how our visual journalism connects with audiences in Newfoundland and Labrador and across Canada. You will champion audience growth and innovation by creating visual news content and by guiding news gathering, editing and packaging on digital-first framing, modular and vertical video news storytelling across our owned-and-operated site as well as YouTube, FAST/streaming channels, TikTok and television lineups.


You combine creative, forward-looking journalistic instincts with hands-on technical execution. You will build and vet scripts, edit video, craft graphics and package content with strong headlines, descriptions and thumbnails to maximize audience reach and engagement. Using analytics and audience research to inform your editorial choices, you ensure all visual content meets CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices (JSP) while driving our multi-platform newsroom forward in the daily news cycle.


Key Responsibilities

 

  • Plan and deliver digital video formats, including vertical video for social packaging (TikTok, YouTube, social desks) and digital-first visual treatments of daily news and current affairs segments.

  • Guide reporters, VJs and video producers on all aspects related to visual elements. Review, fact-check, and vet scripts, rough cuts, and packaged stories for accuracy, tone, fairness and adherence to CBC Journalistic Standards and Practices (JSP).

  • Write intros, headlines and captions in an audience growth mindset. Source, edit and assemble video and audio elements; request and create custom graphics, supers, and maps; and optimize video packaging (such as custom thumbnails and SEO-friendly metadata).

  • Monitor real-time digital performance metrics and analytics to identify high-performing content; ie., collaborate on A/B testing and adjust packaging and distribution strategies to expand local audience engagement.

  • Facilitate constructive feedback, and contribute to shared best-practice documentation.

Qualifications


We are looking for a candidate with the following:


  • Proven expertise in digital video storytelling, vertical video strategies and digital audience engagement across web, streaming and social platforms.
  • Minimum five years of recent journalism experience in a multi-platform news environment.
  • University degree in Journalism or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
  • In-depth knowledge of Newfoundland and Labrador news, culture, communities, and regional realities, along with a firm grasp of national and international affairs.
  • Demonstrated hands-on technical proficiency with non-linear video editing, graphic creation/story treatment tools, newsroom rundown systems and field gathering workflows.
  • Strong line-up and broadcast writing skills with a proven track record of quick, sound editorial judgment under tight deadlines and during breaking news.
  • Thorough knowledge of CBC Journalistic Standards and Practices (JSP), fair use and source/video verification protocols.
  • Experience analyzing digital performance metrics and translating data into actionable editorial strategies.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with an open, collaborative approach to mentoring peers, navigating change and fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace.

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Your Role

 

Reporting to the Program Manager, you will join the Digital Products and Innovation team, where a major initiative to modernize CBC/Radio-Canada's digital ecosystem is underway to make it more resilient in a changing media landscape. This work is being done in close collaboration with several departments and will contribute to building the future of the public broadcaster.

 

As a Project Lead, you oversee the entire lifecycle of your projects. While ensuring adherence to deadlines, budgets, and defined scope, you provide motivating leadership to teams to guide their work, distribute responsibilities, and maintain a high level of commitment.

 

To achieve this, you will first need to contribute to the analysis and feasibility of the projects and propose the best approaches to meet the mandate's objectives. You will also need to plan the lifecycle stages of each project, from initiation to launch. Furthermore, you will need to follow up with relevant stakeholders and members of the various teams involved to ensure project progress, implement proactive risk management, and communicate status updates to stakeholders.

 

Note that our working methodology is hybrid (Agile and Waterfall).

 

What will your responsibilities be?

  • Evaluate, coordinate and optimize human resources material, budgetary and project activities.
  • Advise, guide and provide specialist expertise during the evaluation, planning or development of projects.
  • Recommend solutions taking into account management objectives and CBC/Radio-Canada policies.
  • Orchestrate the team's calendar, including agile events such as daily stand-ups, planning (sprint or kanban), retrospectives, reviews, cross-team dependency alignment, and any other relevant meetings.
  • Develop the timeline based on the Product Manager's priorities (and/or sprints), factoring in scope, estimates, target delivery date, required resources, and budget.
  • Formally manage requests for scope changes in evaluating and communicating their impact on timelines, team capacity and initial budgets.
  • Align project timelines with the interdependencies of other initiatives and ensure that communication remains fluid between the different teams and stakeholders.
  • Establish and maintain the project risk register and develop the necessary mitigation plans.
  • Participate in negotiating agreements with internal and external stakeholders as needed for the projects.
  • Establish control processes at different stages of the project and ensure compliance with acceptance criteria.
  • Take full accountability for project reporting and status updates, and, in collaboration with the Product Manager and Program Manager, serve as the primary point of contact for senior leadership and executive committees.
  • With the help of experts, find solutions to both technical and operational problems and constraints.
  • In collaboration with the program manager, he defines and enforces the project governance structure (e.g., steering committees).
  • Transmit blocking elements to higher hierarchical levels if support is needed.
  • Identify, define, track and analyze key indicators to measure team delivery and performance.
  • Fostering a self-organizing and high-performing team culture by promoting autonomy, accountability and cross-functional collaboration, while helping teams establish and overcome barriers to ensure smooth progress and value delivery.

 

How will you make the difference?

  • Knowing how to apply Agile and waterfall work methodologies (waterfall).
  • Adhere to best project management practices in order to strengthen quality and productivity standards.
  • To foster a culture of collaboration across different teams.
  • Support and motivate your team members.

 

What profile are we looking for?

  • Bachelor's degree in business administration, master's degree in project management, or other relevant university degree (or equivalent experience).
  • Minimum of seven years of experience as a project manager delivering complex digital products and projects, including end-to-end accountability for projects with significant cross-functional dependencies and alignment with governance committees as needed.
  • Proven mastery of the complete project lifecycle: work organization, budget management, capacity management, scope control, risk assessment/mitigation and governance.
  • Ability to manage projects with a strong technical focus.
  • Excellent judgment, strong autonomy, ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Experience in leveraging the iterative cycle: frequent deliveries of new versions enabling rapid improvement.
  • Mastery of Atlassian (Jira, Confluence, Tempo) and Google suite; knowledge of Google's artificial intelligence tools is an asset.
  • Inclusive and unifying leadership, demonstrated ability to mobilize cross-functional teams, build trust and positively influence without formal authority.
  • Demonstrated ability to move with ease and composure in rapidly changing environments. Great personal resilience, ease in the face of ambiguity and ability to positively support teams through change.
  • Ability to quickly assimilate new technologies and adapt to changes by learning.
  • Ability to share one's knowledge.
  • Strong communication skills (oral and written).
  • Excellent level of spoken and written French.
  • PMP certification, agile certification or lean management an asset.
  • Bilingualism (French and English).

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we all have a story to tell. What's yours?

 

If you share our passion for Canadian storytelling and you wish to help us engage with individuals and communities across our various digital platforms, this is where you’ll want to be!

 

Every day, you will have an opportunity to shape the way in which Canadians see themselves reflected in our digital services. Your work will have a direct impact on how millions of Canadians from various communities connect with our products, with one another, and with the diverse voices that make our country so unique.

 

You will have the opportunity to play a part in enlightening and entertaining Canadians through our innovative work in building the mediums that deliver our content. We are an innovative hub, where the talented professionals we work with are respected and valued for their contributions.

 

Our product teams are vibrant and our work culture strives to achieve the highest standards of diversity and inclusion. We believe that hiring people with different career paths and backgrounds is fundamental in our shared success and in building healthy and highly performant teams. When you join our mission, you are not only shaping the vision of the CBC, but the future of our country.

 

There is an opportunity for this to be a full-time teleworking position. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Why This Role Is Important

 

As a key member of our OTT team, you will work closely with product managers, architects and technical leads. Your primary focus will be to drive seamless product development within your domain and co-ordinate the technical initiatives required to deliver new features. You will ensure that all deliverables align with the guidelines, standards and practices established by the development leadership team.

 

This department manages the unified product architecture that powers both ICI TOU.TV and CBC Gem.

 

Benefits you can expect:

  • Flexible work schedule prioritizing you, your family, and your work.
  • Possibility of working from home.
  • Competitive total compensation.
  • Opportunity to work with cutting-edge technologies.
  • Continuous learning and professional development opportunities.
  • Opportunity to be part of our affinity groups.
  • Buddy program and mentoring opportunities, allowing you to learn from the best in the industry.
  • Creative and dynamic work environment where your ideas and contributions are heard, valued, and respected.
  • A supportive leadership team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusion.
  • An environment that encourages experimentation and an iterative approach to achieve the most advanced forms of technical innovation.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Consolidate and coordinate deliverables across five distinct teams and more than five platforms to define and document the scope of our recurring Agile release trains.
  • Coordinate go-live operations and post-launch monitoring alongside platform developers on a rotational basis.
  • Partner with the QA Lead to co-ordinate pre- and post-deployment testing cycles.
  • Define, document and track performance indicators for our deployment workflows.
  • Propose and lead initiatives that accelerate and optimize our deployment workflows.
  • Plan, coordinate and document mandatory updates across all application platforms.
  • Plan, coordinate and document the use of feature flags in close collaboration with product managers.
  • Collaborate with the Technical Lead and Enterprise Architect to define and track Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) objectives.
  • Serve as the subject matter expert for SRE practices, working closely with the Cross-Functional SRE Lead to keep internal expertise up to date and relevant.
  • Foster and lead an SRE community of practice within the OTT team, encouraging team members’ active participation and engagement in community activities.
  • Maintain inventories and documentation for various dashboards.
  • Build strong, high-level collaborative relationships with external SRE teams through cross-functional dashboard integration.
  • Ensure the reliability and continuous improvement of CI/CD pipelines and automated testing frameworks.
  • Maximize uptime and maintain up-to-date development and integration environments, particularly for automated testing.
  • Document the use and manage the inventory of development and integration environments.

 

What You Bring

  • University degree or equivalent experience.
  • Five to seven years’ IT experience (as a developer, QA engineer, etc.).
  • Hands-on experience with Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) tools.
  • Proficiency in scripting languages like Bash or Python.
  • Knowledge of other programming languages an asset.
  • Good general knowledge and a high degree of intellectual curiosity (acquiring and developing new skills and knowledge).
  • A critical mind (challenging the status quo and voicing new ideas).
  • Keen interest in major trends and challenges within the digital landscape.
  • Thoroughness, self-reliance and resourcefulness.
  • Excellent stress management and prioritization skills.
  • Strong analytical and conceptual thinking.
  • Flexibility, initiative and drive.
  • Ability to work well in a team and communicate effectively.
  • Fluency in French.
  • Professional working proficiency in spoken and written English required.

 

Given the scope and responsibilities of this role, you will operate in a bilingual environment where daily work is conducted in both official languages (English and French). The successful candidate will adapt smoothly and collaboratively to thrive in and support this multilingual workplace.

 

Please note that this is a 12-month contract position. At CBC/Radio-Canada, contract roles function similarly to regular full-time positions, offering the possibility of renewal based on performance and skill demonstration.

  • You have completed post-secondary education in Business Administration, Public Administration, Human Resources, Communications, or a related field.

  • You have a deep understanding of the federal public sector ecosystem, Crown Corporations, or large, highly regulated enterprise environments. Familiarity with business planning, ATIP regulations, legislative reporting, and Board of Directors governance is highly preferred.

  • Discretion & Judgment: Unimpeachable integrity and discretion when handling highly confidential, sensitive HR, legislative, and corporate governance files.

The Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) team is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technologies and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

 

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada, but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

 

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Role Vision and Impact

 

The Senior Director, Information Security and End-User Technology, serves as CBC/Radio-Canada’s Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). A strategic, visionary and collaborative leader, the CISO defines, implements and drives the overarching vision for cybersecurity, risk management and technological resilience across all corporate environments.

 

The mission of this strategic role is to protect information assets, data, digital heritage, and production and broadcasting infrastructure across all platforms, while ensuring seamless, agile and uninterrupted media operations. The Senior Director optimally balances rigorous security architecture governance with the flexibility that creative, journalistic and technical teams need to innovate and broadcast without disruption.

 

Operating at a senior executive level, the CISO regularly briefs and advises the Board of Directors (BoD), the Audit Committee, the CBC/Radio-Canada Senior Executive Team (SET) and the T&I Management Executive Team (MET).

 

Supported by a team of experienced directors and senior managers overseeing governance, security operations, end-user technology and identity management, the Senior Director serves as the cornerstone of digital trust and strategic transformation for Canada’s public broadcaster.

 

Key Responsibilities

 

Strategic Vision, Leadership and Executive Relations

  • Develop, champion and execute an enterprise-wide cybersecurity strategy aligned with the Corporation’s business mission, risk profile and digital transformation.
  • Serve as a trusted expert and strategic adviser to the BoD, Audit Committee, SET and MET regarding risk status, security posture and maturity, and required investments.
  • Foster a “Security by Design” culture and establish security architecture governance frameworks that keep operational and production workflows running smoothly while proactively managing risk.
  • Anticipate technology trends and lead the secure integration of artificial intelligence (AI/GenAI) and automation into business processes and security defences across the organization.

 

Securing IT, Cloud, Distribution and Broadcast/Operational Technology (OT) Environments

  • Define and continuously adapt the security strategy across the entire technology landscape, including corporate IT infrastructure, cloud systems, end-user environments, and critical production, broadcast and network infrastructure.
  • Ensure the resilience of content acquisition, processing and distribution workflows against threats targeting the media sector and critical infrastructure.

 

Governance, Risk, Compliance and AI Governance

  • Oversee the governance function responsible for developing, maintaining and enforcing policies, standards, security architecture principles, exception management and industry frameworks (e.g., NIST, ISO 27001, AI frameworks).
  • Lead the third-party and partner risk management program (covering vendors and technology contracts) in close collaboration with the Legal Services and Procurement teams.
  • Co-develop a governance, compliance and ethical framework for the enterprise-wide use of AI and generative AI, assessing specific risks throughout their life cycle.
  • Ensure strict compliance with applicable laws and regulations (e.g., Quebec’s Law 25, GDPR and sector-specific requirements).
  • Drive a cybersecurity culture and awareness program focused on lasting behaviour change across the organization.

 

Defence Operations, SOC and Crisis Management

  • Oversee the performance and modernization of the Security Operations Centre (SOC), advanced detection tools (SIEM, EDR/XDR, automation) and continuous threat monitoring.
  • Direct major security incident response operations and lead technology crisis management, from detection to full business recovery.
  • Oversee regular penetration testing, vulnerability assessments and cyberattack simulation exercises across IT, broadcast and distribution environments.

 

Identity and End-User Technology

  • Guide the strategic vision for Identity and Access Management (IAM, PAM) to provide secure, simple and frictionless access for all staff and contractors.
  • Collaborate closely with the End-User Technology teams to align security with a modern, efficient and intuitive employee experience.

 

Financial Management and Team Engagement

  • Plan and optimize the cybersecurity department’s overall budget and partner with internal procurement teams to negotiate major technology contracts.
  • Inspire, coach and develop a team of directors and senior managers — fostering excellence, innovation and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Lead with the heart.

 

Qualifications, Experience and Core Competencies

 

Education and Certifications

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, cybersecurity, computer engineering, business administration (IT concentration) or a related field.
  • At least one recognized executive-level professional certification: CISSP, CISM, CCISO, CISA or CRISC.

 

Professional Experience

  • Seven to 10 years of experience managing professional teams or equivalent.
  • Deep expertise in technology architecture, cloud security, network infrastructure, cryptography, and identity and access management (IAM).
  • Ability to provide collaborative leadership within the organization to see complex, transformational initiatives through to completion.
  • Demonstrated skills in planning, organizing and engaging teams.
  • Proven ability and track record in leading cross-functional teams.
  • Proven ability to work with cross-functional, agile teams or on projects that have multi-team dependencies.
  • Ability to distil complex issues into clear, concise presentations and reports.
  • Expertise in the various technologies typically used by journalists in a newsroom.
  • Knowledge of business practices, including drafting plans and specifications, contracts, negotiation, finance, and IT management software.
  • Knowledge of software development and the technology infrastructure required for product delivery.
  • Knowledge of workflows for content acquisition, management and distribution, with a focus on storytelling.
  • Innovative approach to technical and operational challenges, paired with sound judgment to protect CBC/Radio-Canada from legal liability and financial loss.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills, with an ability to engage and influence stakeholders and partners at every level of the organization.
  • Excellent ability to listen to and communicate with people having different points of view or competing business objectives.
  • Experience implementing product governance models.
  • Ability to travel occasionally between Montreal and Toronto.
  • Bilingualism (English and French), both spoken and written.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

You will assign, supervise and develop staff running our priority video channels, with a focus on YouTube, TikTok and vertical video.


As a strong editorial leader, you know how to package compelling video and optimize it for audience reach and engagement. You bring a deep understanding of platform behaviours, video formats, publishing best practices, SEO, comments and moderation as well as audience needs and expectations. You can clearly communicate those needs to a news operation producing daily news video.


Through assignments, publishing and other editorial work, you ensure accuracy and balance, as well as compelling visual direction and storytelling on CBC News-branded channels. As a strong critical thinker, you make decisions in line with the CBC Journalistic Standards and Practices and the overall audience strategy.


You drive the editorial agenda on our video channels by responding to audience needs and trends and innovate to grow the audience. You prioritize the audience’s needs. You inspire others to do the same.


Collaborative work is vital in this role as you nurture relationships across the News, Local & Current Affairs division to achieve shared goals. You strengthen our team with inclusive, creative ideas, and encourage open discussions.


You care about the people you work with and have a deep appreciation for different perspectives, opinions and experiences. You live and promote the values of diversity and an inclusive and respectful work culture.


This is a permanent, full‑time position based in Toronto. The hours are expected to be Monday-Friday from 8 am to 4 pm and could change based on the needs of the business. The role will require some overtime and, on occasion, working weekends or statutory holidays as required.

news, live coverage, and features.

optimize for reach and engagement.

learn with your colleagues.

Edmonton


CBC News is expanding its financial and consumer storytelling to help Canadians navigate complex economic realities. Affordability remains top of mind for most Canadians. Purchasing power is being squeezed by inflation and tariff policies. Young people are struggling to land that first job at a time when artificial intelligence and technology are changing the workforce. Canadians are faced with a myriad of complex economic realities.

We’re looking for people who are excited to show up to work knowing anything can happen on their watch, thrives when news breaks, and have a keen interest in the way money and the economy shapes the lives of Canadians. 


On the business beat, you will focus on the intersection of money and everyday life. This means looking beyond the market and financial headlines to break down and bring home complex economic stories.  You will actively track economic, corporate, consumer and policy shifts both nationally and in your region with the goal of helping Canadians understand the financial and money forces that are affecting their lives.

Your task would be to break news and build a pipeline of memorable original stories. You'll experiment with various formats and platforms, from graphics and social media to radio and TV. You’ll have the voice and reporting chops to explain business news and bring to life economic stories.


Data excites you. You use charts, graphs and explainers to provide clarity and context in our storytelling. This role emphasizes mobile-first and vertical video storytelling tailored to reach younger, diverse, and underserved audiences where they consume media.

 

Key Tasks:

  • Consistently pitches original ideas in line with the unit’s mandate and objectives. 
  • Cover stories of regional and national importance, including gathering, writing, vetting, and presenting for all audio, visual, and digital platforms.
  • Maintain a base of sources that allow you to lead on key stories in your region or a beat, including economic experts, business leaders, and voices from underserved communities
  • Participates in all aspects of the production; and brings a willingness to appear on camera for production shoots, as required.
  • Experience writing short-form and vertical video for presentation on mobile and streaming platforms that describes complex business, financial and consumer information in a clear and concise manner.
  • Pivot to breaking news and quickly turnaround stories in a way that enhances the understanding of the audience.
  • Work with the CBC Money team across the country to deliver the stories Canadians need to understand the economy and how it affects them. 
  • That will include collaboration and editing the work of others.
  • As a subject matter expert on business, financial and consumer trends and issues you will describe these issues and events in a clear and concise manner and provide detailed analysis to enhance the understanding for our audience.

Your Profile:

We are looking for a candidate with the following:


  • A minimum of five years of relevant journalism experience including vertical and short-form visual storytelling.
  • Able to analyze complex data focused on business, economics, and money
  • Solid journalistic skills, including an understanding of legal risk, and demonstrated understanding of CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices.
  • Able to work with experienced producers and hosts to develop and produce high-impact short-form and vertical video under tight deadlines.
  • Excellent research, writing and editing skills.
  • Able to keep track of a number of simultaneous activities and prioritize and plan.
  • Able to communicate both verbally and in writing clearly and concisely.
  • Must be available for flexible work hours, that could include overtime, early mornings, evenings and weekends.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

In this leadership role assists the Local Station Manager in achieving Corporation objectives by  leading other employees and providing specialized technical and production guidance to program  areas. This includes assisting the Manager with long-term strategic planning for the  location. Creative problem solving is required to solve operational difficulties, to assess and optimize the use of resources, and to motivate others. Work is generally performed according to  accepted CBC or industry standards but independent action, judgment and initiative are  expected. There are requirements to work in a self-administered environment. This position will  be located in Windsor and has both  television and radio presentations with responsibility to travel through the region to assist smaller stations with regular maintenance and technical issues, including Thunder Bay, London, Kitchener and other stations as required.


Key Tasks: 


♦ Leads and coordinates the maintenance and repairs of (through internal staff or outside  contractors where necessary) all office equipment, including computers, office based  production equipment, and field production equipment. This includes edit suites, live  positions, field gathering, transmission, and telecommunications.  

♦ Operates and maintains IT infrastructure (through internal staff or outside contractors  where necessary) including audio and video servers, and on-line editing facilities in radio  and television. 

♦ Coordinates all physical aspects of the office and the relationship with building landlord,  and sub-tenants (under authority and guidance of Real Estate Department / Managing  Editor). 

♦ Trains new staff and advises management on their progress. 

♦ Coordinates all safety issues in the station including security, fire, technical and building  codes. 

♦ Maintains familiarity with technical or production installations and any associated  equipment. 

♦ Provides operational support and maintenance for the multi-platform servers, editing  systems, presentation systems and CBC’s intercity browser. 

♦ Ensures technical staff maintains equipment in excellent working order and in a ready state for deployment. 

♦ Recommends to Senior Manager, Managing Editor or Senior Director, News Production  Services (or delegate) options for the replacement and upgrading of station equipment as  required, and participates in the design/development and installation of new equipment.

♦ Monitors and recommends strategies for cost reductions with respect to technical  equipment, and work processes.  

♦ Ensures updates of technical drawings for the station are maintained, and submits to CBC  Engineering on an annual basis.  

♦ Ensures all CBC technical standards and practices are adhered to both in operations and  equipment maintenance. 

♦ Verifies the accuracy of time reports and work performed. 

♦ Within delegated limits, plans, assigns, schedules, coordinates and checks the work of  assigned staff and reports on matters related to job performance, conduct and safety.  

♦ As assigned or required, may perform any or all of the following tasks:  

o Performs all or part of the function or duties of equivalent or lower classifications.  o Within delegated limits, hire staff for casual requirements. 

o Provide specialized assistance and works in close consultation with Managing  Editor to provide input to the budget process.  

o Costs and purchases (technical) equipment.  

Education Required:  

Requires a superior knowledge and understanding of production and distribution of media on  radio, television and online platforms. Knowledge generally gained through community college graduation in Radio or Television arts courses, or equivalent industry experience.  


Experience Required: 


Five years related experience.

Radio-Canada Québec is seeking a videojournalist to be based in the Chaudière-Appalaches region. You will report to the Senior Manager, News and Programming. 


We are looking for a skilled storyteller and shooter who can gather and present news stories that deeply resonate with local communities, particularly in the Beauce region. 


Most of the content produced will be digital and will be published on the Info app and all other relevant Radio-Canada platforms. 


To succeed in this role, you must have a strong knack for text-based, audio and video storytelling. 


You will need to be self-reliant and do your own newsgathering (videos, photos, interviews, etc.) using your phone and/or light professional equipment.


This position requires a flexible schedule (including irregular hours) and the ability to travel throughout the coverage area in a Radio-Canada vehicle. You bring fresh ideas and creative storytelling solutions to our news programs, demonstrating strong skills in researching, shooting and packaging your stories.

You may be asked to cover stories for our other platforms and will have to work flexible hours, often independently. Weekend work may be required.


Role:

Shoot footage, write copy and produce reports in keeping with corporate standards and policies.


Key Tasks:

  • Keep up with news through a variety of sources.
  • Cultivate and maintain a network of local contacts.
  • Scout locations. 
  • Set up and operate a light video camera and related equipment. 
  • Ensure the highest-quality sound and images.
  • Ensure that visual material complies with technical and esthetic requirements for digital distribution.
  • Decide on story angles. Script and narrate reports.
  • Suggest an intro. Write various copy stories in the style appropriate for the platform.
  • Edit your reports.
  • Alert the newsroom immediately to any breaking news or special coverage opportunities.
  • Ensure the availability of the resources required to produce your reports.
  • Drive a news vehicle. 
  • Ensure your equipment is in proper working order.

This role requires full-time on-site presence.


Job Requirements:


Qualifications: 

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent.
  • Three (3) years’ journalism experience or equivalent.

Skills:

  • Broad general knowledge. 
  • Good knowledge of current events.
  • Fluency in French (working language).
  • Strong proficiency in the other official language (English) is an asset. 
  • Expertise in platform-specific storytelling and interviewing techniques.
  • Knowledge of and proficiency in video and editing techniques.
  • Knowledge of CBC/Radio-Canada’s Journalistic Standards and Practices. 
  • Dynamic and engaging on-air presence.
  • Ability to write clearly and concisely.
  • Ability to generate original story ideas and creative treatments.
  • Ability to thrive in a high-pressure environment under tight deadlines.
  • Ability to work in a high-pressure, tight-deadline environment, often in unexpected overtime situations.

Workplace Health and Well-being Advisor (PB7)

This role is based in Toronto (Hybrid), reporting into the People and Culture team at the CBC. 

As the Workplace Health and Well-being Advisor, you will review disability case files adjudicated by our third party provider in collaboration with the Disability team, and coordinate employee well-being initiatives across the organization. You will partner with CBC leaders, HR and IR teams to create, maintain and enhance a workplace culture of well-being in CBC newsrooms and across the Corporation.  You will proactively monitor industry trends to guide the development and adaption of relevant policies and procedures.

At CBC/Radio-Canada:

  • Short-Term Disability (STD) and Medical Accommodation claims are administered by a third-party provider.

  • Long-Term Disability (LTD) claims are handled by CBC’s insurer.

  • Workers’ Compensation (WC) claims are managed internally.

  • Support and intervention for journalists is provided by a third party EFAP group, with additional support being provided by a Peer Support network.
     

Key responsibilities:

Supporting Disability Claims

  • Liaises with the third party/insurer for all work-related questions and complex files

  • Consults the HR/Manager Disability system regarding  updates on the status of a file

  • Responds to all HR-related inquiries sent by the third party/insurer

  • Partners with managers for any absenteeism or work-related disability issues 

  • Liaises between the third party, Manager, HR/IR when challenged (eligibility refusal, suspension of benefits, etc.) 

  • Leads and supports the return to work meetings

  • Acts as a resource to  the IR and/or legal team in grievance arbitration or litigation

  • As required and in consultation with HR/IR and Management, prepare mandates for Independent Medical Examinations (IMEs) requested to determine an employee's capacity to participate in workplace meetings or investigations, perform job duties in the absence of an open disability file, or inform decisions regarding employment 

  • Assists management and HR/IR in determining if accommodations recommended by the third party are possible.

Well-being

  • Supports the network of well-being champions with well-being initiatives within the workplace 

  • Participates in the development of well-being training and delivery through L&D, and also delegated through training new trainers; this includes delivery of some Hazardous and Domestic safety training, and other ad hoc training. Makes recommendations to management on programs and initiatives through the lens of journalism and media environment to ensure alignment and relevancy

  • Makes recommendations for the development and delivery of CBC News internal supports, including well-being guidelines and protocols for leadership teams, team planning sessions and debriefs connected to major difficult stories; plays a leadership and coordinating role in Peer Support network 

  • Participates as a well-being leader in manager-approved industry events and groups, including industry well-being working groups, written pieces, conference presentations, and consultations with other well-being leaders working with the CBC

  • Shares relevant well-being information through various communication channels

  • Keeps all well-being resources and documentation current and relevant

  • Drives impactful well-being initiatives, from inspiring challenges to engaging activities, promoting a culture of health and vitality.

Qualifications and Experience

  • Nursing, Healthcare, or psychology degree with experience in disability management 

  • Minimum of 7 to 10 years of experience in Disability Management, Human Resources and/or Occupational Health

  • Knowledge of federal and provincial  disability legislation and Workers’ Compensation processes

  • Proven experience navigating the healthcare industry and its unique operational challenges

  • Experience working with third-party administrators and/or insurers

  • Excellent communication skills (English), written and verbal

  • Bilingualism and/or functional knowledge of French is required

  • Demonstrated experience in designing and implementing workplace well-being and disability management programs

  • Experience working in a unionized environment is required

  • Demonstrated discretion, empathy, and professionalism in handling sensitive information.

  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

  • The ability to work independently and as part of a team, while having a customer service mindset in supporting internal stakeholders 

  • Demonstrated success collaborating with third-party administrators and insurance providers.

  

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

job.title: Accounts Payable Manager
job.description:
Company And Culture   Complex is the definitive platform for global youth culture and music lifestyle, seamlessly integrating cutting-edge content, commerce and live experiences with unparalleled scale. Through innovative content, Complex tells stories of music, streetwear and style, sports, art and beyond. Its content engages in a dynamic conversation with the audience, reflecting and shaping the zeitgeist of convergence culture. A powerful media juggernaut paired with a curated marketplace, Complex is redefining the way fans interact with their favorite brands and artists and reshaping the future of digital culture and commerce.   Why We're Hiring

Complex is a fast-paced company seeking a detail-oriented and self-motivated Accounts Payable Manager with exceptional communication and critical thinking skills, who thrives working in a collaborative environment. This role will oversee the Accounts Payable function and complete required tasks to ensure compliance with internal processes and procedures, and compliance with tax and other local, state, federal and international laws. The Accounts Payable Manager will work closely with the Director of Accounting on day to day accounting operations and special projects, as well as supervising accounts payable staff. 

The Accounting team plays an integral role to each department and their respective business goals. 
The team collaborates with stakeholders, both internal and external, to ensure the financial health of the company through accurate and timely reporting and ensuring payments to all parties arrive on time. 
In this critical role, you will join a group of strategic, detailed-oriented thinkers that thrive in a fast-paced environment while working cross-functionally to ensure the success of the company.

job.title: Financial Analyst
job.description:
Join the largest and fastest growing independent artist merchandise company in the space, work across contemporary recording artist’s e-commerce stores, tours, retail programs, album rollouts + more.

We are seeking a self-motivated and detail-oriented Financial Analyst with excellent communication and critical thinking skills who thrives working in a collaborative fast-paced environment. This role will serve as essential support for the Accounting and Finance operations for TITOL. 

The primary function of the role is performing financial analysis and preparing 3rd party artist reporting including project P&Ls, profit split statements, and royalty statements. The position will work on financials for top-tier artists in the music and merchandise industry, as well as notable brands and collaborators in the fashion and art space. You will work cross-functionally with all teams at TITOL to gather relevant information for accurate reporting.

In addition to statement preparation, the role will complete analysis for project management and day-to-day financial operations, as well as assist in understanding artist profitability. This position will play a critical function in overall financial support, external reporting, and entity level financials.

Working Environment:   In-office 5 days/week with occasional travel or on-site support required. May involve weekend or extended hours during peak seasons. Very fast-paced and detail-driven environment, with a strong emphasis on communication, adaptability, prioritization, and proactive problem-solving.

job.title: Senior Director of Analytics
job.description:
Company And Culture

Complex is the definitive platform for global youth culture and music lifestyle, seamlessly integrating cutting-edge content, commerce and live experiences with unparalleled scale. Through innovative content, Complex tells stories of music, streetwear and style, sports, art and beyond. Its content engages in a dynamic conversation with the audience, reflecting and shaping the zeitgeist of convergence culture. A powerful media juggernaut paired with a curated marketplace, Complex is redefining the way fans interact with their favorite brands and artists and reshaping the future of digital culture and commerce.

Why We're Hiring

Data and analytics are critical to how Complex makes decisions, but this role is about much more than dashboards, reporting, or tracking KPIs. We’re looking for a senior analytics leader who can turn complex, imperfect data into clear business insights and strategic action.

Complex operates across eCommerce, Content, Advertising, and Live Events, creating a uniquely rich—and often complicated—data environment. Understanding how these businesses work individually, and how they intersect, is a core part of the opportunity. The right person will embrace that complexity, quickly identify what matters, and help leadership make better decisions across the organization.

This role requires a strategic thinker who can move fluidly between high-level business questions and detailed analysis. You will partner directly with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to identify opportunities, solve important business problems, and determine where data can have the greatest impact. You will be expected to use AI and emerging analytics tools to accelerate analysis, automate repetitive work, explore new questions, and move from question to insight to action faster.

The goal isn't to build more dashboards. The goal is to help Complex make better decisions and drive better business outcomes.

This role will be on-site 5 days a week at our NYC office or our Los Angeles, CA office.

job.title: KIDZ BOP, Video Editing and Production Coordinator
job.description:
Overview

Founded in 2008, BMG is committed to building the world’s most trusted, forward-looking music company. Following its combination with Concord in 2026, BMG brings together global scale, deep expertise, technology, and partnership to unlock new opportunities for creators while protecting and growing the long-term value and cultural impact of their work.  

 

Headquartered in Nashville with 18 offices globally, BMG is privately held and part of Bertelsmann, the international media, services and education company, with a minority stake held by affiliates of Great Mountain Partners. 

 

KIDZ BOP is the #1 music brand for kids, featuring today's biggest hits, "sung by kids for kids." Since 2001, the family friendly music brand has generated 14 billion streams and currently records in 5 different languages. The brand connects with its fans through year-round music releases, music videos, in-school activations, global partnerships, a dedicated channel on SiriusXM (KIDZ BOP Radio channel 135) and live tours. Each year, KIDZ BOP LIVE, the ultimate pop concert for kids (and grown-ups) hits all major cities across the US. 

Responsibilities

Your Mission:

KIDZ BOP is looking for a creative, highly organized Video Editor & Production Coordinator to support video content across social media, music, marketing, live events and brand partnerships.

 

The ideal candidate is a strong editor who stays current on TikTok, Reels and YouTube trends, brings creative ideas to the table and is comfortable supporting video production from pre-production through post.

 

What You'll Be Doing:

Video Editing & Creative

• Edit video for TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, YouTube, live tour, music releases and marketing.• Create engaging edits using captions, graphics, pop-ups, sound effects, transitions and music-driven pacing.• Stay current on social video trends and help develop fun content ideas that connect with kids and parents.• Take creative feedback well and make revisions quickly.• Explore new editing tools and AI video platforms such as Runway.

Video Production

• Help coordinate approximately 15 KIDZ BOP video shoots per year, including scheduling, call sheets, equipment and freelance crews.• Work with outside production companies and freelancers.• Support shoots on set as needed, including occasional travel, evenings and weekend shoots.• Comfortable with all aspects of smaller scale production including camera, lighting, and sound.• Help build and maintain a network of freelance editors, shooters, motion designers and production crew.

Asset & Project Management

• Manage in-house edit priorities and video requests.• Maintain organized production servers and the KIDZ BOP Video Archive.• Manage video delivery to outside partners and platforms.

Budget & Department Support

• Assist with production budgets and tracking.• Organize invoices and department expenses.• Support additional video and production needs as required.

Qualifications

What You Bring:

• Strong video editing skills with experience in Adobe Premiere.• Working knowledge of After Effects and Adobe Creative Cloud.• Strong understanding of TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and current editing trends.• Strong sense of pacing, music, humor and visual storytelling.• Creative thinker who can pitch ideas as well as execute them.• Highly collaborative, open to feedback and comfortable working through multiple rounds of edits.• Organized, detail-oriented and able to manage multiple projects at once.• Experience with AI video or editing tools is a plus.• Experience working with children or family content is a plus.• Existing network of freelance video and production talent is a plus.• Ability to travel and work occasional evenings and weekends based on production schedules.

 

Salary: $55,000/year

 

*This is a hybrid role requiring 3 days minimum on-site.

 

Please include a portfolio or reel with examples of your editing work, especially short-form or social content.

 

BMG is an equal opportunity employer. We employ, train, compensate and promote regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, disability, age, veteran status, and other protected status as required by applicable law. We believe that diversity, inclusion and equity is paramount for the creation of music, theater and film that celebrates and empowers all cultures.

job.title: Account Executive
job.description:
DISCOVER WHAT’S NEXT. Build Brands. Create Ideas. Make an Impact. Join Connoisseur Media San Francisco | Bay Area The Bay Area is where bold ideas become big things. At Connoisseur Media San Francisco, we bring together the power of local radio, digital marketing, events, and creative storytelling to help businesses connect with audiences, build brands, and grow. We’re looking for an ambitious, curious, relationship-driven Account Executive who sees opportunity everywhere—and knows that great sales begin with great questions, creative thinking, and a genuine understanding of what makes a business successful. If you’re energized by meeting new people, discovering business opportunities, developing smart marketing strategies, and turning ideas into results, this is your opportunity to make your mark in one of the most dynamic markets in the country. MORE THAN RADIO. A WORLD OF POSSIBILITIES. Our Bay Area portfolio connects advertisers with powerful local audiences, trusted brands, and innovative marketing solutions. KOIT — 96.5 The Bay Area’s #1 Adult Contemporary Station with a powerful connection to listeners and the community. KMVQ — 99.7 Now - 1 for ALL THE HITS. KBLX — 102.9 A heritage Bay Area brand playing the best throwbacks and R&B with deep community roots and a loyal audience. KBAY — 98.5 / 92.1 Bay Country - country music, passionate fans, and opportunities for brands to connect authentically. KEZR — MIX 106.5 - The South Bay’s home for today’s best mix and biggest hits. Connrex Digital — Strategic digital marketing solutions that help businesses reach the right people, strengthen their online presence, and drive measurable results. From broadcast campaigns and digital advertising to sponsorships, events, and customized marketing solutions, you’ll have a portfolio of opportunities to turn client challenges into creative, revenue-generating ideas.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Be a business builder. Identify, prospect, and develop new relationships with local and regional businesses, advertising agencies, and key decision-makers. Lead with curiosity. Ask insightful questions, uncover client needs, understand business objectives, and develop consultative marketing solutions—not cookie-cutter proposals. Think beyond the traditional. Combine radio, digital, promotions, sponsorships, events, and creative partnerships into integrated campaigns that deliver value for advertisers. Turn ideas into revenue. Prepare compelling presentations, recommend strategic solutions, negotiate opportunities, close business, and grow existing accounts. Own your results. Take initiative, manage your pipeline, maintain consistent sales activity, and achieve or exceed monthly, quarterly, and annual revenue goals. Build lasting partnerships. Deliver exceptional service, communicate proactively, and become a trusted marketing resource for your clients. Represent brands that matter. Bring the Connoisseur Media and Connrex Digital story to the marketplace while helping local businesses succeed. WHO YOU ARE You are competitive, resourceful, outgoing, and motivated by the opportunity to make things happen. You enjoy opening doors, building relationships, solving problems, and finding new ways to win. You bring: Strong prospecting, cold-calling, networking, and appointment-setting skills. Excellent communication, presentation, negotiation, and relationship-building abilities. A consultative mindset and the confidence to speak with business owners and senior decision-makers. Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple clients, priorities, and deadlines. A goal-oriented mindset, resilience, and a desire to continually improve. The ability to turn clients’ needs into compelling marketing ideas and business opportunities.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED

At least two years of sales experience, preferably in B2B sales, advertising, marketing, media, or a client-facing business development role. A track record of developing business, growing revenue, and working toward measurable sales goals. Comfort working in a fast-paced, evolving environment where initiative and adaptability matter. A valid driver’s license and a fully insured personal vehicle for business use. Even better if you bring:

Experience

selling radio, digital advertising, integrated marketing, sponsorships, or events. A strong local network or knowledge of the San Francisco Bay Area business community.

Experience

creating strategic proposals and delivering engaging client presentations. Familiarity with Microsoft Office and Google Workspace. A bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, communications, or a related field. We value talent, curiosity, drive, and the ability to build meaningful relationships. If you have the right mindset and a passion for helping businesses grow, we want to hear from you. YOUR AMBITION. OUR PLATFORM. BIGGER POSSIBILITIES. At Connoisseur Media, we believe our people are our greatest competitive advantage. We invest in individuals who take ownership of their careers, bring fresh thinking to their work, and want to be part of a team that supports one another and celebrates success. You’ll have the opportunity to work with established local media brands, develop new business relationships, collaborate with creative and digital marketing professionals, and build a career in an industry that continues to evolve. READY TO MAKE YOUR MARK? Bring your ideas. Bring your ambition. Help us shape what’s next for Bay Area businesses and brands. Discover your talent. Build your future. Make an impact with Connoisseur Media San Francisco. Salary: $75,000 to $100,000 plus Commission

Connoisseur invests in people who invest in themselves and offers employees a competitive package of health and welfare benefits. Comprehensive
