job.title: Associate Pastor/Biblical Counselor - Evening Shift
job.description:
Overview

Called to K-LOVE

 

Inspiring People to Move Closer to Jesus

 

At K-LOVE, every role is ministry.

 

We hire first for ministry alignment and a shared commitment to our faith, mission, vision, and values. We then seek talented professionals who can use their God-given gifts, skills, and experience to serve with excellence.

 

If you love Jesus and are called to be part of a ministry that places Christ at the center of everything we do, we invite you to explore this opportunity. If your heart aligns with our mission and you possess the knowledge, skills, and abilities needed for the role, please keep reading.

 

 

This role offers a unique ministry opportunity distinct from traditional church-based pastoral positions. Our K-LOVE & Air1 Pastors specialize in providing direct, one-on-one biblical guidance and urgent intervention for our listeners through phone ministry. They focus exclusively on offering biblical counsel, addressing theological questions, and connecting callers with appropriate resources. Our Pastors maintain scheduled office hours and participate in on-call rotations to ensure consistent availability for those seeking spiritual support and guidance.

 

* This is a Full-Time, on-site position based out of our Franklin, TN offices.*

 

* Available Schedule:   Tuesday - Saturday  2:00pm - 10:30pm or Sunday - Thursday 2:00pm -10:30pm

 

Here's some of what you will be doing.....

  • Provide pastoral and biblical counsel to K-LOVE/Air1 listeners via phone on a variety of life topics from Biblical questions to urgent intervention. As appropriate pray, counsel, and direct listeners to resources in their area for long-term assistance. As part of the goal to take listener calls live, the Associate Pastor will:
    • Maintain scheduled hours and participate in on-call rotation (nights and weekends), assuming the responsibilities of On-Call Pastor during assigned period.
    • Serve as back up for the on-call pastor as needed. Continue to grow in biblical knowledge and counseling skills. 
    • Make referrals to local assistance, e.g. churches, shelters, rehab facilities and counsellors.
  • Regularly pray with and for our listeners. Respond to prayer requests that come in on a daily basis via phone and/or e-mail.
  • Partner as appropriate, especially during pledge drive, with on air and social media staff; i.e. documenting listener stories or sharing listener call experiences.
  • Follow the legal requirements of a mandated reporter under state law.

 

Here's what we're looking for...

  • At least six (6) years’ of pastoral experience handling a wide range of pastoral functions, or equivalent education and experience.
  • Equipped with the knowledge of appropriate counseling methods in order to adequately respond to suicide, child abuse, elder abuse, marriage problems, personal problems, spiritual problems, and/or any other problems associated with life and its experiences and to provide biblical counseling.
  • Committed to grow and gain a further understanding of the pastoral/counseling profession by completing continuing education (i.e. reading and/or attending relevant courses or seminars).
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Ability to build trust and value others; communicate effectively; focus on the listener; and collaborate with others. Customer service experience/orientation preferred.
  • Able to work independently, problem solve and be flexible as the field is constantly changing.
  • Strong computer skills; knowledge of Microsoft Office products (Word, Excel, Outlook), Social Media forums and smart devices.
  • Proof of license and/or ordination.
  • Alignment with our values is top priority. Do our values align with yours?  Mission, Beliefs & Values.

 

Plus, all candidates MUST have both:      

  • Bachelors and/or Associate Degree in the Ministerial or Counseling field from an accredited educational institution
  • Licensed and/or Ordained with a recognized Christian church or Christian denomination and have recognition from the State & IRS as a Pastor.

 

Employment Requirements

  • Must pass a pre-employment reference screen and background check.
  • Proof of legal authorization to work in the United States.
  • Must agree with K-LOVE Christ-Centered Life Covenant and Statement of Faith

 

NOTE: Unfortunately, this position does not allow for Pastoral Housing Allowance

 

 

What can we offer you?

  • Industry leading Medical, Dental & Vision coverage
  • Short/long term disability and life insurance
  • Robust 401K with company match
  • Parental leave with Baby Bonding pay
  • Generous PTO, holiday and sick pay
  • Unique company culture that includes exclusive access to concerts, movie premieres, media industry events, and more
  • Leadership and Career Development Programs

Why work for K-LOVE?

 

K-LOVE is a nonprofit, multi-platform media company on a mission to draw people closer to Christ. Founded in 1982 in Santa Rosa, CA, with a singular radio station, K-LOVE today owns and operates the nation's two largest Christian music radio networks (K-LOVE and Air1) with over 1,000 broadcast signals across all 50 states, streaming audio reaching around the world, and a growing family of media ministries including podcasts, books, films, concerts, and events. K-LOVE employs nearly 500 team members between its office in Nashville, TN and field locations around the country. You can view our mission and values here Mission, Beliefs & Values. 

 

 

APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS:

Writing sample required:  Please upload attachment or include a link to your writing sample.  Samples can include a blog post, devotional, etc. 

 

 

“As an Equal Opportunity Employer, K-LOVE makes employment decisions based on merit and other legitimate reasons. The Company is committed to a diverse and inclusive work environment and equal employment opportunities regardless of protected class, characteristic or status. However, K-LOVE is a religious non-profit organization where all team members contribute to the Company’s mission of encouraging our audiences “to have a meaningful relationship with Christ.” Therefore, pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e I(a)), K-LOVE has the right to hire only candidates who agree with the Company’s Statement of Faith, Mission, Vision, and Values. Also, as a religious non-profit organization, the Company is not governed by the CA Fair Employment and Housing Act.”

The Human Resources Ministry Partner is an experienced human resources professional responsible for providing comprehensive HR support to team members and leaders across the Ministry. This role requires expertise in employee relations, compliance, onboarding, orientation, HRIS administration, and HR operations.  Will also serve as the first point of contact for HR related questions or concerns.

 

* This is an in-office role at our Franklin, TN Office

 

 

Here’s just some of what you will be doing daily…

  • Serve as the primary administrative resource for the HR team, including, but not limited to: development of correspondence for both confidential and non-confidential matters regarding people operations and employee relations processes.
  • Act as the first point of contact for HR related questions or concerns – redirecting team members and elevating issues as appropriate. Clearly and positively communicate solutions with exceptional follow through. Effectively and efficiently route and answer questions within scope of knowledge and authority.
  • Enter and maintain team member data within the HRIS system, ensuring a high level of accuracy, confidentiality, compliance, and timeliness with internal standards. This includes keying new hires, terminations, compensation adjustments, and other changes to team member status.
  • Facilitate new hire onboarding and new hire orientations, ensuring a smooth transition for team members into the Ministry and promoting engagement from day one.
  • Ensure the organization of team member files; maintain confidential records, I-9 documents, and other related employment documentation.
  • Support the VP of Human Resources with conducting investigations into team member complaints, policy violations, worker’s compensation investigations, vehicle accidents, and other workplace issues, ensuring thorough documentation in the Ministry’s case management system.
  • Advise leaders on corrective actions, performance improvement plans, and performance support procedures in alignment with Ministry policies and legal requirements.
  • Partner with payroll to submit Team Member vacation cash out requests, retro-pay amounts, bonus payments (i.e., relocation, sign on, or discretionary bonus amounts).
  • Maintain list of active team members on the Ministry Driver’s Insurance policy. Notifying vendor of changes.
  • Partner with the HR team as needed for Leave of Absences, Workers Compensation, Disability, Unemployment, Employment Verifications, EEO reporting, Public Student Loan Forgiveness, and other related projects.
  • Partner on exit paperwork and interviews.
  • Collaborate with HR leadership and other HR team members to support Ministry initiatives and continuous improvement projects.
  • Assist in the administration of the compliance portal where team members acknowledge policies and trainings.

  • 5+ years of progressive HR experience, with at least 2 years focused on employee relations.

job.description:

As a NOC Technician II, you’ll serve as a central point of communication and action during incidents, partnering closely with Engineering and other teams to monitor systems, resolve issues, and maintain the performance of our nationwide network and IT infrastructure. If you're ready to make an impact in the world of broadcast operations, we want to hear from you!

 

*This is an on-site position that will provide coverage for various shifts (1st, 2nd, or 3rd) depending on the need.*

 

Here's some of what you will be doing:

  • Advanced RF Broadcast Support
    • Respond to complex or recurring RF alarms and outages, using deep system knowledge to identify root causes and implement long-term solutions.
    • Analyze telemetry trends and performance data across multiple transmitter sites to proactively detect degradation or abnormal behavior.
    • Coordinate corrective action plans with Field personnel, ensuring resolution timelines, testing protocols, and proper documentation are followed.
    • Proficiency in database script generation for all equipment and all rack configurations with proper logic for effective SNMP alarm management.
    • Support advanced troubleshooting of audio chain components, including signal flow analysis across encoders, processors, multiplexers, and satellite backhauls.
    • Contribute to RF system upgrades and rollouts, supporting configuration, validation, and remote commissioning of new broadcast equipment.
    • Train and mentor junior NOC Technicians in interpreting remote control data, handling RF alerts, and understanding FCC compliance requirements.
  • Enhanced Network Infrastructure Oversight
    • Resolve escalated network issues involving routing protocols, VLAN configurations, firewall policies, or cross-site connectivity problems.
    • Monitor and validate complex network relationships, including multicast configurations, VPN tunnels, and hybrid cloud infrastructure dependencies.
    • Participate in network maintenance windows, supporting firmware upgrades, config changes, or failover testing as part of the operations team.
    • Support integration between broadcast systems and IT infrastructure, such as IP-based audio transport, SNMP monitoring, or broadcast-over-IP platforms.
    • Lead investigation of intermittent or chronic IT service issues, working with cross-functional teams (IT, InfoSec, Broadcast Engineering) as needed.
  • Operational Process & Reliability
    • Review and improve SOPs for alarm handling, troubleshooting procedures, and shift handoffs to increase team efficiency and consistency.
    • Identify systemic issues and recommend improvements to monitoring thresholds, alert routing, or preventative maintenance plans.
    • Act as lead technician on shift, coordinating team response to major incidents, validating troubleshooting steps, and ensuring accurate documentation.
    • Manage escalations with external vendors, such as satellite service providers, remote connectivity carriers, or equipment manufacturers.
  • Reporting, Documentation & Quality Control
    • Oversee accuracy of log entries, work orders, and event tracking, ensuring completeness and compliance with internal and regulatory standards.
    • Perform root cause analysis and produce post-incident summaries that contribute to long-term operational improvements.
    • Create training documentation and job aids for new tools, procedures, or systems introduced to the environment.
  • Leadership & Professional Development
    • Serve as a technical resource and escalation point for entry-level team members, providing informal leadership and mentoring support.
    • Participate in cross-team meetings, offering NOC perspectives on operational impacts, monitoring needs, or deployment readiness.
    • Demonstrate ownership of assigned systems or regions, proactively ensuring their health, uptime, and documentation accuracy.
    • Continue professional development in areas such as networking (e.g., CCNA-level topics), broadcast engineering, or cloud systems (e.g., AWS fundamentals).

Here's some experience we are seeking: 

  • Associate’s degree in Broadcast Engineering, Networking, or Information Technology.
  • Industry certifications preferred (e.g., CompTIA Network+, SBE CBT).
  • 2–4 years of experience in a NOC, broadcast, network support, or hybrid technical environment.
  • Proficiency in troubleshooting RF broadcast and IT infrastructure issues.
  • Familiarity with monitoring tools (e.g., SolarWinds, PRTG, Kybio) and alarm escalation.
  • Strong documentation skills, able to contribute to process guides and job aids.
  • Ability to mentor entry-level technicians and provide guidance in troubleshooting.
  • Solid teamwork and communication skills across broadcast, IT, and field engineering.
  • Demonstrated capacity to manage multiple incidents and prioritize effectively.
  • A collaborative and flexible style, with a strong service mentality. Need to be seen as a team player.

  • Strong written and verbal communication and presentation skills.
  • Demonstrated commitment to the social sector with a passion for our mission and values.

job.title: Part-Time Sports Content Researcher
job.description:
Keywords Location Search Jobs Part-Time Sports Content Researcher Job ID 10164761 Location Los Angeles, California, United States Business ESPN Date posted Nov. 13, 2026 Part-Time Sports Content Researcher Apply Now Save Job SHARE Facebook LinkedIn Email WhatsApp Links open in new tabs.

Job Summary

Job Requirements You have a head for stats, an eye for a great story, and the range as a writer to be creative and succinct -- and your passion for sports is the beating heart that fuels it all. This is the type of person who thrives as a Sports Content Researcher at ESPN. This position will work on NFL Network and other shows produced in Inglewood, CA, and be part of the company’s larger Research & Graphics squad – with staff also located in Bristol, CT and Charlotte, NC. Our mission is simple to define but incredibly complex to deliver: Provide ESPN’s television, audio, digital and social platforms with statistics, context and historical perspectives that make our sports coverage as interesting to the sports fanatic as it is understandable to the casual observer. It’s no easy feat, but we do it 24/7, and we think we do it better than anyone else. If this sounds like you and you’re up for the challenge, please apply today! Ok, it’s true: You’re in the office on Super Bowl Sunday. And for the NFL Draft. And the NFL schedule release. But the office is ESPN’s production center in Inglewood, CA, and you’re surrounded by people who share your passion. You’re a member of a tight squad of like-minded professionals who feed an endless flow of differentiating content that lands across ESPN platforms. Sports Content Researchers tap their existing reservoirs of knowledge and use ESPN’s vast resources – including access to world-class advanced metrics -- to hone in on the why and how of the sporting events that are most important to ESPN and sports fans. The NFL, college football, and the NBA are year-round staples, with significant coverage of the NHL, WNBA, and college basketball. Any sport could deliver the story of the day, week, or month.

Responsibilities

Many people say this, but in Research, it really is true: Sports news is constant, so no two days are the same. On any given day or night, you might: Create original full-screen graphics and anchor lead-ins for live shows such as those on NFL Network or any ESPN platform , using research you’ve done and copy you’ve written; Post the most relevant news on the ESPN BottomLine/NFL Network ticker – from Breaking News alerts to in-depth coverage and putting complex news stories into context; Put your deep knowledge to work to create game previews for shows that are informative, factually accurate, and unique enough that even die-hard sports fans really learn something; Collaborate with colleagues for every element of a studio show, from unearthing little-known facts to quickly bringing up relevant stats when things such as trades, coaching changes, or injuries are announced; Provide real-time updates for anchors and announcers while they are on the air; Flex your storytelling muscles by developing interesting segments, and help your colleagues flesh out their own ideas; ESPN is known for its cutting-edge graphics, and you will be one of the people who develop visually appealing, factually revealing visuals for our TV and digital feeds; Drop everything when news breaks and use your deep knowledge of advanced metrics, analytics, and research tools to create supporting content, often with a deadline of minutes or seconds! Working in Research also means you: Work a schedule that will vary by month and/or season -- you’ll get to dive deeply into sports and have enough variety to keep your days and week fresh;

Experience

professional growth and development – in addition to onboarding, training, and coaching that is a constant, you’ll meet with your supervisor formally twice a month and receive quarterly performance updates. Basic

Qualifications

Minimum of 1 year of related

experience

in sports, statistics, research, or a related field Full availability for this position to work days, nights, weekends, and holidays Broad knowledge of most sports and deep knowledge of the NFL and several others, including awareness of current/historical sports statistics, milestones, news, and events Elite writing and grammar skills. Must have aptitude to research, write air-ready scripts for BottomLine as well as Event and Studio productions Must be able to communicate information accurately Must be able to adhere to strict deadlines and react to breaking news Must be able to follow all Disney, ESPN, and department policies and directives

Preferred Qualifications

Minimum 2 years of

experience

working with statistics in an online, television, or print media environment Fluency in reading, speaking, and writing Spanish Demonstrated track record of training others and/or managing team-based projects Required

Education

High School diploma or equivalent Preferred

Education

College degree or equivalent #ESPNMedia Disclaimer PAY TRANSPARENCY The hiring range for this position in Los Angeles is $42,280 to $56,630 per year based on a 28 hour work week. The amount of hours scheduled per week may vary based on business needs. The base pay actually offered will take into account internal equity and also may vary depending on the candidate’s geographic region, job-related knowledge, skills, and

experience

among other factors. job.title: Production Coordinator
job.description:
Keywords Location Search Jobs Production Coordinator Job ID 10164416 Location Bristol, Connecticut, United States Business ESPN Date posted Nov. 10, 2026 Production Coordinator Apply Now Save Job SHARE Facebook LinkedIn Email WhatsApp Links open in new tabs.

Job Summary

Job Requirements Management Operations partners with nearly every division of ESPN and many across The Walt Disney Company to ensure ESPN’s Content business is operating at the highest level of efficiency and productivity. Content leaders focus their efforts on the fan while this team focuses on the personnel and business management aspects of how content comes to life. Together, this team consistently maximizes resources for the greatest impact on our content and bottom line. A Production Coordinator supports the day-to-day workforce planning and business operations of ESPN’s Content division. Scheduling resources, vendor & contract management, and legal & policy adherence will all be job functions this role carries out. This role will also find and create efficiencies in processes and workflows along with interacting with all types of content and leaders across our organization.

Responsibilities

Executes workforce planning and business operations for ESPN’s Content division. Works with content leaders to plan, request and allocate resources, schedule personnel and/or facilities, review time entry and expenses, track paid time off, etc. Analyzes content scenarios and creates plans to support initiatives while adhering to resource and financial limits and departmental processes and protocols. Maintains knowledge of the business processes, workforce guidelines, and resource planning required across assigned content areas. Fully understands policies and processes that guide work (Ex. T&E policy, workforce classifications, time entry). Educates, trains, and advises others on policies and processes and promotes adherence. Participates in developing and modifying policy and processes. Partners with and functions as a liaison for various departments (Ex. Production, Operations, HR, Legal, outside entities, etc.) Attends meetings with stakeholders; represents a neutral party in discussions. Participates in developing, implementing, and enhancing technology tools and workflow processes. Provides training to team members, new hires, client groups, and other personnel as needed. Ensures that appropriate timelines are met for all projects and tasks. Deals with time-sensitive and confidential materials and decisions (Ex. budgets, fees, performance). Daily tasks can include: Participate in sourcing, hiring, managing, scheduling, and/or providing feedback on various roles. Train and guide others in the processes of engaging workers and vendors. Process hiring requisitions. Request and/or draft short-form contracts for various roles and/or vendors. Enter, track, and manage contract information in the system of record. Review, approve and reject timecards and expense reports according to Disney timekeeping and travel and expense policies. Create, organize, and distribute various data and reports. Create new vendors in the Disney vendor portal and coordinate with Disney Shared Services on troubleshooting vendor set-ups. During production peak times, remains accessible and may be required to work non-traditional days/hours.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 2 years of business, personnel, production, or operations experience. Strong organizational skills (Ex. budgeting time, prioritizing workload, accuracy, and attention to detail in all tasks). Effective communication skills (Ex. clear and concise in all forms of communication, ability to manage high-volume email, phone traffic, and in-person interactions). Demonstrated ability to take initiative and perform independently with some guidance from management and senior teammates (Ex. suggest ideas and solutions to problems that arise, ability to recognize when an issue is present and provide rectifying solutions). Demonstrated ability to react quickly and positively to a wide variety of sensitive production and personnel situations that arise and are subject to continual change.

Experience

in various aspects of resource management and business operations (Ex. processing contracts/invoices, creating/maintaining/distributing information, resource scheduling/staffing). Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office programs & platforms (Ex. Office 365, Outlook, Excel, Word, One Note, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams) and Smartsheet or similar programs. Demonstrated passion and commitment to fostering an inclusive work environment that enables everyone to belong and thrive.

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledgeable about the sports content landscape. Possesses basic understanding of the production of studio shows, remote events, digital, and/or packaged shows. Understands basic reporting and analytics processes, identifying trends, and developing metrics. Solid analytical and technical critical thinking skills. Basic financial/budgetary management experience. Working knowledge of the following systems/tools: Concur, Kronos, SAP, and business intelligence tools like MicroStrategy. Required

Education

High School Diploma or equivalency. Preferred

Education

Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent years of

experience

from Vocational School, or in Production, Journalism, Business or related field. #ESPNMedia Disclaimer PAY TRANSPARENCY The hiring range for this position in Bristol, Connecticut is $60,400.00 to $80,900.00 per year based on a 40 hour work week. The amount of hours scheduled per week may vary based on business needs. The base pay actually offered will take into account internal equity and also may vary depending on the candidate’s geographic region, job-related knowledge, skills, and

experience

among other factors. A bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be provided as part of the compensation package, in addition to the full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the level and position offered. This position is with ESPN Productions, Inc, which is part of a business we call ESPN. To learn more about Disney's guidelines on the use of AI for candidates, click here. ESPN Productions, Inc is an equal opportunity employer. Applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status. Disney champions a business environment where ideas and decisions from all people help us grow, innovate, create the best stories and be relevant in a constantly evolving world. DISABILITY ACCOMMODATION FOR EMPLOYMENT APPLICATIONS The Walt Disney Company and its Affiliated Companies are Equal Employment Opportunity employers and welcome all job seekers including individuals with disabilities and veterans with disabilities. If you have a disability and believe you need a reasonable accommodation in order to search for a job opening or apply for a position, visit the Disney candidate disability accommodations FAQs . We will only respond to those requests that are related to the accessibility of the online application system due to a disability. Having technical issues? View the FAQs for help. Apply Now Save Job About The Walt Disney Company: The Walt Disney Company, together with its subsidiaries and affiliates, is a leading diversified international family entertainment and media enterprise that includes three core business segments: Disney Entertainment, ESPN, and Disney Experiences. From humble beginnings as a cartoon studio in the 1920s to its preeminent name in the entertainment industry today, Disney proudly continues its legacy of creating world-class stories and experiences for every member of the family. Disney’s stories, characters and experiences reach consumers and guests from every corner of the globe. With operations in more than 40 countries, our employees and cast members work together to create entertainment experiences that are both universally and locally cherished. Hiring Process Where Does Your Story Begin? Explore Disney Careers and the Life at Disney blog to learn about all the amazing opportunities waiting to be discovered at The Walt Disney Company. Be Part of the Story There are many different brands and businesses to explore. Once you've found the opportunity that is right for you, take the next step by completing your application. The Next Chapter Once you've applied, you will receive an email allowing you to access your candidate dashboard. Create your login and make sure to check your dashboard often to see your application progress. Explore this Location Bristol, CT The Heart of Connecticut Bristol, Connecticut is just two hours from Boston and New York and just an hour from the shoreline. From the natural beauty of picturesque hills and fall foliage, to the high tech satellite dishes of ESPN, Bristol’s “City sized” with a small town vibe, offering wonderful memories no matter your pace. job.title: Video Editor
job.description:
Keywords Location Search Jobs Video Editor Job ID 10163558 Location Bristol, Connecticut, United States Business ESPN Date posted Nov. 03, 2026 Video Editor Apply Now Save Job SHARE Facebook LinkedIn Email WhatsApp Links open in new tabs.

Job Summary

Job Requirements ESPN Creative Studio is a unit within the Content division of ESPN. Our staff comprises Motion Graphics, Edit, Visual Storytelling, Production Enhancements and Innovations, Creative Operations, and the Music group. Positions within Creative Studio include Video Editors, Post Editors, Producer Editors, Sound Design, Graphic Designers, Project Managers and Art Directors, etc. We are the go-to destination to conceptualize, develop, and execute content creation across all domestic and international ESPN distribution platforms. The Video Editor, Creative Studio position possesses an advanced ability for non-linear video editing in a fast-paced sport news environment. The Video Editor is expected to be an effective collaborator within various Edit areas and partners to help support the creative process, while editing at an advanced creative level. They help develop personnel, projects, and individual skillsets that propel Edit and Creative Studio into the future.

Responsibilities

Exhibits advanced skill to assemble and create content using non-linear editing software in a fast-paced sport news environment. Strong editing skills, effective communication, and ability to perform well under pressure, high demand, strict timelines, and/or live conditions with little supervision. Ensure all created content meets ESPN’s high standards for video and audio quality. Conducts quality control measuring and corrective action steps to ensure and/or enhance video content. Demonstrates a strong knowledge of edit workflow, software, and facility layout in assigned areas. Responsible for adhering to established organization of media and naming conventions. Establish strong relationships and gain knowledge of our partners, including their impact and/or specific integration with Creative Studio. Advanced organizational, creative, communication, and planning skills are required for team collaborative success. Provides strong service to all collaborative partners. Must have the skill and attitude to train less experienced editors on edit workflows and software. Will write and provide feedback on training initiatives and project contributions. Keep updated on knowledge of industry technology and help establish new workflows to create accurate and effective results on specific or future assignments. Must have the ability to train and learn new. techniques/software platforms that align with industry needs and trends. Ability to identify and quickly escalate issues. Recommend solutions and/or resolve operational errors and equipment failures. Provide strong multi-directional communication to ensure success of assignments and accomplishments. Self-initiate creative projects and pitch ideas towards departmental objectives. Strong understanding of multiple file-based formats and provide file-based ingest support.

Qualifications

A minimum of 4 years of editing or related experience. Advanced understanding of non-linear editing software (Adobe Premiere, Avid, Grass Valley Edius or Qube, etc.). Strong knowledge of Adobe Creative Cloud (After Effects, Audition, Illustrator, Photoshop, etc.). Skilled in media transfer workflows (ingest/publish/export). Strong understanding of audio and video broadcast quality control (video scopes, audio levels, CALM Act compliance, etc.). Ability to collaborate and work in a quick turn-around, sport newsroom environment. Candidates must have a good computer background (Microsoft Office, Slack, Workfront, etc.). Demonstrates strong communication skills, both written and verbal. Ability to work nights, weekends, and holidays. Flexibility to work overtime and alter shifts/days off to accommodate projects and departmental objectives.

Preferred Qualifications

Has in-depth background in non-linear editing in an area including Adobe (Premiere, AE, Audition, etc.) Grass Valley, Edius, etc. Strong understanding of linear, non-linear, social media production workflows. Knowledge of PC or Mac operating system. Bilingual (written and spoken) in both English and Spanish. Required

Education

High School Diploma or equivalent Preferred

Education

Bachelor's Degree in Communications, Studio Production, Journalism, or related field Vocational School or related

experience

job.title: Media Services Coordinator
job.description:
The Media Services Coordinator supports the Media Services team by performing hands-on operational work supporting media intake, asset preparation, metadata, and workflow execution across physical and digital media environments. This role is designed to develop expertise in media workflows, standards, and governance. 

You’ll spend your time organizing media, preparing assets for ingest, applying metadata, managing physical legacy media libraries, supporting internal users, and learning how enterprise media workflows operate from capture through archive.

This role is part of Feld Entertainment’s modernization of enterprise media operations, helping build the systems, workflows, and standards that support millions of media assets across multiple global entertainment brands. You’ll support media used across production, broadcast, marketing, and archive operations for some of the world’s most recognizable live entertainment brands.

Reporting directly to the Senior Manager of Media Services, the Media Services Coordinator builds expertise in media asset lifecycles, metadata standards, file formats, and operational best practices. The successful candidate will actively develop expertise in Media Services platforms, enterprise workflows, metadata standards, and media formats while growing into a trusted operational contributor supporting increasingly complex workflows and stakeholders.

Note: This position is not a Creative Services role and does not involve creative production responsibilities.

job.title: Supercross Operations Manager
job.description: The Operations Manager leads on-site Registration and Will Call for Supercross events, including hiring, scheduling, and supervising seasonal staff and handling registration documents and Will Call funds. The role also manages credentials, tour hotel contracts and rooming lists, unit-level travel and accommodations, budget accounting support, team and crew packets, event supplies and apparel, summary reports, and summit presentations. The ideal candidate is organized, able to manage multiple priorities and deadlines, and comfortable working both independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced touring environment.

job.title: Director, Media Planning and Placement
job.description:
FGS Global (FGS) partners with the world's most influential leaders to move minds and markets. Working where business, government, and public opinion intersect, we advise CEOs, boards, and leadership teams at the most consequential moments. Our expertise spans strategic and financial communications, policy and public affairs, corporate reputation, crisis management, and data-driven digital engagement. Across 31 global offices, our partners draw on the full depth of the firm so clients can operate with clarity, act with confidence, and lead with trust.

FGS is seeking a Director to join our Media Planning & Placement team in our Washington, DC office. The Director will manage day-to-day execution of client advertising campaigns and lead the development of media plans, campaign performance reports and other client-ready deliverables.

Responsibilities

  • Work with clients and internal teams to devise advertising campaign strategy and campaign plans
  • Independently run paid media accounts, managing the day-to-day operations while anticipating client issues and concerns proactively
  • Support new business pitches and draft paid media proposals for existing and prospective clients
  • Interact with external vendors to ensure on-time delivery of plans, creative and performance data
  • Analyze campaign performance, prepare clear client reports and develop actionable recommendations
  • Coordinate with FGS Global Creative teams on campaign production, ad specs and delivery deadlines
  • Assist ad operations in campaign set up, including trafficking, pixel creation, QA/testing and other functions as needed
  • Day-to-day management of media buys, including making regular optimizations based on performance
  • Work with FGS Global finance staff to track and record invoices and vendor bills
  • Mentor junior Media Planning and Placement staff
  • Act as a subject matter expert on advertising, helping educate clients and internal teams on paid media opportunities and best practices
  • Conduct research and develop written materials to support advertising campaign strategy, media planning and client reporting

Attributes

  • A BA/BS degree in a related field, plus 6-10 years of relevant work experience (previous agency and/or public affairs experience preferred, but not required)
  • Experience working in one or more self-serve ad platforms (Meta, X, LinkedIn, Reddit, Google search, etc.) and experience working with an ad server (Campaign Manager 360 preferred)
  • Strong interest in all aspects of digital media and advertising
  • Detail-oriented with exceptional critical thinking and problem-solving abilities  
  • Strong quantitative and analytical skills  
  • Ability to combine strategic thinking with creative problem-solving
  • Ability to prioritize, multi-task, work successfully with teams, and work under pressure  
  • Strong communication, project management and time management skills  
  • Comfort working in a fast-paced and ever-changing environment

The salary range for this role in Washington, DC is $130,000-$170,000. 

 

District of Columbia Salary Range$130,000—$170,000 USD

job.title: Intern Strategic Corporate & Transaction Communication
job.description:
Intern Strategic Corporate & Transaction Communication

FGS Global helps the world's most influential leaders move minds and markets. Working where business, government, and public opinion intersect, we advise CEOs, boards, and leadership teams at the most consequential moments. 

We work as one team across geographies and disciplines - bringing together specialists with backgrounds in communications, finance, law, government, journalism, data science, and digital. Whatever the moment demands, we combine multidimensional perspectives to help leaders anticipate what's next, engage the stakeholders who matter, and drive meaningful outcomes.

Across 31 global offices, we draw on the full depth of the firm so clients can operate with clarity, act with confidence, and lead with trust. This collaborative approach has established FGS as a market leader: we are consistently ranked Band 1 for Crisis & Risk Management and Litigation Support by Chambers and Partners, and were ranked the #1 Global M&A PR firm by deal value and deal count for four consecutive years (Mergermarket, 2025).

 

Join our team in Amsterdam as Intern Strategic Corporate & Transaction Communication starting February 1st 2027.

 

What tasks can you look forward to?

  • As an intern, you will be part of the team from day one and experience everyday life as a communications consultant at first hand.
  • You will support the project teams in the development and implementation of communication strategies for national and international clients in matters of strategic corporate communication and positioning.
  • The topics range from M&A transactions, IPOs and strategic realignments to the communication of digitalization and transformation strategies.
  • Together with our team, you will design compelling communications materials for internal and external stakeholders (e.g., communications plans, press releases, corporate presentations).
  • You follow, monitor and understand Dutch and European media.
  • You help with ad-hoc requests and questions from other offices about the media, economy, and society in the Netherlands.
  • For research and analysis, you will dig deep into relevant topics, exciting companies, media coverage and trends.
  • You bring in fresh, inspiring ideas and innovative communications formats.

 

What should you bring along?

  • You are at the end of your undergraduate or master's degree - the subject is less important than your enthusiasm for communication.
  • Ideally, you have already gained practical experience during your studies, for example in communications, finance, journalism, politics and/or strategy consulting.
  • You are a quick learner and it is recommended that you communicate fluently in Dutch and very well in English.
  • You have a good understanding of the Dutch media landscape.
  • You love variety and new challenges and really thrive when working in a team.

 

What we can offer you

  • The opportunity to get to know strategic communications consulting
  • Insights into the activities of a leading strategic communications consultancy as well as into various industries and areas of expertise as part of our integrated project teams
  • Exciting and varied tasks in an international and inspiring working environment
  • The opportunity to benefit from training & development opportunities
  • Induction and individual support as well as detailed feedback from an experienced consultant
  • A committed, collegial and constantly growing team in which mutual appreciation and team spirit are paramount
  • A company culture that combines excellence with team spirit
  • The opportunity to work flexibly both in our offices and from home
  • Our beautiful office in the heart of Amsterdam- Zuid

 

Don’t meet every single requirement? Please don’t worry! Studies have shown that some groups like women or people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single requirement. At FGS Global, we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. So, if you’re excited about this role and our company but your previous professional experience doesn’t match perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we would like to encourage you to apply anyway. You may just be the right candidate for this or another role.

We look forward to your complete application (incl. all relevant academic and professional certificates and/or reference letters). Feel free to contact us by email via careers-eu@fgsglobal.com.

 More information: FGS Global

job.title: Intern, Social Media & Digital Strategy
job.description:
About FGS Global  
FGS Global (FGS) partners with the world's most influential leaders to move minds and markets. Working where business, government, and public opinion intersect, we advise CEOs, boards, and leadership teams at the most consequential moments. Our expertise spans strategic and financial communications, policy and public affairs, corporate reputation, crisis management, and data-driven digital engagement. Across 31 global offices, our partners draw on the full depth of the firm so clients can operate with clarity, act with confidence, and lead with trust. 

About the Program 
Students interested in digital communications, social media, and technology are encouraged to apply for FGS Global's Winter/Spring 2027 internship program. This paid, part-time opportunity offers hands-on experience supporting client work, exposure to a variety of communications disciplines, and the chance to learn from experienced communications professionals. 

 The internship will begin in January 2027 and end that following May with an expectation of three full days of contribution (roughly 25 hours per week). This position is based in our Washington, D.C. office, and interns are expected to work in-office.  

 Responsibilities:

  • Monitor news, conduct research, create media lists, and aid multiple account teams to help clients with digital channel management, profile raising, crisis, issues management, mergers and acquisitions, litigation support, etc. 
  • Conduct and analyze industry- and company-specific social media research
  • Assist in building, managing, and reporting on performance for digital ad and/or email newsletter campaigns
  • Work under the direction of an assigned mentor to devise recommendations and solutions for clients’ digital channels
  • Recognize and identify noteworthy patterns or changes in social media activity.
  • Assist in planning, brainstorming, and executing social media tactics and strategies
  • Create content for clients across owned social media channels, including Facebook, Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Instagram, Bluesky, and more.
  • Perform social channel research audits and develop social media content calendars.
  • Produce data-driven analytics reports related to social and digital channel performance.
  • Write email newsletter copy, blog posts, and web content as necessary.
  • Work with team members on related digital projects and tasks. 

 Qualifications:

  • Current undergraduate student 
  • Eagerness to learn about digital strategy and our client-facing industry
  • Strong writer and editor
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel as well as our core social media platforms
  • Interest in and enthusiasm for social media, digital communications, and/or public relations
  • Ability to take initiative, ask questions, and manage multiple assignments and deadlines at once
  • Excellent interpersonal skills 

Candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. and not require work authorization sponsorship now or in the future. 

Due to the volume of responses, only qualified candidates will be contacted.  

FGS Global provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, disability, or genetics. In addition to United States federal law requirements, FGS Global complies with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities.

job.title: Acting Lex Columnist
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

 

Our commitment to inclusion and fairness
We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.

We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

 

The role

This is an opportunity for a UK-based financial journalist to cover a period of parental leave at the FT’s award-winning Lex opinion column.

At Lex we write views on companies and markets. No hot takes — only concise, deeply informed, analytical notes on big business, public and private markets and what makes finance tick.

We are looking for a numerate, naturally curious writer who wants to provoke debate with well-reported insights. The Lex column is central to the FT’s premium subscription strategy, and reaches an influential, engaged global audience.

Sector expertise is welcome, but we'll also want to see that you are an all-rounder. We’ll help you hone your ability to write punchy, directional and entertaining opinion.

 

What you will bring to the role

Analytical rigor: A strong grasp of corporate reporting, accounting, and the mechanics of M&A and earnings.

Conviction: The ability to generate clear, directional, and deeply reported views, backed up with numbers.

Intellectual agility: A fearless approach to untangling complex, unfamiliar topics.

Source management: A knack for conducting difficult, probing and diplomatic conversations with high-level sources.

Ambition: A drive to make a tangible impact, both in the market and within the FT newsroom.

 

Please submit your application by the end of the day, Thursday 19th November 2026.

 

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not by default use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role.

The Role Overview

We’re looking for a Cyber Security Engineer to help improve application security across the FT’s cloud-native technology estate. This is a hands-on role focused on making secure engineering easier for product, platform and software engineering teams.

Application security experience is essential for this role. You’ll help improve developer-friendly security guardrails across GitHub-based CI/CD pipelines, application repositories and engineering workflows. This includes working with SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning, vulnerability management and secure coding guidance so that security findings are clear, actionable and owned by the right teams.

You’ll work closely with engineers to support practical threat modelling, triage application vulnerabilities, improve security playbooks and help teams remediate issues in a pragmatic way. You do not need to be a deep AWS or cloud security specialist, but some exposure to AWS, cloud security or infrastructure-as-code security would be useful.

We’re looking for someone with practical AppSec experience who wants to grow their impact - someone who enjoys working with engineers, improving tooling and helping security become part of normal delivery rather than a last-minute checkpoint.

What you’ll bring to the role

Application security experience: practical experience identifying, explaining and helping remediate application security risks in modern engineering environments.

Developer-friendly security mindset: you enjoy working with engineers, explaining risks clearly and helping teams adopt secure practices without unnecessary friction.

Vulnerability management experience: experience triaging and tracking application vulnerabilities from sources such as SAST, dependency scanning, secret scanning, penetration tests, bug bounty reports or third-party advisories.

CI/CD and code security awareness: familiarity with security tooling in development workflows, such as SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning or repository security controls.

Threat modelling awareness: experience participating in, supporting or facilitating lightweight threat-modelling sessions for applications, services or new features.

Automation mindset: ability to write scripts or small tools, ideally in Python, to reduce manual effort, improve visibility or make security workflows easier.

Cloud security awareness: Some exposure to AWS, cloud security or infrastructure-as-code security would be useful, but is not essential.

Growth mindset: willingness to keep developing across application security, cloud security, secure development and modern engineering practices.

Required Experience, Essential

  • Practical experience in application security.
  • Experience working with software engineers to explain and remediate security issues.
  • Familiarity with common web application security risks and secure coding practices.
  • Experience with vulnerability triage, prioritisation and remediation tracking.
  • Experience using or interpreting findings from tools such as SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning or similar.
  • Experience participating in or supporting threat-modelling activities.
  • Ability to write scripts or small tools, ideally in Python, to automate tasks or improve visibility.

  • Familiarity with Agile or Scrum ways of working.

Desirable

  • Exposure to AWS security, cloud security or infrastructure-as-code security.
  • Experience with Terraform or CloudFormation.
  • Experience with container or Kubernetes security.
  • Experience with bug bounty, penetration testing or security testing programmes.
  • Experience with Splunk or similar logging/SIEM platforms.
  • Exposure to AI security, such as LLM-enabled applications, AI-assisted development workflows or prompt/data leakage risks.
  • Experience building dashboards, metrics or reports to support vulnerability management.

job.title: Asia News Editor
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

 

Our commitment to inclusion and fairness

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.

We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

 

The Role

The Financial Times is looking for an Asia News Editor to lead its day-to-day coverage of the biggest and most populous region in the world economy. This is a senior, vital role in the FT’s news operation. Leading a team of editors in Hong Kong, you will commission, edit and publish all our coverage from the region, with full responsibility for the FT homepage during the Asian day.

As an editor, your primary responsibility will be to set the daily priorities and get the FT’s news machine working at the start of the day, generating a strong news report to hand off to London. The range of stories is immense. From Xi Jinping’s likely accession to a fourth term as Chinese president to the region’s booming semiconductor companies, and from Indian corporate titans to miners in Australia, it is for you to drive the news. The FT has a network of world-class journalists spread from Australia to Pakistan; how to deploy them is your call.

One of your biggest jobs will be the homepage. You will make sure that FT readers in the region, and those arriving in the European morning, get presented with a fresh, compelling and accurate menu of news. That will involve making calls on the biggest stories of the day and how to present them with strong headlines and graphics. You will also generate story ideas and commission strategically to help the network deliver big projects and scoops.

Another important responsibility is to manage the tight-knit Hong Kong team, juggling roles and rotas as needed to keep the news desk running. There is also a wider management responsibility: you will act as deputy to the Asia Editor and a de facto member of the main homepage team in London. That will mean helping to interview candidates for jobs across the Asia region, getting involved when we are entering our journalism for awards, and offering advice on strategic goals.

It is an intense, exciting job, based in one of the most cosmopolitan cities in Asia. Hong Kong remains the gateway to China, and offers a high standard of living, with the FT committed to its long-term presence.

With the potential for other positions to become available, we also welcome inquiries from strong editors who do not necessarily have the experience to take on a management role.

 

Your skills

The job requires news editing, communication and leadership skills of a high order. It will suit an experienced journalist with a background as a foreign correspondent, an editor or ideally both.

You will need first-rate news judgement and the confidence to exercise it. For a large part of the day, it will be down to you to assess which stories are the most important and how to present them. Clear and decisive decisions on stories, together with imaginative commissioning, helps to keep the whole Asia operation on the front foot. Prior knowledge of the region would be a big help but is not required.

As a leader, demonstrating strength coupled with empathy is necessary, enabling you to support colleagues through the vicissitudes of life as a foreign correspondent. It is a region where we report on wars and natural disasters, while a range of repressive regimes seek to thwart our journalism. Sound judgement and a calm, no-nonsense attitude are needed to handle the many crises that come along.

As the main point of daily communication with London, you are expected to sell Asia’s story offerings, and communicate why they matter. Your clarity and enthusiasm for the tales we have to tell should inspire confidence in London colleagues and encourage them to keep Asia stories on the homepage. You will also understand London’s news priorities and communicate them to editors and reporters in Asia.

We anticipate this assignment will commence in the summer of 2027 but are open to candidates who want to make an earlier start.

 

Please submit your application by the end of the day, Monday 16th November 2026.

 

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not by default use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. 

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

At the FT, we are committed to creating a fair and inclusive workplace where everyone has equal opportunity to succeed. We welcome and value different perspectives and strive to ensure all employees are heard and supported. We believe people do their best work when they can be themselves and have the flexibility they need to balance their work and personal lives. We are an equal opportunity employer and comply with all applicable laws prohibiting discrimination.

The role / Position overview

FT Specialist is seeking a Data Journalist to join our growing data journalism team, producing exclusive, data-driven reporting and visual storytelling for Ignites and BoardIQ.

This role sits at the intersection of journalism, data analysis and visual design. You will be responsible for sourcing, cleaning, analysing and interpreting complex datasets to uncover original stories covering various aspects of the mutual fund and ETF industry as well as the boards that oversee those products on behalf of investors. You will also create engaging visualisations and interactive content that help our journalism stand out and deliver insights readers cannot find elsewhere.

Working as part of a six-person Data Visualization team, you will collaborate closely with reporters and editors across both publications while reporting to the Managing Editor of Data Visualization. The successful candidate will be equally comfortable developing ambitious long-term investigative and analytical projects as well as delivering shorter-turnaround stories that respond to emerging industry trends and news events.

We are looking for a curious, collaborative and entrepreneurial journalist who is passionate about using data to reveal meaningful stories and who is committed to continually developing their skills in a fast-evolving newsroom environment.

Important: This is an editorial journalism role, not a data analyst or data science position. Candidates must have professional journalism or reporting experience. Applications from candidates whose experience is primarily in data analytics, business intelligence or data science, without demonstrated reporting experience, will be automatically rejected.

Key responsibilities

  • Develop original, data-driven stories covering the mutual fund and ETF industry as well as directors and boards that oversee those products.

  • Source, collect, clean and analyse structured and unstructured datasets using a range of journalistic and analytical techniques.

  • Build compelling charts, graphics and interactive visualisations that enhance storytelling and audience engagement.

  • Identify trends, anomalies and opportunities within datasets that lead to exclusive reporting.

  • Deliver both long-term analytical projects and shorter-turnaround assignments driven by current events and industry developments.

  • Collaborate closely with reporters, editors and visual journalists across Ignites and BoardIQ.

  • Support colleagues in applying data journalism techniques and interpreting quantitative information accurately.

  • Use public records, databases, APIs, web scraping techniques and proprietary datasets to uncover new reporting opportunities.

  • Ensure all reporting and analysis meets the highest standards of accuracy, transparency and journalistic integrity.

  • Contribute to the ongoing development of data journalism capabilities across FT Specialist.

Required skills / experience

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify meaningful insights from complex information.

  • Experience communicating data, research findings or business insights clearly to a range of audiences.

  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced environment.

  • Excellent collaboration and partner management skills, with experience working across teams and subject areas.

  • Curiosity and a proactive approach to uncovering opportunities, trends and areas for deeper investigation.

  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.

  • Experience using data, research or quantitative analysis to support decision-making, storytelling or audience engagement.

  • An interest in developing or expanding technical skills in areas such as Python, R, data visualisation, databases or related analytical tools.

  • Knowledge of FT products, audiences, editorial standards or internal workflows that can help accelerate impact in the role.

We welcome applications from colleagues across Editorial, Product & Technology, Audience, Research, Commercial and other FT business areas who can demonstrate transferable analytical, storytelling or data-focused skills.

Candidates looking to take the next step in their career and grow into a more specialised data journalism role are encouraged to apply.

Please submit your application by Monday, November 30th 2026 by 5pm ET.

The role

We're looking for a Marketing Automation Journey Lead to join our Reader Revenue Group and play a key role in shaping how we engage with customers across their lifecycle.

As our Consumer and B2B subscription businesses evolve towards a more sophisticated, customer-led approach to growth, engagement and retention, Marketing Automation plays a critical role in delivering relevant, connected and effective customer experiences.

Our Marketing Automation teams operate as a Centre of Excellence, bringing together journey expertise, platform capabilities, experimentation, personalisation and measurement to drive customer and commercial value.

Reporting to the Head of Marketing Automation (Consumer or B2B), you'll be responsible for ensuring we're automating and improving the right customer experiences.

Sitting between lifecycle strategy and execution, this is a journey architecture, orchestration and optimisation role. You'll partner closely with Lifecycle Marketing and other collaborators to understand customer needs and commercial objectives, translating these into effective automated experiences.

You'll take a comprehensive view of the automated journey portfolio, finding opportunities to improve how journeys, campaigns, triggers and customer or account states work together. You'll assess existing activity, identify gaps or overlaps, and recommend whether journeys should be optimised, extended, redesigned, consolidated or retired.

Rather than focusing primarily on building individual campaigns, you'll lead the thinking behind journey design and optimisation, developing actionable recommendations and coordinating delivery through Marketing Automation Specialists and Executives.

You'll also work closely with your counterpart in the Consumer or B2B Marketing Automation team, sharing expertise and helping establish consistent standards, experimentation approaches and guidelines across the Centre of Excellence.

This is an opportunity to have a meaningful impact on the FT's customer experience, ensuring automated journeys are connected, measurable and continuously improving.

Key responsibilities

Journey architecture and orchestration

  • Partner with Lifecycle Marketing and other collaborators to understand business objectives, customer needs, target audiences and lifecycle challenges.

  • Translate strategic briefs into effective automation opportunities, challenging proposed solutions where necessary to address the underlying customer or commercial problem.

  • Maintain a comprehensive view of the automated journey portfolio, ensuring journeys, campaigns, triggers and customer or account states work together coherently.

  • Map and visualise customer journeys, identifying gaps, overlaps, friction and opportunities to improve reach, relevance and effectiveness.

  • Determine whether objectives are best achieved by optimising existing journeys, introducing new pathways, adjusting triggers, content or sequencing, or retiring existing activity.

  • Design automated experiences using appropriate audiences, channels, behavioural signals, personalisation, decisioning and timing.

  • Define journey sequencing, eligibility, hierarchy and suppression rules to handle interactions between customer experiences.

  • Work with Data, Technology, Creative and Marketing Automation colleagues to translate journey designs into delivered experiences.

Portfolio optimisation and prioritisation

  • Own and maintain the journey opportunity and optimisation roadmap, prioritising activity according to customer and commercial impact, reach, effort and strategic importance.

  • Regularly audit automated journeys to find opportunities for improvement, redesign, consolidation or retirement.

  • Investigate underlying audience, data, design and execution issues to understand journey performance.

  • Find opportunities to improve customer experiences through behavioural triggers, segmentation, personalisation and multichannel orchestration.

  • Ensure journeys are continuously reviewed and optimised rather than treated as one-off launches.

  • Work with the Head of Marketing Automation to align optimisation priorities with the wider strategy and available capacity.

Measurement, testing and learning

  • Establish clear objectives, KPIs and measurement approaches for significant journey interventions.

  • Incorporate testing and experimentation into journey design, including hypotheses, control groups and learning objectives where appropriate.

  • Use customer, account, behavioural and commercial data to assess journey effectiveness and find opportunities.

  • Evaluate broader journey outcomes alongside individual campaign performance, focusing on measurable customer and commercial impact.

  • Translate analysis and experimentation into actionable recommendations and future improvements.

  • Contribute to shared learning, measurement frameworks and procedures across the Centre of Excellence.

Delivery leadership and collaboration

  • Translate journey recommendations into clear, actionable briefs for Marketing Automation Specialists and Executives.

  • Work with delivery teams to define audience requirements, triggers, branching logic, personalisation, sequencing, testing and data dependencies.

  • Provide architectural direction, reviewing implementation proposals and identifying risks or opportunities for improvement.

  • Coach and support colleagues in journey design, optimisation and effective use of automation capabilities.

  • Collaborate with Consumer and B2B counterparts to share expertise, find opportunities and develop consistent approaches.

  • Contribute to Centre of Excellence playbooks and standards for journey design, testing, personalisation and orchestration.

Platform and capability development

  • Apply a strong understanding of marketing automation and customer data platforms to design effective journeys.

  • Find opportunities to make better use of existing automation capabilities and work with technical colleagues where further development may be required.

  • Combine customer and account data, behavioural signals, segmentation and decisioning to improve relevance and effectiveness.

  • Support the development and adoption of scalable, reusable Marketing Automation standards and ways of working.

Required skills and experience

  • Significant experience in marketing automation, CRM, lifecycle marketing or a closely related field.

  • Strong expertise in customer journey architecture, design and orchestration, with the ability to think across interconnected customer experiences rather than individual campaigns.

  • Experience handling or optimising a portfolio of automated journeys, identifying gaps, dependencies and opportunities for improvement.

  • Ability to translate customer and commercial challenges into clear journey strategies and practical automation solutions.

  • Strong understanding of automation principles, including triggers, segmentation, personalisation, decisioning, channel selection, frequency and journey sequencing.

  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience using customer, behavioural and commercial data to improve outcomes.

  • Experience developing testing and experimentation approaches and applying insights to journey optimisation.

  • Commercial awareness and an understanding of how automated journeys contribute to acquisition, conversion, onboarding, engagement, retention and customer value.

  • Ability to map, visualise and explain sophisticated customer journeys to collaborators with varying levels of technical expertise.

  • Strong relationship management, collaboration and influencing skills, including confidence challenging briefs and recommending alternative approaches.

  • Experience coaching or mentoring colleagues and supporting the development of others.

  • Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise contending opportunities and make evidence-based recommendations.

  • Sufficient technical and platform knowledge to understand implementation requirements, identify dependencies and challenge proposed solutions.

Desirable

  • Experience in subscription, digital media, recurring revenue or other customer lifecycle businesses.

  • Familiarity with sophisticated marketing automation or customer data platforms such as Bloomreach, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Marketo or equivalent.

  • Experience with behavioural decisioning, next-best-action, dynamic content or advanced personalisation.

  • Experience designing or optimising multichannel journeys across email, onsite and other digital channels.

  • Knowledge of account-based marketing, multi-contact buying journeys or complex B2B customer relationships.

  • Experience developing reusable journey frameworks, playbooks or operating standards.

  • Experience working across B2C and B2B audiences or within a Centre of Excellence.
