The portfolio includes 80 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first- and/or second-highest-rated television station in average all-day ratings across 116 such markets measured by Nielsen in 2025. We also own the largest Telemundo Affiliate group, with 46 markets, and Gray Digital Media, a full-service digital agency offering national and local clients digital marketing strategies and the most advanced digital products and services. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About WILX:

Gray Media Lansing (WILX-WSYM) News 10, home of the highly rated NBC and FOX affiliates in Lansing, Michigan, is on a dynamic growth trajectory. Our combined operations produce over 50 hours of local news per week—and counting. We are Mid-Michigan's undisputed media leader, home to Emmy Award-winning journalists, the Michigan Association of Broadcasters’ “Station of the Year,” your exclusive home for the Detroit Lions on FOX 47, and home to Studio 10, our popular daily local lifestyle show. Alongside our powerhouse primary stations, our family of channels includes MeTV (10.2) and the regional Great Lakes Sports & Entertainment Network (47.2).

Beyond traditional broadcast, we are a true 24/7 multi-platform powerhouse. Through www.News10Lansing.com and our dedicated News 10 and First Alert Weather apps, and our continuous livestreaming channel News10+, our audience stays connected to trusted local coverage whenever and wherever they need it.

We are a breaking news and weather-first station with a fierce commitment to original, local reporting. Our respected anchors and reporters live in the community and have made our newsroom their home—including the longest-running sportscaster in the state of Michigan. Our leadership team is equally passionate about mentoring and developing the next generation of top-tier journalists.

Mid-Michigan (the Lansing/Jackson area) is a big news market, home to the state capital and Michigan State University. It is a vibrant, diverse, stable, and highly affordable region that offers an outstanding quality of life. Lansing is ideally located just an hour from Grand Rapids and downtown Detroit, and is perfect for day trips “up north” to explore some of the most beautiful scenic spots in the country. If you love lakes, boating, fishing, camping, beaches, downhill skiing, craft breweries, local wineries, Broadway shows, Big Ten sports, minor-league baseball, and professional NFL, NBA, and NHL games... Michigan has it all! Come grow your career with our winning, forward-thinking team.

Whether you’re crafting the lead story for the evening news, tracking a cold front on our weather tech, or closing a digital ad deal, you’ll be a vital part of our award-winning team from day one. The intern rate of pay can range from your state's minimum wage to $15.00/hr.

job.title: INTERNSHIP/ HETS PARTNERSHIP - KFVS
job.description:
About Gray Media:

Gray Media, or Gray, is a multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. The company is the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 113 television markets that collectively reach approximately 36 percent of US television households. The portfolio includes 77 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first and/or second-highest-rated television station, as well as the largest Telemundo Affiliate group with 45 markets totaling nearly 1.5 million Hispanic TV Households. The company also owns Gray Digital Media, a full-service digital agency offering national and local clients digital marketing strategies with the most advanced digital products and services. Gray's additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About KFVS:

KFVS12 is the #1 local TV station serving as the CBS/CW/MeTV/Outlaw/Telemundo/Oxygen/GRIT affiliate in the Cape Girardeau, Missouri/Paducah, Kentucky/Harrisburg, Illinois market. Founded in 1954, KFVS12 has a rich heritage of serving "America's Heartland" with the best local news and weather information, along with a legacy of community service and disaster relief. KFVS12 produces more local news than any other station in the market, currently offering over 50 hours of news content every week, along with special high-profile, topical local programming. Heartland News on KFVS12 consistently leads the competition in award-winning journalism having been honored this year with numerous Missouri and Illinois Broadcasters' Awards as well as the prestigious Edward R. Murrow Awards.

The Cape Girardeau market covers 45 counties in four states and is home to four division-one universities. It is where the North meets the South and the East meets the West. The area is rich with many diverse communities, including historic riverfront towns, that offer a variety of unique benefits and recreational opportunities. It is also conveniently located for easy travel to St. Louis, Memphis, Nashville, and Chicago.

The station has an exceptional staff that is committed to maintaining the legacy of the institution of KFVS. They are forward-thinking with news coverage in on-air newscasts and 24/7 on numerous digital platforms, consistently leading the competition in digital traffic across the board. This provides exciting opportunities throughout the station including News, Sales, Marketing, Engineering, and more.

Job Summary/Description:

KFVS is seeking applicants for bilingual interns in partnership with Southeast Missouri State University and three universities located in Puerto Rico that belong to the Hispanic Educational Technology Services (HETS) program. Applicants should be in their junior or senior year at a HETS partner University and willing to live in Cape Girardeau, Missouri for a semester while attending Southeast Missouri State University. These positions will teach producing, shooting, and editing skills while contributing and creating content for Spanish-speaking Gray Television outlets. Partnership Universities include:

  • Inter-American University – Universidad Inter American De Puerto Rico
  • Sacred Heart University -- Universidad Del Sagrado Carazon
  • Ana G. Mendez University – Universidad Ana G. Mendez

Qualifications/Requirements:

* Meet enrollment criteria above
* Train with digital producer to produce/write/edit for KFVS digital properties.
* Work with a photojournalist to learn camera operation basics.
* Shadow Multi-Media Journalist to learn how to shoot/write/edit news stories for broadcast and/or streaming.
* Translate relevant stories from English to Spanish for digital properties.
* Enrolled in a HETS-affiliated school.
* Proficient in English and Spanish.

*** Intern rate of pay can range from minimum wage in your state to $15 an hour ***

If you feel you’re qualified and want to work with a great group of people go to https://gray.tv/careers#currentopenings, you may type in the job title, station call letters, or click on "apply now", upload your resume, cover letter, and references

(Current employees who are interested in this position can apply through the Gray-TV UltiPro self-service portal)

About KSLA:

KSLA News 12 is the aggressive, National Edward R. Murrow Award-winning CBS affiliate serving the region known as the ArkLaTex. The station is the market’s leader in timely and accurate reporting of breaking news, investigative journalism, award-winning storytelling, and First Alert Weather. KSLA News 12 serves its community on all on-air, digital, and mobile platforms, embracing the innovation of the industry. In the center of the ArkLaTex is the Shreveport/Bossier City metroplex where the best of Louisiana, Texas and Arkansas culture is combined to create a vibrant and comfortable lifestyle.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you a relentless seeker of facts who refuses to take "no comment" for an answer? KSLA News 12 is looking for an Investigative Reporter/MMJ who doesn't just report the news but uncovers it. We need a storyteller who can turn complex data into high-impact, urgent narratives that demand attention—whether someone is watching on their big screen or scrolling through their feed. If you have the grit to dig deep and the digital savvy with a reach beyond measure, we have just the place for you on our award-winning team. 

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

What You'll Do:
• Lead the investigation: Research, develop, and produce groundbreaking investigative content that holds the powerful accountable and serves our community.
• Own the data: Dive deep into spreadsheets, public records, and databases to find the "smoking gun" that others miss.
• Tell unforgettable stories: Use creative, outstanding storytelling techniques to make complex investigations relatable, urgent, and visually compelling.
• Drive digital impact: Craft digital-first investigative pieces, social media reels, and interactive content that engages our audience across all platforms.
• Balance the beat: Manage a pipeline of longer-term projects while remaining agile enough to apply investigative techniques to daily coverage and breaking news.

Qualifications/Requirements:

What You Bring:
• The "Investigative Itch": At least 2 years of dedicated investigative and general assignment reporting experience with a proven track record of digging.
• Technical Toolkit: Proficiency in computer-assisted reporting (CAR) and proficiency with databases.
• Digital Fluency: You know how to optimize a story for search, engage a social audience, and use digital tools to enhance your reporting.
• Relentless Urgency: A "get it first, get it right" mentality that thrives under deadline pressure.
• Human Connection: The ability to build trust with sources and tell the human stories behind the data.
• Sharp Judgment: Strong news ethics and the legal knowledge to navigate complex public records requests and sensitive interviews.

job.title: INVESTIGATIVE REPORTER/MMJ - WNDU
job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. The portfolio includes 80 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first and/or second highest rated television station in average all-day ratings across 116 of such markets that were measured by Nielsen in 2025. We also own the largest Telemundo Affiliate group with 46 markets and Gray Digital Media, a full-service digital agency offering national and local clients digital marketing strategies with the most advanced digital products and services. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About WNDU:

WNDU boasts a history of more than 70 years and sits on the campus of the world-renowned University of Notre Dame. We cover northwest Indiana and southwest Michigan. We produce over 36 hours of live news each week and continue to expand our coverage. Our team is committed to the highest standards in news, entertainment, informational, and public service programming. Our viewers love having a major research university in their backyard, the history of a strong manufacturing sector, and a robust court system. They also demand accountability from those institutions. The stories are here. We need the right journalist to find the stories and tell them.

Job Summary/Description:

WNDU in South Bend, Indiana is looking for an Investigative Reporter/MMJ. You will dig. You will file records requests. You will work sources. You will gather documents. You will tell complex, consequential stories in ways that are clear, fair, and impossible to ignore. And you will do it across every platform, on air, online, and on social. This role is not just about producing lengthy series pieces; we expect you on air regularly as part of the 16 News Now team. When a breaking news story has an investigative angle, a document, a record, a source with context no one else has, we want you gathering and fronting that information, bringing depth and accountability to stories as they happen, not weeks later. If you have the chops and the experience, we want to hear from you; apply now.

Duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

- Drive original daily investigative and enterprise reporting for WNDU. We need more than a long-form series. We want accountability journalism that shows up in every newscast.
- File and manage public records requests (FOIA, state open records) as a core reporting tool, not an afterthought.
- Use data, documents, and records to build stories from the ground up.
- Develop, cultivate, and protect confidential sources across government, law enforcement, business, and the community.
- Examine breaking and day-of news through an investigative lens - gathering records, sourcing context, and fronting stories that go deeper than the surface.
- Manage longer-form investigations simultaneously at different stages of development.
- Shoot, write, edit, and present your own stories as a full MMJ. Own the story from pitch to air. We do have photographers who will work with you, but you shouldn't be reliant on them for every story or shoot.
- Translate complex investigative findings into compelling, accessible content for broadcast, digital, and social audiences.
- Collaborate with editorial leadership on story development, legal review, and publication strategy.
- Uphold the highest standards of accuracy, fairness, and SPJ ethics - every story, every time.

Qualifications/Requirements:

- Proven investigative or accountability reporting experience; we want to see the work.
- A track record of using public records, data, or documents to break original stories.
- The ability to work at two speeds simultaneously: daily investigative hits AND longer-term series development.
- Strong on-camera presence and MMJ skills; you shoot, edit, and present your own material, and you are comfortable being a visible, recognizable face of the 16 News Now brand.
- Source development skills built over time; you have relationships, and you know how to build new ones.
- The ability to take a dense, document-heavy story and make it matter to a general audience.
- Unshakable ethical standards; you understand the weight of this work, and you handle it accordingly.
- Comfort with legal and editorial scrutiny; you document your reporting, and you stand behind it.
- Resilience: investigations get complicated, sources go cold, and stories take longer than expected, but you do not quit.
- Valid U.S. driver's license and ability to drive a company vehicle.
- A journalism-related degree is preferred, but not required; your body of work must speak for itself.
- Must be able to carry 35+ pounds of gear, and be experienced in shooting and editing unique content. We do have photographers to partner with on appropriate assignments.
- Familiarity with ENPS, Arc, and Edius is a plus, but not required.

Full-Time

About WFSB:

WFSB Channel 3, a Gray Media station, is the undisputed market leader in Connecticut and Southern New England. We dominate on-air, online, and on the stream. 

WFSB is the market’s #1 news brand across traditional broadcast ratings, digital reach, and social metrics. 

We are not just keeping pace with modern journalism; we are leading the way. WFSB produces more live streaming content than any other television station in New England. Located in a scenic region, along the coast between New York City and Boston, WFSB offers the ideal balance of top-tier, fast-paced journalism and the best of New England living.

Job Summary/Description:

WFSB / Gray Media is seeking a forward-thinking, hands-on IT Manager / Assistant Chief Engineer to bridge broadcast operations and modern IT infrastructure. This dual-focus role leads day-to-day station IT operations and systems administration while serving as the primary backup to the Chief Engineer on core television technologies and broadcast facilities.

The ideal candidate possesses deep, fluent expertise in enterprise IT (networking, virtualization, cybersecurity, directory services, and storage) combined with a solid working knowledge of broadcast television systems (SDI/SMPTE ST 2110 signal flow, production switchers, master control automation, newsroom computer systems, and RF transmission basics). You will ensure uninterrupted on-air operations, maintain IT compliance with corporate standards, and serve as technical operations lead when the Chief Engineer is off-site.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

Information Technology & Systems Administration:
● Manage, configure, and maintain all local station IT infrastructure: Windows Server environments, Active Directory/Azure AD, group policies, and enterprise endpoint workstations (Windows/Mac).
● Oversee on-premises and hybrid virtualization clusters (VMware vSphere/ESXi, Hyper-V), SAN/NAS high-speed shared storage, and robust disaster recovery/backup platforms.
● Manage local network topology, including Cisco/Arista/Dell L2/L3 enterprise switches, VLAN segmentation (separating broadcast production, corporate IT, Dante/AES67, and guest traffic), routing, firewalls, and VPN access.
● Champion station cybersecurity posture in alignment with Gray Media corporate IT: endpoint protection, patch management, access control, multi-factor authentication, and rapid security incident remediation.
● Provide direct IT escalation support for newsroom computer systems (ENPS/iNEWS), non-linear editing workflows (Adobe Creative Cloud, Avid, Edius), and field contribution units (LiveU, Dejero).
● Partner with Regional IT leadership and corporate engineering to plan, deploy, and document technology rollouts and software lifecycle upgrades.

Broadcast Engineering & Operational Backup:
● Act as the designated technical backup to the Chief Engineer, maintaining operational continuity across studio, control room, master control, and transmission facilities during absences or on-call emergencies.
● Support and troubleshoot broadcast production equipment, including production switchers (Grass Valley, Ross), Crispin master control automation, Chyron graphics engines, audio consoles (Wheatstone, Calrec), and multi-viewer/routing infrastructure.
● Understand SDI, HDMI, and IP-based media transport (SMPTE ST 2110, NDI, SRT, Dante/AES67) signal flow, conversion gear, and video monitoring systems.
● Assist in monitoring and basic first-line troubleshooting of transmission systems, microwave studio-to-transmitter links (STL), satellite downlinks, EAS decoders, and transmitter facility infrastructure (HVAC, liquid cooling systems, generators, and UPS units).
● Coordinate with production, news, and operations crews to resolve live on-air technical discrepancies quickly and calmly.
● Maintain accurate, up-to-date station wiring diagrams, network schematics, rack elevations, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).

Leadership & Project Management:
● Lead and execute technology implementation projects from scoping and rack installation to commissioning and user training.
● Manage technical vendor relationships, RMA processes, warranties, and software support agreements.
● Promote a culture of proactive maintenance, cleanliness, security, and continuous improvement across all equipment racks and technical spaces.
● Participate in an engineering on-call rotation to support 24/7/365 news and broadcast operations.

Qualifications/Requirements:

Required Qualifications:
● 5+ years of combined hands-on experience in enterprise Information Technology systems administration and broadcast/media production environments.
● Proven expertise in Windows Server administration, Active Directory, DNS/DHCP, VMware/virtualized environments, and enterprise backup solutions.
● Solid understanding of TCP/IP networking, managed switches, VLAN configurations, subnets, QoS, and network troubleshooting tools (Wireshark, traceroute, etc.).
● Working knowledge of basic television broadcast workflows and equipment (SDI signal paths, video routing switchers, audio distribution, sync/timing, and studio cameras).
● Familiarity with newsroom production systems (e.g., ENPS, iNEWS) and digital media encoding/transcoding formats.
● Ability to diagnose and resolve complex technical problems rapidly under live broadcast deadlines.
● Strong organizational, documentation, communication, and interpersonal skills.
● Valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record.
● Availability to work flexible hours, including on-call response for breaking news, severe weather, off-hours maintenance windows, and emergencies.

Preferred Qualifications:
● Associate or Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Broadcast Engineering, or equivalent military/technical training.
● Relevant industry IT certifications (CompTIA Network+/Security+, CCNA, Microsoft Certified, or VMware VCP).
● Broadcast engineering certifications such as SBE Certified Broadcast Technologist (CBT) or Certified Broadcast Networking Technologist (CBNT).
● Familiarity with modern broadcast IP technologies (SMPTE ST 2110, ST 2022-6, Dante, Ravenna, NDI).
● Exposure to transmitter site fundamentals, RF systems, ATSC 1.0/3.0 exciters, or backup power generators.

job.title: MEDIA EXECUTIVE - KSFY/KDLT (SIOUX FALLS)
job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. The portfolio includes 80 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first- and/or second-highest-rated television station in average all-day ratings across 116 of such markets that were measured by Nielsen in 2025. We also own the largest Telemundo Affiliate group with 46 markets and Gray Digital Media, a full-service digital agency offering national and local clients digital marketing strategies with the most advanced digital products and services. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About KSFY/KDLT:

Sioux Falls and the surrounding area remain one of the fastest-growing regions in the Upper Midwest and are home to 300,000 people, constituting more than 30% of the state's population. Healthcare and finance make up much of a diverse and broad workforce. The business climate in South Dakota continues to be one of the top in the nation, fueled by no state income tax and a diverse workforce.

There is never a shortage of activities or events, with summers packed with outdoor festivals and concerts, including free concerts at the Levitt at the Falls outdoor music venue.

Still, many also enjoy the city’s nearly 30 miles of bike trails and parks, including the namesake of the city, the beautiful waterfalls of the Big Sioux River! Yes, winters can be challenging, but it does not mean people hibernate. Colder temperatures provide plenty of outdoor and indoor activities all winter long. From parades like the annual Parade of Lights down Phillips Avenue to outdoor ice skating parks, life does not slow down in the winter in Sioux Falls.

The city is home to a 12,000-seat arena that is continually hosting major events and entertainment acts, ranging from the Professional Bull Riders, college and semi-professional hockey, indoor football, to concerts with names like Paul McCartney, Garth Brooks, and Elton John.

The city is also home to a new indoor aquatic center, an indoor ice-skating facility, a basketball arena, and an indoor tennis complex. Multiple award-winning golf courses, both public and private, surround the city, offering a relaxing and challenging day on the links

Culinary appetites never need to look far from being satiated, as there is no shortage of places to eat. Not only is Sioux Falls home to many familiar restaurant chains, but it’s also known for many great locally owned, nationally recognized restaurants and restaurateurs. For those looking for a quick weekend getaway, nothing to fear. You can drive to Omaha in three hours, Minneapolis in four, and the Black Hills in five. Since Sioux Falls is centrally located in the Midwest, direct and connecting flights to almost anywhere in the United States are often less than a few hours in length.

Dakota News Now is an award-winning television operation serving viewers in the eastern half of South Dakota as well as portions of southwest Minnesota and northwest Iowa. The stations operate from a relatively new studio in downtown Sioux Falls, branding all stations under the Dakota News Now umbrella. The facilities put Dakota News Now on the cutting edge of television and news gathering technology, making it one of the most state-of-the-art television stations in the market and the region. The Dakota News Now team produces 36 hours of news each week.

Some of our employees have been here for more than 25 years. For others, this is their first job out of college. It’s a great mix that gives us different perspectives while covering the news and assisting local clientele in achieving their marketing goals.

Learn more about Dakota News Now & Sioux Falls here: https://www.dakotanewsnow.com/page/ksfykdlt-careers/

The 1011NOW news brand is well-known throughout the region as a trusted source for quality news, weather, and sports coverage.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you the kind of person who sees a complex technical glitch and thinks, "Challenge accepted"? Do you dream in gigabytes and broadcast frequencies, and thrive on the adrenaline of keeping a 24/7 operation running flawlessly? We’re looking for a Media Systems Engineer to be the technological heartbeat of our central and western Nebraska stations. Whether it’s maintaining massive tower sites or ensuring a live stream hits every phone in the state, you’ll be the wizard behind the curtain, making sure our communities stay connected and informed.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

• Master the infrastructure: Maintain and evolve broadcast systems across Hastings, Grand Island, North Platte, and every tower site in between (yes, you’re the guardian of the signal!).
• Drive technical innovation: Don’t just fix things—improve them. You’ll execute a strategic plan to keep our technology modern, digital-first, and ahead of the curve.
• Support the storytellers: Provide expert engineering for studios, post-editing suites, and field production teams so they can focus on telling great stories.
• Own the live moment: Ensure every piece of gear is ready for the spotlight during live broadcasts and streaming events, documenting and crushing technical hurdles before they hit the air.
• Stay compliant and sharp: Keep us in the good graces of the FCC and FAA by managing all regulatory requirements for our tech components.
• Monitor the pulse: Keep a close eye on multiple air channels and transmitters, ensuring our "on-air" product is always high-quality and high-definition.
• Bridge the IT gap: Use your deep knowledge of server and desktop operating systems to keep our newsgathering, weather, and graphic systems running at peak performance.

Qualifications/Requirements:

• The Foundation: An engineering or electronics degree (or equivalent experience) plus 2-3 years in the broadcast or professional tech world.
• Digital Fluency: You’re a pro with IP-based video/audio transport and streaming technologies—you know the future of media is multi-platform.
• Cool Under Pressure: When the "On Air" light is red, and something breaks, you’re the calmest person in the room.
• A Strategic Mindset: You’re detail-oriented, self-motivated, and always thinking two steps ahead of the next technical update.
• Communication Skills: You can explain complex tech to a non-technical producer without breaking a sweat.
• Road Warrior Spirit: You’ve got a clean driving record and are ready to hop in a company vehicle to support our Nebraska properties (with the occasional overnight stay).
• 24/7 Readiness: You understand that news doesn’t stop at 5:00 PM and are ready to support a round-the-clock operation.

job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About KSFY/KDLT:

Sioux Falls is one of the fastest-growing cities in the Upper Midwest and is home to more than 220,000 people. Healthcare and finance make up much of the workforce in Sioux Falls. There is never a shortage of things to do here. Summers are packed with outdoor festivals and concert events. Many also enjoy the city’s nearly 30 miles of bike trails; be sure to stop by the beautiful waterfalls of the Big Sioux River! And winter doesn’t mean people hibernate; there are plenty of outdoor and indoor activities all winter long. In 2014, the city built a 12,000 seat area that has hosted everything from PBR events, hockey and indoor football, to concerts with names like Paul McCartney, Carrie Underwood and Elton John. The city is also home to a new indoor aquatic center, indoor ice skating facility, basketball arena, and an indoor tennis complex. There is no shortage of places to eat either. Not only is Sioux Falls home to many familiar restaurant chains, but it’s also known for many great locally-owned restaurants. And if you want to get away for the weekend, you can drive to Omaha in three hours, Minneapolis in four, and the Black Hills in five.

KSFY/KDLT is an award-winning television operation serving viewers in the eastern half of South Dakota as well as portions of southwest Minnesota and northwest Iowa. The stations operate from a new studio in downtown Sioux Falls as one rebranded organization called Dakota News Now. The facilities put Dakota News Now on the cutting edge of television and news gathering technology, making it one of the most state-of-the-art television stations in the market and the region. The Dakota News Now team produces 36 hours of news each week. Some of our employees have been here for more than 25 years. For others, this is their first job out of college. It’s a great mix that gives us different perspectives while covering the news. People here enjoy the work they do, and everyone steps up to the plate during major news events like breaking news and severe weather.

Learn more about Dakota News Now & Sioux Falls here: https://www.dakotanewsnow.com/page/ksfykdlt-careers/

Job Summary/Description:

Duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

- Analyze raw scientific data, models, and other available and relevant information to create an accurate weather forecast for our viewing area
- Create a compelling, conversational presentation of the weather forecast for broadcast, streaming, digital, and social media audiences
- Develop digital-first weather content
- Accurately forecast and track severe weather

Qualifications/Requirements:

- Bachelor of Science in Meteorology or a related field is required.
- On-air experience is preferred, but we are willing to train the right candidate.

Monday - Friday

Job Type:

Full-Time

Job Summary/Description:

Do you live for the science of weather but also love the art of digital storytelling? We're looking for a Meteorologist who can forecast with precision, deliver clear, concise weather segments in linear newscasts, create a high-energy, daily weather show on our primary streaming channel, and engage viewers on web and social media. This isn't just about reading a map; it's about owning the screen—whether it's a 65-inch TV in a living room or a 6-inch phone in someone's hand. If you're ready to lead the charge in how Vermont, New York, and New Hampshire experience the weather across every platform, we want to talk to you.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Forecast with precision: Deliver accurate, high-stakes forecasts for a topographically complex three-state region (Vermont, New York's North Country, and New Hampshire) where the weather changes as fast as the headlines.
- Create compelling visuals: Use The Weather Company Max systems to build creative, data-driven graphics that tell a visual story, not just show the current temperature.
- Step into the spotlight: Provide high-quality on-air delivery for our weekday noon newscast, and fill-in for our weekday morning meteorologist, maintaining a professional and authoritative presence that our viewers trust.
- Go live in the field: Take the weather story to the streets, covering community and weather events live from the elements and from our StreetView3 weather vehicle.
- Own the stream: Produce and host a daily, interactive weather show on our primary streaming channel, making complex science accessible and engaging for a digital audience.
- Craft digital content: Create "must-click" weather stories and social media updates that stop the scroll and keep our community informed on hard deadlines.
- Collaborate across platforms: Work seamlessly with the news and digital teams to ensure our weather coverage is cohesive, urgent, and first.

Qualifications/Requirements:

- The Credentials: A four-year degree in meteorology or a related field.
- On-Air Presence: Proven experience presenting weather on-camera with confidence, clarity, and a bit of personality.
- Tech Savvy: Deep understanding of The Weather Company Max products and the ability to navigate CMS and ENPS like a pro.
- Audience-First Mindset: A genuine passion for social media and a knack for creating content that resonates on TikTok, Instagram, and beyond.
- Urgency and Accuracy: The ability to stay calm and deliver life-saving information during high-stakes flooding, severe weather and winter storms.
- Communication Skills: You're a skilled writer and a speaker who can translate complex science into "human speak" effortlessly.
- A Clean Record: A valid driver's license and a clean driving record are required.

About KCTV:

KCTV5 is the CBS affiliate serving the Kansas City metropolitan area.

Job Summary/Description:

KCTV5 is seeking a forward-thinking Morning Multi-Media Journalist (MMJ) who knows how to connect with Kansas City viewers wherever they start their day—on broadcast, streaming, or mobile platforms. This journalist will deliver energetic live reports throughout our 4:30–9:00 a.m. newscasts, provide live field updates for our streaming channel, develop focused coverage for our noon show, and create audience-first digital and vertical video content. If you are passionate about reach, engagement, community trust, and turning one story into multiple dynamic outputs, we want you on our team.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

* Broadcast Impact: Report live with urgency, clarity, and personality across our 4:30–9:00 a.m. morning newscasts; write, shoot, and edit a compelling package or report tailored for the Noon broadcast.
* Streaming Coverage: Periodically join our continuous streaming channel live from the field to give viewers real-time updates, deeper context, and "what we know right now" coverage.
* Platform-First Storytelling: Craft vertical short-form explainers (Reels/TikTok/Shorts) and clear digital web stories that prioritize utility ("what this means to you"), community engagement, and verified facts.
* Audience Engagement & Trust: Foster two-way communication by monitoring morning comments, answering audience questions on digital channels, and clearly distinguishing between confirmed facts and developing details.
* Collaborative Daily Pitching: Pitch original, audience-focused story ideas daily that matter to local families, commuters, and workers starting their day across the Kansas City metro.
* Efficient Field Workflow: Shoot, write, and edit high-quality horizontal and vertical assets with reuse in mind, maximizing field time and newsroom collaboration.

Qualifications/Requirements:

* Proven Experience: 2–5 years of professional reporting experience as an MMJ or live reporter in a commercial newsroom.
* Live Broadcast Presence: Demonstrated ability to deliver compelling, active, and unscripted live field reports across a fast-paced multi-hour morning block (4:30–9:00 a.m.) and turn a polished story for the midday/noon show.
* Platform Literacy & Mobile Video: Hands-on experience creating audience-first vertical videos (Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts) utilizing strong hooks, clear on-screen graphics/captions, and authentic mobile delivery (not just cutdowns of broadcast packages).
* Streaming Agility: Comfort jumping on camera for live, conversational streaming updates from the field, explaining breaking developments and answering "what's next" for digital viewers.
* Technical Proficiency: Demonstrated skill operating field cameras, lighting, mobile gear, cellular transmitters (e.g., LiveU), and desktop/mobile editing software (e.g., Edius, Edits).
* Editorial Judgment & Trust: Uncompromising commitment to accuracy, AP style, sourcing, and transparency, with the ability to clearly label what is confirmed versus developing during fast-moving morning breaking news.

About KSLA:

KSLA News 12 is the aggressive, National Edward R. Murrow Award-winning CBS affiliate serving the region known as the ArkLaTex. The station is the market’s leader in timely and accurate reporting of breaking news, investigative journalism, award-winning storytelling, and First Alert Weather. KSLA News 12 serves its community on all on-air, digital, and mobile platforms, embracing the innovation of the industry. In the center of the ArkLaTex is the Shreveport/Bossier City metroplex where the best of Louisiana, Texas, and Arkansas culture is combined to create a vibrant and comfortable lifestyle.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you a relentless newsgatherer who lives for the thrill of a breaking story? Do you believe that great storytelling isn’t just about what happens on a TV screen, but how it connects with people on their phones, social feeds, and streaming devices? We’re looking for a Multimedia Journalist (MMJ) at KSLA News 12 who can do it all—find the story, shoot the video, and deliver a confident live report that stops the scroll. If you’re ready to be a community-centered storyteller who prioritizes the audience over the newscast clock, we want to talk to you.

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

What You'll Do:
• Own the story: Develop deep community roots and pitch original, enterprise stories daily that explore the real impact on local lives.
• Master the craft: Schedule interviews, shoot high-quality video, and edit compelling content that you tailor to a 65-inch TV and a smartphone.
• Lead with digital: Share verified updates, photos, and video from the field immediately—because our audience doesn't expect information on a scheduled timer.
• Deliver dynamic live reports: Bring energy and authority to your live hits, whether you’re standing on a street corner during breaking news or walking through a feature story.
• Write for every platform: Craft "web-native" stories with search-friendly headlines and local context that drive engagement across all digital channels.
• Engage your audience: Create platform-specific content like vertical video for social media and standalone clips for YouTube to meet our viewers where they are.
• Collaborate and innovate: Work closely with producers and digital teams to tailor content for different audiences while using analytics to help guide your storytelling.

Qualifications/Requirements:

What You Bring:
• A storyteller’s soul: You have a knack for finding the "human" element in every story and the technical skills to bring it to life visually.
• Multi-platform experience: You’ve spent at least two years (preferred) reporting, shooting, and editing in a fast-paced environment.
• Digital-first mindset: You understand that "news" happens 24/7 and you’re comfortable going live on social or streaming platforms at a moment’s notice.
• Confident communication: You’re a strong writer and an even stronger live reporter who remains calm and clear under pressure.
• Resourcefulness: You’re a "scrappy" newsgatherer who knows how to develop sources and verify information independently.
• Adaptability: You can pivot quickly when a story changes, manage your time like a pro, and you’re ready to work the shifts the news cycle demands (including weekends and holidays).
• Bilingual skills (Bonus!): If you can communicate effectively in both English and Spanish, that’s a huge plus for our community.
• The right foundation: A college degree in journalism or a related field is what we’re looking for.

We also offer syndicated programming on the CW, myTOK, Gulf Coast Sports & Entertainment Network, and Telemundo Mississippi network. We take pride in serving our viewers, our community, and our advertisers for 71 years.

Our mission is to be engaged with the community and promote civic and economic development with a focus on improving the lives of our viewers. We use cutting-edge technology to provide accurate and timely news information on television and digital platforms.

Job Summary/Description:

WTOK-TV is seeking a multi-talented, highly motivated hybrid Weekend Anchor / Producer / Multimedia Journalist to join our news team. This unique role is perfect for a storyteller who thrives in every stage of news production—from digging up and reporting stories on weekdays to anchoring and producing newscasts on weekends. This position also carries a heavy digital focus, contributing directly to our digital platforms to drive traffic, user sessions, and viewer engagement.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

- Produce & Anchor: Own the weekend newscasts. You will be responsible for stacking, writing, and producing high-quality broadcast rundowns, and anchoring the live broadcasts.
- Digital Ownership: Manage and update our digital news platforms (web, app, and social media) during the weekend shifts to keep our audience informed.
- Content & Trend Monitoring: Actively monitor local social media pages, community groups, and digital platforms on the weekends to catch breaking news, source local story ideas, and gather user-generated content to enrich our coverage.
- MMJ Reporting: Find, pitch, shoot, write, and edit compelling local stories. You will be expected to turn high-quality, accurate stories daily.
- Digital Content Integration: Turn your broadcast stories into digital assets by writing web stories and publishing active social media updates.
- Platform Consistency: You will create and publish engaging post assets (e.g., a 15–25s quick-take vertical video, a photo with bullet points, or a text graphic) across WTOK's social media platforms simultaneously.
- Story Tiering: Adhere to newsroom story tiering workflows (Tier 1 vs. Tier 2) to maximize web users, pageviews, and video plays.

Qualifications/Requirements:

- A degree in Journalism, Communications, or a related field is preferred.
- Experience in shooting, writing, and non-linear editing (Edius, Premiere, etc.).
- Strong on-camera presence, vocal delivery, and teleprompter reading skills.
- Ability to write engaging, concise broadcast copy and AP-style web articles.
- Experience with digital Content Management Systems (CMS) and professional social media publishing.
- Excellent time-management skills and the ability to work independently under tight deadlines.
- Demonstrated ability to work independently as a self-starter and collaboratively within a tight-knit newsroom team.
- A valid driver's license with a clean driving record.

job.title: MULTIMEDIA SALES MANAGER (DIGITAL SPECIALIST) - WLIO
job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. The portfolio includes 80 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first- and/or second-highest-rated television station in average all-day ratings across 116 of such markets that were measured by Nielsen in 2025. We also own the largest Telemundo Affiliate group, with 46 markets, and Gray Digital Media, a full-service digital agency that offers national and local clients digital marketing strategies and the most advanced digital products and services. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About WLIO:

Located in Lima, Ohio, WLIO is proud to bring all four major networks—NBC, CBS, ABC, and FOX—under one roof. As a station serving the Midwest, we enjoy the beauty and variety of all four seasons while staying closely connected to the communities we serve.

WLIO offers applicants the opportunity to be part of a dynamic, collaborative team in a welcoming market where journalists and media professionals can make a meaningful impact.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you a digital dynamo who knows how to turn clicks into customers? Do you thrive on the thrill of the hunt—and the satisfaction of seeing your clients' businesses grow? We’re looking for a Multi-Media Sales Manager who lives and breathes digital strategy but understands the power of a multi-platform approach. At WLIO, we bring all four major networks (NBC, CBS, ABC, and FOX) under one roof, giving you an unmatched toolkit to help local businesses dominate the Lima market. If you’re ready to lead a team that’s as energetic as it is innovative, we want to talk to you.

As our Multi-Media Sales Manager specializing in Digital, you are the catalyst for growth in the Lima market. You aren't just managing a team; you are a digital evangelist, a strategic coach, and a consultative partner to our advertisers. You will lead the charge in growing our digital footprint by developing cutting-edge sales strategies across OTT, SEO, social, and web to ensure all budgets and goals are crushed. From overseeing pricing and inventory to mentoring our Multimedia Executives, you’ll own the digital lifecycle and foster a high-energy, winning culture that puts our clients first.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Drive digital revenue: Lead the charge in growing our digital footprint by developing and executing cutting-edge sales strategies across OTT, SEO, social, and web to ensure all budgets and goals are met or exceeded.
  • Coach for greatness: Provide ongoing digital training and subject-matter expertise to the sales team, helping them uncover new opportunities and close complex multi-platform deals.
  • Craft winning solutions: Partner with local businesses to understand their unique challenges and build custom, integrated marketing campaigns—from programmatic to streaming—that deliver real ROI.
  • Own the market: Oversee digital pricing, inventory management, and revenue forecasting in tandem with the Director of Sales to ensure WLIO remains the go-to destination for innovative advertising.
  • Master the execution: Manage the lifecycle of digital campaigns from order entry to completion, ensuring every tag, tracking detail, and creative asset is perfectly aligned for success.
  • Analyze and optimize: Translate campaign data into actionable insights and reporting, providing clients with the "real talk" and performance recommendations they need to stay ahead of the curve.
  • Promote a winning culture: Foster a positive, high-energy environment where accountability and collaboration are the standard, not the exception.

Qualifications/Requirements:

  • Digital Expertise: Minimum of two years of digital sales experience with a deep understanding of OTT, SEM, social, and programmatic advertising.
  • Proven Leadership: Advanced leadership skills with a track record of achieving budgets and the ability to manage multiple tasks, deadlines, and—most importantly—people.
  • Strategic Communication: Strong presentation experience and excellent written/verbal skills; you can take complex data and turn it into a compelling narrative for a business owner.
  • Problem-Solving Prowess: The unique ability to translate client problems into digital opportunities, maintaining ownership of every challenge until it’s resolved.
  • Technical Proficiency: Expert proficiency in PowerPoint, Excel, social media, and CRM/order-entry systems (experience with Engage is a major plus).
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in marketing, advertising, business, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).
  • The "Gray" Factor: A relentless sense of urgency, a collaborative spirit, and a passion for helping local businesses thrive in a digital-first world.

Why You'll Love It Here:

  • Unmatched reach: With four major networks at your fingertips, you have the most powerful advertising platform in the region to play with.
  • A collaborative culture: We’re a dynamic, welcoming team where your ideas aren't just heard—they're celebrated.
  • Real community impact: You’ll be helping local businesses in Lima thrive, making a tangible difference in the place we call home.
  • Innovation at scale: Gray Media is evolving on purpose, and you’ll be at the forefront of the future of media with access to the best tools in the industry.

Ready to lead the digital revolution in Lima? Let’s create something amazing together.

This isn't just a seat behind a desk; it’s a role where you’ll shape the stories that matter across every screen - from the living room TV to the palm of our viewers' hands.

- Editorial backbone: You have the experience and confidence to lead a newsroom, making quick, smart decisions under deadline pressure.
- Digital-first DNA: You’re already thinking about the streaming and social angles of a story before the cameras even turn on.
- A "Partner" mindset: You’re a collaborator who lifts the team, mentors young producers, and understands that we win as a unit.

- Proven Track Record: 2+ years of experience in a professional newsroom, with significant time spent both anchoring and producing (we need someone who can do both at a high level).
- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Journalism, Communications, or a related field.
- Technical Savvy: Proficiency with newsroom computer systems (like ENPS) and non-linear editing software.
- Streaming Fluency: Experience with or a deep understanding of OTT/Streaming platforms and how to engage a digital audience.
- Leadership Experience: Previous experience in an editorial leadership role (Executive Producer, Managing Editor, or similar) is a huge plus.

About KPHO/KTVK:

Home to 3TV, CBS 5, and Arizona’s Family Sports, Arizona’s Family produces 100+ hours of local news and programming every week. 3TV is #1 in Arizona and one of the strongest independent stations in the country. Our CBS station is highly competitive in news and has top-rated sports and prime content. Our digital reach is also best-in-market—Azfamily.com leads the market in multi-platform unique users and is home to Arizona’s Family Originals (long-form programs, documentaries, docuseries, and podcasts, including True Crime Arizona, nearing 2M downloads). Arizona’s Family Sports features premier properties, including the Arizona Cardinals, Phoenix Suns, Phoenix Mercury, Phoenix Rising, and AIA state championships.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you the kind of person who actually loves the thrill of morning news? Do you thrive on the adrenaline of uncovering exclusive content and the challenge of bringing it to life with demonstrative, high-energy live shots? We’re looking for a Weekend Morning Anchor/Reporter who doesn’t just read the news—you own it. Whether you’re leading the desk on Saturday & Sunday mornings or reporting live from the field with a "show-don't-tell" mindset, you’ll be the face of the best morning show in Arizona. This isn't just a seat at a desk; it’s a multi-platform partnership where you’ll also have the chance to step into the spotlight as a fill-in host for our streaming shows.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

What You'll Do:
• Lead the morning conversation: Anchor weekend morning newscasts with energy, authenticity, and a conversational style that makes viewers feel like they’re waking up with a friend.
• Master the live shot: Deliver demonstrative, active live reports that take the audience to the heart of the story—no "standing in front of a building" here!
• Own the digital space: Engage our audience across all platforms, from social media updates to hosting live Q&A segments and filling in on our streaming shows.
• Drive the editorial engine: Be a newsroom leader who pitches original, promotable story ideas and collaborates deeply with producers to craft a winning show.
• Connect with the community: Get out from behind the desk to build real relationships with news sources and represent the station at local events (yes, you’ll be a local celebrity!).
• Craft compelling narratives: Research, write, and edit in-depth content, including hard news, features, and mini-documentaries that matter to Arizona.

What You Bring:
• A "Morning Person" mindset: You bring the energy even before the sun comes up (and you know how to make it look easy).
• Killer live skills: You’re a pro at field anchoring and can handle the unpredictability of live TV with authority and calm.
• Digital-first curiosity: You’re constantly engaged in the news cycle and know how to pivot your storytelling for streaming and social platforms.
• Community-driven hustle: You’re a natural connector who is always looking for the next great story and isn't afraid to pick up the phone.
• Strong editorial judgment: You have a sharp eye for what’s "promotable" and the writing skills to make every script sing.
• Technical scrappiness: You can edit and rewrite copy on the fly and aren't afraid to get your hands dirty in the production process.
• Urgency and empathy: You understand the weight of the stories you tell and deliver them with the respect and speed they deserve.

Why You'll Love It Here:
• The best team in the desert: You’ll be joining Arizona’s top-rated morning news team in a culture that values innovation and collaboration.
• Multi-platform growth: Between anchoring, reporting, and streaming host opportunities, your career path here is wide open.
• Real community impact: You’ll be telling the stories that shape the lives of our viewers every single day.
• Innovation-led environment: Gray Media is leading the future of local news—you’ll have the tools and the freedom to try new things.

Ready to wake up Arizona and make your mark? Let’s create something amazing together.

Qualifications/Requirements:

- Five years of general on-air news reporting experience. Journalistic skills, editorial judgment with knowledge of editing and photography skills, or equivalent work experience
- Bachelor’s degree in Journalism or Communications preferred

Specific Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
- Ability to work under pressure, adapt to change, meet deadlines, work well as a team and independently.
- Exceptional communication skills and excellent knowledge of current events

KTIV News 4 is the #1 station in Sioux City, Iowa, and the local leader in news coverage on air, online and on the go. We are "Siouxland's News Source”.

- Market-leading impact: You’re joining the #1 team in the market, where your work is seen and felt by the entire community.
- Growth opportunities: We don’t just hire producers; we develop future newsroom leaders through mentorship and Gray Media’s extensive network.

Do you have a passion for storytelling and a drive to be #1? KTIV News 4 is looking for a high-energy News Producer to lead our multi-platform coverage in Sioux City. If you’re ready to own the news cycle and connect with our community across every screen, we want to talk to you.

- Craft compelling newscasts: Write, edit, and produce fast-paced, engaging content for broadcast and digital platforms every single day.

- React with urgency: Pivot quickly during breaking news or severe weather to provide authoritative, life-saving information to our viewers.
- Innovate storytelling: Use creative graphics and multi-platform tools to make complex stories relatable, visual, and shareable.
- Maintain accuracy: Ensure every script and digital post meets the highest standards of journalistic integrity.

- Calm under pressure: You thrive in the "organized chaos" of a live control room and actually enjoy the rush of a ticking clock.
- Technical savvy: Experience with newsroom computer systems (like ENPS) and non-linear editing is a major plus, but your willingness to learn is even better.
- A degree in journalism: Or a related field, paired with a deep hunger to grow in a top-rated, award-winning newsroom.
- Collaborative spirit: You’re a team player who values feedback, lifts others up, and loves brainstorming the "big idea."
- Urgency and empathy: You care about the "why" behind the story and the people in the Siouxland community it impacts.

job.description:

About WECT:

WECT News has been Where News Comes First in Southeastern North Carolina for over 70 years. We're the NBC affiliate in the rapidly growing Wilmington market, serving New Hanover, Brunswick, Columbus, Pender, and Bladen counties that make up the beautiful coastal Cape Fear Region. WECT is the most accessible local news outlet in our market, with WECT.com, News & Weather apps, and streaming platforms. WECT is the dominant #1 station in the market.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you a visual storyteller who lives for the "wow" factor?

Do you thrive on the adrenaline of a breaking story and the satisfaction of a deep-dive community piece? We’re looking for a Multimedia Journalist (MMJ) who doesn't just report the news but owns it—across every screen.

Whether you’re crafting a lead for one of our on-air newscasts, going live on our streaming newscasts in the WECT Digital Studio, or engaging with our audience on social, you’ll be the heartbeat of the Cape Fear region.

If you’re a scrappy, digital-first journalist who wants to make a real impact in southeastern North Carolina, let’s talk.

Duties/Responsibilities will include (but not be limited to):

What You'll Do:
* Own the story: Manage and develop compelling content from initial concept to final publication across digital, social, and broadcast platforms.
* Drive digital engagement: Create platform-specific content that meets our audience where they are—on their phones, their TVs, and everywhere in between.
* Master the craft: Write, edit, and produce high-quality stories with speed, accuracy, and a killer creative eye.
* Respond with urgency: Jump into breaking news situations with authority and calm, keeping our community informed in real-time.
* Connect with the community: Build deep roots in the Cape Fear region, developing sources and uncovering the stories that truly matter to our neighbors.
*Step into the spotlight: Take advantage of potential anchoring opportunities to lead our coverage and connect directly with viewers.

What You Bring:
* A digital-first mindset: You understand that "news" happens 24/7, and you’re ready to feed the beast on social and streaming first.
* Killer storytelling skills: You know how to find the "human" element in every story and make it resonate with an audience.
* Technical chops: You’re a pro with a camera and an editing suite (and you’re not afraid to learn new tools as they emerge).
* Sharp news judgment: You know what’s important, what’s interesting, and how to tell the difference under pressure.
* A positive, "can-do" attitude: You’re a team player who lifts others up and thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced environment.
* Urgency and empathy: You care about the stories you tell and the people they affect, and you move fast to get them right.
* Flexibility: News doesn't follow a 9-to-5 schedule, and neither do you—you’re ready to go where the story takes you.

Qualifications/Requirements:

* Bachelor’s degree in journalism or related field preferred
* Strong writing skills (broadcast and print style)
* Experience with CMS/digital publishing platforms
* Experience with broadcast newsroom software such as ENPS
* Experience with video editing software (preferably Edius)
* Must be able to lift 25-30 lbs and pass a motor vehicle background check

What’s better than working at the #1 station in the nation’s #1 city? We are just 1.5 hours from Milwaukee, 2.5 hours from Chicago, and 5 hours from Minneapolis/St. Paul.

Click here to learn more about the Madison market & working at WMTV: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c7KugIlmEWI

Job Description/Summary:

Are you a news junkie who thrives on the rush of a ticking clock? Do you love making a complex story click, whether it is on a living room TV or a phone? WMTV 15 News wants a high-energy, digital-first Newscast Producer to join our award-winning team. You will be our utility player: own evening newscasts on-air or streaming, lead your own streaming show, and jump in to help across the week.

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

You will be our utility player: own evening newscasts on-air or streaming, lead your own streaming show, and jump in to help across the week. This candidate would flex to different newscasts through the week, covering so fellow producers can build streaming content and special projects. This position is Sunday through Thursday (an atypical work week that gives you a different rhythm than the standard Monday to Friday grind). WMTV 15 News is redefining local news across every screen in vibrant Madison, a capital city and college town where your work truly matters every day. At WMTV, you get hands-on training and the career mobility of Gray Media; this is a place to grow fast while helping build the future.

- Own breaking news: Act with urgency, send push alerts, launch live streams, update WMTV15News.com as news breaks
- Drive the News Now Desk: Handle live feeds, user-generated content, and real-time updates across TV, web, apps, and social
- Write for every platform: Conversational scripts for TV, sharp AP Style copy for digital, aligned to WMTV brand pillars
- Associate producer: Write content and VOSOTs from photographer video and feeds when not in the producer chair
- Partner with leadership: Report to and work with News Director and Executive Producer to execute digital-first strategy

Qualifications/Requirements:

We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, as well as studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About KBTX:

KBTX Media operates the CBS and CW affiliates in Bryan-College Station, Texas, serving an 18-county area known as the Brazos Valley. For nearly 70 years, we’ve been the dominant choice for local news and entertainment. Our team produces nearly 40 hours of broadcast content each week, along with a constant presence online at KBTX.com.
KBTX is routinely recognized among the best in the state by organizations including the Associated Press, RTDNA, and the Lone Star EMMY Chapter of the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences. The station has won four consecutive Texas Association of Broadcasters’ Bonner McLane Public Service awards, and in 2023 won a National Edward R. Murrow Award for Digital content. KBTX is also a recent Texas AP Broadcasters/Freedom of Information Foundation of Texas Station of the Year and Texas Associated Press Broadcasters Station of the Year.

The station has launched the careers of many well-known journalists, meteorologists and network executives, and takes pride in helping talent grow quickly into the nation’s largest television markets. The work family of KBTX is made up of a group of dedicated, professional, and passionate individuals who are the backbone of our daily mission.
Bryan-College Station, Texas, is a community of more than 250,000 people and the largest single metro in the Waco-Temple-Bryan DMA. The twin cities have a unique small-town feeling, but offer big city amenities, including a vibrant arts community, a city-wide, all-terrain trail system, and world-class dining and nightlife. Bryan and College Station are routinely recognized as a leader in quality of life and as one of the fastest-growing communities in the country.
College Station is home to Texas A&M University, the nation’s largest university. Aggie home football games attract more than 100,000 in the stands, with tens of thousands more camped outside celebrating at tailgates during football weekends.

Learn more about KBTX at www.kbtx.com.

Job Summary/Description:  

KBTX Media is looking for a part-time photojournalist to join the Brazos Valley’s most-watched television station. The photojournalist will take an active role in the production of several station franchises and work alongside both the news and creative services departments.

KBTX Media is looking for a part-time photojournalist to join the Brazos Valley’s most-watched television station. The photojournalist will take an active role in the production of several station franchises and work alongside both the news and creative services departments. 

The ideal candidate demonstrates solid news judgment and storytelling abilities, with a passion for delivering original, imaginative content every day. A successful candidate will write, shoot, edit, and present compelling content both on-air and online. You’ll also play a key role in working with other KBTX journalists to develop both long- and short-term stories with a focus on uncovering the human side of each story. 

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to): 

- Identifying the day’s most important stories and sourcing materials relevant to your audience
- Researching, gathering, writing, and editing daily content for television and digital platforms
- Generating daily stories and content, along with regular enterprise reporting
- Working alongside other KBTX team members to produce impactful, high-energy live content
- Meeting daily and weekly deadlines in a fast-paced environment, including a strong digital focus

Qualifications/Requirements:

- You must independently enterprise content, enjoy and remain active on social media, and use your storytelling skills to offer meaningful context to issues affecting the  Brazos Valley. Great writing, a strong eye for content, and a willingness to learn will earn you this position.
- Candidates should also exhibit a good work ethic, strong people skills, the ability to be a team player, and always maintain a professional attitude. This position requires availability to work weekends and may require holiday work.
- Experience in a TV newsroom, as well as a college degree in broadcast journalism or a related field, is expected. Experience in reviewing legal/court documents, submitting open records requests, and an established and responsible presence on digital platforms are a big plus.

About KSFY/KDLT:

Sioux Falls is one of the fastest growing cities in the Upper Midwest and is home to more than 220,000 people. Healthcare and finance make up much of the workforce in Sioux Falls. There is never a shortage of things to do here. Summers are packed with outdoor festivals and concert events. Many also enjoy the city’s nearly 30 miles of bike trails; be sure to stop by the beautiful waterfalls of the Big Sioux River! And winter doesn’t mean people hibernate; there are plenty outdoor and indoor activities all winter long. In 2014, the city built a 12,000 seat area that has hosted everything from PBR events, hockey and indoor football, to concerts with names like Paul McCartney, Carrie Underwood and Elton John. The city is also home to a new indoor aquatic center, indoor ice skating facility, basketball arena, and an indoor tennis complex. There is no shortage of places to eat either. Not only is Sioux Falls home to many familiar restaurant chains, it’s known for many great locally-owned restaurants. And if you want to get away for the weekend, you can drive to Omaha in three hours, Minneapolis in four and the Black Hills in five.
KSFY/KDLT is an award-winning television operation serving viewers in the eastern half of South Dakota as well as portions of southwest Minnesota and northwest Iowa. The stations operate from a new studio in downtown Sioux Falls as one rebranded organization called Dakota News Now. The facilities put Dakota News Now on the cutting edge of television and news gathering technology, making it one of the most state-of-the-art television stations in the market and the region. The Dakota News Now team produces 36 hours of news each week. Some of our employees have been here for more than 25 years. For others, this is their first job out of college. It’s a great mix that gives us different perspectives while covering the news. People here enjoy the work they do, and everyone steps up to the plate during major news events like breaking news and severe weather.

Learn more about Dakota News Now & Sioux Falls here: https://www.dakotanewsnow.com/page/ksfykdlt-careers/

- Operate high-tech multimedia equipment

- While primarily a Monday-Friday position, must be willing to work longer hours and different days as needed

- Experience in television news photography is preferred, but we are willing to train the right candidate
- Ability to operate a field camera, editing software and lighting and audio equipment
equipment

Preferred (but not required):

About WMTV:

WMTV is the NBC affiliate and Gray Television-owned station serving south-central Wisconsin. We are the #1 station—leading the market in news and weather coverage. We are recognized for sharing information with accuracy and immediacy on all platforms.

We work hard and take pride in getting it right. For four years in a row, WMTV was honored as the Wisconsin Broadcasters Association “News Operation of the Year”. As well as being the recipient of the Edward R. Murrow Regional "Overall Excellence" Award.

What’s better than working at the #1 station in the nation’s #1 city? Join our award-winning team and live, work, and play in a community that is consistently named one of the best places to live in America. We are just 1.5 hours from Milwaukee, 2.5 hours from Chicago, and 5 hours from Minneapolis/St. Paul.

Job Summary/Description:

WMTV has an immediate opening for a Technical Media Producer. The Technical Media Producer (“TMP”) is responsible for operating the equipment in our broadcast control center that keeps WMTV’s programming on air and online. The TMP directs live and prerecorded productions as assigned, using our Ross Overdrive production automation system paired with coding in ENPS to deliver a quality News Show. The TMP also handles all master control duties in our facility, such as recording, playback, switching, and quality-checking programming for air. This position offers an opportunity for video editing and field directing.

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

- Monitoring and quality control of all inbound and outbound / broadcast signals, as well as ensuring that all content airs as intended and is logged
- Maintaining compliance with relevant FCC and other governmental agency regulations
- Directing assigned live and prerecorded productions using Ross Overdrive production automation
- Preparing the production rundowns for automation operation by coding the rundown in AP ENPS / Ross Overdrive plugin
- Understanding of all relevant equipment in the studio, production, and technical core areas
- Editing video for playback and working closely with the news team to ensure quality
- Field directing Special projects including WMTV's "Share your Holidays", UW Madison's Homecoming Parade, and our "On the Road segment

Qualifications/Requirements:

- 2 years of previous broadcast or production experience with master control or production control is preferred, but we will train the right person. Ross Overdrive experience is a plus.
- Demonstrated ability to learn new concepts quickly and thoroughly
- Proven track record of prioritizing complex tasks
- Ability to communicate effectively – written and verbal
- Strong commitment to working effectively with others; both being trained by and training others in a team environment is a must
- Positive attitude and ability to adapt to changes
- Must be willing to work holidays and weekends if needed

About KOSA:

First Alert 7 / KOSA-TV is the top-rated, long-time news leader in West Texas and southeastern New Mexico.

Based in Midland/Odessa, we pride ourselves on being the dominant player in a highly competitive market where there is never a shortage of news that impacts people on the regional level, throughout the state of Texas, and very often on the national stage. Our team of professionals is committed to sharing the most compelling stories every day…and we know that requires outstanding writers, creative photographers and an innovative production team. Whether we're following local officers to the nation's capital to remember their fallen brothers; traveling to Marine boot camp to highlight a local man's journey; covering a hometown president (George W. Bush) during his eight years in office; or tracking the latest developments in the oil and gas industry – KOSA is located at the epicenter of some of the most important news stories of our generation.

As the only community in the country with an International Air and Space Port, travel to and from Midland from anywhere in the world (and very soon even out of the world!) is quick and easy. We are also nestled in a picturesque region of Texas, often referred to as a hidden jewel that makes for exciting weekend trips for the outdoors adventurer or the lover of rare or unique art.

Job Summary/Description:

First Alert 7/KOSA-TV seeks a high-energy, self-motivated individual with exceptional communication skills to join our team as a Technical Media Producer (TMP). The TMP is a technical lead for production during live or taped studio broadcast productions and is responsible for the setup and operation of the production switcher and associated technical equipment in the Production Control Room and/or live location environment. They are responsible for evaluating and assigning all video inputs, taking into consideration timing and video levels, all while orchestrating the control room setup. The TMP will operate as the right hand of the News Producer to develop and execute the creative and technical “look” of the production by creating special effects via the production switcher.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

Live/Taped Productions:
- Set up and operate production switchers and all associated technical equipment in a Production Control Room and/or Live Location environment during live game and/or studio broadcast productions.
Orchestrate control room setup while simultaneously evaluating and assigning all video inputs, taking into consideration timing and video levels

KOLO is a station that gets the job done. Many of our employees have been with the company for years, and they pride themselves on their expertise and their ability to succeed. While Reno/Tahoe is a 100+ market, it has all the characteristics of a much larger West Coast market. In fact, some say Reno has a superior lifestyle and outdoor activities to its much larger neighboring markets. For these and many other reasons, KOLO is able to attract top-notch individuals. We pride ourselves on not limiting ourselves to the "news conference or press release journalism" stories that are easy to get. Our journalists know they need to tell stories on issues that matter to the Northern Nevada community and our viewers. Much of the station's identity is from KOLOCares, a program designed to better serve Northern Nevada through the wonderful non-profit organizations that are part of the community. KOLOCares was recently honored by the National Association of Broadcasters' Celebration of Service to Community Award. Every station is tasked to serve their community, but KOLO takes pride in finding unique ways to help our non-profit partners to reach their goals.

Reno has an illustrious history of boom or bust, and right now the area is booming! Life in Reno/Tahoe is not just about work. Northern Nevada boasts remarkable outdoor activities highlighted by the spectacular beauty of Lake Tahoe, world-renowned ski resorts in the Sierra, trout fishing in the Truckee River and Pyramid Lake, placid campgrounds, miles of hiking and biking trails and, yes, casinos. San Francisco, Yosemite, and Napa Valley are all an easy drive for a weekend getaway. Many Northern Californians spend their weekends in Reno, especially with the summer festivities that feature balloon races, Hot August Nights, and the nation's largest BBQ rib festival. There is always something happening in Reno, the "Biggest Little City in the World."
