job.title: 2027-28 POLITICO Fellows
job.description:
Job Description:

The POLITICO Fellows Program, among the most prestigious in the industry, trains early-career journalists in the fundamentals of covering politics, policy and power. It offers a select group of enterprising journalists a front-row seat to the biggest storylines in American and international politics at a time of historic political disruption – and a jump-start to a career in political and policy journalism.


Over a 12-month term, Fellows in the 2027–28 class receive hands-on newsroom experience, structured training and mentorship from POLITICO reporters and editors, preparing them to report for the most influential audiences in politics and policy. Start dates are flexible in 2027. Fellows will work from our HQ in Arlington, VA.


Who You Are:

We’re looking for candidates with at least two years of relevant experience, strong writing and analytical skills, the ability to work on a team, and a passion to learn and grow at the premier news organization covering the intersection of politics and policy in the United States and beyond.


What You'll Do:

  • Report and write stories for POLITICO’s audiences, from fast-turn breaking news to deeper policy explainers
  • Rotate through editorial teams covering the White House, Congress, federal agencies and key state capitals
  • Dig into the policy debates driving decision-making in Washington
  • Pitch your own story ideas and build a network of sources
  • Learn from POLITICO reporters and editors through regular training sessions and one-on-one mentorship
  • Be considered for an open position in the POLITICO newsroom upon successful completion of the program

What You'll Need (Application Materials):

  • Cover letter, sharing your story and stating your interest in politics or policy-focused journalism, plus any policy expertise
  • One-page résumé reflecting at least two years of paid newsroom or other professional journalism experience
  • Two references (list names, email addresses, phone numbers and relationship to the applicant)
  • Three work samples (i.e. published news stories or other articles, video, or audio) that are publicly accessible. Paywalled links will not be considered.
  • Please upload all documents to the Resume/CV section of the application in Workday. Incomplete applications will not be considered.

COMPENSATION: Total compensation of $63,700, plus benefits.


Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The deadline is Dec 18, 2026 at 5pm EST.


The Fellowship generates a high level of interest, so we cannot acknowledge the status of applications upon receipt or during the vetting process, which can take several weeks. We cannot accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us or amendments to applications. We will contact you for interviews as needed, which will start in January 2027.


We value our people. Click here for more on what we offer and what it’s like to work for POLITICO. 


Let’s keep in touch. You can view our list of open positions here.


About Us.

POLITICO illuminates the forces shaping global power. Since 2007, we have delivered intelligence that anticipates tomorrow's headlines, not reports on yesterday's news. As politics has increasingly become the defining force of our era, our work has never been more vital.


Cabinet secretaries and Ministers start their mornings with our analysis. CEOs shape strategy around our reporting. Advocacy leaders rely on our insights to move policy. We deliver the straightforward facts and clear-eyed analysis they need to navigate the most complex political landscape of our lifetimes.


Our 1,100+ publishing professionals across the world's key democratic capitals—Washington, Brussels, London, Paris, Berlin, Sacramento, and New York—form the world's premier politics and policy newsroom. We tell the story of how power really works by explaining who wields it and how they plan to exercise it, connecting dots others miss and delivering scoops from sources others don't even know exist.


Innovation has always been a core tenet of our story. At launch, we bet that depth would trump scale, that talent would trump traffic, and that politics would become central to modern life. In 2011, we made another bet and launched POLITICO Pro to help decision-makers understand the business of government, transforming both how they shape government action and the business of journalism itself.

These bets have made POLITICO the most successful digital news startup of its generation and the indispensable resource for leaders who shape the future. Today, we are a rarity in media: a growing, profitable, and sustainable news organization.


POLITICO is a subsidiary of Axel Springer SE, a family-owned transatlantic media company headquartered in Berlin and New York. Axel Springer is dedicated to shaping the future of journalism in the free world, believing that a free and informed society is essential to democracy. The company’s guiding principles - first articulated as  The Essentials by founder Axel Springer in the aftermath of World War II - remain a cornerstone of the company’s foundation today. Learn more about Axel Springer.

job.title: Executive Director, Human Resources
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking a strategic, consultative, and data-driven Executive Director of Human Resources to lead HR across North America. Reporting to the COO, this leader will serve as a trusted advisor to executive leadership, providing insights, recommendations, and counsel that connect talent strategy to business priorities. 


The ideal candidate brings strong business acumen, sound judgment, and the ability to influence effectively at all levels. They will use workforce data, including attrition trends and employee insights, to identify organizational challenges, inform recommendations, and develop strategies that strengthen retention, leadership effectiveness, and business performance. 


This role requires a balance of strategic advisory leadership and hands-on execution, along with a commitment to developing the HR team and fostering a high-performing, accountable, and engaged workforce. 


Who You Are: 

  • You are a strategic HR leader who operates as a trusted advisor and consultant, challenging assumptions, offering thoughtful recommendations, and influencing decisions that support business outcomes. 
  • You build credibility with senior leaders by combining sound judgment, strong relationships, business acumen, and data-backed insights. 
  • You translate complex workforce trends and organizational challenges into clear, actionable recommendations and measurable strategies. 
  • You are comfortable navigating ambiguity, advising leaders through difficult decisions, and balancing employee needs with business priorities. 
  • You are a strong people leader who coaches, mentors, and develops your team while promoting accountability, continuous improvement, and a solutions-oriented approach. 
  • You work collaboratively with your colleagues globally from talent acquisition, total rewards, HRIS, legal and finance to ensure seamless support for your key business stakeholders. 

What You’ll Do: 

  • Strategic Advisory & Business Partnership: Serve as a trusted advisor to the COO and senior leaders, providing consultative guidance on organizational strategy, workforce planning, organizational design, leadership effectiveness, and talent priorities. Influence decisions through sound analysis, business context, and actionable recommendations. 
  • Data, Analytics & Workforce Insights: Lead the analysis and reporting of workforce trends, including attrition, retention, turnover drivers, engagement, headcount, and talent movement. Translate findings into clear insights and recommendations that inform leadership decisions and shape people strategies. 
  • Attrition & Retention Strategy: Produce regular attrition reporting and insights, identifying trends, patterns, and potential root causes across teams and populations. Partner with leaders to develop targeted retention strategies, monitor outcomes, and assess the effectiveness of interventions. 
  • Leadership Coaching & Influence: Advise and coach executives and managers on leadership effectiveness, team dynamics, performance, accountability, employee development, and complex people decisions. Build leaders’ capability to manage and develop their teams effectively. 
  • Performance & Talent Management: Lead performance management, talent reviews, succession planning, talent mapping, career development, and internal mobility initiatives. Use data and organizational insights to identify talent risks, capability gaps, and opportunities to strengthen performance and retention. 
  • Organizational Effectiveness & Change: Consult with leaders on organizational structure, workforce capabilities, resource allocation, and change management. Provide recommendations that improve collaboration, clarify accountability, and align people and resources with business objectives. 
  • Learning & Development: Identify leadership and workforce capability gaps and establish development strategies, training programs, and learning opportunities that support current and future business needs. 
  • Employee Relations & Engagement: Provide guidance on complex employee relations matters, investigations, performance concerns, and sensitive leadership decisions. Promote a culture of trust, inclusion, accountability, and respect while balancing risk and business needs. 
  • HR Team Leadership: Lead, mentor, and develop the North American HRBP team, establishing clear priorities, strengthening advisory and analytical capabilities, and fostering a proactive, consultative, and commercially minded approach. 
  • Global HR Collaboration & Compliance: Partner with international HR colleagues to align global people strategies while addressing North American business needs and applicable employment requirements. Ensure HR practices are effective, consistent, and compliant. 

What You’ll Need: 

  • Significant progressive HR leadership experience, including senior-level HR business partnership and broad HR functional responsibility. 
  • Demonstrated experience serving as a strategic advisor to C-suite executives and influencing business decisions through sound judgment, consultation, and evidence-based recommendations. 
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret workforce data, identify trends and root causes, and translate findings into practical business and people strategies. 
  • Demonstrated experience producing and presenting HR reporting, particularly attrition, retention, and workforce insights, to inform leadership decisions and measure the impact of interventions. 
  • Expertise in organizational effectiveness, workforce planning, talent management, performance management, leadership development, and employee relations. 
  • Proven ability to coach and influence senior leaders, navigate challenging conversations, and provide candid, balanced advice on complex people matters. 
  • Experience leading organizational change, managing employee relations issues and investigations, and advising on risk and compliance. 
  • Proven ability to lead, mentor, and develop HR professionals and build a high-performing, consultative team. 
  • Knowledge of U.S. employment laws and multi-state HR practices; Canadian HR experience is a plus. 
  • Experience with compensation, HR systems, workforce planning, and people analytics. 
  • Excellent communication, presentation, relationship-building, and influencing skills, including the ability to communicate complex data and recommendations clearly to executive audiences. 
  • Ability to balance strategic thinking and advisory responsibilities with hands-on execution in a fast-paced, evolving environment. 
  • A bachelor’s degree in human resources, business, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. 

What Success Looks Like: 

  • Senior leaders view HR as a credible, consultative partner that strengthens decision-making and business outcomes. 
  • Workforce reporting and attrition insights consistently inform leadership discussions and targeted retention strategies. 
  • Talent recommendations are supported by data, aligned with business priorities, and evaluated against measurable outcomes. 
  • Leaders are better equipped to manage performance, develop talent, and build accountable, effective teams. 
  • The HR team operates proactively, delivers meaningful business insights, and provides consistent, high-quality support across North America. 

Compensation: $190-215k Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.


We value our people. Click here for more on what we offer and what it’s like to work for POLITICO. 


Let’s keep in touch. You can view our list of open positions here and email us careers@politico.com. We hope to see your application soon!

job.title: Reporter, State AGs
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking two aggressive, enterprising reporters to cover state attorneys general as national political and policy actors. Each reporter will be a founding member of POLITICO's new State AGs team, and will report on how AGs are shaping tech, energy, health care, consumer protection and antitrust policy regionally and nationally, and the dynamics shaping multistate and partisan coalitions.

 

The reporters will cover four overlapping areas:

  • The anchor states. California, New York, Texas and Florida run the most powerful AG offices in the country, and their actions on tech, finance, energy and health care often set national standards.
  • Other key states. The offices that drive coalition strategy and national policy fights, including Illinois, Massachusetts, New Jersey and Washington on the Democratic side, and Tennessee, Missouri, Louisiana and Utah on the Republican side.
  • A redrawn AG map. November's elections gave Democrats AG offices in Texas, Ohio, Georgia, Iowa and Kansas. The beat will follow how those offices take shape and how Republican AGs respond.
  • Coalition dynamics. How multistate coalitions form and fracture, who leads and who follows, how DAGA and RAGA shape them, and where AGs of both parties find common ground.

 

A deep source network inside AG offices of both parties will be essential, going well beyond public filings and press releases. Those sources will drive exclusive news on investigations and lawsuits, along with reporting from inside coalition conversations on which cases to bring, which companies to target and which states will sign on.

 

The beat will focus closely on how AGs decide where to intervene, against business or against the federal government. Democratic AGs have become the front line of legal resistance to the Trump administration, while Republican AGs have often acted as its partners and force multipliers. The beat will also track how coalitions form, who leads them and who follows, where AGs of both parties find common ground, and how the office has become a launchpad for national ambition.

 

The policy portfolio will include health care, antitrust, AI and tech platforms, consumer protection, climate and energy, financial services, ESG and DEI, labor, and the limits of federal power — the enforcement fights where AGs are most active and where their actions carry the biggest consequences for companies and investors.

 

The reporters will work hand in hand with POLITICO's California, New York and Florida teams, which already cover their states' AGs closely as political figures and policymakers.

 

What You'll Need:

  • Reporting experience covering politics, policy, government or the law
  • A demonstrated ability to break news and deliver original, incisive reporting
  • Deep familiarity with state politics and with the state-federal legal battles of the past decade
  • The ability to build a network of sources in AG offices, DAGA, RAGA, or the legal and political circles around them
  • A strong interest in the personalities, rivalries and ambitions that drive AG offices
  • An entrepreneurial spirit and eagerness to help build an exciting new part of our journalism
  • The ability to juggle fast-moving breaking news with ambitious enterprise reporting
  • The ability to write clearly, accurately and efficiently on deadline for an influential, professional audience
  • A collaborative spirit and willingness to work with reporters and editors across POLITICO's state, legal and policy teams
  • A rigorous commitment to fair-minded, accurate and nonpartisan journalism

 

We’re open to candidates based in Arlington, VA (HQ); New York, NY; or Sacramento, CA. If you’re not near one of our offices, we still encourage you to apply.

 

Compensation: $90,000-$140,000 Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking an ambitious, enterprising reporter to cover the legal and corporate ecosystem around state attorneys general as part of a new POLITICO newsletter. The reporter will be a founding member of POLITICO's new State AGs team, and will focus on the lawyers, firms, companies and power brokers who work with AGs, against them and around them. 

 

State AGs’ biggest cases are often built and argued alongside outside counsel, and a growing roster of firms has built dedicated state AG practices to defend companies and help them manage AG risk. Those practices are staffed increasingly by former AGs, deputies and senior aides

 

The beat will cover that world closely. The reporter will dig into investigations, lawsuits and settlements, the corporate strategies for fighting or heading off AG action, and the relationships, rivalries and money that determine which cases get brought

 

The beat will also track which companies and industries fund RAGA and DAGA, and how corporate members and donors engage with AGs and try to shape their priorities on both sides.

 

The policy portfolio will include health care, antitrust, AI and tech platforms, consumer protection, climate and energy, financial services, ESG and DEI, labor, and the limits of federal power — the enforcement fights where AGs are most active and where their actions carry the biggest consequences for companies and investors.

 

The reporter will work closely with the State AGs team's other reporters, the product's senior editor, and POLITICO's legal, tech, energy and health teams on sourcing and coverage planning.

 

What You'll Need:

  • Reporting experience covering the law, the legal industry, corporate litigation, or regulation and enforcement
  • An understanding of how state AG enforcement, multistate litigation and settlements work
  • A demonstrated ability to break news and deliver original, incisive reporting
  • The ability to build a network of sources among outside counsel, defense firms, in-house lawyers and former AG officials
  • An entrepreneurial spirit and eagerness to help build an exciting new part of our journalism
  • The ability to juggle fast-moving breaking news and write clearly, accurately and efficiently on deadline for an influential, professional audience

job.title: Senior Product Manager, AgencyIQ by POLITICO
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking an experienced Senior Product Manager to design and deliver new tools and features for AgencyIQ by POLITICO, a policy-driven product for regulatory professionals in the life sciences, food, and chemicals sectors.


AgencyIQ combines expert research, data, and software tools for regulatory professionals in the life sciences, food, and chemicals industries. This Senior Product Manager will shape AgencyIQ’s roadmap and help the product team move from customer insight to working solutions faster. The role spans product innovation (including the development and roll-out of AI-driven tools), commercial strategy, and technology execution—driving measurable growth in subscriber acquisition, engagement, and retention across both product lines.


The ideal candidate has a strong grasp of AI coding tools (Codex, Claude Code, etc.), can speak in technical terms with the engineering team, and has a proven ability to translate subscriber insights into product roadmaps that deliver commercial results.


Who You Are

• You are a highly user-centric product manager with a strong track record of translating research, data, and market insight into clear roadmaps and measurable business impact.

• You are comfortable with both customer discovery and hands-on technical work. You can test an idea with users, understand how it fits into a subscription product, and collaborate with engineers on APIs, data flows, security, and deployment.

• You enjoy enabling others by creating repeatable processes that make the whole team more effective.


What You’ll Do

Product Strategy & Roadmap

• Own and prioritize a roadmap for AgencyIQ features and workflows, balancing customer value, commercial impact, technical feasibility, and engineering capacity.

• Interview customers and prospects; analyze usage, feedback, market developments, and competitors; turn findings into clear product requirements, experiments, and defined KPIs.

• Partner with research, commercial, design, and engineering teams to improve acquisition, engagement, expansion, and retention of customers across the market segments we serve.


AI-Assisted Prototyping and Technical Enablement

• Design and roll out a repeatable workflow that lets others on the AgencyIQ product team use approved AI coding tools, such as Codex or Claude Code, to build and test feature prototypes and data collection tools.

• Work with POLITICO’s engineering and design teams to create reusable templates and documentation that adhere to company standards and connect to POLITICO systems through approved access paths.

• Align new templates and workflows with the tooling, policies, and procedures established by POLITICO’s engineering and operations teams.

• Define how prototypes are evaluated with users, reviewed by engineers, and either hardened for release or retired.

• Build representative prototypes yourself and coach other product managers through the workflow, and improve it based on where they get stuck and what engineers need for an efficient handoff.

• Create reusable evals for prototypes and AI-enabled features, using representative regulatory tasks, expected results, and clear quality thresholds. Run them as designs change and use the results to guide engineering review and release decisions.


Regulatory Data and Delivery

• Scope and prototype reliable ways to collect public data from government sources in the United States, Europe, Japan, and other global jurisdictions using official APIs or structured feeds where available and compliant scraping where appropriate.

• Partner with research and engineering on source provenance, data quality, parsing, change detection, monitoring, and maintainability so promising data prototypes can become dependable product capabilities.

• Write clear specifications, make trade-offs visible, coordinate delivery to make the most of limited engineering capacity, and measure whether shipped features improve customer outcomes.


Required Experience

• 3+ years of product management experience delivering B2B software or data products, with evidence of strong product judgment and measurable customer or business results.

• Hands-on ability to prototype with modern AI coding tools and enough working knowledge of code, APIs, databases, and software delivery to assess output and collaborate credibly with engineers.

• Experience designing usable product workflows from interviews, usability tests, feedback, and behavioral data; fluency in product metrics and prioritization.

• Experience working with engineering on technical requirements, integrations, testing, and release processes; sound judgment about security, data access, and where human review is necessary.

• Ability to teach technical practices to colleagues with different backgrounds and to communicate decisions clearly to commercial, research, technology, and senior leadership teams.


Preferred Experience

• Familiarity with Python or JavaScript, SQL, web data collection, cloud development environments, CI/CD, and API-based integrations.

• Experience in information services, regulatory intelligence, or another B2B subscription business that combines expert content, structured data, and software.

• Knowledge of public regulatory sources or the needs of regulatory affairs, policy, legal, or scientific users.

• Knowledge of the U.S. capital markets—namely public equities and the institutions that trade them.



COMPENSATION: $110,000 - 120,000 Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

job.title: Senior Research Manager, Food Regulation
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking a Senior Research Manager to help lead part of its regulatory intelligence and information services product, AgencyIQ. Since its founding in early 2020, AgencyIQ has quickly become the premier source of regulatory intelligence and analysis for professionals working in the life sciences and food industries.


As a subject matter expert in U.S. food regulations issued by the Food and Drug Administration, Department of Agriculture, and state agencies, the Senior Research Manager will be responsible for analyzing the relevance of regulatory changes and developments, articulating the type and degree of impact on food companies, and providing contextualization to an audience of knowledgeable regulatory intelligence professionals.

 

The Senior Research Manager will join a team of experienced researchers responsible producing a mix of daily content, in-depth research, weekly insights, directed deliverables and presentations. The role will cover a variety of food related regulatory topics including labeling, ingredients, packaging, nutrition, safety, and compliance.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Produce daily (3-4 per week) topical intelligence articles and other content for our subscribers based on emerging regulatory and legislative developments related to food regulatory topics
  • Serve as a subject matter specialist on several food topics for AgencyIQ (e.g., labeling, packaging, nutrition, ingredients, safety, compliance, etc.)
  • Lead or participate in the development and delivery of in-depth analysis, deep-dive research, webinars and email newsletters
  • Collaborate with other members of the AgencyIQ research team focused on chemical, food and life sciences regulation
  • Participate in subscriber- and prospect-facing events, briefings, and business development activities

What you’ll need

Required:

  • Have 5+ years’ experience analyzing U.S. food regulations, guidance and policies from the FDA, USDA, and state authorities (e.g., working for a company, trade group, regulator, or consulting company).
  • Have prior experience writing about regulatory developments in a deadline-driven environment for an executive or industry audience (e.g., for an internal company newsletter or for externally-facing publications); 
  • A strong affinity for writing – efficiently and effectively, and for a business or policy audience – paired with a knowledge of (and passion for) regulation and regulatory policy
  • Experience and comfort working in fast-paced, research-driven environments in which daily delivery of regulatory analyses is the norm
  • An excellent working knowledge of food regulatory frameworks and processes (and in particular the FDA) and capable of delivering expert insights to our knowledgeable subscribers
  • Find enjoyment in reading, analyzing, writing, speaking and learning about challenging or new regulatory topics; Have strong attention to detail and accuracy

 

Preferred:

 

  • Have an advanced degree or certification related to food science, law or policy (i.e., a JD, PhD, or relevant master’s degree); or
  • Have prior experience working in media, including as a journalist or writing a product widely read by others (i.e., a business intelligence product or internal newsletter).
  • Experience presenting on regulatory topics to a variety of different audience types (small groups, large groups) in different environments (virtual and in-person)

Compensation: $135-160k Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

job.title: Team Manager, Customer Success
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is looking for a Team Manager, Customer Success to manage a team of 10 Customer Engagement Specialists and develop scalable customer engagement practices that drive product adoption, customer value, Wallet Retention Rate, and retention rate across the US Professional Subscriptions business. This senior manager level role will focus on coaching and developing team members, driving team performance, and executing strategies that strengthen customer engagement and retention.


POLITICO's mission from the very beginning was to win the audience. We dedicate ourselves to providing accurate, non-partisan, impactful information to the right people at the right time so that they can act with confidence and speed. We experiment to avoid being disrupted and we have fun disrupting others. And we are not afraid to risk failure if it means being the best at what we do.


What You’ll Do:

  • Manage, coach, and develop a team of 10 Customer Engagement Specialists, fostering a high-performing team culture focused on growth, accountability, and results.
  • Partner with the Managing Director, Customer Success to develop and execute strategies that drive customer engagement, product adoption, Wallet Retention Rate, and overall retention.
  • Establish team goals, performance expectations, and scalable processes to improve customer onboarding, engagement, training, and support.
  • Provide ongoing coaching, feedback, and professional development to strengthen individual and team performance.
  • Leverage customer health, usage, and engagement data to identify opportunities, address risks, and improve the customer experience.
  • Collaborate with Account Management and Customer Success leadership to align customer engagement efforts with broader business goals.
  • Partner with Product, Marketing, Technology, and Data teams to share customer insights and drive improvements across the business.

What You’ll Need:

  • Experience in Customer Success, Account Management, client services, customer engagement, or a related field, preferably within SaaS, subscription, or information services.
  • Proven experience managing, coaching, and developing customer-facing teams, with a track record of driving performance and results.
  • Ability to build and improve scalable processes that strengthen customer engagement, product adoption, and retention.
  • Strong leadership, communication, and relationship-building skills, with a passion for developing people.
  • Analytical mindset with experience using customer data and performance metrics to identify opportunities and drive decisions.
  • Ability to collaborate across departments, manage competing priorities, and adapt in a fast-paced environment.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.

COMPENSATION: $85,000 - $100,000 annual salary. This role is also eligible to participate in POLITICO’s commission plan, with a target incentive opportunity of $35,000 - $50,000, resulting in an on-target earnings (OTE) potential of approximately $120,000 - $150,000. Commission payments are variable and are based on achievement against applicable performance goals and the terms of the commission plan. Actual compensation will depend on factors including experience, skills, qualifications, and other job-related considerations.


We value our people. Click here for more on what we offer and what it’s like to work for POLITICO.

Let’s keep in touch. You can view our list of open positions here and email us careers@politico.com. We hope to see your application soon!

 

About Us. 

POLITICO illuminates the forces shaping global power. Since 2007, we have delivered intelligence that anticipates tomorrow's headlines, not reports on yesterday's news. As politics has increasingly become the defining force of our era, our work has never been more vital. 

Cabinet secretaries and Ministers start their mornings with our analysis. CEOs shape strategy around our reporting. Advocacy leaders rely on our insights to move policy. We deliver the straightforward facts and clear-eyed analysis they need to navigate the most complex political landscape of our lifetimes. 

Our 1,100+ publishing professionals across the world's key democratic capitals—Washington, Brussels, London, Paris, Berlin, Sacramento, and New York—form the world's premier politics and policy newsroom. We tell the story of how power really works by explaining who wields it and how they plan to exercise it, connecting dots others miss and delivering scoops from sources others don't even know exist. 

Innovation has always been a core tenet of our story. At launch, we bet that depth would trump scale, that talent would trump traffic, and that politics would become central to modern life. In 2011, we made another bet and launched POLITICO Pro to help decision-makers understand the business of government, transforming both how they shape government action and the business of journalism itself. 

These bets have made POLITICO the most successful digital news startup of its generation and the indispensable resource for leaders who shape the future. Today, we are a rarity in media: a growing, profitable, and sustainable news organization. 

POLITICO is a subsidiary of Axel Springer SE, a family-owned transatlantic media company headquartered in Berlin and New York. Axel Springer is dedicated to shaping the future of journalism in the free world, believing that a free and informed society is essential to democracy. The company’s guiding principles - first articulated as  The Essentials by founder Axel Springer in the aftermath of World War II - remain a cornerstone of the company’s foundation today. Learn more about Axel Springer.

job.title: Assistant Managing Editor, National
job.description:
ProPublica is an independent, nonprofit newsroom that produces investigative journalism in the public interest. 

Applications are being reviewed on a rolling basis. While the anticipated application deadline is December 31st at 11:59 PM ET, the role may close earlier if a candidate is hired. We encourage interested applicants to apply as soon as possible.

ProPublica is seeking an accomplished senior-level investigative editor to help oversee and elevate the accountability journalism produced by editors and reporters on our national staff and serve as part of ProPublica’s masthead leadership team.

The assistant managing editor, national, will supervise teams of editors and reporters and, depending on the candidate, may also directly supervise one or more investigative reporters. The ideal candidate enjoys the challenge of helping editors and reporters envision the most ambitious and creative paths for their projects; deeply understands and embraces ProPublica’s accountability mission; has a facility for high-level story honing and writing; and is dedicated to helping our editors grow and develop. We’re looking for an experienced editor with sound news judgment who is equally comfortable and adept weighing in on what’s working, or not, in a long-form narrative as in a complicated, multipart investigation.

This position involves juggling a variety of high-level projects, weighing in on story selection and direction, providing top-level guidance and editing, as well as working with staffers from other ProPublica teams, from data and research to video and audience. 

The assistant managing editor, national, will report to the managing editor of the national staff.

What you would be doing:

  • Supervising teams of national reporters and editors working on revelatory, important stories and projects.
  • Providing support and guidance to ensure projects are conceived of and told as ambitiously and creatively as possible.
  • Working with editors and reporters to select stories with the potential for impact, and helping them overcome reporting hurdles
  • Editing, including identifying and fixing structural issues and elevating writing when necessary.
  • Helping teams collaborate with researchers, data visualization reporters, engagement reporters, audience and visual staffers, and story producers.
  • Coaching editors to stretch and develop their skills and ambitions.
  • Serving as a champion for accountability journalism.

We’re looking for someone who has:

  • At least 10 years experience overseeing investigative and/or accountability reporting and has managed teams of reporters and editors.
  • A track record as an editor of landing revelatory stories about abuses of power.
  • A passion for and experience with accountability journalism.
  • The ability to juggle many different responsibilities, meet deadlines and handle pressure while remaining calm.
  • Exceptional organizational skills.
  • A collaborative mindset. As a leader, you should work seamlessly with staffers throughout the newsroom. 
  • The ability to adroitly handle fast-breaking stories, monthslong reporting projects and exquisitely written narratives.

This job is full time and includes benefits. 

We’re open to remote candidates based and authorized to work in the United States. Candidates in the New York City region will be expected to work in our office at least two days a week. We also have offices in Washington, D.C.; Atlanta; Chicago; Phoenix; and Berkeley, California. Though not currently in place, an in-person requirement could be introduced at these locations in the future. 

The expected salary range for this position is $200,000 to $250,000.

This is a good-faith estimate of what we expect to pay for this position. The final salary figure will take into account a person’s experience, accomplishment and location. ProPublica is committed to paying its staff equitably, and these ranges should not be considered career salary limits or caps.

What you should send us:

  • The most important part by far is your past work. We’d like to see examples of projects that show how you work as both a direct editor and as a top editor. Specifically: 
    • (1) Send us links to the investigative stories you directly edited that you are most proud of. These should be stories where you worked directly with a reporter to shape and guide the focus of an investigation. Don’t be shy — tell us what worked (numbers and evidence of impact welcome) and how you’d do it differently next time. Editing is about far more than moving around words. Show us how you think. 
    • (2) Send us a project or story in which you made a significant difference as a top editor. This should be where you honed the structure or narrative or where you identified missing elements necessary before publication. Let us know how your contributions elevated the work.
  • Your resume.                              

We will begin reviewing applications as we receive them, but we will continue to consider candidates as long as the posting remains live on our site.

Questions? Send an email to talent@propublica.org. 

No phone calls, please.

We know there are great candidates who may not fit into what we’ve described above or who have important skills we haven’t thought of. If that’s you, don’t hesitate to apply and tell us about yourself.

We are an equal opportunity employer and prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind. All employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age or any other status protected under applicable law. We are dedicated to building an inclusive newsroom and encourage people from all backgrounds to apply.

job.title: Freelance Pitch Form
job.description:
ProPublica is an independent, nonprofit newsroom that produces investigative journalism in the public interest. 

While the vast majority of ProPublica’s work comes from our staff, we occasionally consider supporting ambitious accountability stories or projects from independent journalists whose ideas align with the mission of our organization.

Here’s what journalists submitting proposals should know.

We’re open to investigations that are revelatory or substantially advance what is known on a subject of importance. The investigation should have the potential to trigger needed reforms by identifying a problem, who’s responsible and what should change. It should also clearly show harm. The investigation can be rooted in a place or focus on a person, but it should illuminate an issue of broader relevance.

The best proposals have a clear hypothesis, typically based on significant reporting: They don’t wonder whether something bad is happening, they know it. Please include not only a general description of the topic, but also a sense of the anecdotes/data/documents you have gathered, what you expect to find and possible accountability stories you want to tell.

In addition, applicants should detail, as much as is possible at the outset, what an investigation will require: data work, travel, obtaining public records. It’s also important for us to know what data, documents and/or source relationships the reporter already has. Finally, we’d like to hear a bit about why you are particularly suited to do this investigation.

We will begin reviewing applications as we receive them, and aim to notify candidates regarding your proposals within two weeks of submission. Questions? Send an email to talent@propublica.org. No phone calls, please.

For those proposals we accept, we pay competitive freelance rates, including reporting expenses. Freelancers are independent contractors and will not be treated by ProPublica as employees for any purpose.

Independent contractors are responsible for paying any required taxes on any compensation received and for understanding the applicable tax laws. We will begin reviewing applications as we receive them, and aim to notify candidates regarding your proposals within two weeks of submission. 

We know there are great candidates who may not fit into what we’ve described above or who have important skills we haven’t thought of. If that’s you, don’t hesitate to apply and tell us about yourself.

We are an equal opportunity employer and prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind. All employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age or any other status protected under applicable law. We are dedicated to building an inclusive newsroom and encourage people from all backgrounds to apply.

job.title: Product Engineer, Membership and Front-End
job.description:
ProPublica is an independent, nonprofit newsroom that produces investigative journalism in the public interest. 

We will stop accepting applications for this role on Monday, November 30th @ 11:59PM ET.

ProPublica is hiring a software engineer to work primarily on the systems and services that power our audience data platforms. This important role serves to advance ProPublica’s mission — publishing journalism with real-world impact — by enabling systems that bring us greater understanding of our audiences and donors.

We’re looking for an experienced engineer who believes in our mission and thrives in multifaceted roles, contributing both to the long-term product road map and to hands-on development. Your responsibilities will include shipping high-quality and resilient code and collaborating with designers, product managers, data analysts, other engineers and agency partners. You’ll write code, configure no- and low-code integrations, contribute to our documentation, share your expertise and proactively solve problems.

As a member of our expanding, crossfunctional product team, you’ll work with colleagues across ProPublica’s engineering, audience and membership operations, ensuring that our capabilities align with our principles and advance our organizational objectives. This position reports to our director of product engineering and will work closely with the audience data and insights analyst.

What you’ll do

  • Build and ship reader-facing features that drive membership — calls to action, donation flows, and account and authentication experiences — with clean, resilient code.
  • Integrate the systems behind them: messaging tools, payments and donation processing platforms, user accounts, CDP and CRM, and the data infrastructure that connect them.
  • Instrument the audience and donor journey. Set up accurate and actionable event tracking so every meaningful step is captured cleanly and becomes data we can act on.
  • Support making experimentation routine. Build the infrastructure for A/B testing and, with internal business teams, run experiments regularly so our decisions rest on evidence instead of guesswork.
  • Write front-end  services and integrations as needed. (Our site runs on Wordpress VIP.)
  • Working with our engineering leaders, protect reader privacy and keep us compliant with legal and regulatory requirements.

Required qualifications

  • At least three years of experience in front-end software development and system integrations, with a track record of implementing and maintaining performant, secure, scalable solutions.
  • Experience interacting with audience and reader data platforms, such as Salesforce, Google Analytics, Parse.ly, Sailthru, or similar CRMs, CDPs and analytics tools.
  • Experience working on a customer data platform implementation within the last two years.
  • Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills, with experience in a highly collaborative team environment, supporting diverse stakeholders and adapting solutions to evolving business needs.
  • Clear and effective spoken and written communication skills, with the ability to document technical processes and present complex integration workflows to both technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
  • Ability to travel for occasional staff summits or other required events.

Preferred qualifications

  • Prior experience implementing solutions such as Piano or MonetizationOS or building similar functionality.
  • Working knowledge of Wordpress and/or Wordpress VIP.
  • Fluency with at least one language used in web development, such as PHP, Typescript or vanilla JS.
  • Track record of doing hands-on work with cloud data warehouses like Google BigQuery and customer data platforms such as Braze or Hightouch.
  • Knowledge of newsroom workflows and a passion for journalism.

This job is full time and includes benefits. ProPublica is based in New York, but we’re open to remote candidates. We have offices in New York City; Washington, D.C.; Atlanta; Chicago; Phoenix; and Berkeley, California. Applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S.

This role is subject to an in-office work requirement of two days per week in the New York City office. That requirement may be extended to other offices with 60 days’ notice. 

This job is covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with The NewsGuild of New York, Local 31003, CWA, AFL-CIO

The expected salary range for this position is $120,000 to $145,000.

This is a good-faith estimate of what we expect to pay for this position. The final salary figure will take into account a person’s experience, accomplishment and location. ProPublica is committed to paying its staff equitably, and these ranges should not be considered career salary limits or caps.

We will begin reviewing applications as we receive them, but we will continue to consider candidates as long as the posting remains live on our site.

Questions? Send an email to talent@propublica.org. 

No phone calls, please.

job.title: Video Editor and Motion Designer, Temporary
job.description:
ProPublica is an independent, nonprofit newsroom that produces investigative journalism in the public interest. 

Applications will close on Monday, November 16th, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.

In 2024, ProPublica launched a short-form vertical video team to adapt our long-form investigative journalism for audiences on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts. Since then, the team has amassed nearly 65 million views. Now we’re building out the second phase of our social video strategy and have launched a new YouTube team dedicated to producing midlength adaptations for the platform.

We are looking for a video editor and motion designer who has a passion for accountability journalism and is excited by the opportunity to bring our reporting to an increasing number of viewers who treat YouTube as a platform to learn about the world around them.

In this role, you will work alongside video producers on the YouTube team and will own the creative and technical postproduction for several assigned videos a month. As this is a new team, you will also be a key part of building the workflows and best practices that make our YouTube video pipeline sustainable as well as creating the visual identity that helps to answer: What should ProPublica look and sound like on YouTube? 

The videos you help create for YouTube are meant to serve as standalone editorial products, and we’re looking for your platform-native expertise to drive experimentation that helps us learn quickly, adapt and deliver the most compelling storytelling formats while adhering to our rigorous editorial standards and practices. You should be comfortable working with reporters and editors across the newsroom as well as freelancers we’ll bring on to help with projects.

This is a temporary two-year role that will report to our director of multiplatform audience strategy. The YouTube team sits within the larger ProPublica audience team.

Essential responsibilities 

  • Collaborate with producers to create videos — and related promo cuts — that are grounded in ethical journalistic principles, standards and practices.
  • Use editorial judgment to translate investigations and video scripts with the sensitivity, care and appropriate tone they require.
  • Own the creative and technical postproduction for videos — editing, motion graphic design and animation, color grading and sound design — ensuring projects are shaped and paced for a YouTube-first audience.
  • Own end-to-end motion design workflows, including creating storyboards, animatics and the polished final products for videos.
  • Establish and maintain a central motion design library of MOGRTs, templates, toolkits and other reusable visual assets for teamwide use.
  • Maintain ProPublica’s brand standards and overall design system, collaborating with the design and graphics teams, among others, to ensure visual cohesiveness in videos.
  • Communicate proactively with the team regarding project status and timelines and directly collaborate with producers on scoping and delivering videos on schedule. 
  • Manage multiple projects in various stages of production, sometimes meeting tight deadlines.

About you

We are looking for candidates who have proven that they can use video editing and design skills for journalistic ends.

The ideal candidate will have these skills and attributes:

  • Four or more years of professional video editing and motion design experience in a newsroom, media organization or production studio. 
  • High proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite, with expert proficiency in both Adobe After Effects and Premiere Pro.
  • A portfolio that highlights videos you have edited specifically for YouTube, including hosted, vlog-style and/or explainer formats.
  • Experience building tension in hooks, controlling pacing and navigating tonal shifts in video storytelling. 
  • You are energized by the opportunity of being part of a founding team and creating something from scratch — establishing formats, defining visual languages and building efficient workflows. 
  • You thrive while collaborating, seeking input from others and iterating your work based on feedback. 

And many of these: 

  • Experience being part of a founding YouTube team or launching a new project initiative. 
  • Experience in on-site production, including shooting on professional camera equipment and knowledge of lighting and audio setups.
  • Experience with digital asset management and video archival workflows. 
  • Proficiency in Figma and Google Workspace.

This job is full time and includes benefits. ProPublica is based in New York, but we’re open to remote candidates. We have offices in New York City; Washington, D.C.; Atlanta; Chicago; Phoenix; and Berkeley, California. Applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. and have the ability to travel, as necessary, for team meetings, training and video-related duties.

This role is subject to an in-office work requirement of two days per week in the New York City office. That requirement may be extended to other offices with 60 days’ notice. 

This job is covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with The NewsGuild of New York, Local 31003, CWA, AFL-CIO.

The expected salary range for this position is $90,000 to $115,000.

This is a good-faith estimate of what we expect to pay for this position. The final salary figure will take into account a person’s experience, accomplishment and location. ProPublica is committed to paying its staff equitably, and these ranges should not be considered career salary limits or caps.

We will begin reviewing applications as we receive them, but we will continue to consider candidates as long as the posting remains live on our site.

job.title: Associate Product Designer (Cinmar)
job.description:
CBFG0168Associate Product Designer — Color, Print & Pattern

Location: West Chester, Ohio
Brand/Business: Grandin Road
Reports to: Senior Designer

About the Role

The Associate Product Designer is a developmental role designed to build the skills and experience needed to advance to a Designer position. Specializing in color, print, and pattern, this designer will also contribute to product design and concept development across home categories.

Working under the guidance of the Senior Designer, you’ll help translate global trends and customer insights into brand-relevant concepts and product designs. You’ll support projects from initial concept through revisions, sample review, and final approval—balancing creative vision with business needs, product requirements, and established design processes.

What You’ll Do

  • Curate trend research and develop seasonal and trend boards that balance market insight with brand relevance.
  • Create seasonal color palettes and curate print and pattern direction aligned with the brand vision.
  • Develop and place artwork across product types, creating cohesive capsule collections across categories.
  • Translate global trends into relevant concepts and designs, considering shape, materials, color, and print and pattern.
  • Under the Senior Designer’s direction, develop SKU-level designs from initial concept through revisions and final sample approval.
  • Design within the line plan and support financial growth and profitability, considering assortment strategy, price points, and cost engineering.
  • Ensure designs align with seasonal concepts, big ideas, and the overall creative direction.
  • Present concepts to the design leader for review and approval.
  • Present product concepts and final specifications to cross-functional teams; partner with Merchandising on sketch revisions and approvals.
  • Present final designs to the Executive team.
  • Review first and final samples with Merchandising, helping ensure feedback, revisions, and approvals are completed on schedule.
  • Prepare complete, accurate product design specification packages and meet calendar deadlines.
  • Collaborate with Design, Merchandising, Sourcing, and manufacturers/vendors throughout the development process.
  • Travel for inspiration and to build knowledge of vendor capabilities.

Product Categories

Experience designing for home products is essential, including:

  • Home decorative accessories
  • Entertaining products, including serveware and dinnerware
  • Home textiles, including bedding, decorative pillows, doormats, and table linens

What You’ll Bring

  • Experience designing products for the home market, especially in the categories listed above.
  • Strong design skills and a point of view in color, print, and pattern.
  • The ability to interpret trends and translate them into designs that feel relevant to the brand and customer.
  • An understanding of how to develop designs across product types and create cohesive collections.
  • The ability to work within a design process, follow direction, manage revisions, and meet deadlines.
  • Strong collaboration and presentation skills, including comfort sharing work for feedback and approval.
  • Attention to detail when preparing designs, specifications, and sample comments.
  • A growth mindset and interest in developing toward a Designer-level role.

Success in This Role

Success means creating thoughtful, brand-right designs; contributing to cohesive seasonal direction; supporting product development with care and accuracy; and building the skills to take on increasing design ownership.

Our Total Rewards package includes benefits you’ll love such as competitive compensation, paid time off, an employee assistance program, parental leave, paid volunteer hours, and amazing company discounts! In our US market, you can also expect health care benefits starting on day 1, 401(k), and tuition reimbursement benefits.

job.title: Senior Industrial Engineer
job.description:
Working at QVC Group means joining a live social shopping company with incredible teams, ambitious projects and amazing careers. QVC Group, Inc. is a Fortune 500 company with six leading retail brands - QVC®, HSN®, Ballard Designs®, Frontgate®, Garnet Hill® and Grandin Road.

Your Opportunity, Your Team

As a Senior Industrial Engineer, you will serve as a key technical leader within QVC’s largest and most advanced fulfillment center. This is a highly visible and impactful role and you will lead meaningful impact as both a thought leader and a savvy change agent.

As a technical expert, you will be responsible for optimizing processes, driving innovation, and transforming operations at the site and across QVC's supply chain network. You are part of the leadership team; you will be joining an impressive and highly talented team within engineering, operations, and technology.
You'll lead high-impact initiatives spanning labor optimization, automation deployment, process design, facility layout, capacity planning, and operational analytics. From implementing advanced material handling technologies to developing scalable solutions that support future growth, you'll help shape the next generation of fulfillment at QVC.
You'll have the opportunity to influence decisions at both the site and network level while partnering with cross-functional leaders to solve complex operational challenges. If you're energized by data-driven decision making, large-scale operations, and creating innovative solutions that deliver measurable business results, this is the role for you.


Where You'll Work

This role is onsite and will require you to work from our Bethlehem, PA Fulfillment Center daily. Relocation assistance is not available for this role.
Work visa sponsorship will not be provided for this particular position. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without QVC Group’s sponsorship.


What You'll Do

  • Serve as the senior engineering partner to site leadership, identifying, prioritizing, and executing opportunities that improve safety, quality, productivity, and cost performance.
  • Lead complex industrial engineering initiatives involving labor planning, process optimization, capacity analysis, workflow design, and facility layout improvements.
  • Develop data-driven solutions through statistical analysis, modeling, simulation, and operational research techniques to optimize labor utilization, throughput, and space utilization.
  • Partner with Operations, Automation, Technology, and Finance teams to evaluate, justify, and implement capital investments and automation technologies.
  • Design and refine fulfillment processes, material flows, and operating strategies that support both current operations and future business growth.
  • Influence network-wide standardization efforts by developing best practices, engineering methods, and scalable operational solutions across multiple fulfillment centers.
  • Identify technologies and build business cases supporting automation, equipment, labor, and process improvement initiatives.
  • Utilize warehouse management, labor management, and business intelligence systems to identify trends, uncover opportunities, and drive measurable performance improvements.
  • Lead implementation efforts for automation, process redesign, and operational transformation projects while ensuring successful adoption and sustainability.
  • Communicate engineering recommendations and project results to senior leaders through compelling analytics, visualizations, and operational insights.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Systems Engineering, Operations Research, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • 5+ years of experience in Industrial Engineering, Process Engineering, Operations Engineering, or Supply Chain Engineering within distribution, fulfillment, manufacturing, or logistics environments.
  • Demonstrated experience driving process improvement initiatives, workflow optimization, and operational efficiency.
  • Experience analyzing operational data and translating findings into actionable business recommendations.
  • Ability to collaborate with and influence cross-functional stakeholders and operational leadership.
  • Ability to travel 15–25% to support multi-site projects and network initiatives.

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading large-scale process improvement, facility design, automation, or operational transformation projects.
  • Strong understanding of fulfillment operations, labor planning, capacity modeling, and continuous improvement methodologies.
  • Experience with advanced analytics tools such as SQL, Power BI, Tableau, Python, R, or simulation software.
  • Familiarity with warehouse management and labor management systems, including Manhattan, Blue Yonder/JDA, Red Prairie, LaborPro, MOST, or similar platforms.
  • Experience supporting automation technologies such as conveyor systems, sortation, robotics, ASRS, goods-to-person systems, or autonomous mobile robots.
  • Lean Six Sigma or equivalent continuous improvement certification


Why Engineers Choose QVC

  • Lead projects that directly impact millions of customer orders annually.
  • Influence automation and fulfillment strategies across a multi-site distribution network.
  • Work on challenging problems involving labor optimization, automation, capacity planning, and operational analytics.
  • Join a team that invests in innovation, technical expertise, and continuous learning.

    #LI-MW1

job.title: 21GRAMS- Account Director
job.description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centred creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Job Summary:

Real Chemistry is looking for a Account Director to join our growing team!

21GRAMS, a Real Chemistry subsidiary is an advertising agency born to make healthcare more human. Not just in our work, but in the way we conduct business, approach client relationships, and treat each other. It’s a place where people subscribe to the adage, “Be good to each other, but hard on the work.” A place where people are not just in it for the paycheck, but to make a dent in the universe. Sound like you?

21GRAMS is in search of an Account Director. In addition to being the diplomatic face of the brand, both internally and externally, they accept the role of manager, liaison, thinker, and problem-solver. The Account Director leads broad-based, complex work-streams, is critical to the smooth running of Accounts, is a credible advisor and has very strong marketing communications experience.

The Account Director has mastered communications, project management, and has a strong point of view on the pharmaceutical side. This person should be able to confidently lead client projects and internal teams, encouraging smart, effective and integrated solutions, and always deliver results and client satisfaction. This position offers the opportunity to become an internal leader while developing strong relationships with clients.

This is a hybrid role, based in any of our US offices—including New York City, Boston, Chicago, Carmel, Lambertville or San Francisco—or remotely within the US, depending on team and business needs.

What you'll do:

  • Establish and maintain productive working relationships to drive agency success
  • Demonstrate understanding and knowledge of key messages/message platform, data, and promotional story for brand and competition
  • Develop and align on key agency/client documents that drive success (e.g., Project and Creative Briefs)
  • Read and interpret analytics around programming, tactics, and overall brand performance (e.g., metrics, KPIs, goals)
  • Negotiate, when necessary, to meet and deliver on client needs while managing agency resources and projects effectively
  • Continuously identify new opportunities to make recommendations based on customers, markets, and competitive environments, including corresponding rationales
  • Lead by example: exhibit professional conduct while providing ongoing leadership as a role model for the team
  • Demonstrate a solutions-oriented approach and collaborate across teams to drive success
  • Pursue business objectives, while developing talent and preserving the 21GRAMS culture
  • Supervise, train, and mentor team members to develop the skills and careers of others by providing guidance

This position is a perfect fit for you if:

  • Our Company values, Best Together, Impact Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always, and Accountability with an "I", genuinely resonate with how you work and lead.
  • You demonstrate the Real Chemistry Can mindset by approaching challenges with optimism, accountability, creativity, and a solutions-oriented attitude, always looking for ways to make a meaningful impact for our clients, colleagues, and communities.
  • You are adaptable, resilient, and comfortable adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment. As our business grows and changes, so do we.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful, with strong prioritization skills, intellectual curiosity, and a desire to leverage data to inform decisions and drive outcomes.
  • You are energized by innovation and the transformative potential of AI, actively exploring new technologies, identifying opportunities to work smarter, and championing practical, responsible AI adoption that drives meaningful business impact.

What you should have:

  • Bachelor’s degree in communications, marketing or a related field or equivalent
    experience is required
  • 5-7 years marketing experience, agency environment preferred.
  • Strong ability to multi-task and manage multiple projects with strong organizational
    skills.
  • Excellent business communication skills
  • Strong written and oral communication and presentations skills
  • Experience working on Therapeutic brands a plus
  • Previous experience managing junior staff preferred

Pay Range: $135,000.00-$155,000.00

The anticipated salary range for this position is listed above. Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on job-related, non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to experience, skills, qualifications, geographic location, and internal parity.

In addition to base salary, Real Chemistry offers a comprehensive benefits package and a variety of programs designed to support our employees' well-being, growth, and success.

Real Chemistry reserves the right to update compensation and benefits programs at any time.

 

Real Chemistry is proud to be Great Place to Work® certified; check out what our people shared about our culture and workplace on our Great Places to Work Profile here.

We believe we can do our best when feeling our best, which is why we’ve put together a benefits program designed to give you the support you and your family need at every stage of life. Real Chemistry offers a comprehensive benefit program and perks, tailored to your region. Globally, this includes offices in our key markets with free snacks to keep you running all day long, generous holiday and paid time off, options for private medical, dental, and vison plans, and support in saving for the future. Other perks include mental wellness coaching and support and access to more than 13,000 online classes with LinkedIn Learning.  Learn more about our great benefits and perks and search specific offerings in your region at: www.realchemistrybenefits.com.

At Real Chemistry, we believe we're at our best when we're connected. Our Real Hybrid and Regional Teams (Real HART) approach is designed to foster collaboration, learning, innovation, and meaningful relationships while providing flexibility where appropriate. Because our workforce spans multiple countries, regions, and client needs, work arrangements may vary by role and location. Some positions offer hybrid or remote flexibility, while others require regular in-office presence. For example, certain teams and regions, including some of our UK operations, have office-based requirements. Your recruiter will discuss the specific expectations for the role you're pursuing during the interview process and keep you informed throughout the hiring journey. For employees located within a one-hour commute of a Real Chemistry office, we require in-person attendance two days per week, either from a Real Chemistry office or when working onsite with clients. Employees in regions without a nearby office may work remotely and come together throughout the year for collaboration, culture-building, learning, and team connection opportunities. While these guidelines reflect our current workplace model, we understand that everyone’s circumstances are unique. If you require additional flexibility, we welcome an open conversation with your recruiter and our HR team to discuss your needs and determine what may be possible.

Real Chemistry is an Equal Opportunity employer. We continually strive to build and sustain an inclusive and equitable work environment where our employees feel empowered to leverage all they bring from their personal lived experience and professional expertise, to make our team the best in the industry. We encourage motivated and qualified applicants to apply without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, ethnic or national origin, age, physical or mental disability, genetic information, marital information, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local employment discrimination laws where Real Chemistry operates. Should you require accommodations throughout the interview process please let your recruiter know.

Do not share personal or financial information or make payments to any unverified sources claiming to be connected to Real Chemistry. We are working to stop these unauthorized activities and protect our community. Read more here.
