Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

2027 Weiss Center Ambassadors

*IMPORTANT NOTE*: This application is only for students who are currently enrolled at Syracuse University. If you are not a current Syracuse University student but are interested in applying for Real Chemistry's 2027 summer internship program, please keep an eye out for the job posting, which will go live in December 2026. We look forward to receiving and reviewing your applications then!

2027 Application Deadline: December 4, 2026

About the Weiss Center:
The Weiss Center is a student, faculty and industry-powered incubator that complements classroom curriculum through immersive, real-world application. By connecting classroom learning with the pace and expectations of the communications field, the Center helps students build the skills, perspective and confidence to enter the industry with a leg up.  

About the Role:
Each year, two Syracuse University students are selected to serve as Weiss Center Brand Ambassadors. The program offers a multifaceted experience that allows students to represent the Center on campus, contribute to its programming, and work alongside Real Chemistry experts and clients through a summer internship and other hands-on opportunities. Along the way, Ambassadors build the professional skills, experience and relationships needed to succeed in an evolving communications industry. 

Key Responsibilities: 

  • Summer Internship: Complete a full-time, paid, 10-week summer internship with Real Chemistry 
  • Promote Center programming: Work alongside Real Chemistry staff to drive awareness and provide on-the-ground support for the Center’s fall and spring programming, including the Jim Weiss Lecture Series, expert-led workshops, class visits and other hands-on learning experiences. 
  • Manage social and digital content: Manage Weiss Center social channels and collaborate with peers to develop blog posts and multimedia content. 
  • Build professional connections: Attend exclusive networking opportunities with Real Chemistry executives, staff and clients, as well as Syracuse faculty. 
  • Support a potential NYC benchmark trip: Help plan and attend a visit to the Real Chemistry office and other firms, pending schedule. 
  • SXSW trip: Participate in an all-expenses-paid trip to Austin, Texas to attend Real Chemistry’s events at the SXSW Interactive conference and support social media and digital content development

Candidate Profile:
We are seeking students who are enthusiastic about communications, curious about emerging industry trends and eager to help their peers connect with professional learning opportunities. 

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with an ability to adapt messages for student audiences.
  • Interest in social media, digital storytelling, AI & technology, analytics and/or the evolving communications industry.
  • Creativity, initiative and a collaborative approach to projects.
  • Organization and time-management skills, including the ability to follow through on agreed responsibilities.
  • Comfort engaging with peers and helping foster an inclusive campus community.
    • Other on-campus involvement is a plus 
  • Willingness to learn, receive feedback and contribute new ideas. 

Eligibility for the 2027 cohort: 

  • Qualified Syracuse University sophomores and juniors who will be on campus for the Spring and Fall 2027 semesters.
  • Minimum GPA: 3.0.
  • Selection as an Ambassador is contingent on being qualified for the summer 2027 internship program with Real Chemistry.
  • Particular interest in students with a background or interest in public relations, communications, advertising, marketing and/or information studies. 

2027 Ambassador Program Details:

  • Term: Proposed Spring and Fall 2027 on-campus service, plus a full-time, paid, 10-week summer internship. Note: Specific dates of summer 2027 internship program TBD (tentatively June-August 2027)
  • SXSW attendance: Ability to travel for all-expense paid trip to Austin, Texas (tentatively March 14-17), pending schedule
  • Time commitment: Full-time during the 10-week summer internship (40 hours/week). Anticipate dedicating approximately 2-5 hours per week during the spring and fall 2027 semesters to the Weiss Center Brand Ambassador Program 
  • Location: On-campus availability for the Spring and Fall 2027 semesters, with potential program travel for one to two all-expenses paid events, pending schedule.

job.title: Technical Project Manager
job.description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centred creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Real Chemistry Media

Real Chemistry Media is transforming how medical and healthcare marketers engage healthcare professionals (HCPs) and consumers through data, technology, and omnichannel innovation. Real Chemistry Media's product and technology teams sit at the heart of this meaningful work by building tools that increase impact. In support of our mission to help life-changing medicines and therapies reach their full market potential, we are building an enterprise platform for omnichannel orchestration in healthcare marketing.

Our technology enables healthcare organizations to design, deploy, and optimize HCP journeys through a scalable, self-service product that connects to their existing marketing and data systems. The platform is live with early users and on track with rapid growth milestones, so the decisions made over the next year will be influential in shaping the product's future.

We are hiring a Technical Project Manager to run delivery across the platform. Reporting to the VP, Product, you will be the person who knows where every workstream stands and what needs to happen for the team to be unblocked. This role covers software delivery for a product team, including sprints, releases, and dependencies across teams. The team is small and we're building a lot, so there are a lot of opportunities for ownership and influence.

What You'll Do:

  • Run the delivery plan for the platform, including coordinating milestones and the dependencies between teams.

  • Own Agile ceremonies and keep sprints, backlogs, and release schedules up to date and easy to access.

  • Coordinate delivery across internal teams and external partners, keeping commitments and handoffs clear on both sides.

  • Track blockers and scope changes early and drive decisions with the right people in the room.

  • Manage release coordination across environments and teams.

  • Give leadership and stakeholders a clear, current picture of status and timelines.

  • Build the delivery process as the team scales, knowing when to adjust so it can be followed by all.

 

This position is a perfect fit for you if:

  • You are adaptable, resilient, and OK with adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and focus as we grow. When things change, so do we. We’re always evolving.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful with strong prioritization skills and a desire to dive into the data.
  • You are highly organized self-starter, able to work independently and under tight deadlines.

What You Should Have:

  • 4+ years managing software delivery for product or engineering teams, in B2B or enterprise software.

  • Experience coordinating one program across multiple external vendors or partners and several internal teams.

  • Strong Agile fluency, including running ceremonies, managing backlogs, and adapting the process to the team rather than the reverse.

  • Enough technical depth to follow conversations about APIs, data pipelines, environments, and releases, and to ask the question that surfaces a risk.

  • Skill at turning an ambiguous set of workstreams into a plan people can act on.

  • Experience managing dependencies and timelines across teams you do not manage.

  • Fluency with delivery and tracking tools such as Jira, Asana, GitHub, or Linear, including keeping them accurate as a source of truth.

  • Ability to communicate status and tradeoffs clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Bonus points for martech, adtech, orchestration tooling, or healthcare experience.

 

Pay Range: $90,000-$100,000

This is the pay range the Company believes it will pay for this position at the time of this posting.  Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on job-related, non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, skills, certifications, and geographical location. The Company reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time

job.title: Assistant Manager, Preventative Care & Wellness
job.description:
WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR 

The Assistant Manager will play an integral role in supporting and executing MusiCares’ Preventive Health & Wellness program delivery. Guided by the Managing Director, you will support the growth and sustainability of comprehensive preventive care services addressing the needs of music pros across physical health, mental health and financial health. You will also be responsible for operational, client-focused and administrative team support.

 

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

Support the Managing Director to refine and expand MusiCares’ comprehensive suite of preventive care services based on data-driven needs.

  • Provide key support to ensure high-quality operations including provider engagement, efficient and timely connection with clients and fiscally responsible clinic management.
  • Coordinate ongoing communications between providers and the Preventive Health & Wellness team.
  • Monitor registrations, participation and provider feedback to support continuous improvement.
  • Leverage knowledge of the intersection of physical, financial and mental health to inform the development of a preventive care package that is adaptable based on the unique needs of the music industry.
  • Collaborate with the Networked Care team to ensure providers offer relevant and topical services based on Wellness in Music data and clinic/program feedback.

 

Develop and maintain systems for effective and sustainable referral pathways.

  • Support the Managing Director with development of pre-qualified systems and ongoing evaluations of the client engagement process.
  • Cross-collaborate across Health & Human Service teams, supporting development of referral pathways that improve client access to customized care services. Collaborate with care teams to ensure effectiveness of internal referrals in addition to cross-departmental work with Marketing and Development teams.
  • Serve as a liaison with Recording Academy staff and across affiliates to help promote services and devise protocol to educate broader industry partners about comprehensive preventive care packages.
  • Evaluate efficacy and ROI of services.
  • Create systems to track client feedback that aligns with organizational procedures and data collection methods.

 

Support program effectiveness through data and reporting and contribute to overall Health & Human Services team collaboration.

  • Support compiling, reviewing and reporting of team/program data for the Board of Directors, grant writing, and internal and external partners.
  • Develop strong knowledge of MusiCares’ data that drives programs and services.
  • Assist with staffing and event coordination for on/off site events, including travel as needed.
  • Participate in team meetings and professional development opportunities.

 

Operational support, including administrative coordination to manage team workflows.

  • Work across the Preventive Health & Wellness team through established processes.
  • Strengthen program operations through effective coordination with providers.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to enhance program/team efficiency and effectiveness.
  • Contribute to implementation of organizational strategic vision and plan.

 

 

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

 

  • Bachelor’s Degree preferred.
  • 3+ years of administrative experience, ideally with a non-profit organization with a similar programmatic focus.
  • A passion for MusiCares’ mission and an interest to professionally grow in this area.
  • Commitment to confidentiality and issues of privacy with the ability to maintain both.
  • Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Office Suite, Mailchimp, Eventbrite, Airtable, and/or comparable creative suite software.
  • Knowledge of database products and how to optimize data for reports and departmental analytics.
  • Strong communication skills and high emotional intelligence with the ability to interact with a variety of different constituents with a strong client service approach.
  • Ability to thrive in a collaborative and entrepreneurial business environment.
  • Ability to maintain composure during high-stress, complex situations, particularly when assisting with client care.
  • Ability to adapt well to change while remaining flexible and open minded.

 

 

PHYSICAL DEMANDS FOR CERTAN ROLES

 

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

 

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, and sit for long periods of time, and work at a computer for long periods of time.

 

The employee will be required to lift and/or move up to 60 pounds.

 

 

SALARY AND BENEFITS

 

The starting rate for this position is $31.60 to $34.38 per hour, benchmarked against industry standards. Rates for positions required to be in specific geographic locations reflect the corresponding labor market. 
 
The actual offer extended will depend on the candidate's experience, qualifications, and the role's requirements. Positions working 20+ hours per week also receive our comprehensive benefits package (with medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, generous paid time off, and more). Click here for an overview of our company benefits.


Explore our career opportunities to join a team that values creativity, innovation, and diversity. 

 

 

ABOUT THE RECORDING ACADEMY AND ITS AFFILIATES

 

RECORDING ACADEMY

The Recording Academy represents the voices of performers, songwriters, producers, engineers, and all music professionals. Dedicated to ensuring the recording arts remain a thriving part of our shared cultural heritage, the Academy honors music's history while investing in its future through the Grammy Museum, advocates on behalf of music creators, supports music people in times of need through MusiCares, and celebrates artistic excellence through the Grammy Awards—music's only peer-recognized accolade and highest achievement. As the world's leading society of music professionals, we work year-round to foster a more inspiring world for creators.

 

LATIN RECORDING ACADEMY

The Latin Recording Academy is an international, membership-based organization comprised of Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking recording artists, musicians, songwriters, producers and other creative and technical recording professionals. The organization is dedicated to improving the quality of life and cultural condition for Latin music and its makers. In addition to producing the Latin Grammy Awards to honor excellence in the recorded arts and sciences, The Latin Recording Academy provides educational and outreach programs for the Latin music community either directly or through its Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation.

 

LATIN GRAMMY CULTURAL FOUNDATION

The Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation is a charitable organization established by the Latin Recording Academy in 2014. The organization is dedicated to creating opportunities for the next generation of Latin music creators through scholarships, educational programs, grants, and access to creators and industry executives.

 

MUSICARES

A friend and ally of the music community, MusiCares was established by the Recording Academy to safeguard the health and well-being of all music people. A four-star charity and safety net in times of need, MusiCares offers confidential preventative, recovery, and emergency programs to address financial, medical, and personal health issues. Through the generosity of our donors and volunteer professionals, our dedicated team works across the country to ensure the music community has the resources and support it needs.

 

GRAMMY MUSEUM

The Grammy Museum is a nonprofit organization dedicated to celebrating and exploring music from yesterday and today to inspire the music of tomorrow through music preservation, education, exhibitions, and public programming and aims to create a world in which shared love of music sparks curiosity, creativity, and community. Programs include Grammy in the Schools education programs that are offered year-round for students, teachers, and schools throughout the United States. 

 

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

The Recording Academy, its affiliates, and the music industry have a strong culture of inclusion and respect for everyone. The Recording Academy makes intentional, courageous, and principled decisions for stronger business outcomes and ensures that all creators and professionals live and work in a fair and safe environment. It is the Recording Academy's policy to provide equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees. The Recording Academy does not discriminate on the basis of race (nor traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, religion (including religious dress and grooming), creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions), national origin, ancestry, age, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. The Recording Academy will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities unless doing so would result in an undue hardship to the Recording Academy. This policy governs all aspects of employment, including selection, job assignment, compensation, promotion, discipline, termination, access to benefits and training, recruitment, hiring, transfer, and social and recreational programs.

job.title: Education & Community Engagement Manager
job.description:
This is a hybrid position. Applicants must reside in the Tri-State Area to be on location for occasional programming and meetings.



WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 

The Education and Community Engagement Manager supports the development, implementation, and refinement of Grammy Museum Education & Community Engagement programs with a focus on educator-facing initiatives, curriculum development, professional development, student recruitment, and regional program support. Based in New York City, you will help expand the Museum’s East Coast education presence and support programs primarily East of the Mississippi River including Grammy in the Schools, professional development sessions, and seasonal Grammy Camp support.

 

You will provide curriculum expertise across programs to ensure consistency, continuity, and alignment with the Museum’s educational goals. You will build and maintain relationships with K-12 teachers, school partners, districts, and arts education organizations to support educator engagement, student recruitment, and professional development. You will also support application and recruitment processes for student and educator programs, ensuring outreach, application review, and participant communication reflect program goals and expand access for students and teachers.

 

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 

Professional Development & Educator Engagement

  • Lead planning, development, and facilitation of educator professional development programs, including virtual, in-person, district-based, and conference-based sessions.
  • Build and maintain relationships with K–12 teachers, school districts, arts coordinators, and education partners to support professional development, program participation, student recruitment, and ongoing educator engagement.
  • Identify and cultivate professional development opportunities with schools, districts, conferences, and partner organizations.
  • Collect and synthesize educator feedback to inform future professional development offerings, curriculum tools, and program improvements.

 

Program Alignment

  • Provide curriculum expertise across Education programs to ensure consistency, continuity, and alignment with departmental learning goals, while remaining adaptable to different student, teacher, and community contexts.
  • Develop and refine learning objectives, instructional materials, rubrics, classroom extensions, and develop and maintain program manuals.
  • Support alignment of programs with music education, arts education, career and technical education, college/career readiness, and workforce development frameworks where appropriate.
  • Collaborate with internal team members to connect curriculum and instructional design across Grammy Camp, Grammy in the Schools, Industry Sessions, professional development, and other education initiatives.

 

Recruitment, Applications & Program Process Support

  • Support recruitment for student and educator programs including outreach to schools, teachers, districts, community partners, and professional networks, building an application pipeline.
  • Support application and review processes for selected programs, including outreach, applicant communication, submission tracking, rubric development, review coordination, and documentation.
  • Help ensure recruitment and application processes are accessible, organized, and aligned with program goals, student readiness, educator needs, and equity of access.
  • Collaborate with the Coordinator and program leads to maintain accurate applicant records, support review timelines, and communicate next steps to applicants and participants.

 

Grammy in the Schools Support

  • Support planning and implementation of Grammy in the Schools programs, particularly those based on the East Coast and primarily East of the Mississippi River.
  • Assist with educator and school partner communication, program planning, instructional materials, and on-site implementation.
  • Collaborate with team members to ensure Grammy in the Schools programming is educationally consistent, student-centered, and aligned with the Museum’s broader learning goals.
  • Support development of program resources that help students connect music learning to industry pathways, creative careers, and transferable skills.

 

Grammy Camp Support

  • Support Grammy Camp planning and implementation including curriculum alignment, faculty support, student learning outcomes, and summer travel for on-site program delivery.
  • Support faculty onboarding, curriculum implementation, instructional planning, and integration of curriculum benchmarks across the camp model.
  • Help ensure consistency across camp cities while supporting local adaptation based on partners, faculty, students, and facilities.

 

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with the Vice President, Senior Director, Senior Manager, and Coordinator to support program strategy, planning, implementation, and evaluation.
  • Collaborate with Marketing, Communications, Advancement, Production, Guest Services, and Finance as needed.
  • Support public programs in New York as needed.
  • Represent the Education & Community Engagement team in meetings with schools, districts, partners, artists, faculty, and external stakeholders.
  • Travel for programs, conferences, partner meetings, Grammy Camp, Grammy in the Schools and other education initiatives as needed.
  SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

 

  • Bachelor’s degree required. Master’s degree preferred in music education, arts education, curriculum and instruction, education, music industry, or a related field.
  • 3-5+ years of experience in music education, arts education, curriculum development, professional development, or youth program implementation.
  • Experience designing or facilitating professional development for educators preferred.
  • Strong understanding of secondary music education, music technology, ensemble instruction, career-connected learning, and/or music industry pathways.
  • Experience developing curriculum, lesson plans, educator resources, rubrics, or instructional materials.
  • Experience supporting student or educator recruitment and application review processes preferred.
  • Ability to build relationships and collaborate with educators, students, artists, K-12 schools, districts, partners, and internal teams.
  • Strong writing, facilitation, and presentation skills.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple programs and timelines.
  • Willingness and ability to travel including significant summer travel to support Grammy Camp.

 

 

PHYSICAL DEMANDS FOR CERTAIN ROLES

 

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

job.title: Intern, Advocacy & Public Policy
job.description:
INTERNSHIP DETAILS 

 

SPRING INTERNSHIP 

APPLICATION DEADLINE FOR STUDENTS: 11/20/2026 

SPRING INTERNSHIP PROGRAM DATES: 1/11/2027 – 4/16/2027  

*The Advocacy & Public Policy Intern position pays county/state minimum wage rates, based on work location. 



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR 

 

The Recording Academy Advocacy & Public Policy team is seeking a “rock star” student for a spring 2027 Internship with our team. 


Celebrating music through the Grammy® Awards, The Recording Academy continues its legacy as the premier national organization for honoring achievements in the recording arts and supporting the music community. As a membership organization, we represent the most talented music professionals in the world. Our members include recording artists, producers, engineers, attorneys, music supervisors, composers/arrangers, managers, agents, social media and record label executives and many others. 


Our paid Internship Program offers a unique opportunity for full-time college students (juniors or seniors) to gain on-site training in office administration, advocacy, and public policy, in exchange for college credit. Candidates should be energetic, hard-working and have aspirations of a career in the music industry. 



WHAT YOU'LL DO


  • Internship duration is for a semester (12 weeks or equivalent).
  • Hours are part-time (20-24 hours a week).
  • Intern will work both remotely and in the office during regular business hours. 
  • Intern will require personal laptop.
  • Projects will include assisting with the Academy’s grassroots advocacy initiatives, outreach to congressional offices, legislative research, database management, and administrative office support.



SKILLS & EXPERIENCE


  • Students must be currently enrolled in a College/University for an Undergraduate or Graduate program.
  • One year of course work towards degree in related field is preferred.
  • Letter from school stating that intern will receive college credit for the Recording Academy internship program.
  • Display an interest in music and/or government and advocacy work.
  • Possess strong verbal, written and analytical skills.
  • Exhibit proficient computer skills and social media proficiency.
  • Be a sophomore, junior, senior or graduate student.

job.title: Operations Coordinator, Nashville Chapter
job.description:
This is a hybrid position requiring a minimum of three days per week in the Nashville, TN office.

 

 

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 

The Recording Academy’s mission is to recognize musical excellence, advocate for the well-being of music makers and ensure music remains an indelible part of our culture. The Academy is a professional membership organization of musicians, producers, engineers, and recording professionals that is dedicated to improving the cultural condition and quality of life for music and its makers.

 

We’re looking for a highly motivated, idea-generating self-starter who will coordinate office operations, high-quality initiatives, programs, and content with professionalism for the Nashville Chapter. As part of the Nashville Chapter team, you will be responsible for developing and managing programs to ensure member retention, working with local outreach committees, and building coalitions in our Chapter city as well as the surrounding Chapter region. You will also be responsible for the day-to-day logistics of the Nashville Chapter office. You are a team player ready to roll up your sleeves with impeccable follow-through.

 

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 

Work with the Senior Executive Director to coordinate operations for the Nashville Chapter office:

  • Liaison with the property manager and the Recording Academy’s Facilities Operations department.
  • Manage the schedule for shared meeting rooms including communicating with various stakeholders.
  • Liaison with service vendors including researching best companies, scheduling services, discussing prices, and managing invoicing.
  • Know the building systems including security, internet, fire safety, etc.
  • Coordinate in-office artist visits with Academy staff.
  • Handle all office supplies and needs including general office supplies, postage, kitchen supplies, mail, UPS, FedEx, etc.

 

Facilitate the Chapter’s Grammy U Program, interns, and temps:

  • Recruit and facilitate interviews and the hiring process for Chapter Grammy U Reps.
  • In coordination with the Grammy U Program lead, work with the Grammy U Rep in training on programming, membership presentations and outreach, program Invitations and RSVP process, and copy writing.
  • In coordination with the Chapter Manager, structure a regular meeting schedule to monitor university and membership outreach and set yearly goals for Grammy U membership growth.
  • Facilitate the recruitment, interview, and hiring process for temps and interns.

 

Serve as the staff liaison for a variety of Chapter committees:

  • Work with committee chairs to schedule meetings and minutes.
  • Implement follow-up materials including collaborating with the Chapter Manager on related program initiatives.

 

Execute the Chapter’s social media marketing initiatives and strategy:

  • Work closely with the Chapter Manager on each program’s social media needs, creating the social plan strategy in partnership with the Academy’s social media team and set timeline.
  • Manage the day-to-day administration of the Chapter’s Facebook Group and work to grow followers including best practices to utilize the platform.
  • Manage Chapter’s social media calendar.

 

Legal Agreements:

  • Facilitate all vendor and performance agreements and releases pertaining to Chapter programs and initiatives.
  • Work closely with the Academy’s Legal Affairs and Executive Director department on agreements.
  • Ensure timely delivery and receipt of signatures from vendors and program participants.

 

Programming:

  • Attend all Chapter programs and Board meetings.
  • Work closely with the Academy’s Communications department to book and manage Getty photographers and security guards as it pertains to Chapter programs.
  • Ensure contracts for all security and catering/bartender requests are reviewed with the Academy’s Legal Affairs Department, signed promptly, and paid according to each vendor’s desired schedule, and event confirmation details are appropriately relayed ahead of each event.
  • Coordinate with the Chapter Manager in liaising with the social media and editorial teams, coordinating support and activations for Chapter events.
  • Track RSVPs and coordinate check-in/registration at programs.
  • Other programming duties as needed.

 

 

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

 

  • Bachelor’s Degree required, preferably in music business or related.
  • 3+ years of executive level administration experience in the music industry.
  • Proficiency in Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and various Microsoft applications.
  • Strong marketing skills through social media.
  • Demonstrated ability to maintain composure under pressure and make decisions/problem solve in high-stress situations.
  • Outstanding organizational, time management, and multitasking skills.
  • Adaptability to change and openness to innovative ideas.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills.
  • Proven ability to foster teamwork and contribute positively to team dynamics.
  • Must be proactive with the ability to manage upwards.
  • Ability to uphold the highest levels of integrity and ethics.

 

 

PHYSICAL DEMANDS FOR CERTAN ROLES

 

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

 

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, and sit for long periods of time, and work at a computer for long periods of time.

 

The employee will be required to lift and/or move up to 60 pounds.

 

 

SALARY AND BENEFITS

 

The starting rate for this position is $21.70 to $23.50 per hour, benchmarked against industry standards. Rates for positions required to be in specific geographic locations reflect the corresponding labor market. 
 
The actual offer extended will depend on the candidate's experience, qualifications, and the role's requirements. Positions working 20+ hours per week also receive our comprehensive benefits package (with medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, generous paid time off, and more). Click here for an overview of our company benefits.


Explore our career opportunities to join a team that values creativity, innovation, and diversity. 

 

 

ABOUT THE RECORDING ACADEMY AND ITS AFFILIATES

 

RECORDING ACADEMY

The Recording Academy represents the voices of performers, songwriters, producers, engineers, and all music professionals. Dedicated to ensuring the recording arts remain a thriving part of our shared cultural heritage, the Academy honors music's history while investing in its future through the Grammy Museum, advocates on behalf of music creators, supports music people in times of need through MusiCares, and celebrates artistic excellence through the Grammy Awards—music's only peer-recognized accolade and highest achievement. As the world's leading society of music professionals, we work year-round to foster a more inspiring world for creators.

 

LATIN RECORDING ACADEMY

The Latin Recording Academy is an international, membership-based organization comprised of Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking recording artists, musicians, songwriters, producers and other creative and technical recording professionals. The organization is dedicated to improving the quality of life and cultural condition for Latin music and its makers. In addition to producing the Latin Grammy Awards to honor excellence in the recorded arts and sciences, The Latin Recording Academy provides educational and outreach programs for the Latin music community either directly or through its Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation.

 

LATIN GRAMMY CULTURAL FOUNDATION

The Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation is a charitable organization established by the Latin Recording Academy in 2014. The organization is dedicated to creating opportunities for the next generation of Latin music creators through scholarships, educational programs, grants, and access to creators and industry executives.

 

MUSICARES

A friend and ally of the music community, MusiCares was established by the Recording Academy to safeguard the health and well-being of all music people. A four-star charity and safety net in times of need, MusiCares offers confidential preventative, recovery, and emergency programs to address financial, medical, and personal health issues. Through the generosity of our donors and volunteer professionals, our dedicated team works across the country to ensure the music community has the resources and support it needs.

 

GRAMMY MUSEUM

The Grammy Museum is a nonprofit organization dedicated to celebrating and exploring music from yesterday and today to inspire the music of tomorrow through music preservation, education, exhibitions, and public programming and aims to create a world in which shared love of music sparks curiosity, creativity, and community. Programs include Grammy in the Schools education programs that are offered year-round for students, teachers, and schools throughout the United States. 

 

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

The Recording Academy, its affiliates, and the music industry have a strong culture of inclusion and respect for everyone. The Recording Academy makes intentional, courageous, and principled decisions for stronger business outcomes and ensures that all creators and professionals live and work in a fair and safe environment. It is the Recording Academy's policy to provide equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees. The Recording Academy does not discriminate on the basis of race (nor traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, religion (including religious dress and grooming), creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions), national origin, ancestry, age, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. job.title: Coordinator, Operations
job.description:
About The Company Reservoir is an independent music company based in New York City and with offices in Los Angeles, Nashville, Toronto, London, Abu Dhabi, and Mumbai. Reservoir is the first female-founded and led publicly traded independent music company in the U.S. Founded as a family-owned music publisher in 2007, Reservoir has grown to represent over 150,000 copyrights and 36,000 master recordings with titles dating as far back as 1900 and hundreds of #1 releases worldwide. Reservoir frequently holds a Top 10 U.S. Market Share according to Billboard’s Publishers Quarterly, was twice named Publisher of the Year by Music Business Worldwide’s The A&R Awards and won Independent Publisher of the Year at the 2020 and 2022 Music Week Awards. Reservoir also represents a multitude of recorded music through Chrysalis Records, Tommy Boy Records, and Philly Groove Records and manages artists through its ventures with Blue Raincoat Music and Big Life Management. The Position The Coordinator, Operations supports the day-to-day operations of Reservoir’s New York office while providing executive support to the CEO, COO, and CFO and assisting the Chief of Staff with research, strategic initiatives, and special projects. This hands-on, entry-level position offers a unique opportunity to gain exposure to various aspects of the music business, contribute to company-wide initiatives, and build a strong foundation for career growth within the industry. The ideal candidate is highly organized, resourceful and proactive, with sound judgment and a genuine interest in music. This is an in-office role in New York, reporting to the Chief of Staff.

Responsibilities

include, but are not limited to: Running day-to-day operations of the New York office, making sure workspaces, conference rooms, the kitchen and common areas are organized, stocked and ready for the team and guests. Greeting and welcoming visitors, guests, artists and songwriters, and serve as the team's first point of contact for office needs. Managing office purchasing, vendors, inventory, mail, deliveries, catering and office events. Providing executive support to the CEO, COO and CFO, including calendars, scheduling, travel and expense reports. Partnering with IT so the office's facilities and technology work well, including setup for new hires, meeting rooms and visitors. Supporting the Chief of Staff with decks and materials for leadership and the Company. Conducting research on potential business opportunities, market developments and competitive activity. Analyzing music industry data using platforms such as Chartmetric, Luminate and Billboard to track artist performance, streaming trends, audience growth and emerging opportunities, and summarize key insights for the team and leadership. Keeping trackers, documentation and internal updates organized and current. Scouting new artists, songwriters and producers across DSPs, socials, live shows, playlists. Working with team to identify catalog songs with momentum, and help build sample packs and a pitch-ready library. Handling ticket purchases for shows and events for the New York office. Supporting teams in the New York office with ad hoc tasks and requests.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Music Business, Music Industry, Music Management, or a related field, or equivalent relevant

experience

in the music industry. 0–2 years of professional experience, including internships, with prior exposure to the music industry preferred. Exceptionally organized and detail-oriented, able to juggle competing priorities and follow through. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly, professionally, and effectively across all levels of the organization. Eager to learn, takes initiative, and comfortable owning work from start to finish. Discreet with confidential information, with sound judgment and a professional approach. Genuine interest in music; familiarity with DSPs is a plus. Proficient in Microsoft Office, Slack and Zoom.

Experience

using AI tools to improve productivity, research, and workflows. Equal Employment Opportunity Reservoir is an

equal opportunity employer

committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to age, race, ethnicity, color, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, marital status, military status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We believe that embracing diversity strengthens our culture, drives innovation, and contributes to our continued success. If you require assistance or an accommodation in completing any aspect of the application process, please contact the Reservoir Recruiting team at: jobs@reservoir-media.com.

Senior Project Manager – Media Technology

 

Who we're looking for: 

 

We are looking for a strong leader to join the Broadcast Engineering team within Rogers as a Sr. Project Manager.  In this role, you will be responsible for delivering project management excellence on key strategic initiatives through disciplined execution. The breadth and complexity of these projects cannot be understated. The successful candidate should be able to oversee the impacts, interdependencies and timelines between functional teams and work to ensure project initiatives meet the goals and objectives set forth by the senior and executive leadership teams.

 

What you'll do: 

  • Manage infrastructure-related deployments, upgrades, and strategic technology initiatives from planning through execution.
  • Manage project funding, including Capital Authorization (CA) requests, budget development, forecasting, financial tracking, and variance reporting.

  • Coordinate cross-functional teams to ensure deliverables are completed on time, dependencies are managed, and project momentum is maintained.
  • Conduct analysis and providing recommendations to support operational, financial, and technology decisions.
  • Ensure alignment between project delivery, financial objectives, strategic priorities, and operational goals.
  • Drive accountability across project teams by tracking commitments, following up on actions, removing roadblocks, and ensuring successful execution of key initiatives.

 

What you bring:

job.description:

Are you looking for an opportunity to gain journalistic experience in both the newsroom and the field? Do you want to pitch stories, deliver newscasts, and connect with your local community? Apply to be an Anchor/Multimedia Journalist (MMJ) at Spectrum News NECN.

 

Spectrum News NECN covers MA, NH, ME, VT, RI, and CT. We use innovative journalistic approaches, backed by comprehensive research, to engage and inform viewers on the most essential news, issues, and events taking place in their communities. 

 

Beyond TV news distribution, our newsrooms publish via the Spectrum News app and connected television. We’re committed to providing viewers with 24-hour news—no matter how, when, and where they want it. Check out all the ways we share news on the Spectrum News Mobile App. 


As an Anchor/MMJ, you’ll build a vital connection between a story and your audience. From pitching stories to delivering engaging newscasts, your responsibilities will encompass all aspects of reporting and anchoring. You’ll be part of a collaborative team that creates compelling, timely, accurate, character-driven content to connect with viewers across traditional and digital platforms.

 

WHAT OUR ANCHOR/MULTIMEDIA JOURNALISTS ENJOY MOST

  • Striking a balance between reporting and anchoring
  • Going into the field to discover original stories and delivering news in-studio

  • Working across platforms including TV news, connected television, and digital news

 

As a part of Spectrum News NECN, you’re creative, highly technical, and ready to bring your community’s stories to life in our newsroom. You value accuracy and want to leverage your curiosity and storytelling abilities to share inspiring news across multiple platforms. job.title: Assistant Producer, Brand & Content
job.description:
At Qualtrics, we create software the world’s best brands use to deliver exceptional frontline experiences, build high-performing teams, and design products people love. But we are more than a platform—we are the creators and stewards of the Experience Management category serving over 18K clients globally. Building a category takes grit, determination, and a disdain for convention—but most of all it requires close-knit, high-functioning teams with an unwavering dedication to serving our customers. 

When you join one of our teams, you’ll be part of a nimble group that’s empowered to set aggressive goals and move fast to achieve them. Strategic risks are encouraged and complex problems are solved together, by passing the mic and iterating until the best solution comes to light. You won’t have to look to find growth opportunities—ready or not, they’ll find you. From retail to government to healthcare, we’re on a mission to bring humanity, connection, and empathy back to business. Join over 5,000 people across the globe who think that’s work worth doing.

Assistant Producer, Brand & Content


Why We Have This Role

At Qualtrics, great stories help people connect with our brand, our tech, and the humans behind our customer experiences. We’re looking for an Assistant Producer who has natural storytelling instincts, loves digging into research, and wants to learn the ins and outs of brand producing from the ground up.
If you just wrapped up a degree in Broadcast, Journalism, or Media and want to put your reporting and writing chops to work in a fast-paced creative environment, this role is built for you. Instead of spending your day behind a camera lens or buried inside an editing timeline, you’ll focus on the heart of the narrative: researching guests, setting up shoots, drafting interview questions that get past corporate speak, and serving as a key right hand to our Brand and Content leadership.

How You’ll Find Success

  • A Reporter’s Instinct for a Good Story: You just know when an angle works. You can listen to someone talk for 10 minutes, cut through the fluff, and spot the compelling human hook that makes people stop scrolling and pay attention.
  • Curiosity & Interview Smarts: You love digging into a topic, learning what makes a subject tick, and writing fresh, conversational interview questions that draw out memorable, authentic soundbites.
  • Poise Around Team Leaders: You’re confident jumping into conversations, sharing your point of view, and working side-by-side with senior leaders on the Brand & Content team. You stay one step ahead, anticipating what needs to get done next.
  • Video Production Fluency: You speak the language of video. While you won't be trapped behind a camera or an edit bay, you already understand how shoots run from pre-pro to post, making it easy for you to coordinate with videographers, freelance crews, and editors.
  • Scrappy, Get-It-Done Energy: Production moves fast and plans change. You stay organized, keep your cool when schedules shift, and take pride in coordinating shoot logistics, prepping guests, and keeping projects on track.

How You’ll Grow

  • Learn Directly from Creative Leaders: Work hand-in-hand every day with senior directors and strategists, getting a front-row seat to how enterprise creative campaigns and brand strategies are built.
  • Master High-Stakes Storytelling: Build your portfolio by turning complex business and human topics into engaging video packages, mini-docs, and social-first narratives.
  • On-Camera & Hosting Opportunities: If you have an interest or background in front of the lens, we love putting talented storytellers on camera for social segments, event coverage, and internal features.
  • Cross-Media Versatility: Sharpen your voice across video, audio, social media hooks, and written editorial content.

Things You’ll Do

  • Set Up & Build Interviews: Research internal leaders, customers, and industry experts; coordinate interview schedules and logistics; and write tailored interview guides designed to get authentic, unscripted answers.
  • Own Pre-Interview Prep: Run pre-interviews to vet storylines, brief guests so they feel comfortable before the cameras roll, and flag key talking points for the production team.
  • Support Brand & Content Leadership: Act as a central point person for our creative leaders by drafting briefs, prepping meeting decks, keeping track of action items, and ensuring team projects cross the finish line.
  • Write Supporting Creative Copy: Draft video outlines, social copy teasers, video hooks, and promotional blurbs that support our multimedia campaigns.
  • Coordinate On-Set Logistics: Keep shoot days running smoothly by building call sheets, greeting and prepping talent, managing schedules, and keeping external videographers looped in on creative goals.
  • Help Bridge Pre-Production to Post: Review raw interview footage, pull the best quotes and soundbites, and pass time-coded notes to video editors to help shape the final cut.

What We’re Looking For On Your Resume

  • 1-3+ years of experience in Broadcasting, Videography, or another relevant field.
  • Background in Storytelling: A degree in Journalism, Broadcast Media, Communications, or a related field (or equivalent hands-on student media/internship experience).
  • Interview & Writing Samples: A portfolio or reel featuring work you’ve produced, reported, or written—such as student broadcast packages, interview transcripts/articles, video scripts, or multimedia stories.
  • Organizational Hustle: Experience coordinating shoots, managing production schedules, or juggling multiple creative deadlines in a newsroom, studio, agency, or internship environment.
  • Awesome Bonuses:
    • On-Camera Experience: Experience reporting for a campus news station, hosting a podcast, or presenting on social channels.
    • Basic Editing Literacy: Familiarity with tools like Adobe Premiere Pro, Descript, or CapCut for pulling selects or rough assemblies.

What You Should Know About This Team

  • High-energy, collaborative team culture that values curiosity, fresh ideas, and taking initiative.
  • Fast feedback loops with real opportunities to pitch ideas and see them produced.
  • Direct mentorship from experienced brand storytellers and creative leaders.
  • A hybrid setup that blends in-person creative collaboration with remote flexibility.

Perks and Benefits Highlights

  • Performance-based incentive structure and 100% merit-based promotions driven by impact rather than tenure.
  • Continuous professional growth opportunities and direct creative mentorship.

  • On-site amenities including catered lunches, quarterly team socials, seasonal parties, and Qualtrics swag.
The Qualtrics Hybrid Work Model: Our hybrid work model is elegantly simple: we all gather in the office three days a week; Mondays and Thursdays, plus one day selected by your organizational leader. These purposeful in-person days in thoughtfully designed offices help us do our best work and harness the power of collaboration and innovation. For the rest of the week, work where you want, owning the integration of work and life. #hybrid Qualtrics is an equal opportunity employer meaning that all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected characteristic. Applicants in the United States of America have rights under Federal Employment Laws:Family & Medical Leave Act, Equal Opportunity Employment, Employee Polygraph Protection Act Qualtrics is committed to the inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, Qualtrics will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please let your Qualtrics contact/recruiter know. Not finding a role that’s the right fit for now? Qualtrics Insiders is the one-stop shop for all things Qualtrics Life. Sign up for exclusive access to content created with you in mind and get the scoop on what we have going on at Qualtrics - upcoming events, behind the scenes stories from the team, interview tips, hot jobs, and more. No spam - we promise! You'll hear from us two times a month max with fresh, totally tailored info - so be sure to stay connected as you explore your best role and company fit.

job.title: Associate Producer - Spectrum News 13
job.description:
This role requires the ability to work lawfully in the U.S. without employment-based immigration sponsorship, now or in the future.

Do you have an eye for detail? Are you looking to kickstart your journalism career in a 24/7 newsroom? Apply to be an Associate Producer at Spectrum News.

  

Part of Charter Communications, Spectrum News is made up of over 30 hyper-local news and regional sports networks that are constantly expanding and dedicated to producing original, unbiased, and high-quality content. We use innovative journalistic approaches, backed by comprehensive research, to engage and inform viewers on the most essential news, issues, and events taking place in their communities. 

 

Beyond TV news distribution, our newsrooms publish via the Spectrum News app and connected television. We’re committed to providing viewers with 24-hour news—no matter how, when and where they want it. Check out all the ways we share news on the Spectrum News Mobile App.


BE PART OF THE CONNECTION

As an Associate Producer, you will collaborate with producers in the newsroom to craft compelling stories. Your creativity and upbeat attitude will be essential as you tackle sensitive topics and tell character-driven stories. Alongside the team, you’ll represent what’s happening in your community and connect audiences with the stories that matter.

 

WHAT OUR ASSOCIATE PRODUCERS ENJOY MOST

  • Transforming stories from a simple pitch into a hit that inspires and delights viewers
  • Working with colleagues in a collaborative environment
  • Connecting with neighbors as you dig into the issues that matter to your local community
  • Telling stories across platforms including TV, connected television, and digital

 

As a part of Spectrum News, you’re creative, highly technical, and ready to bring your community’s stories to life in our newsroom. You value accuracy and want to leverage your curiosity and storytelling abilities to share inspiring news across multiple platforms. Each day is fast paced in a constantly evolving work environment with new stories to tell and perspectives to uncover. If you’re a nimble, passionate team player, you’ll find a home on our team.


WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO SPECTRUM NEWS

Required Qualifications

  • Experience: Television news - 0-2 years
  • Education: High school diploma
  • Technical Skills: Knowledge of current events, social media, and industry trends
  • Skills: Ability to collaborate, news writing skills, and attention to detail
  • Travel Ability: Must be open to travel to discover the important stories in your neighborhood and willing to interact with the community
  • Schedule: Ability to work different shifts and be flexible with schedule changes

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Broadcast Journalism or related field, comparable television work experience preferred
  • Working knowledge of general office computer software, newsroom software and basic non-linear editing systems
  • May be required to lift up to five pounds

 

Working Conditions

  • Works primarily inside a climate-controlled environment throughout the year but might be assigned field duties on occasion
  • Semi-noisy newsroom setting

job.description:
Dakota News Live | Bismarck, North Dakota

Dakota News Live, the CBS affiliate in Bismarck, North Dakota, is looking for a talented and motivated Evening News Anchor/Producer to join our growing newsroom.


Essential Functions


As an Evening News Anchor/Producer, you'll play a key role in producing and anchoring our local newscasts. You'll help shape our daily coverage, develop compelling story ideas, write and produce engaging newscasts, and deliver important local news to viewers across Western North Dakota. You'll also have opportunities to contribute reporting, cover major events and breaking news. Plus contribute to our digital platforms, and work with our ABC station in Bismarck.

We're looking for someone with a strong on-air presence, excellent writing skills, sound news judgment and the ability to produce compelling, informative newscasts. The ideal candidate is organized, creative, comfortable making decisions in a fast-paced newsroom and passionate about delivering meaningful local journalism. A journalism, communications or related degree is preferred, but demonstrated ability and experience are also valued.


Why Dakota News Live?


Our newsroom is growing, creating opportunities for you to grow with us. We believe in developing our people, promoting from within and giving journalists the opportunity to expand their skills and advance their careers.


This is an exciting opportunity to join a team committed to providing local news, weather and sports to Western North Dakota Applicants must be legally eligible to work in the United States and able to work for Dakota News Live without employment restrictions that would prevent them from accepting this position.


Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Journalism, Communications, or a related field.
  • Previous experience as a news anchor or broadcast reporter is strongly preferred.
  • Active social media presence - will promote and support brand awareness on multiple social media platforms.
  • Proven media personality, with the ability to remain comfortable and professional while on camera.
  • General knowledge of local, national, and international affairs.
  • Passion for breaking news and current events.
  • Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to improvise on camera when necessary.
  • Ability to work under pressure with strict deadlines.
  • Ethical and professional research, writing and reporting skills.
  • Team player who works well both collaboratively and independently.


Expected compensation for this role is between $50,000 – $60,000, based on qualifications and experience.


ABOUT THE COMPANY

Forum Communications Company is a family-owned media and technology leader with more than a century of delivering trusted, quality journalism and innovative business solutions. Storytelling is at the heart of who we are, but today, we’re so much more than a newspaper. As one of the Upper Midwest’s leading media organizations, we’re driving the future across print and digital news, sports streaming, technology, broadcasting, commercial printing, and full-service agency advertising.

job.title: MMJ & Anchor
job.description:
This role is open to journalists and nontraditional candidates with strong content creation and on-camera experience. We welcome creative storytellers from all backgrounds who can craft compelling content across broadcast, digital, and social platforms. If you can tell a great story, shoot and edit strong video, and engage audiences online and on-air, we’d love to see your work.

At 910 Media Group, we’re redefining what local journalism looks like in today’s media landscape. We’ve evolved into a multi-platform media company delivering news, weather, sports, lifestyle, and community-driven content where audiences actually are. If you’re a storyteller who thrives at the intersection of journalism and content creation, this is the place to grow.

The Role

We’re looking for a Multi-Media Journalist / Anchor who is curious, creative, and deeply connected to the communities we serve.

You’ll pitch, shoot, write, edit, and present stories that spark conversation, inform viewers, and engage audiences on broadcast, digital, and social platforms.

What You’ll Do

  • Research, pitch, and produce compelling stories for broadcast, digital, and social platforms
  • Shoot, write, and edit your own content with a strong visual and storytelling style
  • Anchor newscasts and report live from the field as assigned
  • Create engaging digital-first and social content that complements on-air reporting
  • Exercise strong news judgment while maintaining the highest journalism ethics
  • Build trusted relationships and sources within the communities we serve
  • Interact with viewers and users on social media to extend story reach and engagement
  • Collaborate with producers, editors, and newsroom leadership
  • Contribute ideas for innovative formats, storytelling approaches, and audience growth

What You Bring

  • Background in journalism, digital media, content creation, communications, or a related field (traditional newsroom experience not required)
  • Strong storytelling skills across video, written, and on-camera formats
  • Experience creating content for social and digital platforms (YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, etc.) is a plus
  • Solid writing skills with an understanding of storytelling fundamentals and accuracy
  • Experience or interest in shooting and editing video (Adobe Premiere preferred)
  • Comfortable working independently in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment
  • Creative, flexible thinker who enjoys experimenting with new formats and platforms
  • Strong organizational, communication, and time-management skills
  • Attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy and fairness
  • Knowledge of camera operation and basic production techniques
  • Positive, collaborative attitude and willingness to learn
  • Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record

Why You’ll Love Working Here

  • Competitive compensation
  • Comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, and vision
  • Company-paid life insurance, short-term, and long-term disability
  • 401(k) with company match
  • 17 days PTO plus paid sick time
  • Clothing and grooming allowances
  • Relocation assistance available
  • Ongoing opportunities for professional development and career growth

Our Culture

  • Innovative: We embrace change and encourage new ideas
  • Engaging: We celebrate wins—big and small—together
  • Collaborative: Teamwork drives our success across departments
  • Inclusive: Diverse perspectives make our journalism stronger

Location

This position is based in Traverse City, Michigan, in the heart of Northern Michigan. From freshwater shorelines and sand dunes to miles of trails and four distinct seasons, it’s an incredible place to live, work, and explore year-round.

Ready to Tell Stories That Matter?

If you’re excited to shape the future of local journalism and create content that truly connects with audiences, apply today.

job.title: News/Sports Reporter
job.description:
WDAY, the number #1 station located in the Fargo, ND-Moorhead, MN metro area, broadcasts across the entire state of North Dakota, Western Minnesota, and Eastern South Dakota. WDAY is an award-winning station, taking home multiple Emmy awards as well as regional and national Edward R Murrow awards in recent years. They produce more live, local sports coverage than anyone in the region, and are the proud home of North Dakota State University Athletics and North Dakota High School Activities State Tournaments. WDAY is part of Forum Communications Company, a 5th-generation family-owned media company, and produces over 40 hours of local news, weather, and sports content each week, making them the most watched news station in the state of North Dakota and Western Minnesota.


Job Summary

As a News/Sports MMJ, you’ll cover the stories that matter to our community, from breaking news and major events to local sports. You’ll develop story ideas, conduct interviews, write scripts, shoot video and edit compelling stories for our newscasts and digital platforms. You’ll also report live from the field and have opportunities to develop your anchoring skills and fill in on both news and sports broadcasts.


Essential Functions

  • Research, investigate, and report on assigned topics, events, and issues of public interest
  • Develop story ideas, evaluate news leads/tips, and determine appropriate angles and story focus
  • Gather, verify, and analyze information from multiple sources to ensure accuracy and credibility
  • Conduct interviews with a wide range of sources, including officials, experts, and community members
  • Write clear, concise, and compelling scripts and stories that align with broadcast style, tone, and formatting standards
  • Produce and deliver content for live and recorded broadcasts, including stand-ups and field reporting
  • Collaborate with producers, photographers, and others to create engaging visual and audio elements that enhance storytelling
  • Respond quickly and effectively to breaking news, delivering accurate information under tight deadlines
  • Maintain a strong on-air presence and communicate information in a confident, professional manner
  • Utilize digital platforms and social media to share news content and engage with audiences in real time
  • Ensure all reporting adheres to journalistic ethics, standards, and legal guidelines
  • Stay informed on current events, industry trends, and community issues to inform coverage decisions
  • Build and maintain a network of reliable sources to support ongoing and future reporting
  • Represent the station professionally at community events and in public interactions
  • Drive audience engagement and loyalty by producing timely, relevant, and impactful content
  • Embrace a creative, collaborative approach with other team members and with other FCC departments and locations.
  • Maintain prompt and reliable attendance.


Non-Essential Duties and Functions

  • Perform additional duties as assigned.


We’re looking for someone with strong writing, communication and organizational skills who is eager to learn,

collaborate and deliver impactful journalism. A college degree in journalism or a related field is preferred, but

we’re willing to train the right candidate who brings the right attitude, curiosity and work ethic.

Join a newsroom that values strong journalism, teamwork and professional development while continuing to

expand its local news, weather and sports coverage.



Why WDAY?

  • A collaborative newsroom: Work alongside a great mix of experienced journalists and emerging
  • professionals. We’re committed to helping our team members sharpen their skills, take on new
  • challenges to reach their professional goals
  • A proven path for career growth: WDAY has a strong track record of developing talented journalists
  • who have gone on to advance their careers in Top 20 television markets across the country.
  • Time to recharge: Generous PTO and holiday benefits, with up to 23 paid days off in your first year.
  • Competitive benefits: Comprehensive health, dental and vision insurance, plus a 401(k) plan.
  • Onsite workout room: Convenient fitness facilities available to employees.


Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Journalism, Mass Communications, or a related field preferred; equivalent relevant work experience will be considered
  • Prior experience in broadcast journalism, reporting, or multimedia content creation preferred (internships and student media acceptable)
  • Strong news judgment with the ability to identify compelling stories and prioritize coverage based on urgency and audience impact
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to write clearly, accurately, and concisely under deadline pressure, and while managing multiple assignments
  • Experience using digital analytics tools and social media platforms to inform and engage audiences preferred
  • Ability to shoot, edit, or collaborate effectively on video production is a plus
  • Comfortable delivering live reports and appearing on camera with professionalism and confidence
  • Strong research, interviewing, and fact-checking skills with a commitment to accuracy and fairness and excellent attention to detail
  • Willingness and flexibility to work varied schedules, including mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays as news coverage requires
  • Must possess a valid driver’s license and a driving record that is insurable by the company.
  • Must carry an acceptable level of vehicle insurance as required by the company.


Expected compensation for this role is between $18.26 - $19.23.hr, based on qualifications and experience.


ABOUT THE COMPANY

Forum Communications Company is a family-owned media and technology leader with more than a century of delivering trusted, quality journalism and innovative business solutions. Storytelling is at the heart of who we are, but today, we’re so much more than a newspaper. As one of the Upper Midwest’s leading media organizations, we’re driving the future across print and digital news, sports streaming, technology, broadcasting, commercial printing, and full-service agency advertising.

Forum Communications Company offers the following to all Full-Time and 32-Hour Benefited employees:

  • Health, dental, and vision packages
  • Paid maternity and parental leave
  • Company-paid short-term disability and life insurance
  • Additional options for critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity coverage
  • Retirement benefits with company match
  • Generous PTO and paid volunteer hours

We are an equal employment opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law. FCC currently does not offer employer sponsorship.


$18.26 - $19.23.hr

Notice of AI Use in Job Application Review

As part of our commitment in creating a fair, efficient, and consistent hiring process we may use artificial intelligence (AI) to help our recruiting teams organize, summarize, and analyze information provided by candidates, including resumes, application responses, and other materials submitted during the application process.AI may be used to identify patterns, highlight relevant skills, and experience, and assist in comparing a candidate’s qualifications with the requirement of a specific role. These tools are to improve efficiency and consistency while supporting more informed hiring decisions, which will ultimately be made by the hiring team.

job.title: North Dakota Energy and Government Reporter
job.description:
Full-time

Forum Communications Company is seeking a multimedia reporter to cover the oil and energy industry and its far-reaching impact on North Dakota. Ideally based in Bismarck, this reporter will produce timely, authoritative stories about one of the state’s most consequential industries while traveling as needed to the Bakken and communities across western North Dakota. The reporter will explore how energy development shapes the state’s economy, government, land, infrastructure, workforce and people. The position will also contribute general news coverage from Bismarck for the FCC network, with a focus on state government and legislative developments during active legislative sessions.

This is a multimedia position serving Forum Communications audiences across digital, print and broadcast platforms. In addition to written reporting, the reporter will gather video and other visual content.

The ideal candidate can translate complex subjects into clear, compelling journalism while building strong relationships with industry leaders, public officials, landowners, workers, tribal communities and local residents. Experience covering the energy industry or state government is valuable but not required. We are also interested in candidates who are curious, resourceful and eager to develop expertise in a complex and nationally important beat.


Key Responsibilities

  • Cover North Dakota’s oil and gas industry, including production, exploration, transportation, refining and emerging technologies.
  • Travel regularly throughout western North Dakota to report from energy sites, communities, public meetings and breaking-news scenes.
  • Monitor state and federal energy policy, regulation, taxation and legislation, explaining how decisions affect the industry and North Dakota residents.
  • Contribute general Bismarck news coverage for Forum Communications audiences across the state and region.
  • Provide additional coverage of the Legislature during legislative sessions, including significant bills, debates and decisions beyond the energy beat.
  • Report on the economic impact of energy development, including state revenue, local government finances, employment, housing and business growth.
  • Examine environmental and land-use issues such as water use, spills, emissions, reclamation, pipeline development and abandoned wells.
  • Tell the stories of the people and communities affected by the energy industry, including workers, families, landowners, tribal nations and longtime western North Dakota residents.
  • Cover breaking news involving industrial accidents, spills, regulatory actions and significant business or government developments.
  • Develop enterprise and accountability reporting that goes beyond announcements and news releases.
  • Use public records, data and other reporting tools to identify trends and hold companies and public institutions accountable.
  • Build a diverse network of sources across industry, government, environmental organizations, academia, tribal nations and local communities.
  • Produce journalism in multiple formats, including written stories, photography, social video and broadcast-quality video; may include appearing on camera when appropriate.
  • Use audience data and community feedback to identify coverage opportunities and strengthen engagement.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in journalism, communications or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Previous reporting experience, preferably covering business, government, energy, agriculture, the environment or rural communities.
  • Strong news judgment and the ability to balance daily reporting, breaking news and deeper enterprise work.
  • Ability to explain technical, regulatory, legislative and financial topics in accessible language.
  • Experience using public records and data in reporting.
  • Strong interviewing, writing and storytelling skills.
  • Experience producing video journalism or a willingness to develop skills in shooting, editing and reporting for digital and television audiences.
  • Comfort appearing on camera and delivering live or recorded reports.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing to a collaborative, regional newsroom.
  • Willingness and ability to travel regularly throughout western North Dakota, sometimes on short notice.
  • A valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.

Expected compensation for this role is between $60,000 - $70,000, based on qualifications and experience.

As one of the Upper Midwest’s leading media organizations, we’re driving the future across print and digital news, sports streaming, technology, broadcasting, commercial printing, and full-service agency advertising.
