job.title: Supervising Senior Producer
job.description:
Description

Supervising Senior Producer, Weekends

WNYC

The WNYC and Gothamist newsroom is looking for a motivated and thorough Supervising Senior Producer for our highly-rated weekend magazine shows, Weekend Edition and Weekend All Things Considered. This role will oversee the shows’ sound and editorial direction, supervise producers, and professionally coordinate with hosts and engineers

The Supervising Senior Producer, Weekends pushes the boundaries of our storytelling with their creativity. The Supervising Senior Producer, Weekends eagerly integrates smart data analysis with inventive approaches to storytelling that produce distinctive show segments and elements that make the WNYC air a compelling listen, and represents and impacts all those who live in our coverage area. They also inspire their teams to find inventive ways to reach new, diverse audiences.

Supervising Senior Producers are newsroom leaders who reinforce our culture of audience centricity, professional respect and journalistic excellence. They are the conduit between upper management and individual contributors, and play an important role in our newsroom culture. The ideal candidate has experience overseeing live news coverage as well as managing – directly and indirectly – a team of journalists.

This role, which reports to the Senior Editor of Audio Strategy, will work a Wednesday through Sunday schedule, with conventional business hours on weekdays, and a 7 a.m. start time on weekends. This leader will also be required to flex their schedule as needed to account for developing news and to contribute to weekday shows and special projects as needed.

Responsibilities:

  • Oversee the programming, production and editorial needs of WNYC’s weekend magazine shows. Set the shows’ daily rundown, delegating tasks, and prepare hosts

  • Lead planning for each weekend’s coverage as well as logistics for breaking news.

  • Directly manage producers and daily assignments, providing clear expectations as well as consistent feedback

  • Lead weekly meetings with the weekend hosts and producers; represent weekend coverage at newsroom meetings

  • Hold all content up to the highest standards, editing for adequate sourcing, accuracy, fairness and clarity

  • Collaborate with newsroom editors on assignments, ensuring our reporting is multiplatform and aligned for all our audiences

  • Collaborate with the shows’ engineers throughout each live broadcast

  • Reinforce standards for ethics, professionalism and excellence, regularly articulating how coverage fits into the WNYC newsroom vision of serving the needs of a diverse population, and encouraging the production of content that gives daily utility to listeners and readers.

  • Model and exhibit the highest standards of professionalism at all times.

  • Propose and accept one-time or ongoing assignments or special projects within the newsroom, as decided with their relevant supervisor.

  • Serving on newsroom committees focused on issues such as editorial standards, style or training.

Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of professional experience producing audio news

  • Sophisticated understanding of the broadcast landscape, including applicable metrics, relevant audience trends, and audience engagement techniques. Experience in using audience data to inform good journalistic decisions to drive results

  • Demonstrated commitment and ability to contribute an equity lens to every aspect of people development and management processes, and ability to increase diversity, equity, and inclusion competency in their teams

  • Demonstrated knowledge of complex social and cultural issues

  • The intellectual and emotional depth, maturity, self-confidence and interpersonal skills to work effectively and/or interact with the public and with other staff at NYPR

  • Self-starter with proven ability to meet deadlines and pay close attention to detail and fact-checking

  • Ability to manage several projects concurrently

  • Demonstrated ability to lead and manage a team and supervise content creation

  • Excellent broadcast writing and editing skills

  • Experience working with and managing on-air talent

  • Fluency in audio editing, working in a variety of content management systems, and other broadcast and digital delivery systems

  • Interest and appreciation for the medium of audio and text and how they can be used to reach separate audiences

  • Experience leading breaking news coverage

  • Impeccable journalistic integrity and editorial judgment

  • Excellent communication skills, both oral and written

Additional Information:

This is a full-time role with an annual salary $103,500.00. New York Public Radio also offers excellent medical, dental, and vision insurance, vacation, personal and sick time as well as inclusive family leave.

This role is a hybrid capacity of two days in the office; with the ability to work from home at times. However, this position is part of the NYC staff and will be expected to work from WNYC's Lower Manhattan offices on specified days with regularity.

Commitment to Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

New York Public Radio is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We continuously strive to place our employees at the center of our thinking and elevate inclusive practices to develop and support a more engaged and productive workforce. Our journalism and operations in the service of that journalism benefit from a broad range of perspectives, from all backgrounds, at all levels of the organization. Diversity is essential to honest, authentic, accurate storytelling and reportage; creating an institution in which all voices are encouraged, valued, and heard.

Equal Opportunity

New York Public Radio is an equal opportunity employer committed to achieving the goal of equal employment opportunity for all. Applicants and employees are considered and evaluated for positions without regard to mental or physical disability, race, creed, color, religion, gender, national origin, citizenship status, age, genetic information, military or veteran status, sexual orientation, marital status, employment status or any protected federal, state or local status unrelated to the performance of the work involved.

job.title: Temporary Producer
job.description:
New York Public Radio seeks a dynamic, highly creative Temporary Producer for Terrestrials.This Producer is a content-maker for the show. This work involves producing episodes in close collaboration with the show’s Host and production team. This role is part of a small-but-mighty team who will work together collaboratively to ensure the highest quality for each episode. It is key to our show’s mission that every episode’s production focuses on rethinking expertise and prioritizes the search for diverse sources, and the entire team is tasked with carrying out that mission in the development of all episodes and seasons. This role reports to the Executive Producer, Terrestrials.Responsibilities:
  • Work closely with the team (Host, EP, Producer), freelance contributors, and freelance editor/sound designer to produce episodes of Terrestrials.
  • Pitch exciting, thought-provoking, original ideas for new and bonus episodes of Terrestrials
  • Research story ideas, conduct pre-interviews, book guests, arrange logistics (studios/tape syncs)
  • Source and book captivating guests with diverse voices, experiences, and perspectives
  • Identify, gather, cut and assemble tape
  • With editorial support from Host and SP, develop storyboards and create drafts of episodes in ProTools
  • Coordinate outreach and tape collection for the Badgers segment of each episode.
  • Produce content for social platforms, as needed
  • Contribute to the editorial planning of the show as it evolves, attend pitch meetings
  • Communicate consistently and clearly with other members of the team.
  • Liaise with fact checkers as needed
  • Write and produce content for web, newsletter, social media, and other platforms as needed.
  • Other administrative duties as needed.
Qualifications:
  • 5+ years of experience producing narrative or reported content
  • Experience with booking, pre-interviewing, tape cutting, story development, script writing and host collaboration
  • Experience with audio editing
  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, deadlines, and time-management
  • Demonstrated success in the creation of superb content under pressure
  • An independent work ethic combined with a love for and patience with the collaborative process
  • The ability to learn and understand the content and sound for each show and adapt your style accordingly to reach our target audiences
  • Fluency in audio editing with ProTools, and knowledge of Dropbox, DAVID, CMS, and other systems for broadcast and digital delivery of audio
  • Superb organizational skills, attention to detail, and time-management
  • Joy in working in a group environment, and the ability to give and take direction and feedback well.

job.title: Brand Partnership Manager
job.description:
Welcome page Returning Candidate? Log back in! Brand Partnership Manager ID 3847 Position Type Regular Full-Time Location : Location US-

Overview

Salem Influencer Network, a division of Salem Media, is seeking an early-career seller to develop new brand partnerships across our national influencer portfolio and event opportunities. We connect consumer brands with trusted creators through sponsored content, social campaigns, and live experiences. We’re looking for someone who understands creator culture, follows consumer brands, and can recognize what makes a partnership feel authentic to talent and valuable to an advertiser. If you follow creators, notice which brands sponsor their content, and have ideas about who they should partner with next, this might be the role for you. If you understand what makes a collaboration feel authentic to a creator and compelling to a brand and now you want to turn that knowledge into new business, this is the role for you. This is a revenue-generating, business-development role with a strong focus on bringing partners who are new to Salem into the business. You will build your own book of business through research, proactive outreach, thoughtful pitches, and consistent follow-through. An established client roster is welcome, but it is not required. Ideal background: influencer marketing, talent or creator agencies, brand partnerships, business development, social media, or event sponsorships. Ideal background: influencer marketing, talent or creator agencies, brand partnerships, business development, social media, or event sponsorships.

Responsibilities

What You’ll Do

· Prospect mainstream consumer brands, DTC companies, startups, and agencies that align with our talent’s audiences, content, values, and partnership goals. · Identify decision-makers, personalize outreach, book discovery meetings, and build new brand and agency relationships. · Learn our creators’ voices and communities to develop compelling brand matches across categories such as beauty, wellness, fashion, food, home, family, and travel. · Pitch partnerships spanning sponsored social content, creator endorsements, podcast integrations, paid amplification, and talent appearances. · Develop event sponsorship concepts, including product sampling, on-site activations, and creator content before, during, and after events. · Manage outreach, proposals, negotiations, and closing; coordinate with internal teams on pricing, talent approvals, deliverables, and campaign handoff. · Maintain an organized pipeline, meet new-business revenue goals, and grow first-time campaigns into repeat partnerships.

Qualifications

What We’re Looking For · Approximately 1–3 years of relevant

experience

in sales, influencer marketing, brand partnerships, talent or agency work, or event sponsorships. Strong internship or hands-on

experience

may also be considered. · A working understanding of Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, including creator formats, audience engagement, and sponsored content. · Ability to identify relevant consumer brands and explain a partnership idea through both talent fit and the brand’s marketing goals. · Confidence initiating new conversations, asking discovery questions, presenting ideas, and following up consistently. · Familiarity with campaign deliverables, content usage rights, exclusivity, paid amplification, and measures such as engagement, traffic, and conversions. · Strong writing, presentation, and organizational skills, with a willingness to learn and take ownership of sales results. Existing brand relationships, CRM experience, and exposure to event activations are a plus. Traditional media sales

experience

is not required. Who Will Thrive Here · Sellers who can spot an authentic creator and brand match and explain why it works. · Self-starters who enjoy reaching new contacts and building relationships from scratch. · People who follow consumer trends and understand how brands work with creators. · Persistent, coachable professionals who want to turn creative partnership ideas into revenue.

Benefits

Why Salem Influencer Network · Work with content creators who have large fanbases and engaged communities. · Build brand relationships across influencer campaigns and live events within an established media organization. · Uncapped earning potential with competitive base pay plus commission. · Competitive pay structure based on experience. · Health, dental, vision and life insurance. · 401k retirement plan. · Paid holidays and vacation time. benefits

job.title: Account Executive, KERO
job.description:
We are looking for a driven, creative sales professional who loves helping local businesses grow? KERO in Bakersfield, California is looking for an Account Executive, Local who will be a true partner to the business community — connecting clients to the audiences that matter most through a powerful, multi-platform suite of advertising solutions. From broadcast television to Over The Top (OTT) video, search strategies, social media, digital display, and e-mail targeting, you'll craft customized campaigns that deliver real results and real return on investment. If you're energized by building relationships, closing deals, and making a measurable difference for the businesses in your community, this is your opportunity to shine.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Sell advertising solutions to local and regional businesses and advertising agencies.
  • Apply the Scripps Sales Process (SSP) to analyze current and prospective customer needs and apply customized advertising solutions that provide return on their investment.
  • In addition to television commercial airtime sales, facilitate the customer's ability to take advantage of the full array of digital marketing options available.
  • Independently prospect, secure appointments, perform needs analysis, develop customized solutions, present and close sales to develop and maintain new business from traditional and non-traditional advertisers.
  • Use ratings data, qualitative information and market trends to negotiate program ratings and advertising rates with advertising agencies in order to maximize revenue as well as develop custom solutions for new advertisers.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor with new and existing clients, provide best-in-class customer service, grow accounts, and gain additional business from referrals.
  • Perform client services, including but not limited to media avail negotiations, presentation preparation delivery and execution, copy writing, credit applications and collection of revenue due.
  • Effectively and proactively manage a sales funnel by way of Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems, monitoring and achieving key performance indicators and expected activity levels.
  • Contribute to the creative development of campaigns though client communication and needs analysis, storyboard and concept creation, and assistance in production aspects.
  • Build and maintain strong client relationships, which may include entertaining prospective and existing clients.
  • Perform routine administrative functions of a media salesperson including makegood resolution, continuous update of CRM system with activity, account information and pending revenue, and communication with sales leadership regarding the status of accounts.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • BS/BA in related discipline preferred or equivalent years of experience
  • Generally 2+ years of proven sales success preferred
  • Experience in strategic account management, broadcast ratings and digital execution preferred
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Highly self-motivated and goal focused
  • Highly creative and innovative thinker
  • Strong influencing, selling and upselling skills
  • Effective teamwork and collaboration skills
  • Very strong analysis and data interpretation - able to translate needs and research data into sound marketing proposals
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills
  • Outstanding presentation abilities (in person/virtual, small/large groups, all levels)
  • Strong time management and organizational skills
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel and PowerPoint)
  • Working knowledge of Google Office (Sheets, Docs, Slides) and virtual conferencing platforms (E.g. Skype, WebEx, Zoom or MS Teams etc.)

WHAT WE'LL OFFER:

  • Uncapped sales commission
  • Monthly allowance for mileage and cell phone
  • Extensive Scripps Sales Process training
  • A career path to grow your professional experiences
  • Full medical, dental and vision benefits, as well as certain other health and wellness benefits
  • Retirement savings plan with company match
  • Other key company benefits include disability accident insurance, life insurance, ID protection, pet discount program, and employee assistance program. More details about timing and conditions of benefits eligibility and other plan terms and conditions will be provided upon hire.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Bakersfield is California's ninth-largest city and a place with a character all its own — rooted in agriculture, energy, and a deep musical heritage that gave birth to the Bakersfield Sound, a twangy, West Coast alternative to Nashville country that produced legends like Buck Owens and Merle Haggard. The city is home to the Kern County Museum, a vibrant arts scene, and a calendar full of festivals and community events that reflect its proud, hardworking spirit.

Surrounded by stunning natural landscapes, Bakersfield sits at the southern end of the San Joaquin Valley with easy access to some of California's most spectacular outdoor destinations. The nearby Kern River offers whitewater rafting and scenic hiking, while Lake Isabella is a favorite for boating, fishing, and camping. The southern Sierra Nevada mountains are just a short drive away, putting world-class skiing at Mammoth Mountain and the towering peaks of Sequoia National Park well within weekend reach.

With a lower cost of living than most California metros, Bakersfield gives residents the ability to stretch their dollar further while enjoying a warm climate, a growing restaurant and craft brewery scene, and a close-knit community that takes pride in its roots. The city is well-connected via Highway 99 and is within a two-hour drive of both Los Angeles and the Central Coast — making it an ideal home base for those who want California living without California prices.

#LI-SM2 #LI-Onsite

COMPENSATION RANGE:

Annual Salary: $45,000.00 - $60,000.00


 

Pursuant to state and local salary transparency laws, the salary range posted is specific to candidates who will perform this work in California.



 

WHAT WE'LL OFFER:

  • Extensive Scripps Sales Process training

  • Uncapped sales commission

  • Monthly allowance for mileage and cell phone

  • A career path to grow your professional experiences

  • Full medical, dental and vision benefits, as well as certain other health and wellness benefits

  • Retirement savings plan with company match

  • Other key company benefits include disability accident insurance, hospital indemnity, critical illness, life insurance, AD&D, ID protection, pet discount program, and employee assistance program. More details about timing and conditions of benefits eligibility and other plan terms and conditions will be provided upon hire.

If you are a current Scripps employee, please do not apply on this site. Please access our internal career site at Worklife > My Info > View Open Positions at Scripps.

SCRIPPS’ COMMITMENT TO A CULTURE THAT CREATES CONNECTION:

At Scripps, we are committed to a culture that reflects the audiences and communities we serve. We are intentional about creating an environment where employees, our audiences and other stakeholders feel valued and inspired to reach their full potential and create connections. To successfully deliver on this commitment, we must understand and reflect the values and perspectives those around us embody. That process begins by looking inward to build and celebrate a respectful workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging and connection. By continuing to cultivate an environment where all employees have a fair chance to succeed, are included, valued, and seen, we will strengthen the connections that drive positive business impact and align with our core purpose. 

ABOUT SCRIPPS:

The E.W. Scripps Company (NASDAQ: SSP) is a diversified media company focused on creating connection. As one of the nation’s largest local TV broadcasters, Scripps serves communities with quality, objective local journalism and operates a portfolio of more than 60 stations in 40+ markets. Scripps reaches households across the U.S. with national news outlet Scripps News and popular entertainment brands ION, ION Plus, ION Mystery, Bounce, Grit and Laff. Scripps is the nation’s largest holder of broadcast spectrum. Scripps Sports serves professional and college sports leagues, conferences and teams with local market depth and national broadcast reach of up to 100% of TV households. Founded in 1878, Scripps is the steward of the Scripps National Spelling Bee and its longtime motto is: “Give light and the people will find their own way.”

Scripps Company and its affiliates do not discriminate in its employment decisions on the basis of race, sex, sexual orientation, transgender status, gender, color, religion, age, genetic information, medical condition, disability, marital status, citizenship or national origin, and military membership or veteran status, or on any other basis which would be in violation of any applicable federal, state or local law. Furthermore, the company will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities unless doing so would result in an undue hardship for the company.

job.title: Community Connections Coordinator, WEWS
job.description:
WEWS, The E.W. Scripps Company ABC affiliate in Cleveland, Ohio, is searching for a Community Connections Coordinator. We're looking for a driven, people-first professional to join our team and serve as the vital link between our newsroom and the communities we cover. In this role, you'll cultivate meaningful relationships, surface credible story leads, coordinate community events and listening sessions, and help our journalists connect with the trusted local voices that make our coverage matter. Whether you're in the field building source networks, managing audience tips, or supporting breaking news coverage, your work will directly shape how WEWS serves the people of Greater Cleveland every day.


Application Review: Applications received by 11/04 will receive priority consideration. Applications received after this date may continue to be reviewed as needed.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Build and maintain relationships with community organizations, residents, leaders, and trusted sources to gather community insights and identify emerging issues, events, and story opportunities.
  • Monitor, track, and route audience tips, questions, and leads from community channels, ensuring timely communication and escalation to newsroom teams.
  • Support newsroom listening efforts, community conversations, and source development by connecting journalists with credible and diverse community voices.
  • Assist with breaking and developing news coverage by gathering community context, maintaining source networks, and providing timely intelligence to newsroom staff.
  • Serve as a responsive point of contact for community organizations and residents, fostering positive relationships and trust.
  • Coordinate outreach, maintain partner and contact records, and represent the station at community meetings, events, and activities.
  • Support newsroom talent by coordinating interviews, identifying community contacts, gathering background information, and facilitating community appearances.
  • Coordinate logistics and execution for community conversations, listening sessions, public programs, newsroom events, special coverage initiatives, and station appearances.
  • Manage event-related activities including outreach, scheduling, partner coordination, participant communications, on-site support, and post-event follow-up.
  • Support audience engagement across digital and in-person channels, including live discussions, community groups, neighborhood platforms, and other audience interaction opportunities.
  • Maintain community calendars, project plans, contact databases, and engagement records to support execution of the market community strategy.
  • Track community insights, engagement outcomes, story leads, and best practices, preparing summaries and reports that help inform newsroom and community engagement priorities.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • Associates degree in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Generally, 5+ years of experience in journalism, communications, community engagement, nonprofit work, events, public relations or related fields
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:


  • Strong listening, relationship-building and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to establish rapport with diverse community members and organizations
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Excellent organization, follow-through and attention to detail
  • Ability to identify and communicate relevant community information quickly and accurately
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with journalists and station teams
  • Comfort working independently in the community and adapting to newsroom needs
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, CRM/contact systems, social platforms and collaboration tools
  • Solid news judgment, comfort with newsroom urgency, ability to verify and relay information quickly, and understanding of how community tips can develop into stories
  • Ability to communicate clearly and accurately across digital platforms, maintain professionalism in public-facing conversations and collaborate closely with reporters, producers, anchors, meteorologists and newsroom leaders

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Cleveland is a city of neighborhoods, grit, and genuine heart — and it's having a moment. Situated on the southern shore of Lake Erie, Cleveland combines a rich cultural heritage with a revitalized downtown and a food and arts scene that consistently surprises newcomers. The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, the world-class Cleveland Museum of Art (with free general admission), and Playhouse Square — the largest performing arts center in the U.S. outside of New York City — give the city a cultural depth that is hard to match. Walkable neighborhoods like Ohio City, Tremont, and Little Italy each bring their own distinctive character, cuisine, and community.


Sports are woven into the fabric of Cleveland life. Cheer on the Cleveland Guardians at Progressive Field, follow the Cleveland Cavaliers at Rocket Arena, and join the passionate faithful who rally behind the Cleveland Browns every season. The sense of community pride around Cleveland's teams is infectious, and game days turn the city into one big celebration.


The outdoors are never far away. Cuyahoga Valley National Park — the only national park in Ohio — sits just south of the city, offering miles of hiking, biking, waterfalls, and scenic railroad excursions. Cleveland Metroparks wraps the city in a beloved "Emerald Necklace" of parks and trails, and Lake Erie's shoreline provides year-round recreation from sailing to fishing. With a lower cost of living than many comparable metros, a growing tech and healthcare economy, and a community-first spirit you can feel on every block, Cleveland is a fantastic place to build a career and a life.

job.title: Executive Reporter, KERO
job.description:
KERO, The E.W. Scripps Company ABC station in Bakersfield, CA, is searching for an Executive Reporter to join our team. In this role, you'll be at the heart of our newsroom, driving a mission to elevate the way we connect with our community through compelling, authentic, and impactful stories. You'll inspire reporters, MMJs, and newsroom staff at every level, bringing your passion and expertise to foster a culture of continuous growth and creative excellence. If you're energized by mentoring talent and shaping the voice of a newsroom, we want to hear from you.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Lead, develop, and enhance the storytelling skill and abilities of all reporters and MMJs in the station.
  • Collaborate with other newsroom leaders to consistently execute the content strategy through authentic, meaningful storytelling.
  • Oversee the writing of stories for all platforms; provide timely feedback to foster continuous improvement.
  • Develop and supervise effective workflow strategies and procedures for multiple news programs and outlets.
  • Ensure that all content adheres to journalistic standards and ethical guidelines.
  • Deliver a vision and create trust among reporters, photographers and newsroom staff.
  • May provide on-air, multi-platform coverage for breaking news as needed.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • BS/BA in related discipline preferred, or equivalent years of experience
  • Generally, 7+ years of experience in related field preferred
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:


  • Demonstrated expertise in storytelling
  • Knowledge and demonstration of editorial judgment, journalistic ethics and libel laws
  • Curiosity for the community, city, state and world we report on daily
  • Deep understanding of the content strategy
  • Ability to work a variety of shifts including nights, weekends, early morning, and holidays

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Bakersfield sits at the southern end of California's San Joaquin Valley, a city with a rich cultural identity and a surprisingly vibrant lifestyle. Known worldwide as the birthplace of the Bakersfield Sound — the country music movement that launched legends like Buck Owens and Merle Haggard — the city wears its roots proudly. The iconic Buck Owens' Crystal Palace keeps that musical spirit alive, while a growing arts scene, local breweries, and a diverse and delicious food culture give the city its own modern energy.


The great outdoors is practically at your doorstep. The Kern River draws whitewater rafting enthusiasts, anglers, and hikers year-round, while Lake Isabella offers boating and camping under wide-open skies. Sequoia National Park and Kings Canyon National Park — home to some of the tallest trees on Earth — are just a couple of hours away, making weekend adventures a genuine California experience.


Bakersfield offers a quality of life that's hard to beat for the price. With a significantly lower cost of living than Los Angeles (just about two hours south), you'll find spacious housing, short commutes, and a strong sense of community. From Friday night high school football to the Bakersfield Condors hockey games at Mechanics Bank Arena, this is a city where people show up for each other — and for the stories that deserve to be told.

job.title: Executive Reporter, KNXV
job.description:
KNXV, The E.W. Scripps ABC affiliate in Phoenix, Arizona, is looking for an Executive Reporter who is as passionate about the craft of storytelling as they are about the community. In this role, you'll leading, inspiring, and mentoring reporters and MMJs at every level to discover powerful ways to grow their storytelling skills. You'll partner with newsroom leaders to execute a content strategy rooted in authenticity, impact, and journalistic integrity, all while shaping a culture where great stories aren't just told — they're felt. If you're ready to elevate the voices that matter most and leave a lasting mark on local journalism in one of the country's most vibrant and fast-growing cities, we want to hear from you. 

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Lead, develop, and enhance the storytelling skill and abilities of all reporters and MMJs in the station.
  • Collaborate with other newsroom leaders to consistently execute the content strategy through authentic, meaningful storytelling .
  • Oversee the writing of stories for all platforms; provide timely feedback to foster continuous improvement.
  • Develop and supervise effective workflow strategies and procedures for multiple news programs and outlets.
  • Ensure that all content adheres to journalistic standards and ethical guidelines.
  • Deliver a vision and create trust among reporters, photographers and newsroom staff.
  • May provide on-air, multi-platform coverage for breaking news as needed.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

 

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • BS/BA in related discipline preferred, or equivalent years of experience
  • Generally, 7+ years of experience in related field preferred 

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Demonstrated expertise in storytelling
  • Knowledge and demonstration of editorial judgment, journalistic ethics and libel laws
  • Curiosity for the community, city, state and world we report on daily
  • Deep understanding of the content strategy
  • Ability to work a variety of shifts including nights, weekends, early morning, and holidays

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Phoenix, Arizona, is one of the most dynamic and fast-growing cities in the United States — a sprawling desert metropolis that blends stunning natural beauty with a thriving urban energy. Surrounded by the Sonoran Desert, Phoenix offers year-round sunshine and unmatched outdoor adventures, from hiking the iconic trails of Camelback Mountain and South Mountain Park to exploring the scenic beauty of the Tonto National Forest just an hour away. The city is a haven for golf enthusiasts, cyclists, and outdoor lovers of all kinds.

Beyond the desert landscape, Phoenix boasts a rich and diverse cultural scene. The city is home to world-class museums like the Heard Museum, dedicated to Native American art and culture, and the Phoenix Art Museum, one of the largest art museums in the Southwest. The downtown core is alive with acclaimed restaurants, craft breweries, and a vibrant nightlife, while neighborhoods like Roosevelt Row serve as the beating heart of the local arts community. From the Phoenix Symphony to the bustling farmers markets and food halls, there is always something new to discover.

Sports are a way of life in the Valley of the Sun. Phoenix is home to the NFL's Cardinals, the NBA's Suns, the MLB's Diamondbacks, the NHL's Coyotes, and the WNBA's Mercury — giving residents a full calendar of live sports action. Whether you're catching a game, exploring a new trail, or dining at one of the city's award-winning restaurants, Phoenix offers an extraordinary quality of life in one of America's most exciting and welcoming cities.

job.title: Executive Reporter, KTNV
job.description:
Scripps-owned KTNV, the ABC affiliate in Las Vegas, is looking for a Executive Reporter who believes great journalism starts with great storytelling. In this leadership role, you’ll help elevate the craft across the newsroom, working alongside reporters and MMJs to create authentic, meaningful stories that connect with the Las Vegas community.


You’ll bring a sharp editorial eye, a passion for developing people, and the ability to turn everyday assignments into memorable journalism. You’ll also partner with newsroom leaders to bring our content strategy to life across platforms while maintaining the highest journalistic standards. If you’re an accomplished storyteller who gets energized by helping other journalists grow, this is an opportunity to make an impact both inside the newsroom and throughout the community we serve.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Lead the development and enhancement of storytelling skills for reporters and MMJs across the newsroom.
  • Coach and mentor journalists at all experience levels, helping them discover creative ways to strengthen their reporting, writing, and storytelling.
  • Collaborate with newsroom leaders to consistently execute the station’s content strategy through authentic, meaningful journalism.
  • Oversee story writing and development across platforms, providing timely and actionable feedback that encourages continuous improvement.
  • Develop and supervise effective workflows, strategies, and procedures supporting multiple news programs and platforms.
  • Ensure content consistently meets journalistic standards and ethical guidelines.
  • Create and communicate a clear storytelling vision that builds trust among reporters, photographers, and other newsroom colleagues.
  • Contribute on-air and multi-platform coverage during breaking news when needed.
  • Support evolving newsroom priorities and perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related discipline preferred, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Generally 7+ years of experience in journalism, news, storytelling, or a related field preferred.
  • A valid driver’s license and ability to meet applicable driving requirements for the role.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Demonstrated expertise in compelling, community-focused storytelling.
  • Strong editorial judgment and a thorough understanding of journalistic ethics and libel laws.
  • Genuine curiosity about the people, issues, and events shaping Las Vegas, Nevada, and the world.
  • A deep understanding of content strategy and how strong storytelling can serve audiences across platforms.
  • A coaching mindset and a passion for helping journalists develop their craft and reach their potential.
  • The ability to collaborate, communicate a creative vision, and establish trust across a newsroom.
  • Sound judgment and composure in a fast-moving news environment where priorities and deadlines can change quickly.
  • Flexibility to work a variety of shifts, including nights, weekends, early mornings, and holidays.
  • Ability and willingness to work onsite and drive as required to fulfill job responsibilities.

OUR TEAM:

At KTNV, you’ll join a newsroom united by curiosity, creativity, and a commitment to serving the community through meaningful journalism. Our team brings different backgrounds, experiences, interests, and perspectives to the stories we tell. We value collaboration, thoughtful feedback, strong editorial standards, and the willingness to keep improving our craft. As Executive Reporter, you’ll play an important role in creating an environment where journalists learn from one another, take creative approaches to storytelling, and do work that matters to the people of Las Vegas.


WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Las Vegas offers much more than its world-famous entertainment corridor. The region combines big-city energy with distinctive neighborhoods, a thriving food and entertainment scene, and countless opportunities to discover the people and stories that make Southern Nevada unique. For a curious journalist, it’s a dynamic community with no shortage of stories to tell.


Outside of work, Las Vegas puts the outdoors within easy reach, from desert landscapes and hiking to nearby recreation and scenic escapes. It’s a place where entertainment, culture, community, and the natural beauty of the Southwest come together, giving you plenty to explore when you’re off the clock.

  • Oversee the writing of stories for all platforms; provide timely feedback to foster continuous improvement

  • Develop and supervise effective workflow strategies and procedures for multiple news programs and outlets

  • Ensure that all content adheres to journalistic standards and ethical guidelines

  • Deliver a vision and create trust among reporters, photographers and newsroom staff

  • May provide on-air, multi-platform coverage for breaking news as needed

  • Perform other duties as assigned

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • BS/BA in related discipline preferred, or equivalent years of experience

  • Generally, 7+ years of experience in related field preferred

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Demonstrated expertise in storytelling

  • Knowledge and demonstration of editorial judgment, journalistic ethics and libel laws

  • Curiosity for the community, city, state and world we report on daily

  • Deep understanding of the content strategy

  • Ability to work a variety of shifts including nights, weekends, early morning, and holidays

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK AND PLAY:

Norfolk, Virginia, sits at the heart of Hampton Roads, one of the most dynamic regions on the East Coast. As part of the largest naval installation in the world, Norfolk offers a unique blend of military heritage, maritime culture, and coastal living. The city boasts a revitalized downtown waterfront featuring world-class museums like the Chrysler Museum of Art, vibrant dining and entertainment districts, and the beautiful Elizabeth River.

Residents enjoy easy access to miles of beaches, the Chesapeake Bay, and outdoor recreation year-round. The region's moderate climate means you can explore the Virginia Beach Boardwalk, kayak through the Great Dismal Swamp, or catch a show at the historic Attucks Theatre any time of year. With affordable housing, no state tax on groceries, and a thriving arts scene that includes the Virginia Opera and Virginia Symphony Orchestra, Norfolk offers an exceptional quality of life. Plus, you're just a short drive from the Blue Ridge Mountains, Washington D.C., and the Outer Banks of North Carolina.

job.title: Local Sales Manager, WEWS
job.description:
WEWS, The E.W. Scripps Company's ABC affiliate in Cleveland, Ohio, is looking for a driven and experienced Local Sales Manager to inspire a team of Account Executives and help local businesses grow through innovative, multi-platform advertising solutions. From broadcast television to Over The Top (OTT) video, SEO/SEM, social media, digital display, and email targeting, you'll have a full arsenal of tools to connect clients with the audiences that matter most — and a talented team to lead in doing it.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Collaborate with DOS and other sales managers and departments to accomplish the objectives of the station.
  • Organize, direct and manage the execution and performance of a team of local sales Account Executives.
  • Negotiate ratings, rates and budgets.
  • Develop new business for station utilizing and maximizing all station platforms including but not limited to broadcast, digital and mobile.
  • Develop working knowledge of Scripps Sales Process (SSP) and coach Account Executives regarding SSP in the field.
  • Utilize SSP, resources and tools provided to build effective sales strategies.
  • Collaborate with the Director of Sales and Sales Managers to train, develop and motivate the local sales team so that revenue goals are achieved.
  • Collaborate with the Director of Sales and Sales Managers to foster career growth and development of the local sales team so that a pipeline of talent for future Scripps sales management openings is ready.
  • Maintain positive working relationships with outside vendors.
  • Interface with traffic systems and personnel to ensure efficient management of airtime inventory.
  • Oversee accounts receivable and credit policies.
  • Develop and implement pricing and packaging to fill needs of both client and station.
  • Know the strengths and weaknesses of the competing stations, other advertising mediums and position the station accordingly.
  • Effectively forecast sales revenue and manage department expenses so that financial goals are achieved.
  • Other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • Bachelor's degree in business or related field or equivalent experience preferred
  • Generally, 7+ years proven success in media sales
  • Experience in agency and direct strategic account management, broadcast inventory and digital/video capabilities required
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:


  • Demonstrated aptitude for informal leadership and mentoring; fosters open dialogue, empowers others, addresses conflict quickly and directly
  • Strong coaching and feedback skills
  • Strong ability to motivate others toward team goals
  • Able to foster an environment that enables creative and innovative thinking
  • Strong influencing, selling and upselling skills
  • Effective teamwork and collaboration skills
  • Very strong analysis and data interpretation - able to help others translate needs and research data into sound marketing proposals
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills
  • Outstanding presentation abilities (in person/virtual, small/large groups, all levels)
  • Strong time management and organization skills
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel and PowerPoint)
  • Working knowledge of Google Office (Sheets, Docs, Slides) and virtual conferencing platforms (E.g. Skype, WebEx, Zoom or MS Teams etc.)
  • Proven ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment
  • May require some travel

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Cleveland is a city that surprises — a place where world-class culture, passionate sports fandom, and a thriving food scene come together on the shores of Lake Erie. The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, the Cleveland Museum of Art, and Playhouse Square (the largest performing arts center outside of New York City) give the city a cultural footprint that punches well above its weight. Cleveland's neighborhoods — from the electric energy of the Flats and East 4th Street to the eclectic charm of Tremont and Ohio City — each bring something unique, with independent restaurants, craft breweries, and local markets around every corner.


Sports are a way of life here. Clevelanders bleed orange and brown for the NFL's Browns, cheer on the Guardians at Progressive Field, and pack Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse for Cavaliers basketball. Beyond the stadiums, the region offers beautiful outdoor escapes — from the winding trails of the Cuyahoga Valley National Park to the beaches and marinas along Lake Erie. With a cost of living well below most major metros and a genuine sense of community pride, Cleveland is a city that's easy to love and even easier to call home.

job.title: Meteorologist, KGTV
job.description:
KGTV, The E.W. Scripps Company ABC affiliate in San Diego, CA, is looking for a skilled and passionate Meteorologist to analyze meteorological data gathered by satellites and radar to prepare reports and forecasts for the public. You'll be the trusted voice that helps San Diegans — from the coastline to the inland valleys — plan their days, stay safe during severe weather, and feel connected to their community. Whether you're delivering a daily weathercast or breaking into programming with an urgent update, your work will have a real and lasting impact across TV, radio, and digital platforms.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Prepare and deliver daily weathercasts utilizing all available weather data and graphics computers.
  • Prepare and deliver urgent weather updates interrupting regular programming as necessary.
  • Prepare and deliver all weathercast materials over a variety of mediums, including, but not limited to: TV, Radio, Internet.
  • Prepare and deliver accurate, timely traffic reports across broadcast and digital platforms, including updates on incidents, road closures, and conditions impacting local commuters.
  • Assist management in evaluations of potential new weather data gathering and presentation computers.
  • Receive assignments or evaluate news leads and news tips to develop story ideas.
  • Report live from event sites or mobile broadcast unit.
  • May write and produce quality news and weather stories for multiple media platforms.
  • May report, write, capture visual content, edit, and produce stories for multiple platforms on deadline, such as Internet and digital channels.
  • Work cooperatively with photographer assigned to story, if one is assigned.
  • Gather and verify factual information regarding stories through interview, observation, and research.
  • Perform other duties as needed and assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • Bachelors degree in Meteorology preferred
  • Generally 3+ years experience in related field preferred
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:


  • Computer literacy, including weather and newsroom computer systems
  • Knowledge of broadcast quality camera equipment
  • Knowledge of editing systems
  • Strong broadcast and AP style writing skills
  • Proficient at posting content to various websites
  • Self-motivated and able to work in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

San Diego is one of the most enviable places to live in the country, and for good reason. With its year-round Mediterranean climate, stunning Pacific beaches, and iconic landmarks like Balboa Park, the world-famous San Diego Zoo, and the historic Gaslamp Quarter, the city offers a lifestyle that's hard to match. Whether you're catching waves at La Jolla Shores, hiking the bluffs at Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve, or exploring the vibrant food scene in North Park and Barrio Logan, there's always something new to discover.


San Diego is also a proud sports city, home to the MLB's San Diego Padres at Petco Park and the newest addition to the local sports landscape, San Diego FC of MLS. The craft beer scene is legendary — with pioneering breweries like Stone Brewing and Ballast Point putting the city on the national map. The city's close proximity to the Pacific coast, mountains, desert, and the international border with Tijuana, Mexico, makes it one of the most geographically diverse metros in the nation.


Beyond the beaches and burritos, San Diego boasts a thriving tech and biotech industry, world-class universities, and a strong military community that gives the city a deeply patriotic and community-minded spirit. It's a place where big-city energy meets laid-back coastal living — and once you're here, it's easy to see why so many people never want to leave.

As the trusted voice that keeps the Treasure Valley informed and safe, you'll be at the forefront of weather coverage in one of the most dynamic and growing markets in the Mountain West.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Prepare and deliver daily weathercasts utilizing all available weather data and graphics computers.

  • Prepare and deliver urgent weather updates interrupting regular programming as necessary.

  • Knowledge of editing systems

  • Strong broadcast and AP style writing skills

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK AND PLAY:

Boise, Idaho offers an unbeatable quality of life where outdoor adventure meets urban sophistication. As one of the fastest-growing cities in America, Boise combines small-town charm with big-city amenities. The city sits at the base of the stunning Boise Foothills, offering immediate access to world-class hiking, mountain biking, and skiing at Bogus Basin—just 16 miles from downtown. The Boise River Greenbelt winds through the heart of the city, providing 25 miles of scenic pathways perfect for running, cycling, or leisurely strolls.

Downtown Boise boasts a thriving food and craft beer scene, vibrant arts and culture including the Boise Philharmonic and Idaho Shakespeare Festival, and professional sports with the Boise State Broncos. The city enjoys four distinct seasons with over 200 days of sunshine annually, making it perfect for year-round outdoor recreation. With a growing tech sector, affordable cost of living compared to other Western cities, and a welcoming community atmosphere, Boise truly offers the best of both worlds—urban energy and natural beauty at your doorstep.

job.title: Multimedia Accountability Reporter, KTNV
job.description:
Scripps-owned KTNV is looking for a Multimedia Accountability Reporter who believes journalism should do more than fill a newscast. You’re a creative, curious storyteller who wants to uncover what’s really happening in Las Vegas, hold the powerful accountable and produce work that can make a difference in people’s lives. You’ll have the freedom to dig deeper, follow compelling leads and find fresh ways to bring important stories to life across broadcast, digital, social and emerging storytelling platforms. Whether you’re analyzing data, working sources, shooting in the field or experimenting with a new way to tell a story, you’ll focus on journalism that connects with audiences wherever they are. If you want to push beyond the traditional reporter playbook and create ambitious, memorable journalism with purpose, this is your opportunity.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Develop original news leads and tips, cultivating sources and identifying accountability stories with meaningful impact for the Las Vegas community.
  • Investigate issues through in-depth reporting, public records, research, data and interviews to uncover facts and provide important context.
  • Analyze databases, statistics and other complex information to identify trends, verify facts and strengthen reporting.
  • Gather and verify information through interviews, observation, research and field reporting while maintaining high journalistic standards.
  • Write and produce compelling, accurate stories for broadcast, digital, social and other multimedia platforms, often on deadline.
  • Shoot video and still photography and edit visual content to create complete, engaging multimedia stories.
  • Deliver polished on-camera reporting, including live reports, taped interviews, narration and breaking-news coverage from the field.
  • Own stories from idea through publication, determining the strongest focus, structure, visuals and storytelling approach for each platform.
  • Collaborate with photographers, producers, digital teams and newsroom colleagues to strengthen coverage and maximize the reach and impact of reporting.
  • Contribute to daily news coverage while balancing enterprise and accountability reporting that may require longer-term research and development.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • BS/BA in journalism, communications or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience, preferred.
  • Generally, 5+ years of journalism or related experience preferred, including experience reporting, writing and producing stories across multiple platforms.
  • Valid driver’s license, good driving record and ability to provide proof of insurance meeting company-required limits are required. This position requires driving as part of the job.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Strong investigative instincts, curiosity and the persistence to keep digging when a story demands more.
  • Advanced critical-thinking and research skills, with the ability to make sense of complicated subjects, statistics and records.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills and a strong command of compelling, accurate storytelling.
  • A confident and engaging on-air presence, including the ability to communicate clearly during live and breaking coverage.
  • Multimedia skills and the willingness to report, shoot, write, edit and produce content across platforms.
  • The ability to juggle daily assignments, enterprise reporting and multiple developing stories in a fast-paced newsroom while consistently meeting deadlines.
  • A collaborative mindset and commitment to working effectively with journalists and colleagues throughout the station.
  • Sound editorial judgment and a commitment to accuracy, fairness, verification and accountability journalism.

OUR TEAM:

At KTNV, you’ll join a collaborative newsroom focused on serving the Las Vegas community with journalism that informs, explains and creates impact. Our team brings together journalists with different backgrounds, perspectives, experiences and interests, united by curiosity and a commitment to telling stories that matter. We value colleagues who share ideas, support one another, embrace multiple forms of storytelling and believe great local journalism starts with listening to the community.


WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Las Vegas is much more than the Strip. It’s a fast-growing, diverse community with an endless supply of meaningful stories, from local government and education to housing, growth, water, public safety and the issues affecting neighborhoods across Southern Nevada. For an accountability reporter, it’s a dynamic market where strong local journalism can make a real difference.

When you’re off the clock, Southern Nevada offers world-class dining, entertainment and professional sports alongside incredible outdoor experiences. Red Rock Canyon, Lake Mead and the surrounding desert and mountains put hiking, climbing, cycling and weekend adventures within easy reach, while Las Vegas provides the energy, culture and experiences of a destination known around the world.

job.title: Multimedia Journalist, KERO - Kern River Valley
job.description:
At KERO 23 ABC, we believe every community deserves a journalist who knows its people, understands its challenges, and tells its stories with authenticity. As our Multimedia Journalist serving California's Kern River Valley, you'll be more than a reporter, you'll be the trusted voice covering a region whose stories often go untold by larger markets. This role is designed for someone who thrives working independently, building relationships, and becoming part of the fabric of a close-knit community. Nestled around Lake Isabella and surrounded by some of California's most stunning outdoor recreation, the Kern River Valley offers a unique lifestyle for journalists who value adventure, connection, and meaningful local storytelling. You'll have the opportunity to shine a spotlight on the issues, triumphs, and people that make this region special while ensuring local residents see their communities represented in the news every day.WHAT YOU'LL DO:
  • Develop and pitch original story ideas that are relevant to Kern River Valley communities.
  • Research, write, shoot, and edit daily news stories for multiple platforms.
  • Deliver accurate, engaging live reports from the field.
  • Cultivate sources and build strong relationships with community leaders and residents.
  • Report on breaking news, public safety issues, weather impacts, and community events.
  • Produce compelling digital content, including videos, articles, and social media updates.
  • Work closely with producers, assignment editors, photographers, and newsroom leadership.
  • Generate enterprising story content that reflects the needs and interests of local audiences.
  • Meet daily deadlines while maintaining high journalistic standards.
  • Represent KERO professionally at community events and public appearances.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:
  • Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Communications, or a related field preferred.
  • Previous reporting, multimedia journalism, or newsroom experience required.
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and the ability to travel throughout the coverage area.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:
  • Strong storytelling, writing, and on-camera presentation skills.
  • Ability to shoot and edit video content independently.
  • Sound news judgment and a commitment to accuracy, fairness, and ethics.
  • Excellent organizational and time-management skills.
  • A passion for community-focused journalism and audience engagement.
  • Confidence working in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
  • Proficiency with digital publishing tools, social media platforms, and mobile journalism techniques.
  • Ability to adapt quickly to breaking news situations and changing priorities.
  • Willingness to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as news coverage requires.
  • Ability to safely lift and carry standard field reporting equipment and work outdoors in varying weather conditions.

OUR TEAM:The KERO 23 ABC newsroom is made up of dedicated journalists who care deeply about the communities they serve. We're collaborative, innovative, and driven by a shared mission to deliver accurate, impactful local news. Our team brings diverse experiences, perspectives, and talents together to create meaningful journalism that informs, connects, and empowers viewers across Kern County and beyond.WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:Nestled along the scenic Kern River and surrounded by mountains, lakes, and outdoor recreation, the Kern River Valley offers a unique lifestyle for adventurous storytellers. The area is known for its tight-knit communities, stunning natural beauty, and year-round opportunities for hiking, fishing, boating, camping, and exploring the outdoors.You'll live and work in a region rich with local character and compelling stories, while remaining connected to the broader Bakersfield market. From community celebrations and small-town traditions to important issues affecting local residents, you'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact through your reporting every day.#LI-SM2#LI-Onsite

job.title: Multimedia Journalist, KJRH
job.description:
KJRH, the NBC station in Tulsa, Oklahoma, owned by The E.W. Scripps Company is looking to hire an aggressive and engaging Multimedia Journalist. The MMJ is responsible for researching, writing, capturing visual content, and editing stories for multiple platforms. Tulsa offers a low cost of living and the kinds of stories you’ll be eager to tell. The city is rich with history, has a booming arts and entertainment scene, a popular zoo, and a strong economy. The leadership in this award-winning newsroom will support your career and help you grow as a journalist. Apply today!


WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Receive assignments or evaluate news leads and news tips to develop story ideas.
  • Gather and verify factual information regarding stories through interview, observation, and research.
  • Organize material, determine slant or emphasis, and write stories according to prescribed editorial style and format standards.
  • Shoot video and still photos to illustrate stories.
  • Edit, or assist in editing, videos for all multimedia platforms.
  • Appear on TV during news and other station broadcasts.
  • Go live from scenes and sites of events.
  • Work cooperatively with photographer assigned to story, if one is assigned.
  • Assist news producer in preparing newscast.
  • Assist online staff in preparing multimedia stories.
  • Report, write, capture quality visual content, edit, and produce stories for multiple platforms on deadline, such as Internet and digital channels.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • BS/BA in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Generally, 3+ years of experience in related field preferred

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:


  • Computer literacy required, including newsroom computer systems
  • Videography and non-linear editing experience preferred
  • Knowledge of broadcast-quality camera equipment
  • Edit video on Final Cut Pro editing systems, or similar equipment
  • Strong broadcast and AP style writing skills
  • Proficient at posting content to various websites
  • Self-motivated and able to work in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company's required insurance limits

job.title: Multimedia Journalist, KNXV
job.description:
We're looking for a storyteller who can do it all — shoot, write, report and most importantly - connect with the community. KNXV, ABC 15 in Phoenix, Arizona, is looking for a talented Multimedia Journalist to join our newsroom. At ABC 15, you'll be more than a journalist — you'll be a one-person powerhouse who brings the stories of the Valley of the Sun to life across television and digital platforms. From breaking news to in-depth community coverage, your work will inform, inspire and make a real difference in the lives of viewers across one of the nation's fastest-growing markets.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Receive assignment or evaluate news leads and news tips to develop story ideas.
  • Gather and verify factual information regarding stories through interview, observation, and research.
  • Organize material, determine slant or emphasis, and write story according to prescribed editorial style and format standards.
  • Shoot video and still photos to illustrate stories.
  • Edit, or assists in editing, videos for all multimedia platforms.
  • Appear on television program when conducting taped interview or narration
  • Give live reports from site of event or mobile broadcast unit.
  • Work cooperatively with photographer assigned to story, if one is assigned.
  • Assist news producer in preparing newscast.
  • Assist online staff in preparing for multi media stories.

 

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • BS/BA in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Generally, 3+ years of experience in related field preferred

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Computer literacy required, including newsroom computer systems
  • Videography and non-linear editing experience preferred
  • Knowledge of broadcast quality camera equipment
  • Edit video on Final Cut Pro editing systems, or similar equipment
  • Strong broadcast and AP style writing skills
  • Proficient at posting content to various websites
  • Self-motivated and able to work in a fast-paced deadline-driven environment
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Phoenix is one of America's most exciting and sun-soaked cities, offering an extraordinary quality of life for those who call it home. With more than 300 days of sunshine a year, the Valley of the Sun is a playground for outdoor enthusiasts — whether you're hiking the iconic trails of Camelback Mountain and South Mountain Park, kayaking along the Salt River, or exploring the stunning red rocks just a short drive away in Sedona. The sprawling Sonoran Desert landscape is unlike anywhere else on earth, and it's right at your doorstep.

Beyond the outdoors, the downtown arts district offers a vibrant scene that includes the Phoenix Art Museum, one of the largest in the Southwest, as well as the Musical Instrument Museum — a one-of-a-kind destination that draws visitors from around the globe. The local food scene reflects the city's rich cultural diversity, from authentic Sonoran-style Mexican cuisine and acclaimed farm-to-table restaurants to a thriving craft brewery and coffee culture. The city also hosts beloved annual events like the Barrett-Jackson car auction and the Waste Management Phoenix Open, one of the most attended sporting events in the world.

For sports fans, Phoenix is a major-league city all the way, home to the NFL's Cardinals, the NBA's Suns, the WNBA's Mercury, the NHL's Coyotes, and MLB's Diamondbacks. With a booming economy, a young and diverse population, and world-class amenities at every turn, Phoenix isn't just a great place to work — it's a phenomenal place to build a life.

job.title: Multimedia Journalist, KRTV
job.description:
At KRTV, we tell the stories that matter most to the communities we serve. As a Multimedia Journalist, you'll research, report, shoot, write, edit, and deliver compelling local news content across multiple platforms. You'll be at the center of breaking news, community events, and impactful storytelling, helping viewers stay informed and connected.


This role offers the opportunity to build strong relationships throughout the Great Falls community while developing engaging content for broadcast, digital, and social audiences. If you're a passionate storyteller who thrives in a fast-paced newsroom, we'd love to hear from you.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Research, develop, and pitch story ideas from news leads, tips, and community sources.
  • Gather and verify information through interviews, observation, and independent research.
  • Write clear, accurate, and engaging stories that meet broadcast and digital editorial standards.
  • Capture high-quality video and still photography to support storytelling efforts.
  • Edit video content for television broadcasts, websites, social media channels, and other multimedia platforms.
  • Deliver live reports from the scene of breaking news, community events, and special coverage.
  • Appear on-air for interviews, narrations, and news presentations.
  • Collaborate with photographers, producers, and newsroom colleagues to create compelling content.
  • Assist producers with newscast preparation and content development.
  • Partner with digital teams to publish and promote stories across multiple platforms.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Communications, or a related field preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Three or more years of journalism, reporting, multimedia, or related experience preferred.
  • Valid driver's license, strong driving record, and the ability to provide proof of insurance that meets company requirements.
  • Ability to travel locally for assignments and drive company or personal vehicles as needed.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:


  • Strong broadcast writing skills with knowledge of AP Style.
  • Experience with videography and non-linear editing systems preferred.
  • Working knowledge of broadcast-quality camera equipment.
  • Experience editing video using Final Cut Pro or similar editing platforms.
  • Proficiency with newsroom computer systems and digital publishing tools.
  • Ability to post and manage content across websites and digital platforms.
  • Strong organizational, communication, and storytelling skills.
  • A self-starter mindset with the ability to work independently and collaboratively.
  • Comfort working in a fast-paced, deadline-driven news environment.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds.

OUR TEAM:


At KRTV, you'll join a passionate team of journalists, storytellers, content creators, and community advocates dedicated to delivering trusted local news. We value collaboration, curiosity, innovation, and integrity. Our newsroom brings together people with diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives who share a commitment to serving viewers and making a meaningful impact across north-central Montana.


WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:


Great Falls offers an exceptional quality of life with easy access to some of the most breathtaking landscapes in the American West. Situated along the Missouri River and surrounded by Montana's natural beauty, the area provides endless opportunities for outdoor recreation, including hiking, fishing, camping, skiing, and wildlife exploration.


Whether you're enjoying local restaurants, exploring nearby state parks, visiting cultural attractions, or taking in panoramic mountain views, Great Falls combines small-town friendliness with big outdoor adventure. It's an ideal place for journalists who enjoy connecting with their communities while experiencing all that Montana has to offer.

job.title: Multimedia Journalist, KSBY (Santa Maria/North Santa Barbara County)
job.description:
KSBY, The E.W. Scripps Company NBC station in beautiful San Luis Obispo, California, is looking for a creative, driven and community-focused Multimedia Journalist to join our North Santa Barbara County team. If you are passionate about telling impactful stories that engage people across broadcast, digital, and social platforms, this is a chance to bring your talent to a station that is committed to public service journalism. As a beat reporter based out of Santa Maria, you'll cover towns and cities along California's stunning Central Coast - a vibrant region packed with breathtaking scenery and diverse cultures.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Receive assignment or evaluate news leads and news tips to develop story ideas.
  • Gather and verify factual information regarding stories through interview, observation, and research.
  • Organize material, determine slant or emphasis, and write story according to prescribed editorial style and format standards.
  • Shoot video and still photos to illustrate stories.
  • Edit, or assists in editing, videos for all multimedia platforms.
  • Appear on television program when conducting taped interview or narration.
  • Give live reports from site of event or mobile broadcast unit.
  • Work cooperatively with photographer assigned to story, if one is assigned.
  • Assist news producer in preparing newscast.
  • Assist online staff in preparing for multi media stories.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • BS/BA in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Generally, 3+ years of experience in related field preferred
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:


  • Computer literacy required, including newsroom computer systems
  • Videography and non-linear editing experience preferred
  • Knowledge of broadcast quality camera equipment
  • Edit video on Final Cut Pro editing systems, or similar equipment
  • Strong broadcast and AP style writing skills
  • Bilingual (Spanish/English) skills, preferred
  • Proficient at posting content to various websites
  • Self-motivated and able to work in a fast-paced deadline-driven environment
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Santa Maria puts you in the heart of California's beautiful Central Coast, surrounded by rolling vineyards, scenic open spaces, and easy access to the Pacific. Located in northern Santa Barbara County, Santa Maria Valley offers the relaxed feel of California wine country while serving as a convenient home base for exploring the Central Coast.


Food and wine are a big part of the Santa Maria experience. The region is known for its distinctive Santa Maria-style barbecue tradition, featuring meats grilled over native red oak, and the surrounding Santa Maria Valley is home to wineries and tasting rooms producing acclaimed Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Syrah, and more. The Foxen Canyon Wine Trail winds through the valley, offering another way to experience the area's vineyards and landscape.


If you love the outdoors, you'll have plenty to explore. Santa Maria Valley combines mild weather and wide-open spaces with opportunities for hiking, cycling, golfing, birdwatching, and beach trips. When you're ready for a change of scenery, the surrounding Central Coast offers everything from ocean views and coastal adventures to wine-country escapes.


For a journalist, Santa Maria also offers the chance to live and work directly in the community you're covering, while enjoying everything that makes California's Central Coast such an appealing place to call home. It's a great fit for someone looking for a mix of local community, outdoor adventure, food and wine, and the California coastal lifestyle.
