job.title: Director, Post Production Operations & Support
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The New York Times is continuing to expand its video journalism, identifying compelling video and audio stories across the depth and breadth of our report. We showcase the expertise of Times journalists on-camera, share urgent news updates, produce on-the-ground reporting, pioneering Visual Investigations, and Shows. We are looking for a Director of Post Production Operations and Support to oversee the video post-production workflows, systems, and technical support that enable reliable newsroom video and show production at scale. This role sits within the newsroom's Media Operations team, works across all field and studio production, and manages a team of post production and technical specialists charged with developing, implementing, and supporting best-in-class workflows for our video journalism.

You will report to the Head of Media Operations and partner closely with the senior leaders overseeing our video journalism, the Director of Studios, and the leaders of production management, editorial operations, and cinematography. You are a collaborative, supportive leader with excellent communication skills and a future-oriented approach.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the Post Production Operations and Support function supporting all newsroom shows and video journalism produced globally (current video operations in New York, Washington, D.C., Los Angeles, San Francisco, London, and Seoul)

  • Design, implement, and continuously optimize end-to-end post-production workflows to support fast-turnaround breaking news, Shows, Reporter Video, Field production, and long-form Visual InvestigationsWorkflows including but not limited to: ingest, cloud asset management, cloud edit, captioning and graphics, and finishing/publishing

  • Lead the ongoing transition to cloud and automated workflows to minimize friction for studio and remote production

  • Manage, develop, and grow the global post production operations and support team, including career development, performance management, hiring and training

  • Partner with the Director of Studios on production readiness and the integration of studio systems with post-production and publishing workflows

  • Partner with the IT and Networking functions to manage and scale post-production infrastructure, ranging from storage to high-speed file transfer systems

  • Partner with the Audio Engineering team to unify holistic Audio and Video post workflows

  • Oversee current and future vendor relationships across video and multimedia software, cloud services, media asset management and related services, ensuring production teams have best-in-class tools at their disposal

  • Oversee the implementation and continuous customization of our MAM, to ensure our teams have workflows that best suit their needs, and that all video assets are properly tagged, searchable, and archived

  • Establish, socialize, and maintain quality control standards for color, and other disciplines central to publishing video assets

  • Collaborate closely with Editorial leadership to align post-production resources with editorial priorities and initiatives

  • Maintain current documentation, training and technical onboarding for producers, editors, journalists, engineers and other newsroom partners

  • Establish coverage, escalation and incident-response protocols for breaking news, major events, live productions and after-hours Show support

  • Track operational measures including incident response and resolution, system reliability and quality control, and stakeholder satisfaction

  • Partner with Media Operations leadership on annual budgets, procurement, vendor management, lifecycle planning and resource allocation

  • Source and manage freelance technical and post-production support where needed

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

  • You will report to the Head of Media Operations

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience in video post-production operations

  • 5+ years of management experience

  • Experience supporting both studio and field production

  • Proven deep knowledge of production and post-production systems, media asset management, cloud workflows, networking and digital publishing workflows

  • Proven ability to build and continuously improve scalable systems while supporting urgent, deadline-driven production

  • Demonstrated experience managing technology budgets, vendors, procurement and equipment lifecycles

  • Proven experience leading technical teams in a fast-moving newsroom, media or broadcast environment

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Newsroom experience is strongly preferred

  • Experience supporting shows, podcasts, episodic content or other repeatable multimedia production

  • Strong leadership and collaboration skills, with a record of motivating teams, attracting and developing talent, and working effectively across the newsroom

  • Excellent operational, organizational and communication skills, including the ability to manage competing deadlines and translate complex technical issues for non-technical stakeholders

  • A systems-oriented problem solver who can develop scalable solutions while remaining calm under pressure

  • Willingness to manage or provide after-hours, night and weekend incident or coverage support as breaking news requires

  • Knowledge of The Times' digital video competitors and the video landscape

job.title: Director, Strategic Partnerships
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The Strategic Partnerships team develops, executes and manages partnerships with The Times's most important partners to support our journalistic and commercial goals. This includes subscription-growth oriented partnerships, large licensing deals, complex, multi-faceted deals, as well as managing our relationships with the biggest tech platforms who determine how we reach audiences and distribute our content and products.

As the Director of Strategic Partnerships, you will come with a sharp understanding of and deep interest in the evolving digital ecosystem, including the role of generative AI across audience and technology; how platforms work with respect to social and search audiences; be adept at looking at data to understand performance and trends; be a very strong communicator; and have a deep interest in collaborative work. You'll have experience in working across teams to evaluate new commercial opportunities, and you'll be adept at forming and managing strong relationships with partners.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters, reporting to the Vice President of Strategic Partnerships. You can typically expect to come into the office 3+ days/week.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop, nurture, and manage relationships with the largest tech companies and other strategic partners to advance The Times's objectives
  • Lead complex deals that span multiple parts of the business including subscriptions, IP licensing (including AI licensing), product integrations and advertising, developing deal frameworks, financial analysis, negotiation strategies, and execution plans
  • Work with The Times's newsroom and product teams to support content distribution strategies and opportunities
  • Actively manage relationships between The Times executives and strategic partners
  • Monitor industry trends, platform and tech developments, and prepare and present executive-level communications about them
  • Manage and maintain relationships with key stakeholders and partners, and participate in meetings with senior executives at The Times and at the platforms
  • Be able to engage in lateral leadership and drive results from cross-functional teams
  • Prepare executive briefing materials and facilitate meetings with internal stakeholders and develop detailed communications strategies for internal stakeholders that the entire team implements
  • Ensure the smooth management of deals and partner relationships post-execution
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience in business development, digital media publishing, or digital product development
  • Experience in a partnerships role at a publisher
  • Demonstrated interest in and understanding of news media, social platforms, and Generative AI technologies and their markets
  • Experience executing deals from start to finish — including sourcing deals, building deal frameworks, opportunity analysis, contracting, and execution
  • Excellent operational skills to execute strategies and cross-functional teamwork
  • Deep interest, understanding, and attention to market developments
  • Experience leveraging a network of industry relationships to unlock new partnership opportunities and strategic initiatives

Preferred Qualifications:

  • MBA or JD is preferred
  • Demonstrated expertise in the dynamics of digital subscription models

job.description:

It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The New York Times advertising department's mission is to create work that helps brands make their mark in the world, and our canvas is the full breadth of The New York Times and its associated media platforms, including digital, mobile, audio, print, events and more.

The Advertising Strategy team's award-winning work includes activations across digital, audio, and print and spans the breadth of NYT's portfolio, like Cooking, Wirecutter, Games, and The Athletic, as well as our premier editorial events like the Dealbook conference.

The Director, Strategy will bring experience working cross-category and possess a passion for uncovering how different categories intersect with media and culture to spark inspiring creative ways-in and ideas. Strategy is a team sport, and you will be an expert collaborator with experience leading versatile teams, including creative, program management, sales, and planning, toward a common goal. Success within the advertising strategy team requires the ability to uncover human and cultural truths across multiple categories like finance, media, entertainment, healthcare, and consumer goods as well as a passion for big ideas expressed through media, a love of The New York Times, and a high standard for creating visual presentations.

  • Management and Mentorship: You are a skilled manager with practice and proficiency in teaching and guiding teams through the strategic process.
  • Operational Skills: You have some experience with strategic resourcing of team members and managing stakeholders around workflows
  • Research, Insights, and Creative Brief Development: You are an expert at using proprietary tools, third-party resources and desk research to uncover meaningful insights, human truths and whitespace opportunities that will lead to a compelling way in for creative and media.
  • Creative Briefing: You are experienced in writing compelling creative briefs, briefing creative teams, and being an inspiring strategic partner to creative teams.
  • Media Strategy: You are experienced in making recommendations for how to use media to bring ideas to life in ways that meet clients' campaign objectives. Although you will not be responsible for writing media plans, you are comfortable and expert in guiding internal teams as well as clients in making smart and creative media choices.
  • Client Deliverable Development: You are experienced in owning and creating client-ready visual proposals that are polished and inspiring.
  • Category Fluency: You are constantly learning and reading about macro trends in business and culture.

Responsibilities:

  • Manage 3-6 strategists across 2-3 Categories
  • Co-lead resourcing across the Strategy Team
  • Consult with Sales leadership to improve processes, practices and strategic deliverables
  • Engage with teams across the Ad Department to guide cross-functional solutions and innovations
  • Use research and data to articulate and support sales stories
  • Author and deliver creative briefs on sometimes-tight turnarounds
  • Create and guide others in the creation of powerful proposals with effective storytelling that responds to client needs and telegraphs the value of NYT media offerings
  • Develop a broad understanding of all New York Times assets
  • Lead and project manage across relevant departments (including Sales, Ad Product, T Brand Studio, Ad Operations, Research, Marketing, Events) to create integrated programs for clients
  • Develop, articulate and share innovative programs, partnerships, innovations and opportunities
  • Research, write, and guide others in the creation of content strategy briefs
  • Attend key sales calls to pitch advertising and media ideas to mid/senior-level executives
  • Manage internal senior team members, communicating proposal and program status to management
  • Educate and keep the Strategy team/department abreast of trends and what opportunities or challenges they might present for our business
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Executive Strategy Director

Basic Qualifications:

  • 12+ years of cross-platform Advertising experience in brand and media strategy
  • Interest in managing high-volume categories
  • Experience working on RFPs
  • Experience working in collaborative sales and marketing processes, including working with sales teams or in a sales environment
  • An understanding of the current social, branded content, digital, audio and mobile media landscapes
  • Experience with how to translate the long-term goals of advertisers into solutions and recommendations that can be provided by The New York Times

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree or equivalent work experience

job.title: Editorial Design Intern, Wirecutter
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the position 

Wirecutter strives to be the most trusted product recommendation service on the internet. We obsessively test and report on thousands of items each year to recommend the best of everything. Our goal is to save you time and eliminate the stress of shopping, whether you’re looking for everyday gear or gifts for loved ones. We work with total editorial independence. That means nothing appears on the site as a recommendation unless our writers and editors have deemed it the best through our rigorous reporting and testing.

We are seeking an inventive and motivated intern to join our creative team. In this role, you will learn the ins and outs of our growing, thriving editorial organization and collaborate with different teams to understand and participate in our process.

We also build shared behavioral data products, such as Pageviews, Sessions, and client-side Interactions, so core reader behaviors can be measured consistently across missions and standalone experiences. Mission teams remain accountable for their domain data while we work alongside them as a forward-deployed team to help them onboard and publish.   • Develop and maintain budgets, forecasts and a cost attribution model for your team's cloud solutions

  • Ability to jump in as needed to assist technically with code reviews, design discussions, and analysis
  • Experience using SQL to transform data and a working knowledge of at least one of: Python, Java or Go

job.title: Fellow, A.I. Initiatives
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Join the 2027 New York Times Fellowship class as an A.I. Initiatives fellow in New York.

We are looking for a fellow who will bring a mix of machine-learning and journalism experience to newsroom reporting projects. You will work with journalists across departments to identify, develop and execute projects that use the power of artificial intelligence, machine learning and data science techniques to address investigative challenges. You will be part of the A.I. Initiatives team, which includes editors, engineers and a product designer.

This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. You may be required to work some nights, weekends and holidays as needed.

Responsibilities: 

  • Collaborate with investigative reporters to support projects that benefit from A.I., including large-scale research, transcription, translation, document search, language analysis and computer vision tasks
  • Identify opportunities and experiment with responsible A.I. tools to empower the newsroom
  • Participate in training and social programs designed for the fellowship
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • No more than five years of full-time, professional experience in journalism and/or machine learning
  • Technical proficiency and experience analyzing data, developing applications and conducting research with machine-learning models
  • Editorial experience, such as interning in a newsroom or working on a college newspaper
  • Engineering skills and experience with APIs, front-end web applications and databases
  • Recent experience working with LLMs and other machine-learning models
  • Interest in the intersection of journalism and artificial intelligence
  • Understanding of ethical considerations surrounding the use of A.I. in journalism

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Record of multiple news or opinion journalism internships, or equivalent experience
  • Work demonstrating experience applying A.I. to real-world problems
  • Experience working with large datasets and cloud computing platforms
  • Experience working with Svelte or similar front-end frameworks

To apply, upload a résumé and cover letter. The application will prompt you when to upload materials. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered.

You must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor work visas for the fellowship, but we will consider applicants with valid work authorization or a valid student visa that can be extended with Optional Practical Training.

You may apply to only one fellowship position per year. For instance, if you apply as an A.I. Initiatives fellow, you should not apply for any other positions in the fellowship. Duplicate applications will be discarded.

The application deadline is 5 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on Nov. 20. 

The Times Fellowship generates a high level of interest, so we cannot acknowledge the status of every application upon receipt or during the vetting process, which can take eight weeks or more. We cannot accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us. We will contact you for interviews as needed.

The fellowship program will begin on or about June 7, 2027, and end on May 26, 2028, subject to satisfactory performance. There is no guarantee of a full-time position upon completion of the program. 

For more information about the Times Fellowship, visit here.

 

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of New York.

And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Join the 2027 New York Times Fellowship class as a member of the Audience team in New York. 

As an Audience fellow, you will get a comprehensive understanding of how The Times approaches off- and on-platform audience development and engagement. You should be willing to partner with colleagues across the newsroom and the strategy, product, data and marketing teams.

The fellowship will be divided into rotations with the departments that make up the Audience team:

  • Off platform: You will develop social strategy, visual, copy/framing and news-judgment skills. You will help track trends, shape live coverage on breaking storylines, and optimize headlines and links. 
  • On platform: You will engage readers on our owned surfaces, contributing to our expanding community efforts, as well as through home screen and email engagement.
  • Data and audience insights: You will gain an understanding of our analytics and our audience — whom we reach and whom we need to engage. You also will learn data-literacy skills and work to help desks optimize coverage.


This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. You may be required to work some nights, weekends and holidays as needed.

Responsibilities:

  • Write social copy and help shape how we share our journalism on social, analyze our presence and strategy on existing platforms, and evaluate opportunities on new social platforms
  • Interpret data and signals to shape how we present stories on and off our platforms
  • Optimize stories for search, and identify trending topics and competitive trends 
  • Work on projects to deepen engagement on our owned surfaces, including the home screen, push alerts, email and community products
  • Partner with the newsroom audience analytics team on deep and actionable analysis
  • Participate in training and social programs designed for the fellowship
  • Collaborate with colleagues across the newsroom
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • No more than five years of full-time, professional journalism experience, excluding internships
  • Experience writing in an engaging, smart tone that feels native to social media and is consistent with the values of independent journalism
  • Experience looking at and interpreting data 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Record of multiple news internships or equivalent experience
  • An understanding of all mainstream and some emerging social channels, and a willingness to learn about new platforms
  • Comfort with data and testing, and with iterating to find what resonates with different audiences

To apply, upload a résumé and cover letter. The application will prompt you when to upload materials. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered.

You must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor work visas for the fellowship, but we will consider applicants with valid work authorization or a valid student visa that can be extended with Optional Practical Training.

You may apply to only one fellowship position per year. For instance, if you apply as an audience fellow, you should not apply for any other positions in the fellowship. Duplicate applications will be discarded.

The application deadline is 5 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on Nov. 20. 

The Times Fellowship generates a high level of interest, so we cannot acknowledge the status of applications upon receipt or during the vetting process, which can take eight weeks or more. We cannot accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us. We will contact you for interviews as needed.

The fellowship program will begin on or about June 7, 2027, and end on May 26, 2028, subject to satisfactory performance. There is no guarantee of a full-time position upon completion of the program.

You will be part of the Election Analytics team, which produces The New York Times/Siena University Poll, the live election-night forecast known as The Needle and our polling tracker, in addition to stories that explore voter decisions and analyze past elections.

Election Analytics is an interdisciplinary team of reporters, editors, developers and statisticians. You should have experience working in one of these areas and be excited to learn about the others. You will use your knowledge of elections and voting to contribute to stories, graphics and our longer-term projects.

The exact form of this role will depend on your background. Perhaps you are more comfortable writing than coding and want to deepen your technical skills to more easily answer questions yourself. Or perhaps you bring a background as a developer or statistician and want to work on your ability to communicate your ideas in words.

  • Contribute original analyses of polls, voter registration trends and recent election results for articles or graphics
  • Increase the team’s understanding of elections through data collection, scraping, statistical analysis and reporting 
  • Participate in training and social programs designed for the fellowship
  • Collaborate with colleagues across the newsroom
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

  • No more than five years of full-time, professional journalism experience, excluding internships
  • A deep and demonstrated understanding of American elections
  • Experience working with data
  • Expertise in at least one of the team’s focus areas: 
    • Data-driven reporting, including reporting clips or blog posts that demonstrate analytical findings meant for a broad audience 
    • Statistics, including experience developing statistical models in R or Python
    • Development, including proficiency in R or Python, experience working with cloud computing providers and experience building productionized web applications 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience writing news stories, such as for a college newspaper

Join the 2027 New York Times fellowship as a video journalist in New York.

You will have a focus in two areas: producing videos for our new Watch tab and producing video coverage on our live journalism team. This is a chance to be on the forefront of our newest initiatives and to participate in some of the biggest breaking news stories. You will be part of the first line of defense on developing stories, helping with innovating digital video news and doing ground-level reporting.

You should have newsroom experience and a solid foundation of how to scout social platforms for video content, verify that content and identify video-storytelling opportunities. You should have a grasp of video production, from editing and shooting to scripting. You can work across breaking news, enterprise and investigations.

  • Research and develop news stories for video, including sourcing relevant footage from social media, archives and news wires 
  • Help manage source material, and translation and transcription needs
  • Verify the accuracy and authenticity of media reported across the web and social
  • Contribute to video scripts and social copy 
  • Help coordinate the post-production process for video stories

  • Collaborate with colleagues across the newsroom
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

  • No more than five years of full-time, professional journalism experience, excluding internships
  • Strong news judgment
  • Ability to research, compile and analyze media
  • Familiarity with fact-checking and the ability to parse misinformation and disinformation, and support those findings with evidence
  • Can work with colleagues and reporters to synthesize newsgathering and/or investigations into a tight, informative and engaging video

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in news and media verification and/or fact-checking
  • At least one year of experience as an associate producer or producer in a professional video journalism environment
  • Experience sourcing and verifying news video from social media
  • Experience editing with Adobe Premiere
  • Ability to adapt to change in an unpredictable news and production environment

  • Polish, format and quality-check podcast transcripts, graphics and video elements
  • Respond to changing priorities and demands based on department needs and the news cycle

job.description:

The Upshot is a small, versatile team that publishes analytical and explanatory journalism, often on policy and politics. And we often use data, visuals and interactivity to explain the world in new ways.

As a fellow, you will pitch your own ideas and contribute to group projects in various forms. That work may mean visualizing the Caitlin Clark effect, showing political polarization in action, finding possible insider trading or tracking data centers from the sky.

We are open to proposals on a range of roles. Typically, our fellows come with at least a year of reporting experience (or equivalent), along with technical or domain knowledge — in politics or policy, statistics or data analysis, information graphics, or web development. You don’t need to be an expert with data or technology, but you should be comfortable with it. And you don’t need to be a seasoned beat reporter, but you should be ready to pitch, report and write on complicated topics.

Much of our best work involves working as a team. You should be excited about collaborating with other members of the Upshot and colleagues across the newsroom.

Finally, we want you to know the Upshot and our work. Why do you want to work on this desk, as opposed to a different one? Make clear in your cover letter why the Upshot is the place for you.This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. job.title: Graphics Multimedia Editor, Immersive Researcher
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

The Times has an unparalleled reputation for excellence in visual journalism. We have defined multimedia storytelling for the news industry and established ourselves as the clear leader. Over the past several years, our work with 3D and spatial formats has revealed new and unique opportunities to tell stories that expand our readers’ understanding of the world and help them navigate it.

The New York Times is seeking a temporary Graphics Editor/Developer to explore how Web XR can expand the possibilities of journalism and visual storytelling. This role will sit at the intersection of graphics, visual journalism, design, engineering, and R&D.

You will conduct hands-on research and development, build experimental prototypes, and help establish reproducible approaches for immersive storytelling.

Potential subject areas include climate change, environmental data, science and other complex global issues that benefit from immersive explanation.

The role is designed to advance both published journalism and the wider field through public documentation, open experimentation, and knowledge sharing. In addition to being a part of a team that builds cutting-edge visual experiences, you will collaborate on opportunities to share technical findings, contribute to reproducible approaches for the field, and participate in industry knowledge sharing.

This is a temporary (12 month) in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days a week.

Responsibilities:
  • Conceive, prototype, and test web and WebXR experiences for journalism.
  • Conduct technical experiments across immersive storytelling formats, interaction models, and web-based XR technologies.
  • Develop new methods for translating complex environmental data, systems, and scenarios into understandable immersive experiences.
  • Work with journalists, graphics editors, designers, engineers, and R&D partners to shape concepts from early exploration through prototypes or publication.
  • Apply strong editorial judgment to ensure that immersive experiences are accurate, clear, accessible, and grounded in journalistic principles.
  • Document and share technical decisions, discoveries, and reproducible frameworks throughout the R&D process, disseminating insights to internal teams and the wider creative ecosystem via public posts, conference presentations, peer workshops, or open-source resources.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Special Projects Editor on the Graphics desk.
Basic Requirements:
  • 3+ years of relevant professional experience
  • A portfolio of 3D/immersive work
  • 3D web development
  • Familiarity with Unity or Unreal
  • Expertise in Blender, Maya or Cinema 4D
  • Proficient in 3D modeling, optimization and animation
  • Familiarity with Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop and After Effects and Figma
  • An appetite for experimentation and prototyping
  • Experience translating complex technical workflows, engineering challenges, and 3D graphics concepts into clear, accessible written documentation and case studies.
Preferred Requirements:
  • Experience developing for Apple Vision Pro, Meta Quest or similar HMDs
  • WebXR experience
  • Familiarity with Python and/or Javascript
  • Experience with GLSL a plus
  • Experience using machine learning and AI tools for building 3D scenes and interactions
  • Comfort presenting technical work to diverse audiences, ranging from newsroom journalists and product designers to external developer communities and industry panels.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

job.title: Graphics Multimedia Editor, Shows
job.description:

About the Role

The New York Times' Motion Graphics team focuses on elevating how animated graphics and motion design are used in our video journalism. Working in close collaboration with Video, Shows and Graphics, the team responds to the demands of stories and formats across the newsroom—from news explainers and visual investigations to enterprise series and shows.

As a member of Digital News Design's Motion Graphics team, you will focus on work for Shows, a department created to expand the reach of The Times's audio and video shows. You will collaborate with reporters, editors, producers, art directors and show hosts to craft motion assets and visuals for our expanding roster of shows across a range of formats and platforms.

You will be responsible for identifying creative needs and producing a range of design assets, including motion graphics, typography, animations, and MOGRT templates. In consultation with editors and other newsroom leaders, you'll exercise journalistic judgment and visual creativity to innovate and ensure accuracy, clarity, and validity of the content presented. Design team members are expected not only to make exceptional contributions to our journalism, but also to engage with others to foster an environment of learning and constructive dialogue about our work.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Create original designs and craft video toolkits for a range of shows and show formats.
  • Work collaboratively with show producers, and editors to create engaging and informative videos.
  • Convey visual story ideas and complex information in engaging video sequences and animation.
  • Work alongside other Times design teams to ensure consistent visual languages, and develop best practices.
  • Be a pragmatic innovator whose solutions elicit responses that justify the effort and investment.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Motion Graphics Editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of motion design experience. Expertise with After Effects, designing for motion and animation is essential.
  • Expertise with Figma, Photoshop, Illustrator and Adobe Creative Suite.
  • Strong portfolio of design work.
  • Solid understanding of layout, typography, and storytelling techniques.
  • Experience creating visual presentations that intelligently incorporate audio, video, still images and text.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Enthusiasm for designing and making great animations and design for storytelling to cover current events for The New York Times.
  • Experience making quick decisions under deadlines and a high-pressure newsroom environment.
  • Experience working collaboratively with members of a multidisciplinary team.
  • Experience meeting deadlines and to adapt to change in a daily, unpredictable news and production environment
  • Open to working a flexible schedule.

job.description:

The Real Estate section of the New York Times is looking for an experienced, ambitious and creative reporter to focus on interior design and home coverage. The beat will include covering design trends, renovations, celebrity home tours and service around the home. Our ideal candidate is well versed in visual formats, including video. You should be conversant in the world of design but able to write to the everyday New York Times reader who is not a design or architecture enthusiast.

While much of the work will involve service coverage and home tours, this reporter should be prepared to jump on breaking news and come with ideas for enterprise stories and projects in the world of renovation and design that require real reporting skills and experience. You will constantly develop sources within the industry and deliver regular scoops.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City or Los Angeles and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

You will report to the Real Estate editor.

Responsibilities:

  • Report, write and publish multiple stories a week (a mix of news, service, and features).
  • Cover design trends, create service guides, profile notable houses.
  • Oversee our celebrity-focused home tours and spinoff franchises.
  • Cultivate sources and regularly deliver scoops.
  • Develop stories that include a range of voices and perspectives.
  • Collaborate with visual editors on new story formats and multimedia, including reporter video.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years' experience as a reporter
  • Strong news judgment and instincts
  • Experience in a deadline-driven environment
  • Creativity and willingness to experiment with new story forms, including video

  • Experience interviewing and booking celebrity interviews
  • Positive, collaborative attitude

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the role

The HR Operations Specialist supports employees across the company by coordinating HR transactions, resolving production issues, and responding to questions. This role partners with employees, department managers, HR Partners, Payroll, and other teams to keep HR processes running smoothly and employee data accurate. You will report to the HRIS Operations Supervisor.

This is a hybrid role based in our Norfolk, Virginia office. You can typically expect to work in the office three days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Be the primary contact for employee HR inquiries, partnering with the appropriate teams to provide clear, guidance.
  • Work with department managers and HR Partners to gather information, process employee transactions, and maintain accurate employee data in Workday.
  • Process complex administrative transactions and participate in Workday HR system workflows.
  • Troubleshoot Workday production issues across HCM modules, including HCM Core, Recruiting, Time and Attendance, and Compensation; resolve related support tickets involving HR processes and employee data.
  • Support biweekly payroll processing by reviewing and validating payroll transactions and inputs, processing vacation payouts, and managing paid time off (PTO) adjustments in Workday following established procedures.
  • Work with Payroll and other teams, handling confidential information.
  • Help with user acceptance testing, configuration and reporting requests, and testing for biannual Workday releases.
  • Build and upload Enterprise Interface Builder (EIB) files for employee and company changes.
  • Help employees use HR-related technology by answering questions and contributing to user enablement and training.
  • Develop training materials using Google Sites.
  • Manage end-user channels and the team email group, responding to inquiries from employees, HR Partners, and managers.
  • Audit HR processes and employee transactions to support data quality and integrity; follow security and data-handling protocols.
  • Process employment verification requests.
  • Manage a varied daily workload, reprioritizing to complete incoming transactions and department requests.
  • Take on other tasks as assigned.

Basic qualifications:

  • 2+ years of experience working with Workday HCM processing HR transactions.
  • Solid awareness of how human resources transactions influence payroll processing, financial reporting, and broader operational tasks.
  • At least one year of experience using Microsoft Excel, including formulas and pivot tables.
  • You know how to provide clear, professional guidance.
  • Care for the impact your work can have across related processes.
  • You are resolution-oriented.
  • You have strong attention to detail.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Hands-on experience with Workday Payroll processing.
  • A bachelor's degree in business, information systems, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Familiarity with additional Workday modules and teams, such as Benefits, Payroll, Finance, Security and Integrations.

job.title: Interactive News Engineering Intern
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About Us:

Interactive News Technology is a team of developer-journalists embedded in the New York Times newsroom. We power new story forms and build tools for newsgathering, while also supporting breaking news, exclusive reporting and major events.

We’re looking for a paid summer 2027 intern to contribute to software used by hundreds of NYT journalists and projects that serve millions of readers. Our unique position between the newsroom and technology departments makes us instrumental to The Times’ most ambitious digital journalism.

We work with a range of web technologies, primarily JavaScript, TypeScript, React and Svelte. We run Node.js servers which talk to PostgreSQL databases. We rely on hosted Google Cloud services and serverless technologies, manage code using Git and host it on GitHub, and use A.I. tools such as Cursor and Claude.

This role is focused on software engineering in a newsroom environment. Daily work will be on a software development project team. Interns often have opportunities to contribute to opportunistic data or document journalism using our tools, but the core work is not writing stories or producing graphics.

Previous interns have helped to wrangle nationwide precincts data and international election results, pitched in on Olympics coverage and results, added features to our live World Cup scores and standings, built technology to help reporters reach out to a diverse set of readers, implemented customizable layout configurations for elections results pages, and helped unravel thorny data about metro transit woes.

About Our Summer Internships:

  • The duration is 10 weeks long, starting on June 7th, 2027
  • The rate of pay for this role is $40 per hour. 
  • Interns work 35 hours per week.
  • This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. The intern will work from the office at least 3 days per week.
    • Our intern program team can provide resources and recommendations related to housing and relocation to New York.

Responsibilities: 

  • You will work on one or multiple projects for the summer and collaborate with developers, designers and journalists to build newsroom tools which help our journalists report and tell stories
  • You will contribute to technical design and development of new features within team projects, and use these tools to help with opportunistic reporting
  • You will receive support and mentorship to meet professional goals and accelerate your learning
  • You will expand your understanding of building modern, scalable, software while immersed in a newsroom environment
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • Experience contributing to newsgathering, reporting, editing, and/or news presentation processes
  • Experience in JavaScript or TypeScript
  • Experience taking a technical project from concept to completion, contributing to concept definition, technical design, and technical implementation
  • Experience working as part of a team to develop software
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted software development best practices
  • Interest in a newsroom engineering role that combines technical and editorial thinking
  • Support for our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • A portfolio of work showing innovations and ideas which demonstrate that you think critically about the news, and want to shape meaningful experiences for The New York Times readers

Preferred Qualifications:

The most competitive applications will demonstrate:

  • Experience collaborating with others to advance the purpose and ideas of a project
  • Interest in using software engineering skills to push the limits of what we offer to our readers

job.title: Local Investigations Fellowship Expression of Interest
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times offers a menu of programs and opportunities aimed at up-and-coming journalists and professionals from all backgrounds and with various skill levels.

Learn more about career programs here.

The application window for the Local Investigations Fellowship is currently closed and will reopen in summer of 2027.

Cover Letters for the Local Investigations Fellowship include at least one story idea or pitch, but multiple may be sent in each cover letter. Answers to these questions help us assess where you are in the reporting process and what editorial support and resources the local investigative fellowship could offer you.

  1. What is your investigative story idea or area of focus? How would your story expose something new, something no one else has already revealed?
  2. Describe who has been harmed and in what way. Is the harm enough to spark outrage?
  3. Will your story hold someone accountable? Who and how?
  4. What critical records, data and human sources will be required to tell your story? Describe how you have, or could, obtain these critical sources.
  5. What do you need help with to report this story, and what are the barriers?
  6. Can you give us a sense of what has been written about the subject? Please include clips of notable reporting on the topic.

We appreciate proposals that are as detailed as possible. Previous successful applicants have included specifics about what they aimed to prove through their investigations. 

For example, a reporter for The Baltimore Banner had reason to believe that the city’s overdose crisis was the worst in the nation. Mississippi Today had evidence of abuses in local sheriffs offices. And a reporter for The Desert Sun in Palm Springs, Calif., suspected a pattern of deaths inside local jails. 

Please submit five published clips that show excellence — in evocative writing, through high-impact news stories and by highlighting the voices of local communities. Your clips should be uploaded to the additional materials question below. Please include the full text of your clips, not just the links.

What makes a good local investigation?

  • Starts with high stakes
    How does the story affect people’s lives and livelihoods? Their health, safety and basic quality of life?
  • Has a clear line of accountability
    Great investigations have a line of accountability to someone or some group with significant power.
  • Reveals something
    Does your investigation reveal something that someone or some institution is trying to keep secret?
  • Has a clear sense of place
    The most important element for any local investigation: How is it (e.g. the policy, the circumstance or the failure) unique to your community?

job.title: Operations & Engagement Coordinator, Agency Development & Sales Strategy
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Job Description

About the Team

The mission of the Agency Development & Sales Strategy team is to leverage agencies as our next big source of incremental revenue growth. Our strategy is to create the conditions for our Sales Organization to drive more revenue from agency partners. Our approach is threefold: drive demand by changing perceptions; enable commerce by reducing friction and creating incentives; and standardize ways of working in order to scale. As a small but growing team, we have outsized impact by leveraging other internal teams, including Industry Marketing, Sales, Revenue Operations, and Programmatic Ops.

About the Role

You will report to the Associate Director, Agency Development & Sales Strategy. This role is based in our New York office and follows a hybrid work schedule.

As the Operations & Engagement Coordinator, you will support the operational core of the team. You will help execute day-to-day processes, coordinate projects, and manage logistics that enable successful, long-term partnerships with advertising agencies, with a particular focus on agency-facing activations. You will ensure that information, timelines and logistics stay aligned. You will assist in setting up and maintaining internal systems and workflows that translate strategy into successful agency partnership.

This role is ideal for a highly organized professional with strong project coordination skills, attention to detail, and an interest in agency partnerships, engagements, and media. Success in this role is defined by reliable execution, clear communication, and the smooth, scalable operation of our processes.

Responsibilities

Change agency perceptions of The Times

Agency Engagements: Support the planning and coordination of agency-specific engagements (e.g., Lunch & Learns, leadership gatherings, summits); managing logistics, invitations, venue and vendor coordination, materials preparation, and day-of execution

Scheduling: Maintain an event calendar, track deadlines, manage checklists, coordinate internal stakeholders (Sales, Marketing, Research, Creative), and ensure follow-up actions and reporting are completed on time

Outbound Communications: Help create external-facing materials – such as competitive reports and presentation decks – to strengthen agency relationships

Enable commerce by reducing friction and creating incentives

Agency Partnerships: Support the development and execution of revenue-generating deals with agency partners (e.g., tracking deliverables, updating status docs, coordinating approvals)

Strategic Implementation: Support the roadmapping, scoping and executing of strategic initiatives and work streams aligned with team goals

Prioritization and Planning: Coordinate with Sales, Revenue Operations, and Programmatic teams to identify opportunities, propose priorities, and ensure alignment on agency engagement strategies

Standardize ways of working in order to scale

Workflows: Help design and refine workflows and processes that streamline repeated tasks and external-facing materials, using AI-driven tools and automations where possible

Industry Research: Monitor industry trends and agency needs, collaborating with Sales Ops and Measurement teams to generate insights that enhance The Times' value proposition.

Lifecycle Support: Support the lifecycle of projects by helping to organize information, schedule meetings, capture notes and action items, and follow up with stakeholders to keep work moving

Accountability: Use and help maintain tools and processes (e.g., CRM and reporting dashboards) required to associate our engagement efforts with real traction with agencies (e.g., RFPs, IOs)

Basic Qualifications:

  • 1+ years of experience in operations or project coordination, event planning, business strategy support, business development support, or a related field.

  • Experience coordinating events or programs (professional, academic, or extracurricular), including logistics and communication with participants

  • Experience working collaboratively across teams and build positive working relationships

  • High attention to detail and willingness to roll up your sleeves on both administrative and project-based work

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 1+ years of experience in Media, Advertising, Media Agencies, or Tech

  • 1+ years experience with project management software tools (e.g., Monday.com, Coda)

  • Comfort working with data in spreadsheets and basic reporting tools; familiarity with CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce)

  • Verifying datasets and other forms of quantitative information and analysis.

  • Breaking down quantitative analysis to general, non-expert readers.

  • Experience in survey research and modelling.

  • Data handling experience — fluency in a statistical programming language such as R or Python.

Job Description

The New York Times' Accounting team is looking for a Senior Accounting Analyst who has knowledge reviewing contracts and transactions. You will determine proper accounting treatment, and record following generally accepted accounting principles. You can query and analyze data sets, summarize data in a concise and meaningful manner, and highlight insights that help inform validating recorded transactions. This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Senior Accounting Manager. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

About the Role

As a Senior Accounting Analyst, you will participate in month end closing work including the preparation of journal entries and balance sheet account reconciliations. Have the opportunity to recommend, document, and implement processes to facilitate the proper accounting of revenue and expense contracts. Furthermore, you will collaborate with partners to foster communication, learn about new contracts and products, improve processes, and to ensure the accuracy of accounting and reporting.

Responsibilities:

  • Review customer contracts and other transactions and ensure/document the proper accounting following ASC 606 or other relevant accounting standards.
  • Query, mine, report on data sets and use data analytics tools to validate and support recorded transactions.
  • Help research accounting questions related to internal and external reporting issues to ensure that financial results are reported in a complete and accurate manner consistent with our policies and accounting guidelines.
  • Compile information to satisfy requests from our external auditors.
  • Support NYT's Sarbanes-Oxley program by participating in quarterly and annual assessments, testing, review and remediation of test exceptions.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

  • Degree in Accounting or Finance
  • Certified Public Accountant
  • 3+ years of accounting experience
  • Knowledge of technical accounting pronouncements and standards (GAAP, FASB)
  • Advanced excel skills (i.e. macros)
  • Experienced communicating across multiple partners and ability to work cross functionally, including the ability to understand goals and and translate into transactional and reporting impacts

job.title: Senior Analytics Engineer, People Data and Insights
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The New York Times is rebuilding how we use people data. Instead of one-off reports and ad hoc pulls, we are building governed, reusable data tools that HR leaders, HR partners, and their counterparts use to make decisions. You will help build this layer. People data at The Times lives in several systems, each with its own definitions and history. You will turn that into a modeled, tested, documented foundation that products can be built on repeatedly. You will lead the models, transformations, and data quality behind every product this team ships. You will report to the Senior Director, People Data and Insights. You will work out of the New York office on a hybrid schedule. 

Responsibilities:

  • You will design, build, and maintain the data models and databases that our products run on.
  • You will oversee the transformation layer from source systems into governed, tested, documented models.
  • You will turn metric definitions from the data dictionary into executable logic, so that a definition and the number it produces cannot drift apart.
  • You will build data quality into the pipeline: tests, validation, and reconciliation across sources that surface problems before team members do.
  • You will work with the Program Manager to translate product requirements into models, and push back when a requirement and the underlying data do not agree.
  • You will handle effective-dated and historical data correctly, so that point-in-time questions get point-in-time answers.
  • You will implement and maintain access controls appropriate to compensation, demographic, and other sensitive data.
  • You will document models and lineage so that all can understand why something was built the way it was.
  • You will demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, or an equivalent role building production data models.
  • You are a SQL expert
  • Strong dimensional modeling skills, and the judgment to know when to normalize and when not to.
  • 5+ years of experience with a transformation framework such as dbt, and with version control and code review as part of normal practice.
  • 5+ years of experience handling slowly changing dimensions, dated records, and point-in-time reporting.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 2+ years of experience with HR or people data, and with systems such as Workday, Greenhouse, or One Model.
  • Python for orchestration, API work, or data validation.
  • 2+ years of experience with AWS data services.
  • Familiarity with BI and analytics tooling such as Hex, Tableau, or Looker.
  • 2+ years of experience in an organization with distinct populations operating under different rules, such as union and non-union groups.

Mission Overview & Responsibilities: 

We are looking for a Senior Product Designer to own the design evolution of the Wirecutter Store. You will be the lead designer for our shopping experience, balancing high-conversion UX design with rigorous visual standards. You will oversee the visual and structural integrity of our store, designing intuitive interfaces for our homepage, product detail pages (PDPs), and checkout flows.

You are a strategic partner who will help shape the future of our retail experience. We are looking for someone to bring their expertise in e-commerce best practices, user psychology, and conversion rate optimization (CRO) to help us identify opportunities we haven't seen yet.

This is a remote friendly position.

  • Translate complex business requirements into elegant, high-fidelity designs. You will wireframe, prototype, and refine the interface to create a cohesive store experience across desktop and mobile.

  • Analyze the shopping funnel to identify friction points. You'll design solutions that improve navigation, product discovery, and the overall checkout process.

  • Be the subject matter expert on e-commerce design trends. Audit the site experience to identify growth opportunities and propose improvements to site architecture.

  • Partner with the business team to drive our A/B testing roadmap. You will design and implement UI experiments (e.g., layout variations, navigation updates, promotional treatments) and use data to iterate on those designs.

  • Use your knowledge of the Shopify platform to build, configure, and manage pages. You understand the capabilities and constraints of the platform, allowing you to design features that are both beautiful and technically feasible.

  • Be the design advocate in meetings with our technical partners to ensure our visual standards are maintained during technical implementation.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of relevant design experience.

  • A portfolio showcasing your ability and process to design for e-commerce. You show an understanding of information architecture, interaction design, and visual hierarchy.

  • Experience designing for Shopify. You know how to navigate the theme editor, manage product assets, and collaborate with developers to bring custom layouts to life.

  • Experience designing templates for e-commerce email platforms (e.g., Klaviyo, Shopify Email). You understand how email layout, typography, and clear CTAs impact click-through and open rates.

  • Experience using analytics to understand site performance. You use insights to influence your design process and prioritize changes.

Our infrastructure runs on Amazon Web Services, with Fastly providing edge delivery and caching. We're looking for someone who can make sound architectural tradeoffs, improve the systems they work on, and help other engineers deliver high-quality work.

You will report to the Engineering Manager, Platform squad.

This is a hybrid role based at our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 2-3+ days/week.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the design and evolution of foundational web platform capabilities and shared component libraries, helping Games teams deliver reliable, accessible, high-quality experiences.

  • Lead the design and operation of performant, scalable Go APIs and services that support the evolving needs of the Games ecosystem.

  • Partner with Product, Design, and Production on complex projects. Shape technical approaches, weigh tradeoffs, and turn creative concepts into reliable product capabilities.

  • Improve performance, accessibility, and reliability across the Games suite, applying modern front-end practices and edge delivery capabilities to create a great player experience.

  • Improve developer experience by building and evolving tools, including Claude Code tooling, that help engineering teams deliver high-quality software.

  • Provide technical leadership through architecture and code reviews, clear engineering standards, and mentorship that helps teammates grow and teams deliver.

  • Strengthen production quality by using appropriate testing, monitoring, and operational practices to identify and address issues in the systems you own.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualiﬁcations:

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience building, deploying, and operating high-traffic web applications and distributed systems

  • Lead complex engineering work from design through production, making sound technical tradeoffs and partnering across Product, Design, and Editorial to build maintainable solutions

  • Build accessible, performant web experiences with modern JavaScript (ES6+), semantic HTML, CSS/SCSS, and React or a similar framework

  • Design shared component libraries or platform capabilities used by multiple teams, with attention to API design, documentation, adoption, and long-term support

  • Build performant, scalable APIs and services using Go, Java, or Python

  • Deploy and operate production services in cloud environments such as Amazon Web Services or Google Cloud Platform, using technologies such as databases, Redis, Docker, and CDNs or edge platforms like Fastly

  • Strengthen production quality and reliability through testing, monitoring, and observability; contribute technical leadership through design and code reviews, sound technical decisions, mentorship, and knowledge-sharing

Additional Qualifications:

  • Prior engineering experience in the gaming industry with web-based games, puzzles, or interactive media

  • Demonstrated interest in mission-driven engineering and a desire to partner with an accomplished team to support the journalistic independence of The New York Times

  • Experience with CI/CD automation (e.g., GitHub Actions, Drone, or Terraform) and a "DevOps" approach to platform stability

  • Familiarity with monitoring and observability tools (e.g., Datadog, Sentry, or Grafana) to improve the player experience

  • A "product-ﬁrst" mindset, with an obsession for end-user satisfaction and editorial efficiency

job.title: Senior LLM Engineer, R&D
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About Us:

Research & Development at The New York Times explores how emerging technologies can be applied in service of journalism. We collaborate with designers, developers, reporters, photographers and editors to bring new forms of storytelling to life, from prototyping to publishing.

At The Times, technology permeates every aspect of our business, from our thought-provoking coverage of technological trends to the digital-first transformation of our own business to the changing world of our readers. The Research & Development team explores the new opportunities that emerging technologies may provide the New York Times and our commercial and strategic goals.

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer with a background in applied AI to develop applications using Large Language Models (LLMs) in service of The Times mission and journalistic standards.

You will report to the Executive Director of R&D.

Responsibilities:

  • Design and implement LLM-backed APIs – driving improvements to reach target outcomes through evaluation, grounding and fine-tuning best practices.
  • Deploy reliable services within cloud environments (such as GCP or AWS) to support high-traffic LLM applications.
  • Manage the transition of features from experimental prototypes to stable production systems in a fast-paced environment with evolving requirements.
  • Collaborate with designers, product managers and stakeholders to translate detailed requirements into technical tasks, providing accurate estimates and progress updates.
  • Maintain comprehensive documentation to facilitate feature handoff and future maintenance.
  • Stay at the forefront of the evolving AI and LLM landscape, identifying and advocating for the use of new technologies and best practices.
  • Demonstrate understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

You are comfortable building projects by yourself and enjoy collaboration with a larger team. You are both curious about and skeptical of new technologies. You're excited to apply new tools, but aim to do so in service of solving important problems and making a difference for users. You take pride in your craft and understand the need to capture patterns and support future development.

  • 5+ years of professional software development or equivalent experience.
  • Proficiency with Python and TypeScript/JavaScript.
  • Professional experience architecting and shipping applications that use LLMs. Experience with multi-step chaining and human-in-the-loop workflows.
  • Strong understanding of LLM evaluations. Experience refining products using instrumentation, monitoring, and golden datasets to ensure accuracy and robustness.
  • Experience in algorithmic and AI text processing (e.g. text segmentation, semantic chunking, restructuring).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience building reliable, scalable back-end services in cloud environments (e.g. GCP, AWS).
  • Familiarity with AI orchestration and evaluation frameworks (e.g. AWS Step Functions, Google Cloud Workflows, Dagster, Braintrust).
  • Experience building front-end user interfaces for LLM-backed products.

To apply, please provide work samples (code snippets, URLs, project summaries) describing your most relevant work for this position and how it expresses your approach to software engineering.

This is a temporary position that is expected to last through November 2027.

job.title: Senior Manager, Commercial AI Discoverability Strategy (AEO/GEO)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The New York Times is looking for a strategic, analytical marketer to help improve how AI-generated answers represent our brand, products, subscription value, pricing and customer experience.

In this role, you will build an ongoing understanding of the commercial questions people ask AI systems, the sources shaping their answers, and opportunities to improve the visibility and accuracy of our information. You will identify where to focus, guide experiments, measure results, and turn what you learn into practical recommendations for product marketers and the teams that own or oversee relevant consumer-facing surfaces.

This role sits within the enterprise Marketing team and partners closely with cross-functional colleagues across teams, including Product, Growth, Audience, Communications and Customer Care. It is a full-time, hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You are expected to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor how AI systems answer commercially important consumer questions about The New York Times, including questions about our brand, products, subscription value, pricing and customer experience.
  • Prioritize topics and opportunities based on their strategic importance to the business.
  • Identify the sources shaping AI-generated answers and diagnose gaps in how our brand and commercial value are represented.
  • Recommend experiments to improve the visibility and accuracy of AI answers, guide their execution with partners, and measure whether interventions are effective.
  • Translate research and monitoring into clear, actionable guidance for product marketers, who coordinate follow-up with the teams that own relevant surfaces.
  • Partner with product marketers and relevant teams to improve messaging and content, and help ensure public, commercial New York Times pages can be retrieved and used effectively as sources in AI-generated answers.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of the value of journalistic independence, and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in SEO measurement, marketing, digital strategy, consumer insights, analytics or a related field. Enough technical SEO literacy to tell a crawler or indexing problem from a messaging problem.
  • Experience researching consumer questions, monitoring how a brand or product is represented and perceived, and synthesizing findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Experience designing experiments, estimating impact, evaluating results, and using evidence to recommend next steps. Direct exposure to AI-search measurement, such as designing a prompt set, auditing citations, comparing engines or running an experiment.
  • Strong commercial judgment about which prompts and answer frames matter to subscription and product decisions.
  • Experience translating strategy to technical implications, and explaining complex or technical findings clearly to different audiences and turning analysis into recommendations other teams could use.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Peec, Profound or another visibility platform.
  • Experience marketing consumer products, subscriptions or digital content.
  • Familiarity with teams and consumer-facing surfaces—owned or earned—that help market or educate consumers about a brand, product, subscription, or customer experience.

job.title: Senior Producer, Metro
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company.
