And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The Metro desk at The Times is seeking a creative, knowledgeable and collaborative Senior Producer for its video journalism. Metro's journalism spans fast-moving breaking news, enterprise and investigations on a range of beats, from politics and education to transportation and criminal justice. We bring the issues of New York and its surrounding tri-state region to readers around the world, with deeply-reported narratives and unexpected tales.

You will bring a passion for news, a commitment to fast, authoritative coverage of breaking and developing stories, and the news judgment to identify enterprise stories and exclusives. An experienced video journalist and a manager, you'll help broaden Metro's coverage in a range of video formats. You are a talented storyteller and strong people manager who is passionate about breaking news, live journalism and enterprise.

Metro is known across the newsroom for its collegial culture. You'll work closely with Metro editors and reporters, and build strong relationships across the newsroom — especially Video and Photo — and partner with Metro leadership to shape and drive coverage. You'll bring an innovative, collaborative approach to motivating and inspiring teams to scale video on the desk and deliver fast-turnaround and ambitious work.

You will oversee everything from live streams and news clips to enterprise projects and Reporter Video, managing a team of video journalists to execute on each of those priorities. Your sharp visual and editorial skills will ensure that the right stories are assigned. Before videos are published onsite and on social media, you will ensure that they meet the editorial standards, style and quality of the Times.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • You will drive innovative, exclusive video coverage across a range of video formats, from short-form live-blog updates to Reporter Videos featuring Times journalists, enterprise stories and columns, and occasional field deployments.

  • You will manage and help hire video journalists on the desk.

  • You will help colleagues assess whether a story is suited to video and whether it should be told primarily or exclusively in that format, and mentor them as they develop their video storytelling skills.

  • You will lead story development and story edits.

  • You will review, assign and provide clear feedback on video productions.

  • You will support and guide script writing and visual approaches for effective short-form video.

  • You will oversee production across multiple projects.

  • You will guide interviews and shoots as needed, both in studio and field.

  • You will work with Metro and Video leadership to develop new video approaches and editorial strategies for the desk.

  • You will coordinate breaking news coverage with Video's Daily News and The Times's Live team, which produces real-time updates and analysis.

  • You will work with the Editor, Video Training to identify coaching opportunities for on-camera and shooting skills.

  • You will oversee the production of social content and off-platform video.

  • You will draw ideas from a range of video sources, including wire services, UGC, eyewitness video, archival footage, motion graphics, and originally-shot footage.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the Metro editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years experience producing digital news videos.

  • 4+ years experience managing video journalists or newsroom teams.

  • Demonstrated expertise in sourcing, assessing and verifying video from a range of sources.

  • Expert knowledge of digital storytelling formats.

  • Understanding of mainstream and emerging social channels.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Excellent writing, editing and communication skills.

  • Expert knowledge of current events with advanced level experience covering breaking news stories in New York and experience covering news in the eastern United States.

  • Experience overseeing geolocation and UGC verification work.

  • Experience developing and editing visual material for social platforms.

  • Flexibility to work extended hours and some weekends.

  • Able to meet and make quick decisions under deadlines and to adapt to change in a daily, unpredictable news environment.

We showcase the expertise of Times journalists on camera, share urgent news updates, produce on-the-ground reporting, and pioneer Visual Investigations.

The Video department is looking for a Senior Producer to work on the multi-disciplinary Reporter Video team of video journalists who create powerful videos featuring the expertise of our world-class journalists. Based in London, this role will focus on covering breaking news and major international developments in short-form video, producing a mix of quick-turnaround videos, explanatory and analysis pieces, as well as major enterprise and investigations. 

The Senior Producer will report to a London supervisor and work with the rest of the Reporter Video team in New York and other video hubs, becoming the key manager of the department’s content during the hours that London acts as the main Times hub.

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. About the Role:

The Graphics department at The New York Times seeks to hire an experienced and versatile senior visual editor to manage and execute the presentation of our graphics journalism in formats beyond nytimes.com, including social media, email newsletters and the print newspaper. This is a high-impact role designed for a senior journalist who wants to pioneer best practices and drive our off-platform visual storytelling.

You will guide the adaptation of complex graphics for audiences on social media, including Instagram, Facebook, X and other emerging surfaces. You will be responsible for coordinating strategy with the Social Visuals team and for assigning, editing and in some cases crafting graphics to meet that strategy, and help to do the same for Times newsletters, including The Morning and On Politics. And you will work with the Print Hub to coordinate production and edit graphics for the Times print edition.

You possess impeccable news judgment and have extensive experience creating and editing a wide range of types of information graphics. You operate with autonomy to proactively identify new opportunities to extend the reach of our journalism.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Conceptualize and execute unified visual styles that can effectively translate complex data, maps and diagrams into digestible, high-impact visual assets to fit a variety of formats.
  • Produce and edit news graphics under tight deadlines during breaking news environments.
  • Guide and edit the work of other visual journalists who translate interactives, spatial models and breaking news graphics into these formats.
  • Expertly and independently carry out all aspects of visual production, serving as the primary leader of all off-platform displays.
  • Work with the Social Visuals and Audience teams to direct the packaging of graphics journalism off-platform.
  • Maintain strong relationships and coordinate across other multidisciplinary desks (Graphics, Design, Video and the Print Hub) to track projects and establish publishing workflows.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to a deputy graphics editor.

Ideal candidates should have some journalistic or editorial experience and should know how to translate the unique sensibilities of the magazine into compelling and sophisticated video stories.

In this role, you'll be expected to work with reporters, editors, producers, art directors and designers at the magazine to craft video assets that feature the expertise of our world-class journalists. The goal is to help readers understand the world through powerful video stories, reaching our core audience as well as new viewers who increasingly consume journalism in video. We will experiment with a mix of direct, immersive vertical video forms that can bring our audience with us on the ground.

You will join a multi-disciplinary team of video journalists that will shape this work. This role is based in our New York office, working remotely with correspondents in the field to produce, edit and publish stories. You should have a refined understanding of video production and storytelling, including video editing, shooting and writing for narration, with a clear sense for how to creatively use graphics and animation to illustrate complex ideas. 

Your news judgement about what makes a good story in video will be crucial, as will creative ideas for how to reenvision the basic elements of foreign correspondence, across news, features and analysis. You must be an effective collaborator and a strong communicator who can work closely with regional editors and video colleagues to shape our approach to this coverage. You are capable of working independently and decisively.

This position is based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. 

Responsibilities:

  • Write, produce, edit and publish videos with hybrid correspondents, in close partnership with regional editors.
  • Devise new approaches to digital video storytelling both on and off platform.
  • Work with correspondents to create a playbook for how to cover a region or beat in video.
  • Collaborate closely with International editors, correspondents and video colleagues.
  • Guide the work of cinematographers, editors and other collaborators.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • The role reports to the Senior Producer, International in New York.

  • 8+ years experience producing news video journalism for digital or broadcast news.
  • A strong portfolio, preferably of inventive short-form video.
  • High-level editorial judgement, and excellent writing, editing and communication skills.
  • Proven ability to work independently to lead production on complicated projects.
  • Demonstrated broad knowledge of current events and news.
  • Deep curiosity about video habits and users and platforms.
  • Strong organizational skills, including the ability to manage field crews and hire and manage freelancers when necessary.
  • Hands-on experience in the trenches of production, including editing, shooting and field production.

  • Experience covering international news.
  • Foreign language fluency.
  • Strong experience with archival research, including sourcing and clearing user-generated video content.

job.title: Staff Engineer, GraphQL Platform
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The GraphQL Platform team builds and operates The New York Times' federated API layer that helps product and engineering teams deliver trusted journalism and experiences across our products. We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to shape the architecture and technical direction of this mission-critical platform as it scales in traffic, complexity, and the number of teams building on it.

Responsibilities:

  • Set technical strategy and architecture for the GraphQL federation platform.
  • Design capabilities to improve reliability, performance, traffic management, and cost efficiency.
  • Establish schema and operation governance, including guardrails for query complexity and safe federation.
  • Resolve system bottlenecks using observability, load testing, and incident analysis.
  • Enhance developer experience through automation, documentation, tooling, and safe AI workflows.
  • Partner across product, infrastructure, and feature teams to align platform capabilities with product needs.
  • Participate in on-call response, root-cause analysis, and operational improvements.
  • Mentor engineers and promote technical standards through design reviews, code reviews, and feedback.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Senior Software Engineering Manager.

Basic Qualifications:

  • You have 7+ years experience building and operating production APIs or distributed services.
  • Deep practical experience developing and scaling GraphQL APIs.
  • Experience with Apollo Router, Apollo Federation, schema composition, router plugins or extensions, and supergraph operations.
  • Software development skills in at least one statically typed backend language; our platform uses Go.
  • Experience leading complex technical projects across multiple teams and communicating with non-technical partners.
  • Experience improving reliability, performance, or observability in production systems, and using data to guide technical decisions.
  • You value learning and improvement, sharing knowledge, and welcoming constructive feedback.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience building schema or query governance, developer tooling, or paved paths for service teams.
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted development or GraphQL-aware tooling, including the security and quality controls needed to use it responsibly.
  • Experience with high-traffic APIs, Kubernetes or cloud-native systems, autoscaling, load testing, caching, or CDN integration.

job.title: Staff iOS Engineer - News Product
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. The News Product team at The New York Times is looking for a Staff iOS Engineer. You will work with our Native squad to lay the foundations for satisfying native app experiences. You will deliver world-class journalism to millions of daily readers in a responsive and performant medium. You will lead efforts to enhance the quality, performance, and long-term maintainability of the News app codebase. You will establishing a technical vision that ensures our native experiences remain responsive and reliable for all readers. As part of the News Product organization, you will work with designers, other mobile engineers, and web engineers, and more on a team.

This is an opportunity to use different tools, ranging from SwiftUI to hybrid web technologies - whatever will best solve the problem at hand. You'll be part of an engineering organization that values transparency and openness, diversity, learning, community, and continuous improvement.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week.

You express:

  • Belief in our mission: You have passion with the news and for making the Times an indispensable daily destination for our readers.

  • Technical competency: You have knowledge of iOS frameworks and Swift, and keep up to date on changes in the frameworks, language and overall developer community.

  • Code cleanliness: You understand what makes code well structured, maintainable and flexible and aim to create a culture where quality code is valued.

  • User focus: You care about how design, engineering and product decisions help create a seamless, engaging and enjoyable user experience.

Responsibilities:

  • You will lead the design and implementation of core architectures, shared frameworks, and infrastructure using Swift, SwiftUI, and UIKit that accelerate our feature teams.
  • You will work with your team to build solutions that are scalable, maintainable and reliable.
  • You will guide app-wide architectural decisions, shape the long-term technical roadmap, and set engineering standards for the iOS platform.
  • You will lead technical understanding, collaborating with backend engineers, web teams, and other internal dependency owners.
  • You will help promote standards in iOS and Swift delivery, and engage with the community of iOS developers at the Times.
  • You will lead programs to help the quality, performance and maintainability of the News app codebase
  • You will mentor engineers and contribute to/participate in Communities of Practice
  • Where applicable, you will integrate with broader New York Times Swift platform code
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, with 5+ years focused on large-scale iOS applications.
  • Experience setting technical direction, guiding engineering teams, and leading mobile architecture.
  • Deep mastery of iOS runtime mechanics, memory management, advanced design patterns, and Swift Concurrency.
  • Hands-on experience designing complex data persistence layers, advanced networking, and scalable test suites.
  • Expertise in mobile performance engineering, including app launch optimization, binary size reduction, and memory profiling.
  • Experience designing client-side observability infrastructure using Datadog or similar platforms.
  • Experience orchestrating large-scale architectural migrations (e.g., UI framework shifts, monolithic decoupling, automated refactoring).
  • Experience with framework design and modularization, including internal SDK development.
  • Product and Developer Experience (DX) mindset with the vision to translate complex goals and developer friction into scalable code.

job.title: Staff Photo Editor
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

The Times is seeking a versatile, experienced and fast-adapting journalist and visual editor to join the photo department in a dual role working both with the special projects team and as a floater photo editor on various desks and projects as needed.

As a photo editor working with the Projects and Initiatives (P&I) team, you will collaborate with P&I editors and relevant desk editors to shape the visual approach for a variety of stories or series throughout the year. You will assign and research a wide array of news and feature photographs, working productively with staff and freelance photographers, wire services, agencies and all other sources of visuals. Projects will range across subject areas and may be visually rooted in archival photography, traditional news and documentary work, or image-making that experiments with new technology.

As a floater photo editor, you will temporarily take on photo editing roles across various desks and a wide range of beats and subject areas. Flexibility is essential, as your schedule may vary week to week and can include nights, weekends, and holidays.

You are an editorial generalist with deep curiosity, and you thrive in a collaborative environment — working productively with editors, designers, videographers and developers. You are capable of pivoting between disparate subject matters—from hard news to culture and features and long-lead enterprise—without sacrificing quality or editorial depth. Also, you bring a strong demonstrable passion for visual journalism across modern digital formats.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Conceive, pitch, develop, edit, pace and help build powerful and innovative visual stories with attention to detail in a fast-paced newsroom.
  • Maintain the highest standard of photography and multimedia assigning for feature, news and enterprise stories for all platforms including mobile, print and social.
  • Seamlessly toggle between breaking news workflows and long-lead enterprise projects, recalibrating editing pace and narrative style as coverage demands.
  • Identify, vet and onboard new contributing photojournalists as needed. Ensure that new contributors are versed and committed to ethical journalistic rigor, independence and integrity. Build relationships with the photographers you are directing through briefings, regular contact and feedback.
  • Collaborate with designers, writers, reporters, video journalists, editors and photographers to shape ideas into visual story opportunities.
  • Demonstrate strong editorial judgment, working with Times editors and legal department for all vetting, copyright, legal and ethical questions.
  • Focus on working with a diverse range of subjects and photographers, keeping our global and multigenerational audience in mind.
  • Coordinate with newsroom desk editors and security team members to ensure the utmost preparation, training and safety of our photojournalists in the field.
  • Maintain and work within the photo budget, process/approve invoices.
  • Actively contribute to photo department meetings with reports and updates of your desk's visual priorities.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to a Deputy Editor of Photography.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience in a newsroom or equivalent.
  • Experience assigning and directing photojournalists in a variety of situations.
  • Proven deep research skills.
  • Expertise in handling electronic images, photographic usage and copyright issues.
  • Strong technical skills, including proficiency in digital tools and programs, including content management systems, Photoshop, PhotoMechanic, video editing tools and social media platforms.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • An enthusiasm for visual journalism and current events, coupled with keen news judgment and a firm sense of journalistic ethics.
  • Strong organizational, communication and collaborative abilities.
  • Knowledge of Adobe Premiere.
  • Experience prioritizing and managing multiple projects in fast-moving environments
  • The initiative to take on and learn new technologies and tasks.
  • Openness to working a flexible schedule as news demands.
  • Experience making quick decisions under deadlines and a high-pressure news environment.

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

job.title: Staff Software Engineer, Application Delivery
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The Developer Platforms mission at The New York Times builds the foundational platforms, tooling, and paved paths that help product teams ship high‑quality experiences quickly and safely. Our Application Delivery team owns the shared software delivery platform (CI/CD, artifact management) and deployment workflows used by hundreds of engineers across News, Cooking, Games and Audio to ship software.

As the Times leans into AI‑assisted and agentic development, Application Delivery is where those changes become real. You will set the technical direction for how AI‑generated and agent‑driven change flows safely, observably, and at scale through CI/CD.

You'll help teams reduce release risk with modern deployment patterns, and turn effective delivery practices into reusable pipelines and templates that scale across the organization, much like our GenAI platform roles turn internal practices into reusable tools and agents. When you improve this platform, you change how The New York Times ships software.

You will report to the Engineering Manager of the DevEx Application Delivery team. This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the technical direction of software delivery as a shared product: shape paved paths in our shared platform that improve code health, release quality, and delivery speed for product teams.

  • Set the technical direction for agent‑ready delivery: design the policy, guardrails, and paved paths that turn AI‑generated and agent‑driven changes (migrations, test generation, pipeline maintenance) into safe, observable releases at scale by partnering with our Developer AI team.

  • Collaborate with Product, engineering leaders, and internal users to shape the roadmap for the delivery platform and bring measurable impact on quality and speed.

  • Deliver scalable, secure, and observable software delivery systems and workflows that improve reliability, and overall software quality and velocity.

  • Champion engineering excellence in delivery by setting best practices for testing, deployment strategies, progressive delivery, and observability that are easy to adopt through the platform.

  • Mentor engineers across the mission, contribute to hiring, and help foster an inclusive, collaborative engineering culture centered on shared platforms and high‑quality software delivery.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our mission and values and a commitment to our purpose to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience building the technical strategy and driving software delivery (Github Actions, Argo CD or equivalent CI/CD systems) or similar platform work with broad organizational impact beyond operations.

  • Experience building and scaling a platform as a product for internal engineers with multi-tenancy serving many teams through self‑service paved paths, with attention to adoption, backward compatibility, and isolation/guardrails between tenants

  • Demonstrated proficiency in building and maintaining production services in one or more general‑purpose programming languages (e.g., Go, Python, TypeScript/Node.js, or Java), including code review and debugging complex issues.

  • 5+ years of experience with containers, Kubernetes, package management tools(Helm or equivalent), IAC tools(Terraform or equivalent), Gitops‑based deployment workflows and cloud services such as AWS, GCP.

  • Experience using delivery and productivity metrics (e.g., DORA, SPACE) and platform observability to measure and improve release quality and delivery.

  • Proficiency with GenAI‑assisted developer tooling (e.g., Cursor, Copilot, or Claude Code) and judgment about how to integrate agentic workflows into CI/CD safely.

  • Experience leading cross‑team technical work, communicating trade‑offs, and building understanding among diverse partners including Product, platform, and product engineering teams.

  • Experience mentoring engineers and contributing to an inclusive, collaborative engineering culture.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Exposure to artifact/package management (e.g., Artifactory or similar) with attention to security, retention, cost, and ease of use for engineers.

job.title: Technical Product Manager II, Content Data Products
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Publishing group at The New York Times builds and maintains the content management system powering all Times platforms. We empower engineering teams to evolve digital experiences while providing creators with interconnected tools to uphold our journalistic mission.

The Content Data Products team governs the centralized, compliance-cleared platform for all Times content data. Partnering closely with the New AI Products and Platforms (NAPP) team—whose Discovery Engine (search, knowledge graph, and AI) relies on our infrastructure—we ensure our rich archive is ingested, structured, attributed, and indexed across all brands (News, Cooking, Wirecutter, The Athletic, Games) and multimedia formats (articles, video, interactives).

We are looking for a Technical Product Manager II to lead our content data warehouse roadmap and its feeding pipelines. Reporting to the Senior TPM for NAPP, you will partner with engineering to bring product strategy across editorial, AI, and partner requirements.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week.

Responsibilities:

  • Roadmap Execution: Lead the strategy and delivery for the content data warehouse and ingestion pipelines for new content types and metadata enrichment.

  • Data Modeling & Indexing: Define specifications for modeling, ingesting, and indexing new content formats (e.g., video, interactives, acquired brand content) for search, retrieval, and AI use cases.

  • Catalog Optimization: Partner with operations, legal, and teams to audit archival structures, address metadata gaps, and improve catalog completeness.

  • Collaboration: Gather requirements, establish data contracts, prioritize features, and communicate roadmap progress and risks across engineering, design, editorial, and leadership.

  • Product Delivery: Guide the end-to-end product development lifecycle from concept to launch with high quality.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3–5 years of experience in technical product management with a focus on content data and platform infrastructure.

  • 3+ years of experience launching complex software products in close partnership with engineering teams.

  • Demonstrated experience with unstructured or multimedia data ingestion pipelines and downstream integrations (e.g., search indexes, analytics, ML/AI systems).

  • Experience navigating ambiguous spaces, conduct research, define technical requirements, and experience communicating complex technical concepts to a variety of audiences to diverse audiences.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Science, Journalism, or equivalent experience.

  • Familiarity with search/retrieval systems and how structured metadata powers search engines and AI capabilities.

  • Working knowledge of SQL, relational database architecture, and schema auditing.

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The New York Times is hiring a Vice President, Audience Insights to lead a high-impact team of researchers working to inform company-wide priorities. 

You will oversee rigorous, insightful, and actionable research for partners spanning our data, design, growth, product, marketing, and strategy organizations, as well as the newsroom. You will also work with company leaders to shape a research agenda that helps The Times continue to understand, reach, and engage the audiences that our mission and business rely on.

This is a hybrid position, and you will work out of our NYC headquarters at least three days per week. You will report to the SVP, Strategy and Corporate Development.

Responsibilities

In this role, you will:

  • Lead and mentor a team of multidisciplinary researchers, and nurture the team’s joyful and collaborative culture. 
  • Oversee audience research programs with product and design teams to define our target audiences, understand their needs, and inform roadmaps.
  • Oversee audience research that shapes our marketing strategy, creative development and messages, and measures the effectiveness of our campaigns and other communications.
  • Oversee research to help drive audience engagement with our site and apps, subscription conversion, retention and win-back.
  • Shape audience research programs that support newsroom strategic priorities.  
  • Communicate widely about both internal and external research, putting findings in context for Times executives and teams. 
  • Harness best practices for research, including the use of A.I., that enhance productivity and quality while maintaining methodological integrity.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of the value of journalistic independence, and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications

  • 15+ years of experience in primary research, market research, UX research, and consumer insights, including in a content or digital product company.
  • 7+ years of experience managing high-performing teams and navigating matrixed stakeholder environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence decisions through research-based insights.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced degree in a quantitative or social science field.
  • Experience with both digital product design and traditional market research.

job.title: Vice President, Head of Privacy (Privacy, Cyber Security, Consumer Compliance)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:  

As part of the Commercial Business and Legal Affairs team and reporting to the SVP, Associate General Counsel & Strategic Partnerships, the Vice President, Head of Privacy (Privacy, Cyber Security, Consumer Compliance) is responsible for all legal aspects of data privacy, information security, and consumer marketing and subscriptions-related compliance across the company and for managing the Company's privacy compliance function. You will work closely with senior executives and operational leads as well as the working team, including the areas of marketing operations, subscription growth, product, engineering, technology, data governance, information security, commercial contracts, and marketing and advertising technology. In this position, you will manage a team. 

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Advise all internal clients on the risks and operational controls related to the development, collection, use, transfer, and governance of personal data of consumers, employees, and other stakeholders. This will include privacy, online safety, and cybersecurity (from both U.S. and international perspectives). 

  • Advise key business stakeholders on the company’s data governance, cybersecurity, marketing and subscriptions compliance efforts in a manner consistent with the Company’s goals and culture.

  • Drive measurable improvements in privacy program maturity, incident readiness, vendor governance, compliant product launches, and privacy risk reduction. Manage privacy program resourcing, vendor support, and outside counsel engagement for privacy matters, as applicable.

  • Draft and/or update privacy program-related policies and standards, public-facing and internal; as well as terms of use, terms of sale, and other consumer-facing acceptable use and moderation policies.

  • Supervise and oversee the preparation and updating of Data Protection Impact Assessments and other risk assessment and audit activities as needed. Conduct comprehensive business risk assessments; develop/implement risk mitigation and corrective action plans where needed.

  • Advise on privacy regulatory and contractual compliance in marketing, ad sales, direct and programmatic advertising, identity resolution, data clean rooms, and third-party data and ad tech integrations to help ensure compliance with privacy and consumer protection laws and industry standards.

  • Review, draft and negotiate data protection agreements and security exhibits and work closely with the appropriate teams to advise on third party risk reviews. 

  • Advise on all relevant consumer protection, subscriptions and marketing laws, regulations and best practices.

  • Provide product counseling to include privacy, cybersecurity and consumer compliance legal advice as well as other areas of related legal need – in connection with product and platform developments and releases. 

  • Regularly track and counsel clients on legal US and international developments in areas of data privacy, cybersecurity and consumer marketing and subscription compliance.

  • Serve as legal lead for all security incident response, working closely with the company’s Chief Information Security Officer and other key stakeholders; draft and update information security policies and procedures.

  • Provide advice and guidance to data science and analytics teams on privacy-compliant deployment of machine learning models and personalization.

  • Oversee and develop company-wide training strategy and execution for areas of coverage.

  • Serve as point of contact for data protection authorities, regulatory inquiries, and industry groups.

  • Excellent judgment and professional integrity.

  • Handle high-volume workload efficiently.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Juris Doctor is required and must be a member of the New York Bar.

  • 15+ years of experience in US and international data privacy and protection; negotiating data privacy-related agreements, building, implementing, and maintaining a global privacy program; supporting cybersecurity. 

  • 5+ years of experience managing people with proven experience effectively managing cross-functional relationships and competing priorities.

  • 5+ years of previous in-house experience.

  • Experience advising on online safety laws such as age-appropriate design codes and app store age signals laws, and sensitive data privacy regulations such as laws governing health data in ad tech and biometric privacy.

  • Experience advising or managing legal professionals who advise on a wide variety of consumer-related issues both domestic and international, including payflow, subscription offerings, marketing, auto-renewal and click-to-cancel laws, anti-spam, Telephone Consumer Protection Act, unfair and deceptive practice laws, customer care complaints and escalations, and payment card rules.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5+ years in-house experience at a tech platform, media company, and/or subscription-first company.

job.title: Video Journalist, International
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times International desk is looking for a Video Journalist to produce and edit stories with multimedia correspondents. You will join a team tasked with creating new approaches to our international reporting in video, working with a growing group of foreign correspondents who work in video as well as text.

The goal is to help our audience understand the world through powerful video stories, reaching our core audience as well as new viewers who increasingly consume journalism in video. We will experiment with a mix of direct, immersive vertical video forms that can bring our audience with us on the ground.

You will join a multi-disciplinary team of video journalists that will shape this work. This role is based in our New York office, working remotely with correspondents in the field to produce, edit and publish stories. You should have a refined understanding of video production and storytelling, including video editing, shooting and writing for narration, with a clear sense for how to creatively use graphics and animation to illustrate complex ideas. 

Your news judgement about what makes a good story in video will be crucial, as will creative ideas for how to reenvision the basic elements of foreign correspondence, across news, features and analysis. You must be an effective collaborator and a strong communicator who can work closely with regional editors and video colleagues to shape our approach to this coverage.

This position is based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. 

Responsibilities:

  • Write, produce, edit and publish videos with hybrid correspondents, in close partnership with regional editors.
  • Devise new approaches to digital video storytelling both on and off platform.
  • Work with correspondents to create a playbook for how to cover a region or beat in video.
  • Collaborate closely with International editors, correspondents and video colleagues.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • The role reports to the Senior Producer, International in New York.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of video storytelling, video editing and production experience at a news organization.
  • A strong portfolio, preferably of inventive short-form video.
  • Excellent writing, editing and communication skills.
  • Broad knowledge of current events and news.
  • Deep curiosity about video habits and users and platforms.
  • Hands-on experience in the trenches of production, including editing, shooting and field production.
  • The ability to edit quickly and accurately with Adobe Premiere. 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience covering international news. 
  • Foreign language fluency.
  • Strong experience with archival research, including sourcing and clearing user-generated video content.
  • Fluency with animation and motion graphics as an integral part of your script writing process.
  • Strong organizational skills, including the ability to manage field crews and hire and manage freelancers when necessary.
  • Proven ability to meet deadlines and adapt to change within an unpredictable news and production environment.
  • A record of working with teams of journalists in difficult field assignments.
  • High creative standards and a drive to push work to its best possible form.

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

In order to be considered for this role, please submit your resume, cover letter and link to your portfolio.

The New York Times is an industry leader in visual journalism with reporting that includes extraordinary news coverage, investigations, and culture and lifestyle reporting. The Reporter Video team identifies compelling stories and brings the depth and breadth of our news report onto our site and other platforms through video that features the expertise of our world-class journalists.

This is a role for someone who wants to produce, edit and publish short-form vertical videos daily and is versatile enough to work on news, features, enterprise and investigative projects with colleagues across the newsroom. You have expertise in video storytelling, including video editing and writing for narration and social copy, as well as a sharp sense of the digital landscape.

Your portfolio and work samples should reveal a strong grasp of modern mobile video storytelling, and it should show that you're a quick learner with creative ideas and the ability to work on small or large teams. You are solid technically, ideas-oriented and have solid news judgment. Cinematography skills are an added asset. We're looking for someone who excels on deadlines and has experience juggling multiple projects at any given time.

Please note we have three positions in the newsroom. Please speak to your expertise and/or interest(s) in your cover letter:

  • General news

  • Investigations

  • Enterprise

These are in-office positions based in New York and include regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Write, produce, edit and publish short-form vertical videos every day.

  • Help to identify breaking news and enterprise across our news report and create video that features the expertise of our journalists, whether working with reporters on camera or using voiceover or visual storytelling techniques including graphics and animation.

  • Write scripts, wordsmith text and copy edit.

  • Experiment with various forms of short-form vertical video storytelling.

  • Collaborate with visual editors to generate video formats that bring our best journalism to new audiences.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to a Senior Producer.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of video storytelling, video editing and production experience at a news organization.

  • Excellent news judgment and proven ability to work with colleagues and reporters to synthesize newsgathering and/or investigations into a tight, informative and engaging video.

  • Experience producing shoots and interviewing experts on camera.

  • Experience creating original videos that intelligently incorporate audio, video, still images and text.

  • Strong video editing skills with Adobe Premiere.

  • Facility in using photo, video, audio, graphics and animation in storytelling.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Able to meet deadlines and adapt to change within an unpredictable news and production environment.

  • Design and animation skills including experience with design and animation software (Figma, Illustrator, Photoshop and After Effects).

  • Experience working collaboratively with members of a multidisciplinary team.

  • Available to work a flexible schedule.

job.title: Forward Deployed Product Engineer
job.description:
Keywords Location Search Jobs Forward Deployed Product Engineer Job ID 10165150 Location Burbank, California, United States Business The Walt Disney Company (Corporate) Date posted Nov. 13, 2026 Forward Deployed Product Engineer Apply Now Save Job SHARE Facebook LinkedIn Email WhatsApp Links open in new tabs.

Job Summary

Job Requirements The Enterprise Technology mission is to deliver technology solutions that align with business strategies, enable enterprise efficiency, and promote cross-company collaborative innovation. Our group drives competitive advantage by enhancing consumer experiences, enabling business growth, and advancing operational excellence. We are seeking a Product Manager with

experience

building and launching AI-powered products. In this role, you will identify high-value business problems, define product strategy and requirements, prioritize opportunities, and partner closely with engineering, design, data, AI/ML, and business stakeholders to bring solutions from concept through production and adoption. You should have strong product judgment, technical fluency, and hands-on

experience

working with AI and LLM-powered products. You understand concepts such as LLM APIs, prompt design, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agents, evaluation, data integration, and human-in-the-loop workflows well enough to make informed product decisions and effectively partner with technical teams. You are comfortable operating in ambiguity, translating business needs into clear product direction, testing ideas quickly with users, and using data and feedback to determine what to build next. We'd love to see something you've helped build. Please include a portfolio. This team works in the office Monday through Thursday.

Responsibilities

Define the product vision, strategy, roadmap, and priorities for AI-powered products and capabilities. Identify high-value business and user problems and translate them into clear product requirements, user stories, workflows, and success criteria. Lead product discovery by partnering with users and stakeholders to understand pain points, validate opportunities, and test assumptions. Partner closely with engineering, AI/ML, data, design, and business teams to take products from concept and prototype through production launch and ongoing iteration. Prioritize features and investments based on customer value, business impact, technical feasibility, risk, and effort. Define measurable product outcomes and KPIs and use product analytics, user feedback, and experimentation to guide product decisions. Shape AI-powered user experiences, including workflows, automation, agent interactions, and appropriate human-in-the-loop decision points. Understand and help define effective uses of LLM APIs, prompt design, RAG, agents, and AI evaluation approaches. Partner with technical teams to establish appropriate quality, evaluation, security, privacy, monitoring, and reliability expectations for AI products. Drive pilots and prototypes with real users, gathering feedback and determining whether solutions should be iterated, scaled, or discontinued. Develop product requirements and clearly communicate tradeoffs, decisions, dependencies, and priorities to technical teams and senior stakeholders. Drive product launches, adoption, change management, and continuous improvement across enterprise users and business teams. Build strong relationships across multiple business areas and align stakeholders around a shared product direction.

Required Qualifications

3 + years of Technical Product Management

experience

building and shipping software products for production users.

Experience

contributing to or leading the development of AI, GenAI, LLM-powered, data, or other technically complex products. Demonstrated

experience

defining product strategy, roadmaps, requirements, priorities, and measurable success criteria. Strong understanding of the software development lifecycle and

experience

partnering directly with software engineering, data, AI/ML, and/or design teams. Working knowledge of modern AI concepts and methods, including LLMs, prompt design, agents, RAG, APIs, and evaluation.

Experience

conducting product discovery, gathering user feedback, validating requirements, and translating ambiguous business problems into actionable product direction. Strong product and business judgment with the ability to connect product decisions to user needs and measurable business outcomes.

Experience

using data, experimentation, qualitative feedback, and product metrics to inform prioritization and product decisions. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts, product decisions, and tradeoffs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Strong learning agility and comfort operating in a rapidly evolving technology environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience

launching AI/GenAI products or capabilities into production.

Experience

with AI product development concepts such as RAG, agentic workflows, prompt design, model selection, evaluation frameworks, and human-in-the-loop systems.

Experience

experimenting or prototyping with tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or similar AI development tools.

Experience

working with AI engineers, software engineers, data scientists, data engineers, UX/design teams, or forward-deployed engineering teams.

Experience

defining success metrics and evaluation frameworks for AI products, including approaches such as golden datasets, human evaluation, LLM-as-judge, trace analysis, and production monitoring.

Experience

job.title: Lead Data and Governance Engineer
job.description:
Keywords Location Search Jobs Lead Data and Governance Engineer Job ID 10165197 Location Lake Buena Vista, Florida, United States Business The Walt Disney Company (Corporate) Date posted Nov. 13, 2026 Lead Data and Governance Engineer Apply Now Save Job SHARE Facebook LinkedIn Email WhatsApp Links open in new tabs.

Job Summary

Job Requirements Lead Data Governance Specialist The Disney Decision Science and Integration (DDSI) team leverages advanced technologies, data analytics, and scientific approaches such as optimization and statistical modeling to build innovative tools that shape business decisions across The Walt Disney Company. We support Disney Entertainment (ABC, The Walt Disney Studios, Disney+, Hulu), ESPN, Disney Experiences (Theme Parks, Cruise Line, Consumer Products, DVC), and Corporate Finance with strategic applications that enable data-driven decision-making. This team works in office. What You Will Do As the Lead Data Governance Specialist, you will own the data governance craft for our team: the operating model, policies, standards, and stewardship practices that make Disney's data trusted, well described, properly protected, and genuinely easy to use. You will work closely with Data Engineering, Architecture, the Ontology/Semantic Librarian, Security, Privacy, and Legal to see them applied. Your time will be split roughly evenly across two mandates: Project Initiatives Projects that focus on unifying data and accelerating access to it across The Walt Disney Company. You will own the governance workstream that makes unified data safe to share and reuse at pace. Lead the development, adoption, and enforcement of the data governance policies, standards, and best practices that span the Data Unification Accelerators program, including the operating model and decision rights that let data be shared and reused safely at speed. Design governance guardrails that accelerate delivery rather than gate it: documented data ownership, pre-agreed classification and data sharing rules, reusable approval paths, and templates that delivery teams can self-serve. Define the metadata, glossary, lineage, and cataloging standards that make unified data discoverable and explainable — business definitions, critical data elements, ownership attributes, and provenance — partnering with the Ontology/Semantic Librarian so that business meaning, ownership, and governance attributes stay aligned with the semantic layer. Set and operate data quality standards for unified data assets: quality dimensions, measurable rules for critical data elements, profiling and scorecards, issue triage, and clear remediation ownership. Shape the governance of the internal Data Marketplace by defining what a data product must satisfy before it is offered to the enterprise — publishing and documentation standards, certification criteria, access and entitlement models, and usage terms. Partner with Security, Privacy, Legal, and the Data Engineering teams to translate privacy, residency, and regulatory obligations into practical, implementable requirements — data classification and sensitivity tiering, role- and attribute-based access, masking, and retention — and assure that those requirements are met. Establish the governance that allows analytics and AI to consume unified data responsibly: approved use, data provenance and attribution, human accountability, and the controls that underpin responsible AI. Define and report the program's governance metrics, maturity measures, risks, and compliance posture to program leadership and enterprise governance forums. Divisional Data Governance Design, Advisory, and Delivery The data governance voice for our division, covering both the design of the capability and the hands-on delivery of it. Act as the division's trusted data governance advisor — the person teams come to for a clear answer on data ownership, classification, sharing, quality, retention, and acceptable use. Design and stand up the divisional governance operating model: data owners and stewards, governance forums and councils, charters, decision rights, RACI, and escalation paths that fit how our teams genuinely work. Author, socialize, and maintain divisional data policies, standards, and procedures, together with the exception and waiver process that sits behind them, keeping all of it aligned to enterprise and corporate policy and current as data protection and AI regulation evolves. Run governance-by-design reviews of new solutions, data products, and third-party or vendor data arrangements, giving teams practical requirements early rather than audit findings late. Deliver governance outcomes hands-on for priority data domains: populate the catalog and business glossary, assign and confirm ownership, stand up quality monitoring, and close the gaps you find. Own the divisional data issue and risk register end to end — intake, root cause analysis, remediation planning, and tracking to closure — and support internal audit, external audit, and regulatory requests. Run access governance for divisional data, including entitlement design, request and approval workflow, periodic access reviews, and least-privilege recertification. Build data literacy and governance capability through training, onboarding material, office hours, and a steward community of practice, and drive the adoption and behavior change that make governance stick. Assess governance maturity, build and sequence a prioritized governance roadmap, and report progress, value, and risk to divisional and senior leadership.

Required Qualifications

& Skills 7+ years of

experience

in data roles with significant

experience

in data and information governance with a focus on enterprise-scale initiatives, including ownership of a governance framework end to end rather than contribution to someone else's. Deep expertise across the core data governance disciplines: operating models and decision rights, policies and standards, data ownership and stewardship, metadata management and business glossary, data quality, data classification, and data lifecycle and retention. Demonstrated

experience

designing and standing up a data governance operating model — councils and forums, charters, data owner and steward networks, RACI, and escalation — and authoring the policies, standards, procedures, and exception and issue-remediation processes that make it operable and adopted. Strong data quality management

experience

defining dimensions and rules for critical data elements, profiling and measurement, scorecards and service levels, root cause analysis, and driving remediation through to closure. Practical working knowledge of data privacy, data protection, and compliance requirements in large enterprises (such as GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, COPPA, PCI DSS, and SOX) and of how to translate them into data classification, access, masking, and retention requirements alongside Privacy, Legal, and Security partners.

Experience

with access and entitlement governance, including role- and attribute-based access models, dynamic masking, request and approval workflows, and periodic access review and recertification. Background in GRC (Governance, Risk, and Compliance) programs, covering risk and control frameworks, control design and evidence, issue management, audit support, and reporting into governance committees. Hands-on

experience

with data governance tooling across catalog, business glossary, lineage, data quality, and policy enforcement (for example Collibra, Alation, Atlan, Informatica, Microsoft Purview, Immuta, or OneTrust), and with governing data held in modern cloud platforms such as Snowflake and Databricks.

Experience

governing data used for analytics, machine learning, and Generative AI, covering provenance, approved use, and responsible AI principles. Excellent communication, facilitation, and influencing skills, with a track record of bringing business, engineering, legal, and privacy stakeholders to a shared decision, and the ability to write clearly for both executive and practitioner audiences. Sufficient technical fluency to engage credibly with data engineering, architecture, and semantic modeling teams on data models, access controls, and platform capabilities, without owning the build. Proven ability to run two mandates in parallel — a large cross-company program and a divisional advisory and delivery portfolio — and to prioritize independently in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment. Desired

Qualifications

Experience

leading data governance in large, complex enterprises, preferably in media, entertainment, or hospitality. Governance

experience

in a federated or multi-domain operating model, such as data mesh or domain-oriented ownership, where authority is shared rather than centralized. Familiarity with industry governance frameworks and standards (DAMA-DMBOK, DCAM, EDM Council, ISO/IEC 38505, NIST Privacy Framework) and

experience

running a maturity assessment against one of them. Professional certification such as CDMP (DAMA), DCAM, CIPP/E or CIPM (IAPP), CISA, or CISM.

Experience

governing data products and internal data marketplaces, including data contracts, certification, and usage terms.

Experience

of master data and reference data management governance.

Experience

with records management and retention schedules, and with privacy operations such as data subject access requests, consent, and data minimization. Awareness of semantic technologies — ontologies, taxonomies, knowledge graphs, and semantic layers — and of how governance metadata, ownership, and quality rules attach to them.

Experience

of responsible AI or AI governance programs, including model and use-case inventories and review processes under emerging AI regulation. Working SQL skills, or the ability to read a data model and profile data, sufficient to validate quality findings and ask sharper questions of engineering teams. Required

Education

Bachelor's degree and/or equivalent work

experience

Preferred

Education

Master's degree and/or equivalent work

experience

job.title: #2 Operator in PrePress - 2nd Shift
job.description:
#2 Operator in Prepress, 2nd Shift


Job Description

We are hiring a #2 Operator in Prepress for our printing plant team in Eagan, Minnesota. In this mid-level operator role on our Core Print Solutions team, you will provide leadership and work direction, and train and develop crew members to consistently optimize overall performance.

Location: Eagan, Minnesota


Schedule: 2nd Shift 2:30p - 10:30p, with occasional overtime of up to 4 hours per day and occasional weekend shifts


Key Responsibilities

  • Review job specifications for material and set-up requirements
  • Perform or delegate set-up tasks
  • Monitor equipment and product throughout the job run to ensure high quality
  • Perform moderately complex troubleshooting related to product or equipment
  • Communicate effectively during the shift and at shift hand-off
  • Evaluate the mechanical condition of equipment, complete preventive maintenance, and involve Maintenance as needed
  • Use computer-based workflow applications to manage files
  • Work independently, since results are not typically checked by others
  • Provide leadership, work direction, and training to crew members to consistently optimize overall performance

Required Qualifications

  • High School Diploma, GED, or higher
  • Ability to read, interpret, and explain safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and production orders
  • Experience with Lean and continuous improvement
  • Good communication skills, including experience sharing information across shifts and departments
  • Proven success as a trainer
  • Competence with rulers and measurement tools
  • Able to regularly lift at least 5 lbs. above the shoulder, and occasionally push, pull, and lift at least 10 lbs. up to 50 lbs.
  • Able to regularly stand, walk, crouch, bend, reach, and kneel
  • Able to pass a background check and drug test, as applicable for the role

Preferred Qualifications

  • Vocational or technical degree

#LI-CB1

 

 

What’s in it For You?

  • Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our commitment of empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.

  • Career Development and Growth: By fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development, we prepare our talent to tackle tomorrow’s challenges and deliver real-world solutions. Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.

  • Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include paid leave, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.

  • Culture: Globally recognized, award-winning reputation for inclusion and belonging, flexibility, work-life balance, and more. We live by our values: Obsess over our Customers, Compete to Win, Challenge (Y)our Thinking, Act Fast / Learn Fast, and Stronger Together.

  • Social Impact: Make an impact in your community with our Social Impact Institute. We offer employees two paid volunteer days off annually and opportunities to get involved with pro-bono consulting projects and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives.

  • Making a Real-World Impact: We are one of the few companies globally that helps its customers pursue justice, truth, and transparency. Together, with the professionals and institutions we serve, we help uphold the rule of law, turn the wheels of commerce, catch bad actors, report the facts, and provide trusted, unbiased information to people all over the world.

 

 

In the United States, Thomson Reuters offers a comprehensive benefits package to our employees. Our benefit package includes market competitive health, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance programs, as well as a competitive 401k plan with company match. In addition, Thomson Reuters offers market leading work life benefits with competitive vacation, sick and safe paid time off, paid holidays (including two company mental health days off), parental leave, sabbatical leave. These benefits meet or exceeds the requirements of paid time off in accordance with any applicable state or municipal laws. Finally, Thomson Reuters offers the following additional benefits: optional hospital, accident and sickness insurance paid 100% by the employee; optional life and AD&D insurance paid 100% by the employee; Flexible Spending and Health Savings Accounts; fitness reimbursement; access to Employee Assistance Program; Group Legal Identity Theft Protection benefit paid 100% by employee; access to 529 Plan; commuter benefits; Adoption & Surrogacy Assistance; Tuition Reimbursement; and access to Employee Stock Purchase Plan.

Thomson Reuters complies with local laws that require upfront disclosure of the expected pay range for a position. The base compensation range varies across locations. For any eligible US locations, unless otherwise noted, the base compensation hourly range for this role is $21 USD - $39 USD. Base pay is positioned within the range based on several factors including an individual’s knowledge, skills and experience with consideration given to internal equity. Base pay is one part of a comprehensive Total Reward program which also includes flexible and supportive benefits and other wellbeing programs. This role may also be eligible for an Annual Bonus based on a combination of enterprise and individual performance.

About Us

Thomson Reuters informs the way forward by bringing together the trusted content and technology that people and organizations need to make the right decisions. We serve professionals across legal, tax, accounting, compliance, government, and media. Our products combine highly specialized software and insights to empower professionals with the data, intelligence, and solutions needed to make informed decisions, and to help institutions in their pursuit of justice, truth, and transparency. Reuters, part of Thomson Reuters, is a world leading provider of trusted journalism and news.

We are powered by the talents of 26,000 employees across more than 70 countries, where everyone has a chance to contribute and grow professionally in flexible work environments. At a time when objectivity, accuracy, fairness, and transparency are under attack, we consider it our duty to pursue them. Sound exciting? Join us and help shape the industries that move society forward.

As a global business, we rely on the unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences of all employees to deliver on our business goals. To ensure we can do that, we seek talented, qualified employees in all our operations around the world regardless of race, color, sex/gender, including pregnancy, gender identity and expression, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, disability, age, marital status, citizen status, veteran status, or any other protected classification under applicable law. Thomson Reuters is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer providing a drug-free workplace.

Thomson Reuters makes reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities, including veterans with disabilities, and for sincerely held religious beliefs in accordance with applicable law. If you reside in the United States and require an accommodation in the recruiting process, you may contact our Human Resources Department at HR.Leave-Expert@thomsonreuters.com. Disability accommodations in the recruiting process may include things like a sign language interpreter, making interview rooms accessible, providing assistive technology, or other relevant accommodations. job.title: Account Manager, Migration
job.description:
Job Description


This account manager position leads the migration of existing Thomson Reuters Corporate SMB customers to CoCounsel, working a defined list of assigned target accounts from first conversation through completed migration. You will be expected to meet/exceed migration and customer engagement activity targets (emphasis on account outreach, discovery conversations, and migration progression) as established.


This position supports the efforts of the SMB Corporates organization within Thomson Reuters Legal by accelerating CoCounsel adoption across our existing customer base. This role requires a seasoned, consultative seller who can quickly diagnose each customer's current workflows, articulate the value of CoCounsel, overcome resistance to change, and guide accounts through a smooth upsell transition.

Key Responsibilities

In this opportunity as a CoCounsel Account Manager, you will:

  • Achieve and exceed monthly and annual migration quotas, measuring accounts migrated within set KPI’s and sales processes
  • Proactively engage decision-makers and end users at assigned accounts using outbound calls, emails, and LinkedIn Sales Navigator to schedule discovery and migration conversations
  • Gather and log all call information, migration orders, and account activity within Salesforce, Thomson Reuters CRM system, correctly and accurately, ensuring migration status and stage are tracked for every target account
  • Develop and deliver accurate migration forecasts and account-level progress reporting against the target list
  • Identify and escalate migration risks (contract and renewal timing, technical or adoption blockers) and build account-specific plans to resolve them
  • Assume other responsibilities as required or requested by Sales Management
  • Own a defined list of existing Corporate SMB target accounts and drive each account from initial outreach through completed transition to CoCounsel

Relationship Management

  • Serve as the trusted advisor for each assigned account through the migration, using consultative discovery to map current workflows to CoCounsel capabilities and demonstrate clear value
  • Work with organizations (Customer Success, Onboarding and Training, Product Specialists, Order Fulfillment, Customer Service, etc.) throughout Thomson Reuters to ensure migrations are executed efficiently and accurately and customer issues are resolved in a timely manner
  • Actively contribute to and works responsibly in a team environment, including collaborating with Account Managers and key stakeholders who own the broader customer relationship
  • Capture customer feedback, objections, and competitive insights from conversations and share them to refine playbooks and product strategy
  • Maintain expert knowledge of CoCounsel and the legacy products being migrated, along with migration programs and incentives within the sales division
  • Actively participate in meetings, training sessions and individual professional development and skill building

Required Qualifications

You’re a fit for the Account Manager if your background includes:

  • Minimum of 4 years of B2B sales experience with a consistent record of quota attainment, ideally including customer conversions, incremental sales, renewals, or technology transitions
  • College Degree in business, sales or related field strongly preferred
  • Proven ability to manage a defined book of accounts and drive change with existing customers; outbound outreach experience required
  • Experience selling AI, SaaS, or legal technology solutions strongly preferred
  • Strong organizational and time management skills coupled with the ability to embrace change
  • Pipeline management skills in the CRM environment required – Salesforce.com experience strongly preferred
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office applications; including ability to demonstrate online products using web-based tools (Microsoft Teams, Zoom, WebEx, etc.)
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to negotiate migration terms, pricing, and timelines with customers within set parameters
  • Demonstrated knowledge of proper telephone etiquette and professional attitude and integrity
  • Legal industry knowledge or experience, particularly with corporate legal departments, strongly preferred
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent migrations and prioritize effectively across the assigned target list

Preferred Qualifications


  • N/A

This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.

  • Career Development and Growth: By fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development, we prepare our talent to tackle tomorrow’s challenges and deliver real-world solutions. Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.

  • Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.

  • Culture: Globally recognized, award-winning reputation for inclusion and belonging, flexibility, work-life balance, and more. We live by our values: Obsess over our Customers, Compete to Win, Challenge (Y)our Thinking, Act Fast / Learn Fast, and Stronger Together.

  • Social Impact: Make an impact in your community with our Social Impact Institute. We offer employees two paid volunteer days off annually and opportunities to get involved with pro-bono consulting projects and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives.

  • Making a Real-World Impact: We are one of the few companies globally that helps its customers pursue justice, truth, and transparency. Together, with the professionals and institutions we serve, we help uphold the rule of law, turn the wheels of commerce, catch bad actors, report the facts, and provide trusted, unbiased information to people all over the world.
